fix(anthropic): Claude models fail with a missing API key after an earlier Claude CLI sign-in (#168074)

Related: #167963

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude models that Claude CLI sign-in did not add fail with "No API key found for provider anthropic" for anyone who signed in to Claude CLI on a release since native Claude CLI login (#129052), because those configs predate the `anthropic/*` runtime entry that #167963 now writes at sign-in. Sign-in also still added deprecated catalog models such as `claude-opus-4-8` to fresh configs.

## User Impact

User impact: after `openclaw update` (or `openclaw doctor --fix`), an earlier Claude CLI sign-in routes every Claude model through Claude Code, the same as a fresh sign-in. Fresh sign-ins no longer add deprecated catalog models; an existing entry for one, such as `claude-opus-4-8`, is kept.

Configs with an Anthropic credential, an API default model with a Claude CLI fallback, a provider-level Anthropic runtime, or an existing `anthropic/*` entry are left unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Anthropic plugin now owns a Doctor config repair (`doctorContract.configRepair`). It adds `agents.defaults.models["anthropic/*"] = { agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" } }` only when all of these hold:

- the default model is an `anthropic/...` ref whose entry pins `claude-cli` (what sign-in writes);
- no `anthropic/*` entry exists, whatever runtime it names;
- no `models.providers.anthropic.agentRuntime` (the wildcard would outrank it);
- no Anthropic credential is visible to config repair: an `anthropic` auth profile, a provider `apiKey` other than the retired `anthropic:claude-cli` marker, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN` in the environment or config `env`.

Specific model entries keep winning over the wildcard, so entries that name a runtime are unaffected. Runtime reads only the canonical entry; there is no new compatibility reader. The change is reported as a Doctor change (`openclaw doctor` lists it, `--fix` writes it).

Sign-in seeding filters catalog rows with `status: "deprecated"`. Route probing and the setup picker still see every row.

## Update Behavior

The installed updater cannot be patched, so the repair keys only on config that shipped Claude CLI sign-ins already wrote. During `openclaw update`, the candidate's own Doctor runs twice: once as `doctor --fix` in the candidate rehearsal on a private state snapshot (`candidate-doctor`), then as `doctor --repair --non-interactive` in a fresh process after the package swap (`openclaw doctor`). The second run writes the repair through Doctor's normal backed-up config write (`openclaw.json.bak` ring plus `openclaw.json.pre-update`), so update rollback restores the earlier config. The update result lists the change under the Doctor migration notes. Gateway startup does not apply it to a valid config. After a manual package replacement, run `openclaw doctor --fix`.

## Evidence

- Regression tests fail at the parent commit and pass here:
  - `extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts`: `registered cli sign-in seeds no deprecated Claude CLI catalog rows` fails at the parent (`expected { …(12) } to not have property "anthropic/claude-opus-4-8"`). Its second case shows an existing `claude-opus-4-8` default and entry survive sign-in. Three existing seeding expectations drop `claude-opus-4-8`.
  - `extensions/anthropic/doctor-contract-api.test.ts`: covers the repair, idempotency, both kinds of existing wildcard, an API default with a Claude CLI fallback, a non-Anthropic default, auth profile, provider API key, config env key, process env key, provider-level runtime, and the retired provider marker. At the parent the module does not exist.
- Published-driver × candidate cells: Docker `bare` image, published `openclaw@2026.9.9` from npm, sign-in through the published `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --auth-choice anthropic-cli` with a stub `claude` that only answers `claude auth status`. Then `openclaw update --tag file:<candidate tgz> --no-restart --yes --json` to a package built by `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` from this head:

  | Cell | Config before update | `update` | `anthropic/*` after | Other model entries | Post-update `doctor` / `config validate` |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | A | 2026.9.9 sign-in: 11 seeded rows pinned `claude-cli`, default `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, no wildcard | `status: ok`, `2026.9.9 (bcfc888)` → `(587456f)`; result notes `Doctor migration: agents.defaults.models["anthropic/*"]: added the claude-cli runtime …` | `{ agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" } }` | unchanged (only `anthropic/*` differs); `.bak`, `.bak.1` and `.pre-update` have no wildcard | exit 0, no further Anthropic finding / `Config valid` |
  | B | A plus `"anthropic/*": { agentRuntime: { id: "openclaw" } }` | `status: ok` | still `openclaw` | unchanged | exit 0 / `Config valid` |
  | C | A plus an `anthropic:default` API-key auth profile | `status: ok` | absent | unchanged | exit 0 / `Config valid` |

  Replaying the candidate Doctor on a copy of cell A's pre-update config: `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` lists the `agents.defaults.models["anthropic/*"]` change and leaves the file unchanged. `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` writes `{ agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" } }` and rotates `openclaw.json.bak`. The same replays leave cells B and C unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files: clean. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed every lane, including the doctor contract declaration and closure guard tests and the extension typechecks, except the dead-export scan. That scan flags only untouched files (`extensions/telegram/src/sequential-key.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`). With `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1` it exits 0.

## Merge Danger

One-way door: `openclaw update` and `doctor --fix` write `anthropic/*` into existing configs. A revert stops new writes but does not remove entries already written; the pre-update backup still has the earlier config. Blast radius: Claude CLI users with no Anthropic credential visible to config repair. Claude IDs without a specific runtime-pinned entry move from a failing API route to Claude Code. A user whose only Anthropic API key lives in the auth store, with no config auth profile or env var, and who sets a Claude CLI-pinned default model, would also see unpinned Claude IDs move to Claude Code. That is the routing a fresh Claude CLI sign-in now produces.

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

fix(doctor): skip redundant continuation writes inside service inspection deadlines (#168069)

fix: hide unfinished reasoning in truncated replies (#156939)

* fix: hide MiMo inline thinking leaks with strict reasoning-tag partitioning

MiMo v2.5+ models served through vLLM/OpenAI-compatible endpoints with the
mimo reasoning parser can stream inline <think> markup into content, and on
tool-result turns the closer is absorbed server-side. The non-strict
partitioner then flushed the unclosed opener as visible text, leaking
thinking into the UI despite reasoningDefault=off and /reasoning off.

Mark a fresh copy of stream options strict for MiMo v2.5+ models both in the
Xiaomi extension wrapStreamFn hook and as an extra-params fallback for
custom OpenAI-compatible proxies, reusing the existing strict
reasoning-tag partitioning path. Legacy mimo-v2-pro/omni (reasoning_content
carries final answers) stay untouched.

* fix: scope MiMo reasoning-tag hiding to a stream-safe on-flush level

Review follow-ups for #156939:

- Introduce a second strictness level (STRICT_REASONING_TAG_TEXT_ON_FLUSH)
  so the MiMo wrapper hides unclosed inline thinking at each flush boundary
  without downgrading the public strictReasoningTags contract used by TTS,
  labels and compaction (full strict keeps its buffer-everything semantics).
- Rename the MiMo-specific SDK wrapper to the generic
  createStrictReasoningTagsWrapper with an injected model predicate and a
  shouldMarkStrictOnFlush option so the seam no longer encodes one provider.
- Document and test the per-flush-segment guarantee boundary (post tool-call
  segments classify fresh) in the partitioner interface and stream suites.
- Resolve the tri-state transport mode via one shared helper
  (resolveStrictReasoningTagsMode) used by both mapping sites.
- Extract MiMo wiring from extra-params.ts into the sibling
  extra-params.mimo-reasoning.ts to satisfy the line-cap ratchet.
- Assert symbol propagation in the xiaomi extension tests and add
  provider-options mapping tests; keep both MiMo model-id lists annotated
  with explicit cross-list sync notes.

* fix(ci): keep MiMo reasoning-tag seam knip-clean

MIMO_STRICT_REASONING_TAGS_MODEL_IDS is only consumed in-module, so drop its
export; the classification predicate stays exported for the focused fallback
test with a scoped knip ignoreIssues entry, matching the precedent for
test-consumed seams (e.g. embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle).

* fix(plugin-sdk): document strict reasoning-tag helper, drop test-only classifier export

- extra-params.mimo-reasoning: `isMiMoStrictReasoningTagsModel` remains the
  in-module classifier used by `createMiMoStrictReasoningTagsWrapper`, but is no
  longer exported; nothing outside the module consumed it except its test.
- knip: reverse the exemption for `extra-params.mimo-reasoning.ts` added in
  a79d1c7e, which only existed to suppress that test-only export.
- test: assert the full `MIMO_STRICT_REASONING_TAGS_MODEL_IDS` matrix through the
  observable extra-params seam (every set member plus proxy/`:suffix` and
  non-completions negatives), which is stricter than the removed direct call, and
  assert the captured options are defined so negative rows cannot pass vacuously.
- docs: list `createStrictReasoningTagsWrapper` under
  `plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared`, where it is actually exported, with its
  caller-supplied predicate called out.

Co-authored-by: Alfredo Medrano <alfredomedranosanchez@gmail.com>

fix(update): reclaim dead legacy child-lineage handoff leases in update repair (#168043)

Admission mistook the unbound legacy reservation for a detached process group, and repair ignored child-only rows. Repair now reclaims legacy update rows, including child-lineage descendants, when every recorded executor and helper is proven dead, retains recovery evidence and records the reclaimed keys; live or uninspectable owners (for example hidden by /proc hidepid) still refuse with an actionable message. feat(discord): show per-tool glyphs on progress draft tool rows (#168032)

## What Problem This Solves

Discord progress drafts show tool-log rows without a per-tool glyph (`• Exec: running`), while Telegram shows `🛠️ Exec: running` since #167392. Discord already marks the 🧠 reasoning and 💬 commentary lanes, so its tool rows were the only unmarked lane.

## User Impact

Discord tool-log rows in progress drafts now start with the tool's text glyph (`🛠️ Exec`, `📖 Read`, `🩹 Apply Patch`). The 🧠 / 💬 lanes, plan rows, approval rows, and plain status rows are unchanged. No config changes. Slack and other channels keep plain rows.

## Why This Change Was Made

#167392 added the core opt-in (`toolIcons?: boolean` on `createChannelProgressDraftCompositor`, glyph table in `src/channels/progress-tool-glyphs.ts`) and left Discord as a follow-up. This PR sets `toolIcons: true` on every Discord compositor so all Discord paths render the same:

- live draft preview (`message-handler.draft-preview.ts`)
- retained progress continuation after handoff (`message-handler.progress-continuation.ts`)
- retained-card `edit` action rendering a progress snapshot (`runtime.messaging.messages.ts`)

No Discord-specific glyph code. Rows that already carry an explicit `icon` keep it.

## Tests

- `message-handler.draft-preview.rest.test.ts`: new regression through the real draft preview and Discord REST client: `🧠 _Planning the check_` / `💬 Looking at the workspace` / `🛠️ Exec: running` / `📖 Read: running`. Fails on main with `• Exec: running` / `• Read: running`.
- `message-bodies.test.ts`: a retained row's explicit icon (`🧪 Read`) wins over the tool glyph.
- `message-handler.process.draft-final.test.ts`: existing expectations updated to the glyph rows.

## Bounded cost

- One static `Record` lookup per core-built tool row on Discord (core opt-in from #167392).
- No new config keys, protocol fields, network calls, or extra Discord sends/edits; the draft text gains one glyph and a space per tool row, inside the existing per-message length bounds.
- Production: +3 lines. Tests: +65/−5. Docs: +3/−3. No extra Discord sends or edits in the runs above beyond the existing progress-draft cadence.

## Evidence

Isolated gateway (`HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` under `/tmp`) with the real bundled Discord plugin against QA Lab's Crabline Discord provider server, `streaming.mode: "progress"`, `progress.toolProgress: true`. Rows below are the Discord REST bodies the plugin sent, from the Crabline provider recorder (`artifacts/crabline/discord-provider-server.jsonl`).

**Live model `openai/gpt-6-astra`** (`qa suite --provider-mode live-frontier --model openai/gpt-6-astra --channel-driver crabline --channel discord`), prompt asked for one exec then one read:

```
POST  "Working\n\n🛠️ Exec: running\n🛠️ Exec: running"
PATCH "Working\n\n🛠️ Exec: running\n🛠️ Exec"
PATCH "…\n\n🛠️ Exec\n🛠️ Exec\n🛠️ Exec: running"
PATCH "…\n\n🛠️ Exec\n🛠️ Exec\n🛠️ Exec\n📖 Read from glyph-proof.txt"
POST  final reply (separate message)
```

**Scripted model (`mock-openai`)**, commentary + one exec:

```
POST  "Working\n\n💬 SLACK-QA-COMMENTARY-200C8C6D"
PATCH "Working\n\n💬 SLACK-QA-COMMENTARY-200C8C6D\n🛠️ Exec: running"
PATCH "Working\n\n💬 SLACK-QA-COMMENTARY-200C8C6D\n🛠️ Exec"
POST  "SLACK-QA-COMMENTARY-DONE-200C8C6D"
```

The 💬 commentary lane keeps its prefix, and the final reply is one separate message, as before. Before this change, the same rows render as `• Exec: running` / `• Read: running` (the new REST regression fails on main with exactly that diff).

fix(anthropic): Claude models fail with a missing API key after Claude CLI sign-in unless sign-in seeded them (#167963)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after Claude CLI sign-in (`openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic --method cli`), any `anthropic/<id>` that sign-in did not seed fails with `No API key found for provider "anthropic" … missing-provider-auth`. This affects Claude models published after sign-in and IDs typed with `--model`, `/model` or `models set`, such as `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`.

## User Impact

User impact: Claude-CLI-only users can type or pick any Claude model and it runs through Claude Code. The model picker still lists only models the Claude CLI catalog serves, so `claude-mythos-5` (direct API only) stays hidden. Users with an Anthropic API key and no Claude CLI sign-in keep the API route. Exact model entries that name another runtime still win. A session pinned to an Anthropic API-key account keeps that account's models, including `claude-mythos-5`, in its picker.

Existing installs that signed in on an affected build get the new routing only after they rerun `openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic --method cli`. This PR adds no Doctor migration.

User-authored `provider/*` wildcards for other CLI backends behave exactly as on `main`. For example, `google/*` → `google-gemini-cli` keeps the same picker rows, and its typed IDs run as before. The picker gate is keyed on the `anthropic/*` → `claude-cli` entry that sign-in writes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #129052, Claude CLI sign-in persists no OpenClaw auth profile. At run time, `resolveCliRuntimeExecutionProvider` (src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts) found no runtime policy for unseeded IDs and no `claude-cli` profile it could alias. The turn then fell to the embedded Anthropic API path. An instrumented isolated Gateway on 58ba7ede092 showed `policy=undefined … viaAuthProfile=undefined` and then `useCliExecution=false`.

- Sign-in (`extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.ts`) now also writes the existing, documented provider wildcard `agents.defaults.models["anthropic/*"] = { agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" } }`. It does not overwrite a wildcard that already names another runtime.
- Catalog decisions (`src/agents/model-catalog-cli-wildcard.ts`, used by `model-catalog-decisions.ts`) mark a row unavailable, with no "sign in" reason, when all of these hold: native Claude CLI credentials supplied the availability (`evidence: "runtime"`), the row reaches `claude-cli` only through that sign-in wildcard, the Claude CLI catalog does not list it (bundled manifest plus published catalog), and it is not a configured row. Availability from a selected or pinned API account is never narrowed. Run-time routing is unchanged, so typed IDs still run.

Production change: 3 lines in cli-migration.ts, 15 net lines in model-catalog-decisions.ts and a new 58-line module (about 45 code lines). No config keys, schema or SDK surface change.

Provenance (f8b06fbb69b, #166037): prepared catalog decisions keep saved account, model and runtime choices and their provenance. `createCliRuntimeModelAuthEvaluator` returns a pinned non-native account's own provider-auth result, and `evaluateNative` keeps host results for selected accounts. The wildcard gate now only narrows availability that came from native Claude CLI credentials, so a saved account choice keeps the models that account can use.

## Evidence

Real proofs used the machine's existing native `claude` login, OpenClaw's real sign-in flow, isolated profiles and a loopback Gateway:

- Before, on `main` 58ba7ede092: `models set anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` plus one turn failed with `missing-provider-auth`, and the instrumentation showed no CLI route.
- After, on b35cc8eae0e: the picker lists `available` rows that exactly match the 11 Claude CLI catalog IDs. `claude-mythos-5` and `claude-haiku-4-5` are not listed.
- After: a turn typed with `--model anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` returned `OK` with `runner=cli` and `winnerProvider=claude-cli`.
- After: `models set anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` plus a turn returned `OK` through `claude-cli`.
- API-key control: on a profile with `paste-api-key` (key piped on stdin) and no Claude CLI sign-in, an `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` turn returned `OK` with `runner=embedded` and `winnerProvider=anthropic`. Mythos stays listed for API users, as on `main`.
- Regressions:
  - `extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts`, including the registered non-interactive sign-in entry: 4 failures without the fix, 40/40 pass with it.
  - `src/agents/model-catalog-decisions.test.ts`: the Claude CLI wildcard test fails without the gate (`expected true to be false`). With the gate, it covers a listed row, an API-only row (unavailable, no reason), an exact pinned row, a configured typed row, an exact override to `openclaw`, and an unchanged `google/*` → `google-gemini-cli` row even when that backend lists its own rows.
  - Same test, selected-account case (added on 41f26e5206f): with the wildcard and a session pinned to an Anthropic API-key profile, `claude-mythos-5` is available with `selectedProfileId: "anthropic:work"` in both `evaluateEntry` and `evaluateNative`. With only native Claude CLI credentials it stays unavailable. On 651801e5843 this fails (`expected { availability: false … } to match object { availability: true … }`). With the fix, 24/24 pass in the file, and `model-auth-availability.test.ts` plus `cli-migration.test.ts` pass.

- New-model simulation on 651801e5843, in a throwaway worktree with `claude-fable-5` removed from local knowledge: both bundled manifest rows (`anthropic`, `claude-cli`), the `fable-5` alias, the model-catalog-core alias and the Claude CLI context alias. `models.catalogRefresh.url` pointed at a loopback copy of `catalog.openclaw.ai/models/v2/catalog.json`, served at first without `anthropic/claude-fable-5` and `claude-cli/claude-fable-5`.
  - Before: `models.list {view:"configured", refresh:true}` (the Control UI view) returned 10 Claude rows and no Fable 5 row.
  - I added both rows back only in the served copy, with a newer `generatedAt`, then ran `openclaw models refresh` and `models.list {refresh:true}`. The Gateway PID did not change. The first response was unchanged because adoption starts after that response. The next read listed `claude-cli/claude-fable-5` as available, but not `anthropic/claude-fable-5`. A Gateway restart gave the same rows, so the refresh lifecycle is not the cause.
  - Turns: `--model anthropic/claude-fable-5` returned `OK` on the same Gateway PID with `runner=cli`, `winnerProvider=claude-cli` and `winnerModel=claude-fable-5`. `--model claude-cli/claude-fable-5`, the row the picker shows, also returned `OK` through `claude-cli`.

Upgrade cell (published v2026.9.9 → this PR, disposable Docker container from the `scripts/e2e/Dockerfile` `bare` stage, candidate packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` from 41f26e5206f, build `2026.9.9-41f26e5206fc`). `api.anthropic.com` resolved to loopback in the container, so the fake key never left it. npm `latest` is still 2026.9.9.
- Existing state was written by the published CLI. It had a Claude CLI-style `agents.defaults.models` with three `anthropic/*` IDs on `claude-cli` and no wildcard, primary `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, and an `anthropic:work` API-key profile from `paste-api-key` with a fake key. Through the v2026.9.9 Gateway, `sessions.create` and then `sessions.patch {model:"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5@anthropic:work"}` saved this session selection: `providerOverride=anthropic, modelOverride=claude-sonnet-5, authProfileOverride=anthropic:work (user), agentRuntimeOverride=claude-cli`.
- `openclaw update --tag file:<tgz> --no-restart --yes --json` exited 0 with `status: ok` and all steps at 0. The CLI now reports `OpenClaw 2026.9.9 (41f26e5)`. The updater's doctor, `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` and `config validate` passed (`valid: true`, no warnings). Doctor warnings matched the baseline: a plaintext gateway token in the fixture, loopback bind and no service manager. The saved session selection and `agents.defaults.models` read back identical to the pre-update values.
- Claude CLI sign-in again, with the real `openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic --method cli --set-default` under a pty. It needs a TTY. Without a `claude` binary it stops with `Claude CLI is not authenticated on this host`. With a stub `claude` on `PATH` that only answers `auth status --json` with `{"loggedIn":true,"authMethod":"claude.ai"}` and `--version`, and never runs a model, it exited 0. That was the only stubbed part; the sign-in, config write and Gateway are the shipped code. After the first sign-in, `"anthropic/*": {agentRuntime:{id:"claude-cli"}}` was present once. A second sign-in left it present once. The three existing entries and the primary were unchanged, the session selection was identical after each sign-in, and `config validate` and doctor passed.
- Candidate Gateway with the wildcard present: `models.list {sessionKey, view:"all", provider:"anthropic"}` for the session pinned to `anthropic:work` listed `claude-mythos-5` as `available: true`. `models.list {agentId:"main"}`, with no selected account, listed it as `available: false`, which is the accepted Claude CLI-first behavior.
- Not covered: no real Claude Code turn ran in the cell. Real turns are in the evidence above. The update's package swap took 23 min on a loaded host; an earlier v2026.9.9 cell on the same host took 7–11 min for the whole update. No Telegram Test Server run.

Gap: a Claude model that the published catalog adds later appears in the picker without a restart, but only as `claude-cli/<id>`, not `anthropic/<id>`. `anthropic` is a `refreshable` catalog provider, so its published rows appear only when live `/v1/models` discovery returns them, and that discovery needs an API key. The `src/agents/model-catalog.ts` guard says "Only live registry or refreshed rows may publish those provider models". `claude-cli` is `static`, so its published row appears. The sign-in wildcard gate only marks existing `anthropic` rows unavailable and never adds rows, so the `claude-cli` row has no `anthropic` twin to fold into. Both refs run through Claude Code. Showing `anthropic/<id>` would need a separate change to the refreshable-provider guard in `model-catalog.ts` or to the CLI twin collapse in `model-runtime-aliases.ts`.

## Merge danger

Medium-low. The run-time change is config written only by Claude CLI sign-in. The picker change sits in shared catalog decisions, but it applies only when an agent's `anthropic/*` entry names `claude-cli` and the row is neither configured nor listed by the Claude CLI catalog.

fix(channels): Telegram progress drafts lost per-tool emoji on tool rows (#167392) ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Telegram progress drafts lost the leading per-tool emoji on tool-log rows (`🛠️ Exec`, `📖 Read`) after #165095 moved tool display metadata to semantic icons. ## User Impact User impact: Telegram tool-log rows show a per-tool glyph again, in standard and rich-message previews. Slack and every other channel keep plain rows, and graphical clients are unchanged. No config changes. ## Why This Change Was Made #165095 (42ebb9d7348) replaced each tool's `emoji` with one semantic `icon` and moved status-reaction emoji to a reaction-only table. As a side effect, core stopped setting `ChannelProgressDraftLine.icon`, so Telegram's renderer no longer had a glyph to show. Removing the glyph was not the goal of #165095. Core now owns the text presentation of those icons, following the native-client pattern from #165095: - **One table.** `src/channels/progress-tool-glyphs.ts` maps each semantic tool icon to a text emoji. A coverage test fails if a configured icon has no glyph, like the Swift and Android tables. - **One producer.** `buildNamedProgressLine`, where draft lines are built, fills `line.icon` only when the caller passes `toolIcons`. Plan and approval rows stay plain, commentary/reasoning rows are unchanged, and lines a plugin builds with its own `icon` keep it. - **Per-channel opt-in.** Tool emoji look out of place on some channels, Slack especially, so the default is plain. A channel opts in with one optional SDK field, `toolIcons?: boolean`, on `createChannelProgressDraftCompositor` (next to the existing `reasoningLinePrefix`/`commentaryLinePrefix` lane markers) and on the `buildChannelProgressDraftLine` options. Telegram opts in; nothing else does. This PR began as a Telegram-only fix by @keshavbotagent that reused the status-reaction emoji table inside the Telegram plugin. Per maintainer direction it now uses a core owner. That reaction-table use is gone, and Keshav's commit and credit remain. Follow-up for a maintainer decision: Discord already passes the 🧠/💬 lane markers and could opt in with `toolIcons: true`. This PR leaves Discord unchanged. ## Bounded cost - When a channel opts in, each core-built tool row costs one static `Record` lookup. Channels that don't opt in skip it. - No new config keys, protocol fields, network calls, or extra Telegram sends or edits. In the live runs below, before and after each sent one progress message, six edits, and one final reply. - Production: +63/−1 lines (47 of them are the glyph table). Tests: +50. Docs: +5/−2. ## Evidence **Regression tests (each failed on clean `origin/main` and passes on this head):** - `src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts`, the `prefixes generated tool rows with text glyphs…` case. With `toolIcons` it renders `💬 _Checking_\n🛠️ Exec: running\n🧪 Read: running`. By default it renders `• Exec: running`. In both cases commentary is unchanged and an explicit plugin icon (`🧪`) wins. On main: `- 🛠️ Exec: running / + • Exec: running`. - `src/channels/progress-tool-glyphs.test.ts`: every icon in `TOOL_DISPLAY_CONFIG` (tools and fallback) has a glyph. - `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.preview.telegram-http.test.ts`: real Telegram dispatch over HTTP Bot API. The progress card keeps `🛠️ Exec` through the failure edit. On main: `expected 'Working\nExec failed…' to contain '🛠️ Exec'`. - These suites also pass: the focused channel, streaming, and tool-display suites, plus the Telegram dispatch suites (preview, progress-card, final-delivery-lifecycle, reply-targets, draft-stream). **Telegram Test Server, live `gpt-6-astra` (real-user DM, `streaming.progress.toolProgress: true`).** Prompt: run `printf glyph-check > note.txt` with exec, read `note.txt`, then reply `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK`. Each run made 5 `gpt-6-astra` requests, all 200. | | Progress card, last edit | Final | | --- | --- | --- | | Before (`origin/main` aa60a5fa072) | `Working ⏎ Skill Search write read local text file ⏎ … ⏎ Exec ⏎ Read lines 1-10 from note.txt ⏎ Exec` | `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK`; card deleted | | After (this PR, 126e5c37fa4; later commits change tests only) | `Working ⏎ 🔎 Skill Search write and read a local text file shell printf ⏎ … ⏎ 🛠️ Exec ⏎ 📖 Read lines 1-10 from note.txt ⏎ 🛠️ Exec` | `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK`; card deleted | **Slack stays plain (isolated formatter check).** Core progress lines from the real compositor, built with Slack's flags (no `toolIcons`) and rendered through Slack's real `formatSlackProgressDraftLine`, `buildSlackProgressTextBlocks`, and `buildSlackProgressCardBlocks`: ``` Slack flags: draft "• Exec: running\n• Read: note.txt"; card "Exec — running\nRead — note.txt · running"; glyphs: none control toolIcons: draft "🛠️ Exec: running\n📖 Read: note.txt"; card unchanged (Slack cards ignore icon) ``` The existing Slack dispatch suite still asserts plain `Bash` / `Apply Patch` task titles. **CI:** Everything is green on c6a2d40d952 except one test, `extensions/whatsapp/src/send.delivery-recovery.test.ts` ("preserves long styles and quotes only the first chunk"), in `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle`; `openclaw/ci-gate` fails only because of it. chore(qa): Telegram E2E runs can create and delete their own forum topic (#168012)

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram forum-topic proofs could not run on the Test Server unless someone had already prepared a forum, because the harness only created run-owned forums for private production accounts.

## User Impact

No product change. Maintainers and agents can pass `--create-forum` with a `--scenario` to the Telegram E2E runner: it creates a run-owned forum supergroup and topic under the leased QA user, sends the scenario's messages to that topic, and deletes the forum before the lease is released, including after a failed or interrupted run.

## Why This Change Was Made

- One forum owner in the user driver now serves both environments, and each command family keeps its own guard: `prepare-forum`/`cleanup-forum` run only on Telegram's Test Server with the leased QA user, while `prepare-private-forum`/`cleanup-private-forum` stay production-only for operator-owned accounts. Only the production family creates the one-use invite link that its local-app participants need.
- The runner prepares the forum through the existing readiness path, which then checks the new chat as a selected forum target: bot membership, privacy and tester write access. Forum cleanup is chained ahead of the credential release, the same way run-owned groups are cleaned up. `summary.json` records the forum and topic ids with the setup and cleanup result under `testForum`.
- The recovery helper's `cleanup-group` is now `cleanup`: it cleans a retained run-owned forum and group before releasing the lease.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Live Test Server run with a Convex lease and the mock provider (no live model), on unused ports:

```

  --gateway-port <unused> --mock-port <unused> --create-forum \
  --scenario <send + in-run getChat command> --timeout-ms 45000 \
  --record <proof>/events.ndjson --output <proof>/summary.json
```

| UTC | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| 22:44:57 | Run starts; readiness creates the forum supergroup and topic 3, then verifies it as the selected forum target |
| +0.6 s | QA user message `@<sut> Please answer with OPENCLAW_E2E_OK only.` lands with `topicType: messageTopicForum`, `topicId: 3` |
| 22:45:35 | In-run SUT Bot API `getChat` on the forum: HTTP 200, `type: supergroup`, `is_forum: true` |
| +34.1 s | SUT reply `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK` in the same topic (`messageTopicForum`, `topicId: 3`); 7 mock provider requests |
| 22:46:11 | After cleanup, before the lease release, the same bot's `getChat` on the forum: HTTP 403 `bot was kicked from the supergroup chat`; `summary.json` `testForum.cleanup.status: "deleted"` |

An earlier attempt used a broken proof probe that made the lease release throw. The forum was already deleted, so this was a test of the recovery path on a real retained lease: the QA user's TDLib `getChatMember` on its own former forum returned `CHANNEL_PRIVATE`, the history read returned `Can't access the chat`, and `telegram-test-recover.mjs <lease> cleanup` reported `forum.status: "deleted"` and `group.status: "not-created"`, then released the lease.

Locally, `check-changed` passes every lane before `deprecated API usage`, which fails on the base commit at `src/gateway/server-methods/agents.ts` (unrelated to this diff). fix(openai): ChatGPT-only model list offers unlisted pro models that fail (#167975)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: for a user signed in with only a ChatGPT account, the default model list offers `openai/gpt-5.4-pro` and `openai/gpt-5.5-pro` even though that account's model listing doesn't include them, so choosing either one fails.

## User Impact

ChatGPT-only users stop seeing these two models in the default model view (TUI and the Gateway `models.list` default view). Models the account lists stay, and so do hidden rows the account is entitled to, such as `gpt-5.5`. A user who also has an OpenAI API key still sees both pro models.

## Why This Change Was Made

- A successful ChatGPT account listing now records every model id it returned, hidden rows included, as private `listedModelIds` on the ready provider outcome. The public `providerOutcomes` projection still carries only provider, profile and status.
- The picker's availability check uses that list. A model served both by an API key and by ChatGPT, but missing from the account's listing, can't be used through the ChatGPT account. It stays available only if a usable non-subscription credential exists.
- The list applies only to the credential that made it. The check reads the ready outcome whose `profileId` matches the selected ChatGPT profile; another account's listing never narrows or widens it, and a profile with no ready listing of its own keeps today's behavior.
- When the model is unavailable, no reason code is attached, so the UI and `/models` show a neutral "Unavailable" instead of "Sign-in needed" or "add a key". The user is signed in; this account just doesn't have the model.
- This change covers the picker only. If someone types an unlisted id by hand, the request can still reach OpenAI and fail with OpenAI's own error.
- To stay within the line-cap ratchet, two pieces moved: the runtime credential overlay now lives in `model-auth-availability.runtime-overlay.ts`, and the ready-outcome builder now lives in `extensions/openai/model-service-tiers.ts`. Neither move changes behavior.

## Evidence

Real ChatGPT account (device-code sign-in), isolated profile, loopback Gateway. Same profile, main build `d0fc39e` vs this branch `f53ad9c`:

| Gateway `models.list` view=default, provider openai | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| ChatGPT-only | 11 rows: 8 listed + `gpt-5.4-pro`, `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.5-pro` | 9 rows: 8 listed + `gpt-5.5` |
| ChatGPT + OpenAI API key (control) | n/a | `gpt-5.4-pro`, `gpt-5.5-pro` present and available |

`openclaw models list --provider openai --plain` (configured view) showed the same 8 listed rows on both builds; that view was never affected.

- Regression: `src/agents/model-catalog-decisions.test.ts` "with a ChatGPT account listing". An unlisted dual-route id is unavailable with no reason code. A hidden listed id stays available. With an API key, or when the listing is unavailable, the subscription route is kept.
- Multi-account regression (same file, "uses only the selected account's listing"): profiles A and B, A's ready listing omits `gpt-5.5-pro` and `gpt-5.5`, B selected. B with no outcome or an unavailable outcome keeps the subscription route; B's own listing that includes the model keeps it available; B's own listing that omits it makes it unavailable even when a third account lists it. The no-observation, unavailable, and omits cases fail on `de076ec6362` and pass on the fix. The real-account run above was not repeated: the OpenAI catalog hook already stamps the ready outcome with the discovering profile's id (`projectOpenAICatalog`), which is the selected profile in the single-account case, so that path is unchanged.
- Provider: `extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts`: `listedModelIds` includes hidden rows.
- Suites: model-auth-availability (4 files), model-catalog-decisions, model-catalog-service-tiers, openai-provider (3 files), models-list-result.provider-outcomes. All pass.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passes. This includes the line-cap ratchet, tsgo core and core tests, and plugin boundaries. `oxlint --type-aware` is clean on the changed files.

## Merge Danger

- Adds an optional `listedModelIds` field to `ProviderCatalogOutcome` (the plugin SDK `provider-catalog-shared` type). The change is additive and documented in `docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins/model-catalogs.md` as private provenance that is never projected publicly.
- Touches `src/agents/model-auth-availability.ts`, which has prior history from pash-openai (`4573635c77f`). That history includes `extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts`.

feat(model-catalog): lead NVIDIA recommendations with its featured models (#167989)

## What Problem This Solves

The hosted catalog's recommended models ignore the models a provider itself features, so NVIDIA's own picks show up in OpenClaw's global order (or not at all, like Nemotron 3 Super trailing at the end).

## User Impact

Model pickers for NVIDIA list NVIDIA's featured models first, in NVIDIA's order, followed by the remaining global recommendations. Other providers are unchanged, and catalog v1 is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog publication now reads a small per-provider table of provider-published featured lists (initially only NVIDIA's `featured-models.json`). Each featured id is matched to that provider's served, non-deprecated rows by canonical id, so `z-ai/glm-5-3` matches `z-ai/glm-5.3` and a missing `nvidia/` prefix still matches. The provider's own row ids lead its `recommendedModels`, followed by the global list's matches that are not already included. Provider picks win as listed: the family/successor rule only trims the global part. Unserved or deprecated featured ids are skipped and logged. If the feed is unavailable, malformed, empty or matches nothing, publication falls back to the global list with a warning (no warning for an empty feed). This is publish-time only: no SDK, protocol, schema or runtime state changes.

fix(cron): hold failure repair and alerts while a provider-outage retry is pending (#167957)

Related: #161007, #162702, #162772

## Problem

A recurring automation that hits a short provider outage (DNS failure, refused connection, 5xx, overload, rate limit) spends its one owner-conversation repair request, or sends a failure alert, at failure 2, while the scheduler's quick retry is still pending and the provider is still down. The next failure then sends the normal alert even if the outage has already ended.

## Solution

`applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer-outcomes.ts`) already decides whether a transient error gets another run. It now records that decision as `pendingTransientRetry` and passes it to `finalizeCronFailureNotifications` (`src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts`), which skips the alert and the owner repair for that cycle. Incident and unresolved-failure bookkeeping still run, so a success during the hold clears the incident silently.

The hold is bounded:

- Only while the transient retry budget remains (`DEFAULT_MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES`, 3), whichever path schedules the next run: the dedicated quick retry, or ordinary backoff on short-interval jobs (for example every minute) whose next slot comes first. Schedule length never extends it.
- Never when no next run exists: a disabled job, a one-shot retired after its retries, or a schedule with no future slot (`nextRunAtMs` undefined).
- Never for failures the job causes itself: cron's own execution watchdog timeout (`isCronTimeoutErrorText`), script failures (including script timeouts), and command-job timeouts. This keeps the #161007 case: a slow helper script is still repaired at failure 2.

Provider transport failures have no `network` failover reason: `ECONNREFUSED`, `EAI_AGAIN`, `fetch failed` and similar classify as `timeout` (`src/agents/failover/message-patterns.ts:180` and `:204`), and that structured reason is authoritative for the cron retry category (`src/cron/retry-hint.ts:62`). So the predicate (`holdsFailureNotificationForRetry`, `src/cron/service/timer-trigger.ts`) cannot exclude the `timeout` category wholesale; it excludes the job-owned cases above.

Docs: `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md` and `docs/cli/cron.md` describe the hold and its bounds.

## Impact

- During a provider outage the scheduler runs its quick retries (30s, 1m, 5m) first. If one succeeds, nothing is sent. If all fail, the owned job gets one repair request (unowned: one alert) with the full failure count.
- Upgrade behavior: notifications for provider outages arrive after the retry budget is used up, about 6.5 minutes after the first failure (failure 4), instead of at failure 2. No config key, schema, or stored-state change.
- Job-caused failures (watchdog timeout, script failures, command timeouts) keep their current timing.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Unit (`src/cron/service.failure-repair.test.ts`):

- Owned hourly, unowned hourly, and owned every-minute jobs with a DNS failure: 0 repairs and 0 alerts through failure 3; failure 4 sends one repair (owned, brief says "failed 4") or one alert (unowned).
- A success during the hold clears the incident and sends nothing.
- Provider `ECONNREFUSED` (`lastErrorReason: timeout`) is held; cron watchdog timeout and helper-script timeout still repair at failure 2.
- Bounds: a weekly job past the budget repairs; a one-shot retired after the budget alerts; a disabled job and a cron schedule with no future slot (both within the budget, `nextRunAtMs` undefined) are not held.
- The hold rows fail on origin/main; the every-minute row also fails on this PR's first revision.
- `pnpm test src/cron`: 238 files, 2318 tests passed. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: green.

Real Gateway (QA lab, mock provider dropping the TCP connection for the job's model requests, owned `every 1h` job, `fallbacks: []`, scheduled runs only):

| Build | Failures (from job creation) | After failure 3 | After failure 4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| This PR | +96s, +206s, +350s, +739s | 0 repairs, 0 alerts | 1 repair ("failed 4 consecutive runs"), 0 alerts |
| origin/main | same ladder | 1 repair + 1 alert | n/a |

Telegram Test Server (Convex-leased credential, isolated Gateway built from each tree, `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` behind a front that drops the TCP connection for the job's model requests; no live model). Each run created its own forum supergroup and topic, ran the owner turn in the topic, added an owned `every 1h` job whose owner is that topic session and whose delivery and alerts target it (`failureAlert: { after: 2, cooldownMs: 0 }`, `fallbacks: []`), then deleted the forum. Times are seconds after job creation; message IDs are the observer's IDs in that run's topic.

| Build | Job failures | SUT messages in the topic after job creation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| This PR (d6cd8eed80d) | +81s, +190s, +320s, +689s | none through failure 3 and up to failure 4 (about 11.5 min); then msg 6 at +700s, the owner repair turn's reply. No alert. |
| origin/main (ea6022cae60) | +68s, +185s, +316s | msg 6 at +228s (repair turn's reply after failure 2), msg 7 at +355s (failure alert after failure 3: `Automation "tg-cron-outage-proof" failed 3 times ... An automatic repair was requested in its owner conversation; it is still failing.`) |

In both runs the only earlier SUT message is msg 5, the reply to the topic owner turn, and the mock saw the same repair-turn request shape (one repair turn). Dropped connections: 30 (this PR, 4 runs), 22 (origin/main, 3 runs).

Merge danger: two-way door. It only changes when notifications are sent, writes no new state, and a revert restores the old timing. Blast radius: cron failure alerts and owner repair requests for transient provider failures. If the classification is wrong, those notifications are delayed by up to about 6.5 minutes; they are not lost.

fix(compaction): large sessions wait minutes for compaction because summary work grows with the context window (#167916)

Related: #164220, #164246, #164263, #130971

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a large session, automatic compaction keeps the user waiting about six minutes, and often times out, because the summary work grows with the size of the context window.

## User Impact

User impact: large sessions compact in about 25 seconds instead of about 6 minutes, and each compaction costs about 33k summary input tokens instead of about 700k. On a 1M-token window the user's next answer arrived in 85 s instead of 454 s. Timeouts like #164220, and the lossy no-summary fallback from #164246, become rare. No new config keys, messages, or warnings.

Tradeoff (approved by the maintainer): when the history to summarize is larger than one request's budget, the summarizer sees a sample of it, not every message. The newest messages stay verbatim; the user's older messages (asks, decisions, corrections) come next and are all kept when they fit; then the oldest messages and evenly spaced runs of the rest. Every gap is marked with the number of messages left out. The transcript still stores every message; only the summarizer input is bounded. Histories that fit the budget are summarized exactly as before, byte for byte.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause.** Compaction fires at `contextWindow − reserveTokens` (about 984k tokens on a 1M window) and keeps only `keepRecentTokens` (20k) verbatim, so about 880k tokens go to the summarizer. `summarizeInStages` then split that into two stages of sub-chunks sized at `contextWindow × 0.4`, summarized each serially with a running summary, and merged the parts: five serial reasoning-model requests (about 250k, 105k, 250k, 110k input tokens, then a merge). A failed quality audit repeated all five. Work, latency and cost grew linearly with the window, so every larger model made compaction slower. #163636 and #164263 stopped the watchdog from killing healthy requests and #164246 recovers from a real timeout; none of them reduced the work.

**Fix.**
- *One bounded request* (agent-core `runSummarizationCompletion`). The conversation input is capped at 160,000 CJK-weighted characters, lowered to fit the summarizer's own context window next to the system prompt, the previous summary, the instructions and the output reservation. `serializeConversationWithinBudget` (`utils.ts`) fills it in order: the newest entries verbatim (half; the newest entry keeps both ends when it alone is larger); older user messages (a quarter, each trimmed to at most 2,000 characters, spread evenly across the history when they do not all fit), because they carry the asks, decisions and corrections; the oldest entries (a tenth); and eight evenly spaced runs of the rest, trimmed to 6,000 characters each. Gap-marker cost is charged exactly, and the whole input never exceeds the budget. Gaps carry `[... N entries omitted ...]`, and the prompt tells the summarizer not to guess what they said and to keep the previous summary's facts. In sampled input each tool result names the call that produced it (`[Tool result of exec(cmd="...")]`), matched by call occurrence, because sampling can separate the two.
- *Window budget:* the input budget reserves the largest completion the transport may request. `resolveCompletionTokenReservation` (`@openclaw/ai/transports`, next to `applyAnthropicThinkingOptions`) adds the thinking budget only for budget-based Anthropic Messages thinking; other transports keep `maxTokens` as the total output limit. A history that fits is always sent unchanged. When the prompt alone overflows the window, or the history must be sampled and the window leaves under 4,000 characters, the request returns a non-retried `SummaryOutputBudgetError` that names `agents.defaults.compaction.model`, without a model call.
- *Callers:* `summarizeCompactionHistory` (`src/agents/compaction.ts`) replaces `summarizeInStages` and keeps its retry policy (3 attempts; caller abort, transport timeout and output-budget errors are terminal) and the `toolResult.details` and runtime-context stripping. The safeguard hook makes one call and passes the previous summary as `previousSummary`; the quality audit, corrective retries, split-turn prefix summary, preserved turns, and the #164246 timeout fallback are unchanged.
- *Removed:* the stage split, sub-chunking, merge request, history-prune pass and its extra dropped-chunk summary, oversized-message and partial-summary fallbacks, adaptive chunk ratio, and the planning worker that only computed those plans (`compaction-planning-worker*.ts`, `compaction-planning.worker.ts`, `compaction-planning-projection.ts`) with its tsdown entry, knip entry and worker-kind registrations. Safeguard runtime fields `contextWindowTokens` and the unused `maxHistoryShare` are gone with the factory params that only fed them.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/compaction.md` describes the bound and the sampling; config help and the provider docs no longer name `summarizeInStages`.

## Evidence

### Live: Telegram Test Server, real `gpt-6-astra`

Same harness as #163636/#164263: real-user DM, built `dist` of each head, default context engine, default compaction settings (safeguard mode), a forwarding proxy that records timing only, and the same deterministic 1,250-message seed (3.53M chars, 901k estimated tokens). BEFORE = merge base `24ca81d55bce`, AFTER = `f750b6e5ca9c` (clean tree).

The seed carries no provider usage, and current `main` no longer starts preflight compaction from the transcript estimate alone, so both runs also set the seeded session row's persisted usage to `totalTokens: 963000, totalTokensFresh: true` (transcript bytes unchanged). Both gateways then logged `preflightCompaction triggered: tokenCount=963040 threshold=902000 trigger=tokens`.

| | before `24ca81d55bce` | after `f750b6e5ca9c` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| history summary requests | 5 serial: summarize, update, summarize, update, merge | 1 |
| per request (body / input / duration) | 1.24 MB 38.5 s; 523 KB 47.5 s; 1.24 MB 73.0 s; 543 KB 91.3 s; merge 39 KB 111.9 s | 164 KB / 32,754 input tokens (provider usage) / 20.9 s |
| compaction (`[compaction-diag] end`) | `outcome=compacted durationMs=370348`, plus `finalized artifact truncated; loss=summary-tail` | `outcome=compacted durationMs=25369`, no truncation |
| after compaction | 30 messages, 23,333 est. tokens | 30 messages, 22,712 est. tokens |
| question → visible reply | **454.5 s** | **85.4 s** |
| reply | "Your last request concerned billing-api: splitting its lazy backfill job in Python. Next, look at the existing job implementation and tests; …" | "Your last request was to split the lazy backfill job in billing-api (Python). Next, look at its implementation and tests to identify safe split boundaries; …" |
| follow-up 22 min later | answered in 13.0 s, no compaction | answered in 22.1 s, no compaction |

AFTER's summary request carried 8 gap markers. BEFORE input tokens are estimated from body size at AFTER's measured 5.02 bytes per token (the BEFORE proxy did not capture usage of streams the client closes). Both runs also spent 36–52 s in the pre-compaction memory flush, which sends the full transcript and is outside this change. The seed has no tool calls, so the live run does not exercise the tool-result labels; the tests below do.

**Re-run with user-message priority** (`2ed02d442b1`, same seed, override and trigger gate): still one history-summary request, 164,544 B and 33,235 provider input tokens, `outcome=compacted durationMs=54821`, normal answers to both questions, and no compaction on the follow-up. The request carried 112 of the span's 612 user-role entries (each trimmed to 400 characters at that density), 96 gap markers and 1,085 omitted entries. Two differences from `f750b6e5ca9c`: the summarizer wrote 2,762 output tokens instead of 1,092, so the request took 49.4 s instead of 20.9 s, and the safeguard's 16,000-character artifact cap clipped the summary tail again (`finalized artifact truncated; loss=summary-tail`, as on `main`). End-to-end reply latency (243.6 s) is not comparable: the host load average was 43–50 during that run, the gap between compaction end and the answer request alone was 40 s instead of 4.7 s, and the answer model request itself took 2.6 s.

### Tests

New `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/summarization-input-budget.test.ts`, through `generateSummary` and the serializer:
- A small history is sent byte-identical to `serializeConversation`.
- A 1,250-turn tool session (5.5M characters) produces one request within 160,000 weighted characters. The newest turn is verbatim, the oldest turn is present, gap counts plus kept entries equal the total, every kept tool result names its own call, and the previous summary and omission instruction are in the prompt.
- A 32k window keeps prompt plus output inside the window. A 4k window with a large previous summary returns `SummaryOutputBudgetError` without a model call, for long and short histories alike, while a short history on a 4k window without that summary is still sent unchanged. Budgets below one gap marker send nothing.
- Anthropic Messages with high thinking reserves the 16,384-token thinking budget on top of the output; an OpenAI request with the same settings reserves no thinking budget.
- An oversized newest entry keeps both ends. A 1M-character mixed CJK/ASCII newest entry keeps an excerpt.
- CJK text counts by token weight.
- Tool-result naming across budgets 4,000–60,000, after the ninth-image omission note, with a 30,000-character argument, with a 24-call batch, with a user message between a call and its result, and with repeated call IDs (matched by occurrence through `createToolCallOccurrenceQueue`).
- User priority: in a 400-turn tool-heavy history, all 400 user messages (including four decisions in the middle) reach the summarizer; with 2,000 long user messages that cannot all fit, every tenth of the history keeps some.

Negative controls: each case above fails on the commit before its fix, except the "every tenth" spread case, which guards the stride against a newest-first regression and also passes on the earlier even sampling. Migrated suites (deleted tests covered only removed mechanisms; kept behavior moved to `summarizeCompactionHistory`): `compaction.summarize-fallback`, `compaction.summary-format`, `compaction.tool-result-details`, `compaction.identifier-preservation`, `compaction.abort-http`, `agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard*`, `embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks`, `compact.summary-fallback`, `compact.small-context`, `extensions`, `agent-session-tool-result-redaction`, and `src/agents/sessions/` (small-window sessions). All pass, as does `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main` (typecheck all lanes, oxlint, import cycles, ratchets, config docs baseline).

### Review

`gpt-6-astra` review, eleven rounds on this branch. Rounds 1–6 found, and this branch fixed: a mixed CJK/ASCII newest entry could be dropped; an oversized newest entry lost its end; tiny summarizer windows could overflow or send markers only; a dead export; and four cases where a sampled tool result could lose its call. The last one led to the self-describing result labels. Round 7: **LAND, no findings**.

Hosted review then found three more, fixed in `f55ae2a202f` and `2e7cc05cafd`: a short history was rejected on a tiny window before measuring it; budget-based Anthropic thinking adds its budget on top of `maxTokens`; repeated call IDs mislabeled results. Round 8 found that the first thinking fix also reserved thinking on OpenAI, so the reservation moved to the Anthropic transport owner. Round 9: **LAND, no findings**.

`4786e7233fa` adds user-message priority (maintainer request). Round 10 found that when the prompt alone overflowed the window, closing the only gap refunded the marker cost and let a short history through; `2ed02d442b1` enforces the overall budget in every selection and rejects a negative budget. Round 11 on `2ed02d442b1`: **LAND, no findings**.

Rebase: onto `bc1d44c838e`. The only conflict was in `compaction-safeguard.ts`, where #167816 had folded the adaptive chunk-ratio code into a `resolveMaxChunkTokens` helper that this PR deletes, so the resolution keeps this branch's side.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes: their commits on touched files only touch `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` and an unrelated test in `compact.hooks.test.ts`.

Merge danger: two-way door. No schema, stored-row, config or protocol change; a revert restores the staged pipeline. `@openclaw/ai/transports` gains one additive export, `resolveCompletionTokenReservation`. Blast radius: every built-in compaction summary (default and safeguard modes, manual `/compact`, preflight and overflow recovery). Histories that fit 160,000 characters (about 40k tokens) are unchanged; larger ones are summarized from the sampled input. Plugin compaction providers still receive the full messages.

fix(xai): Grok subscription models ignore listed reasoning efforts (#167949)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: some Grok models on an xAI subscription (OAuth) sign-in offer only `off`/`ultra` thinking, reject `--thinking low`, and run with reasoning on even at "off". This happens whenever the account's model listing names effort levels for a model OpenClaw's built-in model-ID rules don't cover (today: `grok-4.7-build-fast`).

## User Impact

User impact: for Grok subscription sign-ins, the thinking levels in the picker and the reasoning effort sent with each request now follow the efforts the account's listing reports. Models whose listing has no `none` effort no longer offer `off`. Every other Grok model keeps exactly the same levels and requests as before. Accounts that signed in before this change need to sign in again to refresh their saved model rows (documented).

## Why This Change Was Made

`cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/models` reports `supports_reasoning_effort` and `reasoning_efforts` for each model, but the xAI plugin chose effort support by model ID alone. `grok-4.7-build-fast` lists `low/medium/high/xhigh` (default `high`). OpenClaw offered `off`/`ultra`, and "off" left out the effort field, so the proxy ran it at its default `high`.

- The OAuth listing projection now copies the listed efforts into the existing `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` field.
- The xAI runtime compat reads that field first and maps each level to the listed effort, or to the nearest listed one. `off` sends `none` only when `none` is listed; otherwise `off` is unsupported, the same as current Grok 4.5+ behavior. Model-ID rules apply only to rows that list no efforts.
- The xAI thinking profile offers the listed levels. Rows that runtime normalization stamped with their own ID-rule list keep their existing ladder; this keeps Grok 4.3's `minimal` level and `low` default.

There are no schema, config, SDK, or core changes. **Known gap (not fixed here):** agent runs take thinking options from the model rows saved in config at sign-in (`src/agents/command/prepare.ts:303` `buildConfiguredModelCatalog`; `src/agents/command/model-selection.ts:524-531` skips hydration through `needsThinkHydration` because the saved row counts as resolved). The picker uses the live listing instead. So until an account signs in again, the picker can offer `low` while `--thinking low` is still rejected. This is the same shared gap the Anthropic listed-capabilities work (#167658) hit, and it is tracked as one core follow-up.

## Evidence

- Regression tests, both failing on `origin/main` code and passing here:
  - `extensions/xai/index.test.ts`: a listed row with efforts reaches the thinking profile (`low..xhigh`, default `high`) and runtime compat (`off: null`, `low: "low"`, …).
  - `extensions/xai/runtime-model-compat.test.ts`: `off` sends `none` only when it is listed; unknown efforts are dropped; nearest-effort mapping.
  - `extensions/xai/provider-policy-api.test.ts`: Grok 4.3's ladder is unchanged after runtime normalization stamps its efforts.
- Real Grok subscription account (device-code sign-in), isolated `--profile` Gateways. A loopback forward proxy (`proxy.proxyUrl` plus a proof-only CA) recorded each outgoing `/v1/responses` shape. Cells marked stub got a canned stream; the rest were forwarded unchanged to the real proxy.
  - Listing: 4 rows (`grok-4.7`, `grok-4.7-build-fast`, `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.5`), all `api_backend: responses`, all `supports_reasoning_effort: true`.
  - Picker levels on merge base `164210c` and on this branch for all 8 shown xAI rows: identical except `grok-4.7-build-fast` (`off,ultra` default `off` → `low,medium,high,xhigh,ultra` default `high`).
  - Request parity: 8 models × `default/off/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/ultra`, 64 cells per build. Accepted/rejected levels and the `reasoning` field match for every cell. Two cells differ only because a background `grok-4.6` request (effort `high`, 12 tools) landed in a different cell on each build; that request has the same shape on both builds.
  - Fresh sign-in on this branch: models appear without restart; saved rows carry the listed efforts. Real turns: `grok-4.7-build-fast` default → sent `effort: high`, 200, proxy echoed `high`. `--thinking low` → sent `low`, 200, proxy echoed `low`. `--thinking off` → rejected: "Use one of: low, medium, high, xhigh, ultra". Control `grok-4.7` default → `high`, 200 on both builds.
  - Before (merge base): `grok-4.7-build-fast` default sent no `reasoning`; `--thinking low` was rejected ("Use one of: off, ultra").
- `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files; `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/` (563 passed before the final small type/lint fixups; focused files rerun after them).

**Merge danger:** low. Only the xAI plugin changes. On the real account, request bodies for every model except `grok-4.7-build-fast` are byte-identical in the recorded fields. fix(github-copilot): listed Chat Completions-only and new Claude models fail their first turn (#167941)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub Copilot models fail on their first turn when the account lists a chat model that only serves Chat Completions (`kimi-k3` today), or a Claude model OpenClaw does not recognize yet (a newly launched Claude).

## User Impact

User impact: every chat model a Copilot account shows in the picker now answers its first turn, including Claude models released after the installed OpenClaw version. No config, schema, or protocol changes.

Merge danger: low. Shipped models keep their current transport and thinking shape (the transport only changes when the account's listing says the default endpoint is unsupported; Claude capabilities are only derived for rows that list `xhigh`, which every currently listed adaptive Claude model already matches by ID). Older listings without `supported_endpoints` keep the ID rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copilot's `/models` already says how each model can be called:

- `supported_endpoints` names the endpoints a model accepts. OpenClaw picked the transport from the model ID only, so a non-Claude, non-Gemini ID always went to `/responses`. `kimi-k3` lists only `/chat/completions` and was rejected (`unsupported_api_for_model`). The Copilot plugin now keeps the family transport when it is listed and otherwise uses a listed endpoint, with the existing Copilot Chat Completions request options.
- Copilot lists effort levels instead of Anthropic's capability tree, so Claude request shaping fell back to ID rules. An unknown Claude ID got manual `thinking.type: enabled` budgets, which current Claude models reject (`Use thinking.type.adaptive and output_config.effort`). Claude rows that list `xhigh` (only adaptive-thinking Claude models offer it) now carry the existing `params.claudeCapabilities` contract (#167658), so they get adaptive thinking and the listed xhigh/max levels before OpenClaw learns their ID.

The `fetchCopilotUsage` tests moved from `models.test.ts` to `usage.test.ts` (their owner) to keep `models.test.ts` under the line cap; no test was removed.

fix(anthropic): newly listed Claude models stay hidden until an OpenClaw release (#167658)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: new Claude models that an Anthropic API key already lists stay hidden from the model picker until an OpenClaw release, and a typed-in unknown ID can be sent a request shape the model rejects.

## User Impact

User impact: Anthropic API-key users see newly listed Claude models as soon as `/v1/models` returns them, and the first turn uses the thinking type and effort levels Anthropic advertises for that model. Shipped rows Anthropic does not list, configured rows, and catalogs saved before discovery runs keep today's model-ID rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

Request shaping keyed only on model-ID rules, so #113757 hid any unknown model whose advertised capabilities disagreed with them. This change makes shaping follow the listing:

- The Anthropic plugin owns its `/v1/models` projection through the existing `modelDiscovery.projectRows` hook. It runs the shared default projection first, so a listed ID that the manifest does not ship still inherits `compat` (including Code Mode) and `thinkingLevelMap` from the closest shipped model, exactly as before. It then adds the advertised flags to each listed row as `params.claudeCapabilities` (`adaptiveThinking`, `xhighEffort`, `maxEffort`, and `disabledThinking` when listed) and sets `thinkingLevelMap.xhigh`/`max` to match.
- The shared Claude predicates `supportsClaudeAdaptiveThinking`, `supportsClaudeNativeXhighEffort`, `supportsClaudeNativeMaxEffort`, and `requiresClaudeMandatoryAdaptiveThinking` read a listed flag first and use the ID rule only when that flag is missing. Sonnet 5.5's between-tools off mode is preserved. `supportsClaude1MContext` still uses ID rules only.
- The Claude thinking profile reads row params, so the picker offers the levels a listed model advertises.
- The agreement gate is deleted. An unknown row with no readable capability data stays hidden.

No schema changes. One export is added to the private-local `plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-runtime` subpath: `buildOpenAICompatibleLiveModels`, the existing default projection, so the Anthropic projection composes with it instead of copying its template inheritance. `params` is the existing free-form model-params field; `params.canonicalModelId` is the precedent. The Anthropic provider docs now name the key. `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` was not used because Copilot's `anthropic-messages` Claude rows already set it without any adaptive marker, so the shared predicates would misread those rows.

The public SDK option `acceptUnknownModel` is unchanged. The Anthropic plugin no longer sets it, and instead passes the same kind of gate (listed capabilities present) straight to the shared projection. Bedrock, Vertex, Copilot, Foundry, OpenRouter, and Claude CLI rows never carry `params.claudeCapabilities`, so they behave as before.

## Evidence

- Regression tests, each failing on `origin/main` code and passing here:
  - `packages/llm-core/src/model-contracts/anthropic.test.ts`: listed flags override ID rules one flag at a time.
  - `packages/ai/src/anthropic-listed-capabilities-transport-parity.test.ts`: provider and transport builders send adaptive + `xhigh` for an unknown listed model, budget thinking when adaptive is withheld, and keep thinking on when disabled thinking is rejected.
  - `extensions/anthropic/live-discovery-auth.test.ts`: an unknown listed model appears with its capabilities; a row without capabilities stays hidden; a listed ID the manifest does not ship (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) keeps the shipped Sonnet row's `compat.codeMode: "preferred"` while its effort map follows the listing (this case fails on `80606329c81`).
  - `extensions/anthropic/provider-policy-api.test.ts`: the effort ladder follows listed capabilities.
- Real `pnpm openclaw` Gateway turns in an isolated profile. Traffic to `api.anthropic.com` went through a loopback forward proxy (`proxy.proxyUrl` plus a proof CA) into a fake API that lists `claude-sonnet-5` (known), `claude-sonnet-9` (unknown, adaptive + xhigh + max), and `claude-haiku-9` (unknown, no adaptive, no effort):
  - `origin/main`: neither unknown ID is listed. A typed `claude-haiku-9` is sent `thinking: adaptive` with `effort` `high`/`low`, which this model rejects. `claude-sonnet-9 --thinking xhigh` is refused with "not supported".
  - This branch: both unknown IDs are listed. `claude-sonnet-9` gets adaptive thinking with effort `high`/`xhigh`/`max` and thinking `disabled` by default. `claude-haiku-9` gets `thinking: enabled` with `budget_tokens` 16384/8192 plus the interleaved-thinking beta. `claude-sonnet-5` is unchanged.
- Real Anthropic API key, isolated `--profile` Gateways, the same loopback forward proxy now forwarding each request unchanged to the real `api.anthropic.com` and recording the outgoing `/v1/messages` shape and the real status. The baseline is this PR's merge base `447144510b8`; the branch is `80606329c81`.
  - `/v1/models` lists 14 Claude IDs, and every row has a capability tree. The picker (`models list --provider anthropic --all --refresh --plain`, with and without a Gateway) shows the same 16 rows on both builds: the 14 listed IDs plus the shipped `claude-mythos-5` and `claude-haiku-4-5`. The real listing has no ID that the baseline hides.
  - Request parity covered all 14 listed models at `default`, `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `adaptive`, and `ultra`. Sonnet and Haiku models got real turns at `default`/`off`/`low`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`. Opus and Fable models got one real turn each at `default` on each build. All other cells were captured with a proxy stub, so the request was recorded but not sent. The `anthropic-beta` header, `thinking` (type, budget, display, block binding), `output_config.effort`, `max_tokens`, `context_management`, `service_tier`, sampling fields, and top-level keys are identical for every model and level. Both builds reject the same levels (for example `off` on `claude-opus-5-5`/`claude-fable-5`/`claude-fable-5-1`, `xhigh` on `claude-sonnet-4-6`/`claude-opus-4-6`). All 80 real requests returned 200.

The baseline's default projection copies `compat` and `thinkingLevelMap` from the shipped model with the longest shared ID prefix; `projectAnthropicLiveModels` had built those rows from scratch. It now runs that default projection and only adds the listed flags.
  - Rerun on `2022ebb00d5` (same real key, same proxy, compared with the frozen baseline captures): 46 requests across those five models at every level the baseline accepts, plus `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` and `claude-sonnet-5` at `default`. Real turns: `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-6`, and `claude-sonnet-5` (unchanged control) at `default`, all 200. Everything else used the proxy stub. Every request equals its baseline capture on every recorded field: `anthropic-beta`, `thinking`, `output_config`, `max_tokens`, `context_management`, sampling fields, top-level keys, message/system counts, and the tool list hash. The five models now send `[exec, wait]`, and Haiku 4.5 still sends `[tool_call, tool_describe, tool_search]` on both builds. The branch still refuses the same levels as the baseline (`xhigh` on `claude-sonnet-4-6`/`claude-opus-4-6`; `xhigh`/`max`/`adaptive` on `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`/`claude-opus-4-5-20251101`).
  - Unknown-model path: the real listing has no hidden ID, so a throwaway local build of `80606329c81` masked the ID rules for `claude-opus-4-7`. With the mask, the request came only from the advertised capabilities: thinking `disabled` by default and adaptive thinking with `xhigh`/`max` effort, the same as the unmasked branch. Real turns at `default`, `xhigh`, and `max` returned 200. This simulation was not repeated on `2022ebb00d5`. The fix changes only what an unknown row inherits from its template (`compat`, thinking-map entries other than `xhigh`/`max`, and input). The listed flags that shape the request are set the same way.
  - Known gap, not fixed here: masking `claude-sonnet-5`, which the manifest ships, sent the advertised adaptive thinking but made the CLI refuse `xhigh`/`max`. The CLI level check (`src/agents/command/model-selection.ts`, via `prepareCommandModelCatalog`) reads the manifest catalog row, and `needsThinkHydration` skips the live, provider-scoped catalog whenever that row already declares `reasoning`. So listed capabilities never reach the ladder for a shipped ID. Fixing this means changing the shared thinking-catalog hydration policy, which is used by several callers (`model-selection.ts`, `run-embedded-attempt.ts`, `agent-runner-run-params.ts`) and every provider. That is out of scope here. Today the ID rules for every shipped model match their listing, so nothing is visible.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` on `2022ebb00d5`: typecheck, boundary, Plugin SDK export/surface, format, and ratchet lanes pass. The dead-export scan fails only on pre-existing unused exports in files this PR does not touch (`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication.ts`, `src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.ts`). With `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1` the run exits 0. `oxlint --type-aware` is clean on the changed files.

## Merge danger

- For known models that Anthropic lists, the listed capabilities now override the ID rules. Request shapes change only if Anthropic's listing disagrees with the curated rules.
- An unknown listed model inherits `compat` (including Code Mode), `thinkingLevelMap`, and input modalities from the shipped model with the longest shared ID prefix, as the shared projection already did before this PR. It gets zero pricing and ID-rule image sizing until OpenClaw ships its entry. Listed `xhigh`/`max` flags override the inherited thinking map.
- For a shipped ID, the CLI/agent thinking-level check still uses the manifest row's ID rules, not the listed capabilities (see the known gap in Evidence).
- The behavior depends on Anthropic's capability fields staying as documented. Real-key proof shows that today's listing matches the ID rules for every listed model.

fix(catalog): stop publishing models providers no longer serve (#167855)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the hosted model catalog keeps publishing and recommending models that a provider no longer serves. For example, NVIDIA's `recommendedModels` still listed `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro` and `minimaxai/minimax-m3`, which are absent from NVIDIA's live `/v1/models`.

## User Impact

User impact: model pickers and recommended lists stop offering dead models for providers whose model list is public. A configured exact reference to a retired model still resolves, because the row is marked `deprecated` rather than removed. Providers whose `/models` needs an API key (32 of them) are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publish script added models from models.dev, but nothing ever retired a row. Manifest rows win over models.dev, and models.dev liveness is unreliable for NVIDIA in both directions: it marks the live `moonshotai/kimi-k2.6` deprecated and lists the dead `nvidia/nemotron-voicechat` as active. The provider's own inventory is the authority.

During publish, each provider whose keyless `/models` returns the exact ids that requests send is fetched through the existing source loader, with the same size and timeout limits. Those providers are Chutes, DeepInfra, Hugging Face, Kilo Gateway, Novita, NVIDIA, OpenCode Zen, OpenCode Go and Venice. A published row missing from the inventory gets `status: "deprecated"` and a `statusReason` in the published bundle only; manifests are not edited. The schema already has this status, and `projectRecommendedModels` and the pickers already filter it.

- Ids are compared exactly. The exception is Novita: its list mixes case (`Sao10K/…` and `sao10K/…`), so a Novita row is retired only when it is missing even case-insensitively. Published ids are never rewritten.
- If the inventory is unreachable, malformed or empty, that provider publishes as authored with a warning, the same as the models.dev missing-provider path.
- Each provider gets one summary line: `inventory provider=<id> retired=<n> ids=…`.
- Excluded providers:
  - Featherless: the loader's request gets HTTP 404 `Gone.`, and the 200 body is 5.01 MB, at the loader cap.
  - Ollama Cloud: its list holds tags and aliases, not request ids.
  - Every provider whose `/models` needs a key.
- Manifest rows that are intentionally absent from `/models` (aliases): none among the included providers. Kilo's `kilo-auto/balanced` is listed in its inventory.

## Evidence

The proof is a local `node --import tsx scripts/publish-model-catalog.mts --out … --out-v2 …` run against today's live sources, comparing `origin/main` with this branch.

`nvidia.recommendedModels`:
- before: `kimi-k3, deepseek-v4.1-flash, glm-5.3, deepseek-v4-pro, glm-5.3-flash, minimax-m3, nemotron-3-ultra, nemotron-3-super`
- after: `kimi-k3, deepseek-v4.1-flash, glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, nemotron-3-ultra, nemotron-3-super`

Retired per provider (rows already deprecated are left alone):
- nvidia (4): `z-ai/glm-5.2`, `minimaxai/minimax-m3`, `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro`, `nvidia/nemotron-voicechat`
- deepinfra (4): `stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash`, `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code`, `Qwen/Qwen3-Max`, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B`
- chutes (1): `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5-TEE`
- novita (33): `kwaipilot/kat-coder-pro`, `deepseek/deepseek-v3-0324`, `deepseek/deepseek-v3-turbo`, `deepseek/deepseek-v3.1-terminus`, `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2-exp`, `deepseek/deepseek-v3.1`, `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2`, `xiaomimimo/mimo-v2-flash`, `xiaomimimo/mimo-v2-pro`, `baidu/ernie-4.5-vl-28b-a3b`, `baidu/ernie-4.5-vl-28b-a3b-thinking`, `inclusionai/ring-2.6-1t`, `inclusionai/ling-2.6-1t`, `inclusionai/ling-2.6-flash`, `zai-org/glm-4.5`, `minimax/minimax-m2.5-highspeed`, `minimax/minimax-m2.1`, `minimax/minimax-m2`, `qwen/qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruct`, `qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507`, `qwen/qwen3-next-80b-a3b-thinking`, `qwen/qwen3-coder-next`, `qwen/qwen3-omni-30b-a3b-instruct`, `qwen/qwen3-max`, `qwen/qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct`, `qwen/qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct`, `qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507`, `qwen/qwen2.5-7b-instruct`, `qwen/qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct`, `qwen/qwen3-vl-30b-a3b-thinking`, `qwen/qwen3-vl-8b-instruct`, `qwen/qwen-2.5-72b-instruct`, `sao10K/l31-70b-euryale-v2.2`.
