fix(doctor): keep automatic Skill Workshop learning for approval-policy configs (#167846)

Reverts #167641.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after `openclaw doctor --fix`, operators who had `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: "auto"` (or unset) with `approvalPolicy: "pending"` have learning turned off. Before the Skill Workshop cutover, those setups already learned automatically.

## User Impact

User impact: these operators keep automatic learning after upgrade. Doctor only removes the retired `approvalPolicy` and `maxPending` keys, as it did before #167641.

## Why This Change Was Made

#167641 assumed `approvalPolicy: "pending"` gated all skill writes. It did not. In the docs and code just before #161057 (`cfee851150c5^`):

- `autonomous.mode: "auto"` meant "direct per-turn and weekly Workshop maintenance" with normal file tools, and immediate repair in `auto` "scans and applies it immediately" (`docs/tools/skill-workshop/configuration.md:70`, `docs/tools/self-learning.md:29-31`).
- `approvalPolicy: "pending"` only added an approval prompt when the foreground agent called `apply`, `reject` or `quarantine` on a proposal (`docs/tools/skill-workshop/configuration.md:71`).

So `auto` + `pending` operators already had direct background writes, and mapping them to `off` takes away learning they had. Only the foreground proposal-apply prompt is gone; it went with the proposal system in the approved #161057 cutover.

## Evidence

- `git revert eda09031`, clean. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.skills.test.ts`: 6/6 pass, including `maps the removed propose mode to off and drops proposal settings`.
- **Published updater to candidate** (Docker `node:24-bookworm`, secretless, candidate tarball packed from `71baa3e0`). Both cases installed `openclaw@2026.9.9` (`bcfc888`), seeded the config with an agent skills allowlist `["github"]` and `maxSkillBytes: 8000`, then ran `openclaw update --tag /candidate.tgz --yes --json --no-restart`.

  | Seeded Workshop config | After update | Backup `.bak.1` | Second `doctor --fix` | `config validate` |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `mode: "auto"`, `approvalPolicy: "pending"`, `maxPending: 20` | `{ autonomous: { mode: "auto" }, maxSkillBytes: 8000 }` | original keys kept | no Workshop changes | valid |
  | mode unset, `approvalPolicy: "pending"`, `maxPending: 20` | `{ maxSkillBytes: 8000 }` (default `auto` applies) | original keys kept | no Workshop changes | valid |

  - In both runs the update `status` is `ok` and every step exits 0, including `candidate-doctor`, `candidate-config`, `candidate-gateway-startup` and `package-swap`. The installed build is `71baa3e`.
  - The agent skills allowlist and the gateway settings are preserved.
- The restored behavior is the one that shipped on main before #167641.
- No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes: `git log origin/main --author=pash@openai.com --author=sjf@openai.com` on the touched files is empty.

chore(models): report NVIDIA featured models missing from the recommended list (#167850)

Related: #166738

## What Problem This Solves

NVIDIA asked us to use its featured-models list. The daily recommended-models suggestion report never looks at it, so a model NVIDIA features can go unnoticed if it's missing from the curated list.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The daily report now has a "NVIDIA featured, not listed" section. It lists every featured model that isn't in `scripts/lib/recommended-models.json`, along with its suggested rank. The list itself is unchanged; the section is only a signal for the reviewer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The script fetches https://assets.ngc.nvidia.com/products/api-catalog/featured-models.json on every run, with no cache, the same way it fetches its other sources. NVIDIA's ids are inconsistent: some lack a vendor prefix (`nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b`) and some use a dashed version (`z-ai/glm-5-3`). The existing `canonicalModelKey` already folds both forms (`glm-5-3` → `glm-5.3`), so the script adds no normalization of its own. A failed or malformed fetch doesn't fail the report. Instead, the Sources section shows the error and the NVIDIA section reads "Unavailable". The featured list doesn't affect ranking or the suggested diff.

Reporting models NVIDIA stopped featuring would need state from earlier runs. The report keeps no state, so that part is left out.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Local runs of `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/suggest-recommended-models.mts`, 2026-10-09:

Real list. All four featured models are already listed:

```
- NVIDIA featured models (4).
...
## NVIDIA featured, not listed

None.
```

The list with `glm-5.3` and `nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` removed (`--list`). The dashed and prefix-less ids map to the list keys:

```
## NVIDIA featured, not listed

| model | NVIDIA id | suggested |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b | nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b | no signal yet |
| glm-5.3 | z-ai/glm-5-3 | #20 |
```

NVIDIA unreachable (only the NVIDIA host routed to a dead proxy). The run still exits 0:

```
- NVIDIA featured models unavailable: fetch failed
...
## NVIDIA featured, not listed

Unavailable; see Sources.
```

`test/scripts/suggest-recommended-models.test.ts` passes. Its fetch stub returns 404 for the NVIDIA URL, so it also covers the non-fatal path. `codex review` found no issues.

Merge danger: two-way door. The change only touches the output of a maintainer-only report script; reverting it restores the old report exactly. Blast radius: the daily suggestion report only.

fix(doctor): keep approval-first Skill Workshop setups from writing skills unreviewed (#167641)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after `openclaw doctor --fix`, operators who had `skills.workshop.approvalPolicy: "pending"` with learning `auto` (or unset, which now defaults to `auto`) lose their approval step, and agents start writing skills without review.

## User Impact

User impact: approval-first setups migrate to `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: "off"`, the same result as the retired `propose` mode. Doctor prints the command to turn on `auto` when the operator is ready. Setups with `approvalPolicy: "auto"` keep their mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skill Workshop no longer has approvals. Before this change, Doctor deleted `approvalPolicy` but kept the mode, so it silently replaced "review before writing" with direct writes. Mapping to `off` keeps the operator's choice; turning learning back on is one command.

## Evidence

fix(openai): ChatGPT-login picker lists models the bundled Codex rejects (#167633)

Reverts #167387.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with ChatGPT login, the model picker can list a model that then fails with HTTP 400 on the default runtime, when npm's newest Codex is ahead of OpenClaw's bundled Codex.

## User Impact

User impact: ChatGPT-login model discovery again reports the bundled Codex version (`0.160.0`), so it lists only models the bundled Codex can run. New ChatGPT models appear when the bundled Codex pin moves, as before #167387.

## Why This Change Was Made

#167387 made discovery report npm's latest stable `@openai/codex` version. With ChatGPT login and `agentRuntime` unset/`auto`, turns on the official ChatGPT endpoint run on the Codex harness with the bundled, pinned binary (`docs/providers/openai/runtimes.md`). That binary reports its own version on each turn, and the backend gates models on it. So a model whose minimum Codex version is above the pin is listed but rejected. This is the 2026.9.8 GPT-6.1 failure (bundled 0.158.0, model needs ≥ 0.159.2) for the next gated model. Codex's own discovery also reports the real package version (`client_version_to_whole()` in `codex-rs/models-manager`).

This restores the alignment contract from #113615 (discovery version = bundled Codex version, guarded by `test/scripts/codex-client-version-contract.test.ts`). Hermes reports `99.0.0`, but its default ChatGPT runtime talks to the backend directly and its Codex app-server mode is opt-in with a user-managed binary, so the same trade does not fit OpenClaw's default.

No failing model was observed: all currently listed ChatGPT models need Codex ≤ 0.155. This removes a reachable failure, not a reported one.

## Evidence

- Clean `git revert` of 41a8839930e; the bundled pin is still `0.160.0`, so the restored constant matches and the contract test passes.
- `openai-provider`, `openai-codex-discovery`, `openai-model-discovery-auth-order` and `codex-client-version-contract` tests pass.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. No stored state, config or schema. Blast radius: ChatGPT-login model discovery; models gated above the bundled Codex version stop appearing until the pin moves.

fix(gateway): Gateway stalls after startup recapturing plugins for model catalog updates (#167544)

Related: #160959

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: shortly after every Gateway start, the scheduled remote model catalog refresh copies every external plugin a second time and loads it cold. With a large plugin, this blocks the Gateway for as long as the startup capture did.

## User Impact

User impact: when the hosted model catalog is newer than the installed build (the normal case for released versions), adopting it no longer re-copies or re-evaluates external plugins. The Gateway stays responsive after startup. Prepared turns keep using the Gateway's unchanged plugin instances, as they already do after config hot reloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

#161267 made prepared model runtimes borrow unchanged plugin instances from the admitting Gateway. The lender is resolved from the Gateway registry scope of the work that triggers the rebuild. Hot reloads already run their prepared-runtime refresh inside that scope (`server-reload-hot.ts`).

The post-ready `update.remote-model-catalog` scheduler job calls `applyRemoteModelCatalogUpdate` with no registry scope. The prepared rebuild therefore finds no lender, and its inbound registry cold-loads every plugin. This change runs scheduled catalog adoption inside the live Gateway registry scope, the same way the hot-reload refresh does. No new cache, manager or module sharing is added. Each registry keeps its own load and dispose lifecycle, and borrowing follows the existing #161267 contract.

## Evidence

**Trigger proven on origin/main 6070074.** Runs were isolated Gateways with an external plugin used as the context engine, each held 60 s after `ready`, with scratch probes outside the repo:
- Catalog refresh enabled: 8/8 runs captured and loaded the plugin a second time after ready. The probe at `loadPreparedInboundPluginRegistry` logged `lender=false requestScope=false` during `applyRemoteModelCatalogUpdate`, followed by `remote model catalog applied`.
- Catalog refresh disabled (`models.catalogRefresh.enabled: false`): 3/3 runs had no second load.
- Full stack of the second capture: `buildSnapshotBatch → prepareWorkspacePluginRegistries → loadPreparedInboundPluginRegistry → loadAgentRuntimePluginRegistryHandle → loadOpenClawPlugins`.
- Cost on main with an 8k-file plugin: `startup.maintenance.plugin-registry` took 46.2 s and 57.7 s with event-loop max 45.2 s and 57.3 s, plus a 78 s post-ready reload in another run.

**With this change.** Same harness:
- On 6070074 with this patch: 7/7 runs had 0 loads after ready. In each run the catalog was refreshed (`status: updated`) and applied, and the probe logged `inbound lender=true requestScope=true`.
- On this PR's exact head versus its exact parent: these builds are newer than the current hosted catalog, so the runs serve the same hosted catalog with a newer `generatedAt` from a loopback `models.catalogRefresh.url`. Each run was held 60 s after ready, and the catalog was refreshed (`status: updated`) and applied in every run. fix(release): reclaim docker disk and gate the data root before the sandbox image build (#13479) (#13481)

* fix(release): reclaim docker disk and gate the data root before the sandbox image build (#13479)

The nightly release's docker lane died 24 minutes into its test step when
the self-hosted runner hit ENOSPC and the runner worker crashed, after
passing the job-start disk floor gate (run 37374675168). The gate predates
the sandbox image build by up to an hour, and the lane's pre-build prune
only removes labelled images — BuildKit cache and dangling layers on the
shared pool's persistent daemon store are out of its reach.

Prune BuildKit cache alongside the labelled-image prune, then re-gate the
docker data root filesystem at a build-sized floor (8 GiB) immediately
before the build. A host with reclaimable docker garbage now gets reclaimed
and builds; a genuinely saturated host fails fast with a legible ::error::
so a re-run lands on an instance with headroom, instead of the runner
worker crashing mid-build and killing even the cleanup steps.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(release): harden the docker disk reclaim and data-root floor gate (#13479)

Address the round-1 review of #13481: add the missing dangling-image
prune, bound the BuildKit cache prune with timeout 20m inside the host

other check-disk-floor.sh call site, warn on every gate-skip path,
re-gate after the build (the #13479 death landed in the vitest phase),

feat(managed-agent): H6b/H6c automation runtime for persistent definitions (#13598)

* feat(managed-agent): H6b/H6c automation runtime for persistent definitions

The runtime part of slice H6 of #12827 (stage H of #12380), after the H6a
record contract (#13536): definitions, the single-claim scanner, the
occurrence ledger, overlap and catch-up, and persistent execution.

- Definitions are created, revised, read and retired under the
  Workspace-bound Session their creator owns. The control plane relays
  each mutation to the Session's Hosted Harness, whose authority publishes
  the prompt as a Session resource and commits the definition revision;
  the control plane replays by Idempotency-Key and answers 202 with the
  committed resource. The two public automation routes move from planned
  to partial and gain the mutation routes and the detail read.
- The scanner derives each armed definition's due slots on the host tz
  database (a shared slots fixture pins the cron semantics, DST gap and
  fold rules in TypeScript and Java), claims the definition under a lease
  with a fencing token, records every occurrence decision (fired, skipped,
  missed, or unknown after bounded retries) in the V53 ledger, and fires
  one idempotent Harness operation whose claim row was durable first; a
  manual run is the same operation keyed by its Idempotency-Key. A
  scanner that lost its lease can move neither the watermark nor the
  ledger; a manual run holds the same lease.
- Firing commits the run's claim revision and then, in one journal
  transaction, its dispatch revision with the run's input and wake; the
  embedded wake scheduler runs the input as a text turn; the journal's turn
  settle settles the run on the settle path and again on open, and the close
  path ends a never-run input as cancelled with a proven execution.
- Run identity is derived from the definition and the occurrence in both
  languages; the authority and the Java store refuse an underived id or a
  run that does not bind to its live definition at the current revision,
  so two claims of one occurrence meet one committed run.
- Both domains are enabled for submission for the persistent target mode
  only (MANAGED_SESSION_ENABLED_SCHEDULE_SESSION_MODES); per_run and the
  delivery policy stay refused until H4b and H5b/H5c land, and the scanner
  and mutation routes stay behind qwen.managed-agent.automation.enabled.
- Closes the H6a verification follow-ups: promptRef is Session-scoped and
  closed by both stores, the shared fixture gaps are pinned, and the Java
  text validator checks its clauses in the shared order.

Design: docs/design/2026-10-07-managed-automation-runtime.md (bilingual);
the H6 design's status and slice table are updated in both languages.

* fix(managed-agent): close the three runtime findings on H6b/H6c

R2-1 (P1): a mutation relay carried a fresh operationId per attempt and
the funnel deduped on content alone, so a request whose answer was lost
between the Harness commit and the control-plane command row could be
retried into committing its content over a newer revision (create rev 1
→ update rev 2 → retry commits rev 3, replayed=false, in both
languages). The relay now derives the operationId from (tenant,
Idempotency-Key), the funnel defines/retires answer the operation's
originally committed revision from the journal (rebuilt across reopens)
before touching the chain, and the control-plane mirror never regresses
past the revision it tracks while the remembered result is the
operation's own.

R2-2 (P1): runAutomationOperation skipped the Workspace admission every
other new-work verb runs, so a cached attachment kept firing and
mutating after the creator's grant was revoked. It now runs
requireReadyForNewWork before every relay.

R2-3 (P2): a prompt within the raw 64 KiB bound fails its fire when the
wrapped, JSON-escaped input envelope exceeds the 65,536-byte inline
resource bound, stranding an admitted/intent run. Admission now computes
the exact worst-case wrapped input of the merged definition (largest
route-admitted identities, real escaping) and refuses the definition.

One residual is deliberately deferred: a mutation relay that matched
the committed content appends no revision, so it leaves no operation
fact; its lost-answer race with a later commit needs a journal-level

* fix(managed-agent): keep store faults retryable and bind idempotency across operation kinds

Two findings from the fourth review wave on PR #13598:

A store HTTP or transport fault surfaced to the route through the
ManagedSessionRecordError superclass, so a fire_run whose prompt read hit
a transient 503 was answered 400 — and the scanner's definitive-4xx
branch settled the occurrence skipped forever, while redrive only visits
firing rows. assertReplayContent's validation catch likewise wrapped
promptOf's read into a conflict, so an honest retry of the identical
request became a 409. The route now classifies both store fault classes
as a retryable 503 and the content check reads the prompt outside the
validation try; only the request's own shape is still a 400/409.

The mutation replay looked up history by (operation, operationId), so a
cross-kind retry under one Idempotency-Key — a retire(K) after a
committed create(K), when the control plane lost its command row before
remember() — slipped past and really cancelled the definition. The
funnel now consults the journal for any committed operation under the
derived identity and refuses another kind with
automation_operation_conflict, matching the public one-key-one-operation
constraint; the journal rebuild makes the check hold across a Harness
restart, and the fake mirrors the rule at control-plane level.

Regression tests in both languages: funnel cross-kind refusal (same
session and across a reopen), a store fault passing through the replay
content check as itself, a route-level fire answered 503 whose claim
still dispatches after the store recovers, a scanner fire answered 503
staying firing for the redrive, and a service-level cross-kind retry
conflicting with the mirror left live.

* fix(managed-agent): refuse a cross-Session idempotency-key reuse before relaying

The operation identity derived from (tenant, Idempotency-Key) is tenant-scoped, while the journal proving it is Session-scoped: create(K, S1) committed and mirrored, the command row lost before remember(), a create(K, S2) would relay to S2's Harness and mint a second definition under the same scheduleId, which the mirror then shadows behind the first Session's resource. create() now checks the durable mirror for the derived scheduleId first and, when it landed on another Session, answers automation_operation_conflict instead of relaying; identical retries on the same Session still pass through to the funnel's replay. Regression: the lost-row cross-session create conflicts with nothing relayed and the mirror still naming the first Session.

* fix(managed-agent): claim automation operation identities before the side effect

The mirror check added for the cross-Session reuse only sees answers that already landed: a create whose Harness committed but whose answer was lost has neither a mirror nor a command row, and a concurrent request can pass the check before the first one mirrors — both windows then committed the same derived scheduleId a second time, shadowing the first definition.

create() now claims (tenant, Idempotency-Key) with an atomic pre-relay insert into the command ledger: the primary key arbitrates concurrent racing, a claim held by a different request body conflicts idempotency_conflict before anything relays, and the identical request falling back into an unanswered claim redrives it so the funnel replays what it committed. remember() settles the claim row rather than adding a second, and the same-Session mirror guard stays for rows the control plane lost on its own.

Regression: a lost-answer create keeps its claim so the cross-Session retry conflicts while the owner redrives to its committed revision, a foreign mid-flight claim conflicts with zero side effects, and the lost-answer retry path asserts the claim-shaped row.

* fix(managed-agent): guard claim settlements by owner, claim every ledger mutation, release on definitive refusals

The shared remember() settled by (tenant, key) alone while update and retire did not claim first: an update that had passed its replay check before a concurrent create could overwrite the create's completed result_json — the row kept the create's digest and scheduleId, so the create's honest retry was then answered with another automation's resource with replayed=true.

update() and retire() now join the pre-relay claim protocol create() introduced: every mutation using the command ledger binds (tenant, Idempotency-Key) to its request before any side effect. The settlement itself is guarded twice — request_digest and actor must match the row's owner, and only an unanswered claim can be filled — so a late re-driven mutation can neither steal the row nor rewrite a completed result; the guarded settle is pinned red against the pre-fix unguarded form. Since only commit-proven refusal answers exist on the Harness, a definitive 4xx now releases its own unanswered claim instead of burning the key, so a fixed re-send of a refused request succeeds; the retired-definition replay branch settles its own claim the same way.

* fix(managed-agent): release claims only for refusals proven pre-commit

A blanket 4xx release read too much into the answer: invalid_automation_operation answers both a malformed new request — committed nothing — and an integrity failure while reading a previously committed resource, where the original operation may well have landed. Releasing the claim in the second case orphaned exactly the definition the claim was binding, opening the same-key-on-another-Session window the protocol exists to close.

Claims are now released only for 4xx codes that answer exclusively before any commit (not found, mode gate, conflict, stale revision, retired, quota); a proofless answer keeps the claim, so the other request conflicts and the owner still re-drives. The fake gains a pre-commit mutation-refusal seam, and the regression pins the proofless 400 keeping its claim, blocking the second Session and settling on the owner's retry — verified red against the blanket form first.

* fix(managed-agent): release claims only on refusals audited pre-commit

The 4xx-minus-400 partition still read proof into answers it cannot have: a re-attach that finds the Session running a Turn answers 409 hosted_session_already_attached — an attachment state, not a commit verdict — and a takeover that misses the Session answers hosted_session_not_found, equally mute on whether the mutation landed. Releasing the claim on either orphans a definition the original Session may well hold.

The release set is now an audited enumeration of the funnel's own business refusals, each with a single pre-commit answering path — automation_not_found, mode gate, operation conflict, stale revision, retired, count limit — closer to exhaustive proof than to convenience; every other answer keeps the binding. The attach-conflict regression mirrors the proofless-read one: same claim surviving, second Session conflicting, owner re-driving to its own answer; verified red against the loose form first.

* fix(managed-agent): release claims only on request-determined verdicts

A quota refusal is a verdict about the moment, not about the key: the claim row is shared by every attempt under one Idempotency-Key, so delivering an early attempt's automation_count_limit 409 and releasing the row dissolves the binding its later sibling may already have committed against — after which a third body under the key mints a second definition and the sibling's delayed success settles to the wrong mirror.

What may release is now exactly what cannot move between attempts: the mode gate, decided by the definition's sessionMode against the deployment's admitted set, identically every time the same request is sent. Capacity, existence, binding, revision and terminal verdicts all evaluate shared state and keep the claim; the quota regression mirrors the family's other pins — refused attempt, foreign body conflicting, sibling committing and settling — and was verified red with quota back in the set first.

* fix(managed-agent): map wake-turn ids to path-safe Broker sessions, and refuse fires a blocked Session can never run

The round-2 real-stack pass found two walls. Every automation turn whose model calls a Workspace tool died at the Broker's path-safe Runtime Session id rule (`arun_…:input` rejected at acquire), blocking its Session: wake input ids are committed as the turn id, so every Broker handle built from a prompt id now maps a non-path-safe one to a stable `wake-<sha256>` instead (`hostedRuntimeSessionId`); the mapped form is itself path-safe, so the map stays idempotent wherever lease/record paths already carry it. And a recovery-blocked Session kept answering 202 to fires, committing runs that can never start while its slots kept scheduling: `fire_run` now answers 409 `hosted_session_blocked` unless the occurrence's run is already dispatched (a pure replay answer carrying no new fact), the scanner recording the slot skipped with that reason. The run the F3 path settles `failed`/`outcome_unknown` now consumes its crashed input too — a `turn_result` settles its turnId — so a reload stops classifying the same crash as recovery and re-blocking the Session every time.

Regression: the id mapping (stable, idempotent) and a route-level wake turn whose tool call reaches acquire under the mapped id (red on the raw form); a blocked Session refusing a fresh fire while replaying its crashed run, consuming the crash, and firing after reload; the scanner recording `skipped(hosted_session_blocked)` on the new refusal. * fix(managed-agent): settle the runtime park and silence of a crashed wake turn

The round-3 real-stack pass found two new walls past F6/F7. When the Harness crashes inside an automation turn's tool call, the F3 settlement left the checkpoint parked at await_runtime — every later turn on that Session refused (await_runtime is not a model-start phase) and the wake Broker session held the Workspace execution lease for every Session on it. When the crashed turn's prompt was text, its naked user record merged into the next turn's model history, so the crashed instruction ran a second time inside an unrelated run.

In the F3 recovery path: when the crashed turn's checkpoint holds in-progress Runtime items, the existing stop/cancel helpers drive them to terminal, settleParkedTurnCancelled records each cancellation as its cancelled tool_result — so the checkpoint advances out of await_runtime and the history stays well-formed — and the wake session's Broker lease is released. The Session unblocks only once that park is provably settled: a failure to even read the checkpoint, or to stop or release any part of it, keeps the block rather than letting a fire run against an unproven park. The consume write of the crashed input's turn_result gains bounded retries on SessionTranscriptChangedError, so a concurrent route claim cannot drop it and resurrect every reload classifying the same crash as recovery. The fire refusal itself is unchanged: while blocked, anything that would commit a new fact answers 409 hosted_session_blocked.

For the history side, runHostedHarnessTextTurn's assembly now excludes every user record whose prompt id ended with an error or cancelled turn_result (excludeTerminallyEndedUserRecords): a turn that ended without an answer is over, so the next turn never meets the crashed instruction as live work — pinned one level up in the runner's own suite (the crashed prompt is absent from the chat's setHistory while an answered older prompt passes through).

* fix(managed-agent): one aftermath for a crashed wake turn, reconciled and retried until proven

Round 4 of the real-stack pass found the round-3 recovery still wedging in three shapes and the F9 fix dead on the real path. A crash inside a wake turn's Runtime call whose park settlement fails once consumed the input anyway — after any restart nothing classified the crash again, so the Session and its Workspace lease wedged for good (one transient Broker 503 sufficed). With overlap skip, Spring skipped every later slot, so nothing ever loaded the crashed Session at all and its wake Broker session kept the Workspace execution lease while every other Session span on workspace_busy with no upper bound. The first user Turn to load a crashed Session raced the recovery behind the load and failed post-admission. And the round-3 history exclusion read turn_result records from a projection that never carries them, so the crashed prompt still merged into the next turn's model history.

The crashed wake turn now has one aftermath, keyed on the journal and the checkpoint rather than on which settle ran before it: the run fails with its execution unknown; the parked Runtime executions stop to terminal and settle cancelled — each cancelled tool_result committed once so the checkpoint leaves await_runtime with the call and its answer paired; the wake session releases its Broker lease, re-attempted on every pass since the journal cannot record whether an earlier pass landed it; and only then does the input's own turn_result consume it, with a transient journal conflict retried. An unproven settle keeps the block and the input pending, so the wake pump's blocked cycle — re-armed across a dead pass — the next load, and the fire that loads the Session all retry the same sequence instead of hinging a permanent wedge on one transient fault. For the case nothing loads the Session — overlap skip darkens the definition — the scanner, before recording a count-based refusal (never the open-Turn one), asks the Harness a fourth verb, reconcile_run, which commits no new fact, classifies and settles the crashed wake turn, and answers its run; the decision prices the count off those answers rather than the lagging mirror. A prompt arriving while the park is unsettled is refused pre-admission with the retriable 409 hosted_turn_recovery_required. And a turn that ended without an answer keeps its prompt out of every later turn's model history, filtered against the journal's turn.settled events at both history builders — the dead record-layer exclusion is gone, replaced by a pin through the real builder path: with the exclusion deleted, the new test fails.

Witnesses: six new Harness pins (park settle after a Broker fault with cancelled tool_result / lease release / in-process unblock, the reconcile route both polarities, consume retry, history exclusion, pre-admission prompt refusal) and three Java scanner pins (a wedged run reconciled into the very slot that asked, an unanswered reconcile keeping the refusal, an open Turn never triggering a reconcile); the fake gains the reconcile verb. ci(sdk-java): re-check open PRs for Flyway version collisions as main moves (#13770)

The Flyway uniqueness guard checks a pull request merged with the main of
the moment it ran. Nothing re-ran it when main later gained a migration, so
a PR that went green before another PR took its version stayed green and
turned main red once it merged; it also cannot see several open PRs
claiming one version.

A new workflow runs after every push to main that changes a migration and
every 30 minutes. It checks out main, reads each open PR's changed paths
from the GraphQL API (no PR code is fetched), and sets the
'Flyway migration version uniqueness (latest main)' commit status on each
PR head that adds a migration: failure when a version it adds is taken in
the merge result, success otherwise naming the other open PRs that claim
the same version, and error when the file list could not be read in full.
A head whose status would not change is not written again, and a head that
already carries the status is always re-evaluated so a stale failure clears.

The naming rules move into a shared module used by both scripts; the
guard's behaviour is unchanged and its workflow also triggers on that
module.

Fixes #13742

* feat(managed-agent): H5b/H5c channel runtime for the email reference adapter

Make the two channel domains executable end to end on the managed path.
Inbound: a trusted adapter submits an authenticated platform event to the
control plane, which dedupes it on the four-part ingress identity (the
V47 route row), resolves or creates the route's Session idempotently, and
asks the Harness to commit the route binding revision, the staged
attachments, the input and its wake in one journal transaction; the row
turns admitted only after the Harness answered, so every crash window
replays to the committed admission. The embedded wake scheduler runs the
input as an ordinary text turn. Outbound: a settled channel turn plans its
reply as a channel_delivery record; the adapter pulls claims through the
control plane, each step is a record revision the Harness commits first
and the V47 ledger follows; a claim that outlives its lease settles
unknown and is never resent; an explicit resend opens a new chain. The
three public channel resources move from planned to partial.

Both domains join the enabled list behind an adapter gate (email only)
that the authority checks on every first route revision through the
committed policy; a delivery binds to its committed route at the pinned
revision in both languages. V52 adds the registered connections, the
route catalog and the claim ledger. The email adapter gains a managed
mode (qwen channel managed-email) that reuses the Legacy parsing and
transport helpers and keeps its own locked state.

* fix(managed-agent): close the remaining ledger findings (F2/F6/F10/F13)

F2: the email adapter bounded inbound text by characters only, so a
multibyte body under the 32,000-char line could still overflow the
Harness's 64 KiB *byte* envelope verdict and refuse deterministically.
Clamp admitted text by bytes (ENVELOPE - 4 KiB headroom) with a

inbound is admitted truncated instead. Witness: an 汉 x22,000 mail is
admitted with its text under the byte line, and the adapter keeps

F6: a settleInterrupted hook that itself faulted (e.g. a rejected
terminal-record write) escaped createMonitorWakeRunTurn as a generic
wake failure and latched the Session. Catch it, log, and answer 'busy'
so the next wake attempt re-drives the settle — the turn's own
transient account. Witness: first hook call faults -> busy, Session
unblocked; second call -> settled, attempts == 2.

into a deterministic 400, so a transient Session Store flap

record still answers 400 invalid_channel_operation; the healthy path
admits the same input afterwards (202).

against a never-acquired runtime session only answers 404, which the

* feat(agents): define the session-centric multi-agent contract

Introduce the shared contract for collaboration inside an ordinary chat
session: agent_mention / agent_message record payloads, the
external_record ext method, live run frames, per-session bindings, the
program adapter interface, and Host protocol v2 payloads. The browser
copy lives in the SDK and mirrors the core definitions.

Design: docs/plans (session multi-agent redesign).

* feat(agents): run @-mentioned agents inside the chat session

Record path: the daemon asks the ACP child to write `agent_mention` and
`agent_message` records through the new
`qwen/control/session/external_record` ext method. The child persists
them, shows them live with the same projection transcript replay uses
(so reload, /resume and export match), and hands their envelope to the
main model on its next turn without starting one. Writes that arrive
during a main-model turn are deferred until it settles, so a record never
lands between a tool call and its result.

Orchestrator: a per-workspace SessionAgentOrchestrator queues one run per
(chat session, agent), coalesces new triggers into the queued run,
resumes the agent's native session, streams live run frames on
`agent/session-events`, relays tool approvals, routes @mentions in
replies (chain limit setting, default unlimited), and exposes a leased
remote queue for Host v2. New routes: mentions, runs snapshot, cancel,
stop all, permission vote. Agents started this way are not capped at
read-only tools; writes go through approval.

The thread subsystem is untouched and removed in a later commit.

* feat(agents): Claude/Codex adapters, Host protocol v2 and in-session UI

Adapters: drive Claude Code (`claude -p` stream-json, approvals through
`--permission-prompt-tool stdio`, never bypassed) and Codex (`codex
app-server` JSON-RPC, approvals held open until the person answers) as
session agents; probe installed programs; a hidden `qwen agents
session-send-mcp` stdio MCP server gives agents a `session_send` tool.
Local agents may now name a program.

Host protocol v2: remote runtimes pick up session turns, stream ordered
event batches, receive approval decisions over heartbeat/events, return
the native session id, run turns concurrently, and relay `session_send`
through a loopback-only route. Runtime-side routes no longer depend on the
boot-time collaboration flag, connections made with `/hosts/connect` are
persisted and re-established on boot, and `qwen agents join <link>`
connects a running daemon. Hosts auto-create one agent per available
program. A remote qwen turn is authorized by a Host-local binding that
carries the coordinator's persona.

WebShell: @-mentions post to the current session instead of opening a
thread; agent replies render inline with their author, live status,
steps, token usage, per-message approvals, stop and stop-all. Thread
pages, sidebar collaboration rows and the agent activity tab are gone;
the Agents page keeps the roster and Runtimes, shows each runtime's
programs, and can join a coordinator.

Threads, thread runs, statuses, priorities, budgets, sub-threads, the six

Orchestrator: frames report when the agent's record is in the transcript;

* fix(agents): resend history when an agent's native session cannot be reused

A remote agent picked up by a different Host, a local agent that moved
from a runtime, or an agent whose program changed starts a fresh native
session that has seen nothing, yet was given only the delta after the old
cursor. Bindings now record the program with the runtime, and the read
cursor is ignored whenever the native session cannot be reused, so the
agent gets the conversation from the start within the input budget.

* feat(agents): bound agent chains by a token budget; pin Codex to approvals

A session now tracks the tokens its agents spend between two human
messages. Once `experimental.agentTokenBudget` (default 1,000,000, 0 =
unlimited) is spent, agents still answer what they were asked but cannot
wake other agents until a person posts again; the refusal is written on
the reply. This restores the cost boundary the thread design had, without
capping the number of hops.

Codex threads are started with a read-only sandbox and `on-request`
approvals, so every write or command is escalated to the person in the
session instead of passing silently under a workspace-write default.

Also fixes the two prefer-const lint errors CI reported.

a coordinate-don't-do protocol); members the leader mentions are tracked
per session, every member reply wakes the leader (coalesced), and the
engagement ends when the leader delegates nothing further. A leader with
nothing to do replies empty, recorded as no_action and shown as a muted
row. Hops count against the chain limit and the token budget. Agents
page gets a Squads section; the @ picker lists squads; leader replies are
labelled leader · squad.

* fix(a2a): release the reservation when a post is permanently refused

A post the orchestrator permanently refuses — an over-long first message
past `MAX_MENTION_TEXT_CHARS` is the reachable shape — left the chat
session `createSession` had just made behind. `attachExternalSession` had
already recorded it, so the empty session stayed in the owner's list and
every retry of the same request reused it instead of starting over.

Add `releaseExternalReservation`, which undoes `attachExternalSession`: it
drops the reservation's `sessionId` and, when no other entry names that
session, its context — a context is what makes a `contextId` continuable,
so one another task still needs stays. `a2aSendMessage` calls it for a
`refused` post into a session this call made, then removes the session.
Release comes first: removing a session the reservation still names would
send the retry to a session that is gone. A retryable `unavailable` keeps
both, so that retry continues where it stopped.

* fix(a2a): discard a session whose first post is refused for good

A permanently refused mention (A2ASessionError kind 'refused') used to keep
the just-created chat session and its reservation forever: one empty
'A2A . <caller>' session per over-long first message, visible in the
owner's WebShell list, never recordable again. Track the session this call
created and, on a permanent refusal, release the reservation's sessionId
(new releaseExternalReservation) and discard the session, so a retry starts
over in a fresh one. The session's context is dropped only when no other
entry continues through it. Also pin that a retryOf cycle in a store file
ends the follow walk instead of recursing without end.

* fix(cli): read live agent runs before a roster change, and refuse a disable that strands one

Two ways a roster change could strand a session-agent run, both because the
gate that is supposed to catch it did not run:

- `hasLiveRuns` read `getSessionAgentOrchestrator`, which answers "none"
  for a workspace whose orchestrator this daemon has not created yet — the
  state right after a restart. A run a previous daemon left queued was
  therefore invisible, and the first DELETE or `execution` PATCH after a
  restart was allowed over it. The gate now creates the orchestrator the
  way the Host routes do; its startup recovery adopts those runs, and
  `liveRuns()` waits for that recovery.

  enabled-driven settlement of queued runs was removed with the thread
  backend, and the route only checked live runs when `execution` was in the
  patch. A queued run of a disabled agent can never start and nothing ends
  it, so the agent could neither run nor be retired (`409
  agent_has_live_work`). Disabling now refuses while the agent has a queued
  run; a run already executing does not block it.

comment that now names the paths that cover `enabled`.

createBrowserBackend() skips Native Messaging host registration outside

* feat(managed-agent): H4b child Session runtime

Slice H4b of #12827 (Stage H of proposal #12380), stacked on H4a's
child/acceptance record contract: the child Session runtime — the four
producers of the H4a bodies, the first cross-Session dispatcher, the
close cascade, and kind-selective enablement, on the server-first order.

declaration set behind a per-kind gate; startChildRun commits the launch
intent with the definition pin and the derived record key before any
side effect; the foreground arm waits on the committed chain alone and
answers from evidence, the background arm returns a task handle and
takes its result through a durable notification input plus wake, with
accepted delivered after the answer and consumed after the consuming
turn settles — two independent, separately observable facts.

relay ledger qwen_managed_child_result_relay (the reserved task-event
name stays reserved); createChildSession under the parent's exact
binding stamps parent/root lineage idempotently from the launch record
key; the relay drives creation, attaches, copies the terminal result
and receipt digest-bound, submits the acceptance, marks orphaned at a
closing parent and unknown past bounded retries, never re-executing.

children through the ordinary close pipeline before the Harness close.

MANAGED_SESSION_ENABLED_CHILD_RUN_KINDS=['child_agent'] so H3's shell

and WebShell surface do not move.

* fix(managed-agent): Close the H4b review round's relay, cascade and wake-consumption gaps

The review round found five child-runtime gaps this commit closes:

- findChildLineage returned a null row for a root Session through
  Stream.findFirst() and threw, breaking every Hosted Session create.
- The relay binding probe read the tool-session Runtime record, which a
  text-only child never acquires; it now reads the physical Runtime
  binding that warm() creates when the Hosted tool turn is constructed,
  and the tool-session read path is retired with it.
- The close cascade treated a child created but not yet attached as
  unstarted; it now resolves the child through the relay ledger before
  judging, and closes it through its own Session lifecycle (admitted
  idempotent close, owed until terminal Session status) instead of a
  bare daemon DELETE — child creation inherits the parent creator's
  workspace grant so that admission passes the creator checks.
- Journal debt (stop or terminal revisions faltering) re-arms the
  whole close instead of being dropped, with the acceptance-answered
  early-out restricted to arms past delivering so the relay still owes
  its own mark_accepted.
- The wake-turn pump treated its blocked sentinel branches as settle
  proof and consumed the delivered child result without a Turn; the
  consumption wrapper now requires a genuine settle.

Terminal-classified relay rows also leave the discovery set so a
grown ledger cannot starve the fleet scan, the funnel routes conflict
and record refusals as typed errors instead of message matching, the
turn-settle flush keeps the unconsumed remainder owed when it dies
mid-commit, and the design documents carry the corrected semantics in
both languages.

* fix(managed-agent): settle Shell-lane parents and children without Workspace close

SessionLifecycleService admits protocol 1 only for the Files profile;
the Shell lane keeps the protocol-0 close whose child cascade passes
ordinary authorization, so a H4b parent close/delete no longer ends
RECOVERY_BLOCKED workspace_lifecycle_profile_unavailable.

ChildResultRelay no longer holds a parent's settlement hostage to a
close the host cannot dispatch: without Workspace-close support the
relay still settles failed and over-bound child records and retires
the ledger row instead of retrying forever.

The harness-session route test now pins the lifecycle authority
stamped on the Store client at verb-commit time.

* fix(managed-agent): retain the child-close obligation as a discoverable close debt

On a host that cannot close Workspace Sessions at all, retiring the
relay row alongside the parent settlement discarded the only durable
record that still owed the child Session its close: the child stayed
ACTIVE with no ledger scan and no close cascade able to find it again,
even after close capability returned.

The settlement now still commits on time, but the row parks as
close_debt — claimed, named by the child id, due on the heartbeat, and
surfaced by the discovery page's cancelled arm — until a capable scan
admits the close and only then retires. A parked debt outlives the
orphaned early-out and never re-enters the give-up chain, whose
settle-and-classify already happened for this row.

* fix(managed-agent): renumber the child lineage relay migration to V53

#13163 took V52 for the mutation-attempt sequence while the branch was
in flight, so the merged tree carried two V52 migrations and Flyway
refused every context. The golden-list IT now expects 48-53 and passes
against a live MySQL on the merged migrations; the module's 1439 tests
pass with the renumbered layout.

* fix(managed-agent): reconcile the close obligation before orphaned classification

The settlement of a child run can be committed while its close_debt
ledger write never lands — a crash or a lost reply between them. If
the parent then closes or deletes before the next scan, the settled
task is already invisible to the close cascade's live-scope walk, and
the orphaned classification erased the ledger row that was the only
durable holder of the owed close: child ACTIVE, zero CLOSE operations,
zero future discovery.

The non-ACTIVE-parent branch now reconciles before it classifies: a
settled delivery whose child Session still stands (row id or committed
lineage, short of CLOSED/DELETED) parks as close_debt instead and
discharges through the ordinary admission. Unsettled rows classify
orphaned exactly as before — the cascade owned their stop.

* fix(managed-agent): read the close capability once in the give-up chain

The admission order and the retention flag each re-read closeSupported();
a TOCTOU flip between the two could mark the debt settled without ever
admitting the close. One cached read now feeds both.

* test(managed-agent): pin the give-up chain to a single capability read

Sequencing closeSupported() true-then-false must still admit the close
and call hte accessor exactly once — the TOCTOU window between a double
read is what lost the debt silently in the first place.

* docs(managed-agent): renumber the design's migration cites to V53 and record the close debt

The renumbers (V51 took main's lifecycle, V52 #13163's mutation attempt)
left both language versions citing a migration id that no longer exists,
and the close-retention machinery added since the doc landed had no
ledger description. Both versions stay synchronized: V53 everywhere plus
the close_debt / orphan-reconciliation paragraph in decision 8.

* fix(managed-agent): retain the close obligation at task settlement, from every intermediate ledger state

Task settlement leads delivery settlement: the run record settles and
projects task completed while delivery still says accepting, so the
close cascade's live-scope walk never sees it — the retention predicate
must read task-settled evidence, not terminal delivery alone.

The discovery page's settled arm now admits every non-terminal ledger
state too: a give-up whose settle committed but whose close_debt write
failed sat in binding, outside the old arm-2 list, permanently
undiscoverable even before a parent close. Arm 2 now mirrors arm 1's
terminal-only exclusion; the in-flight work sets stay disjoint by
delivery, and the due/lease predicates still own eligibility.

* fix(managed-agent): never re-enter the walk for a settled-cancelled record

Widening arm 2 to every non-terminal ledger state made the settled arm
discover a creating/binding row whose create-or-fail reply or terminal
classification write was lost. On the next scan work() replayed the
record into create() and actually launched a child already recorded as
creation_failed / not_started_proven.

The walk now reconciles such rows instead: a standing child owes exactly
its close (parked close_debt, ordinary discharge), and with none the row
classifies unknown. The settled arm keeps reaching them; only the
creation/execution arms close.

* fix(managed-agent): keep retained close debts from starving new child work

On a host that cannot close Workspace Sessions, every finished child
parks a close_debt row due again every five seconds, and the discovery
page ordered by created_at always served those oldest rows first —
about 150-200 delegations in, the freshest launch is never reached and
no new child Session is ever created (real-stack evidence on the macOS
rig).

Breaking the starvation breaks nothing of the retention: due debts now
sort after every other owed row on the page, and a host that cannot
discharge a debt at all revisits it every 300 seconds instead of every
heartbeat — nothing could land before a restart returns the capability,
and a capable scan still discharges on its very next visit.

* fix(managed-agent): fence relay creation recovery against settled evidence at every seam

The same lost-write interruption can hide behind three seams, and each
authorized the wrong outcome on its own snapshot:

- The claimed walk read the discovery page's captured delivery. A record
  settled between the page and the claim retired or relaunched on the
  stale snapshot; retirement authorization now re-reads the committed
  projection (falling back to the page only when the row is gone).
- A stalled creator whose relay lease lapsed minted the Session anyway
  after another worker's give-up committed creation_failed and retired:
  the creation admission never read the run's terminal verdict. It now
  fences that mint inside its own transaction with FOR UPDATE on the
  run's task line, so a settled record refuses and unanswered replay
  still answers.
- A give-up with a lost relay session id resolved no attach and read
  no lineage: it claimed creation_failed while a real child ran. The
  child now resolves from the committed lineage before the proof, and
  a vetoed attach replay consults the child's own committed Turn
  before started=false may be claimed.

* fix(managed-agent): never admit children queued behind a cancelled wait

A batch whose foreground wait was abandoned by cancellation returned
control to the batch loop, which then admitted every agent call queued
behind it — work the cancelled turn never started, including a
successful 'started in the background' answer. The admission gate now
checks the abort signal before describing, bounding or stamping
anything; keeping an already-launched child running stays documented.

* fix(managed-agent): close the launch-admission edges codex flagged behind the quota line

Three adjacent admission edges all authorized against the wrong party:

- Quotas counted the replayed child: a re-driven batch whose siblings
  filled the active run quota got count_limit for the launch it was
  already running. The record lookup now precedes the quota verdict,
  and children.admit's replay identity answers as before.
- The background workaround was recommended where it deadlocks: a
  Session-owned mount (Hook catalog or MCP owner) survives the Turn
  and releases only at Session close, so a background child launched
  under it parks on workspace_busy. The background arm refuses there,
  and only turn-sourced holds keep the foreground hint.
- A wake turn's id embeds its commissioning run id, so chained
  background launches grew one suffix per hop into the 128-char
  lineage bound by the third hop. The launch key from a wake turn is
  now a sha256-truncated digest of the same stable name — replay
  deterministic, hop-bounded, and lineage-parser-legal at every hop.

* fix(managed-agent): never let a verdict race past a still-committing settlement

Two seams in the same family both read pre-collapse evidence and then
acted durably on it:

- Between the walk's read of the projection and the orphaned
  classification commit, another worker's settlement can still land —
  and the classification would orphan the child that settlement just
  made owable. The verdict now locks the record row FOR UPDATE inside
  one transaction for the re-read: losing that race only says the truth
  settled, and exactly one fresh evaluation assigns the close debt
  instead of retirement.
- A give-up's  verdict committed on the no-child proof
  while the stalled creator resumed and minted between the proof and
  the failure commit. At the commit seam, the lineage is re-read: new
  child evidence arrives after the proof owes one more bounded wait,
  never the confidently wrong pairing.

* fix(runtime-broker): read every page for the newest READY binding

findLatestBindingByHarnessSession returned from inside the first page
that held any READY row (and advanced the keyset cursor only when it
held none), so a greater-id READY binding on a later page was never
considered — the live Runtime identity for a child's first controlled
binding could pin a stale generation on generation-lite bindings. The
whole bucket now traverses, keeping the greatest READY id seen, and
returns after the traversal ends.

* fix(managed-agent): retention defaults on the standing child, never the racing verdict

A classification now orphaned only children that no longer stand —
whichever side wins the settle-vs-verdict race, a child that still
owns its Session keeps its one discoverable holder, ending the
orphan-burial shape in both directions at once (forward settle-then-
verdict and inverse verdict-then-settle). The atomic
classify-when-unsettled from R20 folded away in favour of the simpler
default; orphaned remains for the child who genuinely stands no more.

* fix(managed-agent): stamp out three launch-side certification gaps codex pinned

- A non-plain-object lineage field on session create now knows it:
  arrays (which object() maps to null) no longer stand in for accepted
  ancestry; only absent/null lineage is root. Anything else is the
  debuggable 400 invalid_hosted_lineage, never a 200 root that carries
  a malformed ancestry silently.
- The restarted-wake-turn recovery probe asks the durable record about
  child dispatch under the same collapsed key the launcher wrote —
  acceptChildAgent's wake-turn key derivation is now shared with the
  PostToolUse re-query (sha256-truncated digest of  identities), so resume finds it instead of losing
  ded though no test pinned its wake shape before.
- A lifecycle claim stamped by the children/operations middleware now
  restores on EVERY exit of the route — including the early-refusal
  arms (invalid operation, unavailable profile, blocked session) that
  previously ran before the try and leaked the claim onto the shared
  store client for the rest of the process where a future claim's
  generations match no longer comparison.

* fix(managed-agent): prove close debt by fact and address the fence by key

Two avoidance-class truths respected:

- A close debt whose child no longer stands is discharged by fact,
  not retried by suspicion — dischargeCloseDebt now re-reads the
  child's status before it admits, so an already-closed/deleted child
  never faces a permanently-refused admission, and an unproven-null
  read does not discharge against an unconfirmed child that we know
  exists. Default mock fixtures now answer ACTIVE for a child whose
  recovery would need it.
- The child-creation terminal-truth fence addresses the parent's real
  launch row by primary key (session scope + record key, the same key
  the idempotent admission derives), so its FOR UPDATE never becomes
  a cross-tenant table scan against MySQL's default REPEATABLE READ.

* fix(managed-agent): settle close-road blockers by evidence, not retry or wire-code faith

Three segments, each adjudicated prior to code:

- On a host that cannot close Workspaces, the close cascade's child
  close admission is fake-owed, and the delivery taxonomy gets a plain
  IllegalStateException it cannot file — the parent retries forever
  under an unnameable retry instead of the typed blocked code it
  already uses when the cascade had nothing to do. On such a host the
  admission is simply skipped, and the parent close proceeds into that
  typed gate.
- A lineage-named child with no body facts, no ledger creation key
  and no READY binding has no replay source: that evidence settles as
  creation-never-attached with started: false once, not an eternally
  re-armed debt on empty proof.
- A give-up's creation_failed verdict is now proved off the record's
  own transition field: intent (legally holding no attach or past
  dispatch successors) is answered never-started were nothing physical
  contradicts; dispatch_started or past is answered started; a
  physically-ran child with an intent record whose binding cannot
  name its dispatch answer gets deferred instead of invented verdicts.

* fix(managed-agent): let a never-started verdict name its minted Session

The create→attach window leaves exactly one durable fact — the minted
child Session's lineage — and the terminal revision that retires such a
run could never record it: the validators required the Session to stay
null until a dispatch admitted it, to have a Runtime binding, and for
creation_failed in particular to be anonymous. A retired run then left
its mint behind with nothing able to discover it again.

The contract now lets a not_started_proven settlement carry
childSessionId with no binding — bounded to that one terminal, the only
state with no dispatch to host from. The fail/close_scope operations
accept an optional childSessionId, the builders restate the same id
replay-safely and refuse a rename with child_operation_record, and the
shared fixtures pin the newly-lawful shapes in both languages.

Pins: core record/operation suites (190) replay the amended fixtures
and the naming/rename rules; the harness-session route pin drives the
wire contract end to end (named 202, replay 202, rename 409, malformed
400). Prettier, ESLint and tsc clean in cli and core.

* fix(managed-agent): arbitrate terminal verdicts against the mint at commit

R22's give-up wedge: executionState read the runtime_state projection
(unbound/provisioning/ready) while the caller compared execution enum
values, so intent and dispatch-started rows never matched — every row
looked started, the refused started verdicts repeated forever, and the
owed work never retired. The proof now reads the committed record body
through its inline resource; an unreadable body owes a bounded retry,
never a guessed verdict, and a self-proven not_started_proven execution
pairs the unstarted verdict directly.

R21's inverse race (a give-up verdict evaluated over an empty lineage,
then the mint lands) closes at commit time: ingestion of any
not_started_proven terminal revision locks the run's own row FOR UPDATE
— the same row the creation fence reads — and requires the verdict to
name exactly the Session the lineage proves minted, or refuses the
commit. The refused verdict defers the relay, whose retry re-reads the
lineage and names the child; every give-up verdict now names its child
whenever the child is known.

Mutation witnesses, all reverted byte-identical afterwards: a
runtime_state read fails the execution-body pin (an intent fixture
answers unbound); a no-arbitration gate fails the two refusal pins and
passes the two admission pins; dropping the verdict's naming fails the
relay's intent-family naming pin.

Suites: relay 36/36, relay store 13/13 (new execution-body pin and the
never-started pairing), verdict-reconcile decision table 4/4, creation
fence 3/3, and the full managed-agent-server verify green (checkstyle,
SpotBugs, 117 suites).

* fix(managed-agent): bind the close cascade's started call to any-state evidence

A creation key is an attempt id, never a start, and a READY binding's
absence says nothing — R22 reproduced both halves at this head: the
cascade wedged a parent in CLOSING behind a ledger-known child whose
binding had retired (the repair demanded warmth the retired row could
never offer again), and it committed not_started_proven over a child
whose own Turn had durably completed. A start is now proven by the
body's committed dispatch facts, by a binding row in ANY state (the new
findLatestBindingByHarnessSessionAnyState — a retired RELEASED/LOST row
still proves its dispatch and names the repair's identity, while the
relay's repair-for-warmth read stays READY-only), or by the child
Session's own durable Turn.

and names the Session the lineage minted; with any, the repair rebuilds
dispatch and attach from that evidence and the settlement commits
started:true. The READY-read Javadoc is also reworded to name the rule
the method implements (the greatest READY binding id across the full
traversal; generation is not consulted), closing the R1-16 follow-up
note that the old comment argued against the rule.

* fix(managed-agent): close the arbitration on the production topology, the retired binding, and the pre-admission Turn

R23 reran the preserved schedules on the arbitration head and broke each
side of it in one class apiece:

- The verdict/mint seam reopened on MySQL 8.0.46 REPEATABLE READ: the
  committing transaction's snapshot was established by its ordinary reads
  long before the verdict's row lock, so a plain lineage SELECT missed a
  mint committed after that snapshot — the unnamed never-started verdict
  still committed, exactly the interleave the seam exists for. The
  lineage read now runs FOR UPDATE as well: a locking read always sees
  the latest committed data on either InnoDB default, and takes the same
  extension-then-session lock order the mint uses. Witness on live
  MariaDB REPEATABLE READ with two connections: a plain read goes RED
  ("Expecting code to raise a throwable" — the gate accepted the mint-
  after-snapshot verdict), the locking read stays green; the H2 decision
  table is unchanged. The temporary MariaDB used for the witness is torn
  down after the run.
- The give-up's physical-child repair required READY, so a child whose
  binding retired (RELEASED) before the record recovered wedged the
  attempt budget behind an answer that could never come — no failure, no
  close admission, no settlement. Terminal reconciliation needs the
  historical dispatch identity, not warmth, so the repair replays from
  the any-state read too. The relay-side pin drives dispatch/attach/fail
  off a retired row whose READY answer is empty; its RED mutation witness
  (READY-only lookup) leaves the same row parked in binding, exactly the
  repro's shape.
- A Turn no longer proves a start by existing: only its G3 dispatch pair
  (submission mark or harness epoch) does, mirroring the cancellation
  store's own predicate. A Turn the coordinator failed before warm-up or
  submission is a pre-admission failure and settles the named
  never-started pairing instead of sending the repair after a binding
  that never existed — R23's parent-CLOSING wedge, pinned in the relay
  (creation_failed settles named, no repair attempt) and the cascade
  (close_scope started:false named, parent completes). The RED mutation
  witness for both qualifications (dropping the dispatch pair) wedges
  all three pins exactly as reproduced.

All mutation witnesses were reverted byte-identical (sha256/cmp checked).
Suites: relay 38/38, relay store 13/13, coordinator 12/12, gate 4/4, and

* fix(managed-agent): fence the never-started verdict against runnable Turns, and keep its refusal rollbackable

R24's two probes held against the arbitration head, both in fresh code
from this branch:

- A live ACCEPTED child Turn waiting for its coordinator shares the
  undispatched shape with the terminal pre-admission failure, so the
  give-up's new dispatch-pair qualification minted creation_failed over
  a Turn the coordinator then claimed, submitted and completed (the
  close-incapable host has no admission guard to catch it). The relay
  now defers bounded on any Turn that neither dispatched nor terminally
  failed pre-admission; only the terminal undispatched half settles the
  named never-started pairing. Pin: an enqueued ACCEPTED Turn sends
  nothing and parks at binding until the admission settles FAILED, when
  the named verdict commits; its mutation witness (deducting the
  qualification) fires the verdict at once, exactly the reproduction.
  The close cascade needed no sibling branch — the active-Turn close
  admission already continues past the same window there, and the
  terminal truth settles on the next walk (verified at coordinator
  12/12 without touching its flow).
- The gate's 409 reached the Hosted writer as a generic record
  rejection, which the HTTP client's refusal classification did not
  recognize: ManagedSessionAuthority latched writeFailure and the
  relay's corrected named retry could never commit on the resident
  parent. The gate now answers its own child_run_lineage_minted code,
  and the client maps it to ManagedSessionCommitRejectedError — the
  rollbackable non-commit class the authority rethrows without the
  latch. Pinned at all three levels: H2 decision table and the MySQL IT
  assert the exact wire code, and the TS client suite drives a one-shot
  409 into a typed rejection (writesStopped false) followed by the
  corrected retry committing (two attempts, one landed); its mutation
  witness (mapping removed) rethrows a plain HttpError.

Witnesses were reverted byte-identical (sha256/cmp). Suites: relay 39/39,
store 13/13, coordinator 12/12, gate 4/4, TS http store 65/65, full

* fix(managed-agent): treat the withdrawn submission mark as evidence-neutral, never as non-admission proof

R25's probe held against the intent reconciliation: G3's
withdrawSubmissionAttempted after a lost admission reply leaves the Turn
CANCELLED with neither dispatch mark nor epoch — the identical field
shape as a genuine pre-admission failure — while the historical binding
(READY → retired) remains. The terminal-shape check certified that as
never-started, converting an unanswered admission into a proved
non-admission: the relay then committed creation_failed over a child
whose admission outcome nobody had disproved.

The rule is now ordered by what can actually prove the verdict. An
outstanding Turn (live, neither dispatched nor terminal pre-admission)
always owes the bounded defer; the proven pair or the historical binding
row takes the dispatch replay with the same identity — a terminal status
never upgrades G3's reset to a proof. Only their joint absence plus a
terminal pre-admission failure settles the named never-started pairing.
The legacy space closes the same way it always did: no Turn, no binding,
no pair.

Pin: a CANCELLED Turn with no marks drives the dispatch/attach replay
from the binding's identity and settles child_failed named, never
creation_failed. Mutation witness (dropping the binding from the
dispatch-evidence disjunction) fires the never-started verdict in the
exact repro shape and is reverted byte-identical afterwards. Suites:
relay 40/40, store 13/13, coordinator 12/12, gate 4/4, full
managed-agent-server verify green. Design amended in both languages.

* fix(managed-agent): make the role CHECK byte-exact and unmask its tests

on their evidence and verified independently here:

  the CHECK's presence or the role default's absence. Every negative

fix(ui): resolve the provider dropdown key to the slug the backend declares (#43707)

* fix(ui): resolve the provider dropdown key to the slug the backend declares

The Add Model form submits the `provider` field from /public/providers/fields
verbatim, but provider_map is keyed by hand on the frontend, so the two sides
disagree for 14 of the 124 providers the backend serves. Some differ only in
case ("MINIMAX" vs "MiniMax", "CURSOR" vs "Cursor"), others have no key at all
("MILVUS", "LANGFUSE"). getProviderModels looked the key up, got undefined,
matched no models, and the model field silently degraded from a dropdown into
a free-text input with no candidates

Both call sites now go through resolveLitellmProviderSlug, which prefers an
exact provider_map key and otherwise lowercases the value. That resolves every
provider in the catalog to the litellm_provider slug the backend declares for
it. Matching provider_map case-insensitively instead would look tempting and be
wrong: "SAGEMAKER" and "SageMaker" are two distinct providers with two distinct
slugs, and a case-insensitive lookup collapses both onto sagemaker_chat

The regression test drives the real provider_create_fields.json rather than a
fixture, so a provider added to the catalog with a mismatched key fails here
instead of reaching users as an empty dropdown

feat(rust): one LitellmParams type for a config and a caller (#45642)

litellm-router-types mirrors litellm/types/router.py: LitellmParams holds the
model, the credentials, one flattened group per credential family from
auth-types (aws, vertex), the deployment settings a config spells, and every
other key in extra, as Python's extra="allow" keeps it. Config parses it
directly, so config::LiteLlmParams and its untyped additional_fields are gone
and a mistyped provider param is a parse error. fields() and specs() derive
from the families' param specs for hosts that project kwargs and fold module
globals. Spelled<T> is the one untagged shape for a typed value or the text a
config spells, organization takes the list Python's router expands, and the
callback shorthand keeps a value-level one-or-many. No credentials wrapper
group: serde's flatten only consumes keys for struct-shaped children.

feat(rust): type the Vertex AI connection params and where Python reads them (#45641)

VertexParams in auth-types holds the vertex_* fields of CredentialLiteLLMParams
in both spellings, with one ParamSpec per setting: the wire names, the litellm
module global VertexBase.get_vertex_ai_* consults, and the environment names.
A credential deserializes from text or the JSON object a config spells, an
empty object counts as absent, and both credential fields are redacted in
Debug. auth-gcp is split so lib.rs is the entrypoint (config, auth,
constants), its lookups resolve through the specs, secret_names() derives
from them, and get_vertex_ai_project_from_credentials reads a service
account's project_id for hosts that need it before a token exchange. The OCR
host folds the module globals in by spec at projection, so OcrSettings no
longer carries vertex_project and vertex_location.

feat(rust): type the AWS connection params and where Python reads them (#45610)

AwsParams in auth-types holds the aws_* fields of CredentialLiteLLMParams
with one ParamSpec per field: its wire name and the environment names it
falls back to. fields() and secret_names() derive from the specs, the AWS
helpers take the struct instead of a map, aws_auth_config and the region
resolution read through the specs, and a missing region is
AwsParams::REGION.missing("AWS"), whose message is rendered from the spec.
Bedrock Converse, Bedrock transcription, Textract OCR and the Bedrock
Messages config build the struct at their one untyped boundary.

The entry is rejected without max_budget, /team/info reports may_raise_max_budget to the caller, and the Admin UI nests the new checkbox under Max Budget with a tooltip and shows the team admin a hint under the budget field.

* fix(ui): shorten the raise_max_budget tooltip and link it to the docs

* fix(teams): pin the organization in the guarded team budget write

A granted raise is checked against the team's organization at read time, so the write now also requires organization_id to be unchanged. A concurrent move into a budgeted org returns 409 instead of landing an uncapped raise. Also types the new test helpers.
