test: fix stale and flaky tests across CircleCI, GHA and Buildkite (#45530)

* test(integration): poll the partition lock witness off the event loop

The witness poll ran a blocking psycopg connect and query on the test's event loop, so the partition DDL task only progressed during the 20ms sleeps and missed the 3s deadline on loaded runners. Polling through asyncio.to_thread lets the DDL reach the held lock concurrently, and the deadline is 10s since it only bounds how long the DDL takes to start waiting

* test(e2e): retry the reasoning turn until the model emits a reasoning item

Whether gpt-5.4-mini emits a reasoning item next to a forced function call is up to the model, and it skipped it on four scheduled runs while a same-SHA rerun passed. The first turn now retries up to three times before the unchanged reasoning-item assertion

* test(e2e): retry a Bedrock Converse model once when it reports no cache tokens

Opus on Bedrock Converse reported zero cache tokens on half of the scheduled runs while a same-SHA rerun passed. A model that comes back uncached is asked once more inside the 5 minute window, and the non-zero cache token assertion is unchanged

* test(e2e): poll until a deleted stored response stops being retrievable

Azure kept serving a just-deleted streamed response for a moment, so a single retrieve did not raise. Both delete tests now poll retrieve until it returns an error and still require a 4xx

* test(e2e): give the Together prompt cache five primed attempts

Together documents its prefix cache as best-effort, and three primed attempts came back with zero cached tokens once while a same-SHA rerun passed

* test(e2e): allow 30s for the idle RSS reading at session start

A loaded router replica took longer than 10s to answer the session-start memory read, which pytest reruns cannot recover. The RSS budget assertion is unchanged

* test(e2e): scope the MCP submission check to its own card

The register call timed out at 15s on a loaded stack and leaked a submitted server, so the retries matched two "3 passing, 1 failing" cards. Registration gets 60s and the check reads only the submitted server's card

* test(router): wait for the primary success record before counting it

The shadow fan-out test waited only for the two shadow success events and then asserted exactly one primary success, which the logging worker sometimes had not delivered yet. It needed a rerun on 5 of 59 main runs

* test(proxy): give the spend-log cleanup run a 1s budget

A 0.25s budget could expire before the first batch on a loaded xdist worker, leaving rows_deleted at 0. One second still stops the 50-batch, 5-second loop on the deadline, which is what the test proves

* test(autorouter): release the slow token count at 2.05s instead of 2.3s

The count only has to finish after a quarter of the 8s worker budget, and the planner gives it 3s, so releasing at 2.3s left 0.7s of slack that a loaded runner used up. 2.05s is still past the quarter mark with almost 1s of slack

* test(xai): run the reasoning-effort tests on grok-4.6 with a prompt that needs reasoning

grok-4.7 now returns reasoning tokens without any reasoning text, so reasoning_content was never set and both tests failed on every scheduled run. Called directly, grok-4.6 returned reasoning text 6 of 6 times on a step-by-step arithmetic prompt but only some of the time on a bare greeting

* test(integration): give the two worker-kill chaos tests the owned-proxy time budget

Each test spends about 50s on the burst and then up to graceful_stop_seconds() stopping its owned proxy, which overran the 90s default pytest timeout on loaded runners. They now use the same 2 * graceful_stop_seconds() + 120 budget as other owned-proxy tests

* test(integration): compare regional image responses without their created timestamp

Two identical generations that straddle a second boundary differ only in created, which failed the byte-for-byte comparison. Every other field and both spend rows are still compared

* test(integration): count only the S3 logger's flush task

The set of asyncio tasks created while the logger starts also picked up client close finalizers left by earlier tests, so the count ranged from 1 to 8. The test now counts the periodic_flush task it owns and cancels

* test(integration): send guardrail timeout probes eight at a time

All 44 probes went at once to a two-worker proxy, so on a loaded runner some guardrails used their whole 1s timeout before their request left the proxy, and the sink never saw them. A different set of providers failed on each run. Eight in flight still overlaps the waits

* test(integration): count a killed Arize chaos worker as gone once it is a zombie

psutil reports an unreaped zombie as still running, so the 10s death check failed whenever the supervisor was slow to reap the SIGKILLed worker, and the stop then overran the 90s default timeout. The test now accepts a zombie or a missing process and has the owned-proxy time budget

* test(integration): send the Typesafe connection test its real model and endpoint

The test passed the proxy alias as litellm_params.model, and /health/test_connection lays the request over the stored deployment, so the alias replaced the real typesafe/ model and the check failed with "LLM Provider NOT provided" on every run since it landed in #45481. It now sends the provider model, api_base and api_key directly

* test(integration): keep DB-stored models out of the usage-routing Redis read test

The owned proxy inherited store_model_in_db and the job's shared database, so a model another test left behind joined the router and added its cooldown key to the MGET the test compares exactly. Reproduced locally with one /model/new model present (3 failed), and green with model loading from the database turned off

* test(vertex_ai): prove the batch upload streams by laziness instead of peak memory

The two tracemalloc ratio tests flaked on unrelated PRs because peak memory on a shared xdist worker includes other threads' allocations and garbage from earlier tests. They are replaced by deterministic checks of the same property: the upload stream parses and maps a row only when it is pulled, so a body whose tail is not JSON yields its valid rows first, and a Path source reflects a row rewritten on disk after the upload started. Making the parse, the output, or the file read eager fails these tests

* test: type the counting mapper and the Bedrock rerun helper

* test: annotate the new test locals as Final and build them as tuples

* test(vertex_ai): prove pull-driven transforms with the garbage tail alone

Installer differential: ignore winget's partly filled download bars (#13172)

A main-vs-main run of the Windows installer differential (head 6c723f7477)
failed on progress frames alone: one side logged an extra partly filled
winget bar ('█████▒▒▒▒▒  <percent>' and '<size> / <size>'). How many partial
frames reach the log depends on the network, the same class of noise as the
spinner frames #12965 dropped.

Drop a line only when it is a partial frame (a bar with a '▒' left followed
by a normalised percent or size). The full bar a finished download ends on
still compares, so a download that stops finishing is still reported, and
the real differences in that run (diffusers main now skipped, audio.cpp now
installing) still fail the comparison.

Clean machine install: assert the no-git path by what setup.ps1 prints since #12971 (#13170)

The winget=masked Windows leg has failed on every main run since #12971
with "setup.ps1 found git on this machine, so the scrub leaked it back".
The scrub held: the install log shows "git  not found (not required)" and
"so git is not needed". The assertion keyed on "Git not found --
attempting install via winget", which #12971 rightly stopped printing on a
consumer install, since setup.ps1 now reaches for winget only when
something clones.

Prove the row ran without git from the "not found (not required)" step
line, fail if a consumer install attempts the winget git install at all,
and match the git gate in both its old and current wording, in this leg
and the virgin container leg. The old check passed a log in which the
consumer install tried to install git.

Studio: stop RAG PDF parsing from starving the server on scanned pages (#13137)

* Studio: stop RAG PDF parsing from starving the server on scanned pages

pymupdf4llm guesses each page's background colour by rendering its four
corners. When a scan image covers a corner, that render decodes the whole
image inside one PyMuPDF call that holds the GIL (about 2 s per JPEG2000
page), so the event loop could not answer /api/liveness and the desktop
watchdog killed the backend during linked-folder ingestion.

Skip the background probe only on pages where an image overlaps a probed
corner; every other page keeps the upstream behaviour and output.

Fixes #13094

* Compare scan image boxes in rotated page coordinates

* Skip the background probe only for scan-sized corner images; let each call build its own header table

Studio: stop with a clear error when a pre-cast text encoder fails and its dense shards were skipped (#13117)

* Studio: stop with a clear error when a pre-cast text encoder fails and its dense shards were skipped

The load plan leaves a text encoder's dense shards out of the prefetch when a
hosted pre-cast copy replaces them. If that copy failed to load (os error 1455
on Windows in #12860), _te_prequant_pipe_kwargs returned {} and assembly died
on a shard that was never downloaded. Now it falls back only when the dense
weights are on disk, and otherwise raises with what to do next.

Studio: speculative decoding for the MLX inference backend (#13014)

* feat(studio): speculative decoding for explicit MLX modes

An MLX load with an explicit speculative_type (mtp, dflash, dspark, eagle3, ngram, or <kind>+ngram) now loads through mlx-vlm, resolves a drafter (a named spec_draft_model, then a model's built-in MTP head, then cached companions of that kind), prices it into the memory fit, and decodes eligible single replies speculatively through unsloth-zoo's speculative engine. auto, off and an absent setting leave MLX loads unchanged.

Such loads serve replies one at a time: the resident and fixed batches decline them. Requests with tools, logits processors, penalties or video, diffusion models, and models whose forward threads encoder state (Mllama, Florence2, Nemotron Parse) decode as before. A drafter that does not fit, does not build, or is of another kind is passed over with a spec_fallback_reason rather than substituted silently; n-gram copies stand in when the mode allows them.

/estimate-memory prices the drafter the load would attach, /load and /status report spec_drafter_kind and spec_fallback_reason, generation timings report draft_n and draft_n_accepted, and an identical reload is reused only when the speculative settings match.

* feat(studio): speculative batches and auto mode for MLX

A load with a drafter now serves its resident batch and its fixed n>1 batch through the unsloth-zoo speculative BatchStream instead of declining them; the fixed batch uses the resident session because stream_batch has no speculative mode, and it requires what that session requires. Every row reports its draft_n and draft_n_accepted, including rows withdrawn by a cancel or a stop sequence.

Auto (and an absent speculative_type) attaches a built-in MTP head or a cached assistant drafter on loads that already go through mlx-vlm, only when the drafter-inclusive fit equals the fit without it. Span companions (DFlash, DSpark, EAGLE-3) stay explicit-only, since they slow concurrent replies; auto reports auto_span_drafter when one is cached and nothing attaches, auto_context_cost when a priced drafter would shrink the context, and no reason for refusals or unpriceable fits. /estimate-memory mirrors the same choice.

* feat(studio): MLX speculative settings in saved per-model config

The server-side per-model settings that API auto-switch loads read now accept the MLX modes (eagle3 and each drafter kind with n-gram copying), keep draft tokens for them, and store an optional spec_draft_model (a repo id or local path) under any mode that loads a drafter, auto included. The settings save route carries a stored drafter over for clients that do not send it (mirrors_spec_draft_model), matching the tuning and reasoning groups. A GGUF load drops MLX-only modes with their draft tokens and never receives the drafter, so its launch flags behave as before. Status and load responses report spec_draft_model (None on GGUF).

* feat(studio): resolve MLX speculative settings and carry the drafter in the frontend

MLX loads now read the standing speculative preference through a resolver: a model's own choice always wins, while the standing preference (written by GGUF loads) reaches MLX with its ngram read as auto, and MLX loads never write it. An MLX model's explicit Auto is kept in its per-model config; GGUF saves still store Auto as "follow the standing preference".

The per-model config gains an optional companion drafter (specDraftModel), kept only with a drafter mode. It flows through the server-side saved settings (with mirrors_spec_draft_model so a save can clear it), the runtime store, the load echo, status hydration, rollback, the memory estimate and the visible-runtime restore. MLX loads send it, and only a same-model reload without a staged config reuses the resident's speculative settings; every other MLX load takes the drafter from that model's config and falls back to the standing preference, never to another model's live settings.

The resident-reuse match now compares an MLX resident's mode, draft depth and drafter, and llama.cpp's retry arms no longer apply to MLX.

* feat(studio): MLX speculative decoding control and fallback notice

An MLX model's advanced settings now offer Speculative Decoding with the MLX modes (Auto, MTP, DFlash, DSpark, EAGLE-3, Ngram, each drafter kind with +Ngram, Off), a Draft Tokens limit and an optional Drafter (a cached repo id or a local folder) for the modes that read them. Left unset, the control shows the mode the load would send; a draft-token or drafter edit made while unset pins that mode, since storage keeps either value only beside a mode that reads it. The editor re-seeds when the live drafter changes.

When an MLX load reports a speculative fallback reason, the chat run settings show why and what can be tried. Each message states only what every backend path behind its code implies, and names what runs instead, since a reason can describe a drafter passed over while another attached. The GGUF control and notice are unchanged.

* feat(studio): let MLX auto speculation attach every cached drafter kind in preference order

* feat(studio): make MLX Draft Tokens exact within the drafter's trained depth

* docs(studio): describe exact MLX Draft Tokens as drafting every step

* feat(studio): seven MLX speculative modes, every drafter kind with n-gram copies

An MLX load now runs seven modes: auto, mtp, dflash, dspark, eagle3, ngram and off, and the MLX speculative control offers exactly those. Every drafter kind also copies repeated text from the prompt and reply, as auto already did; the draft controller picks copy, draft or plain decoding per round on measured throughput, so a copy is only used where it is expected to be faster. Measured on Qwen3.5 0.8B (MTP head), 4B (DFlash), LFM2.5 (DSpark), Gemma 4 26B (EAGLE-3) and Qwen3.8 27B (DFlash2, DSpark, MTP), copies were neutral or faster on chat and repetitive prompts.

`<kind>+ngram` is no longer a mode but stays an accepted spelling of its kind: an MLX load reads it as the kind and reports the kind, saved overrides keep it, and the resident-model comparison and the MLX control read it as its kind, so it neither reloads on every pick nor shows an empty control. GGUF keeps `mtp+ngram` as its own llama.cpp mode. An explicit kind whose drafter does not attach now drafts with copies alone and reports why, as the `+ngram` modes did. The Auto descriptions now say it attaches the first cached drafter in preference order (DFlash2, DSpark, DFlash, EAGLE-3, then an MTP head or assistant).

* feat(studio): keep the MLX speculative draft on replies with penalties or a logit bias

A reply with a repetition, presence or frequency penalty or a logit bias decoded without the draft, and model families whose recommended sampling includes a penalty (Qwen3.5, 3.6, 3.8) therefore never drafted by default. Those processors now declare that they read only the history, the single path hands them to the draft and passes a repetition penalty as a processor rather than mlx-vlm's shortcut when a draft is attached. Grammar-constrained replies, tool turns, video and diffusion models decode without the draft as before.

* feat(studio): MLX Auto prefers an MTP drafter, then DFlash, DSpark and EAGLE-3

Auto tried cached companions in the order DFlash2, DSpark, DFlash, EAGLE-3 and an MTP head or assistant last. It now tries the built-in MTP head, an MTP companion, then DFlash2, DFlash, DSpark and EAGLE-3; the built-in head goes first whether or not an MTP companion is cached.

* refactor(studio): drop the <kind>+ngram speculative spellings that never shipped

dspark+ngram, dflash+ngram and eagle3+ngram were introduced and then aliased to their kind within this unreleased work, so nothing can have stored or sent them. mtp+ngram stays: it is a llama.cpp mode, and an MLX load reads it as mtp.

* feat(studio): pick the MLX drafter from the cached drafters of the model

The Drafter setting was a free-text field. POST /api/inference/mlx-drafters lists the cached drafters that match a target, with the matching the load uses and filtered to what the account may see, and the settings page offers them in a dropdown: every kind under Auto, else the chosen mode's kind. A saved value that is not listed stays selectable. spec_draft_model itself still accepts any cached repo or local folder.

* feat(studio): match cached MLX drafters by config shape and weights instead of repo name

A cached drafter was paired with a model when their repo-name stems were equal and their vocabularies agreed. That listed repos holding only a config, missed models whose names carry extra words (UD, OptiQ, abliterated), and checked nothing else about the architecture.

A drafter is now a candidate when it has weights and its config fits the model: the hidden size it consumes, the layers it taps or states, the vocabulary, and for a separate MTP head the layer count and text model type. A dimension either side does not state cannot refuse. The name only ranks: a drafter whose name is a prefix of the model's is what Auto attaches, and the rest are offered in the picker as "same architecture", since two generations of one architecture (Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B) have identical shapes and Auto must not attach the other one's drafter silently.

* fix(studio): serve a queued MLX command or stop within a token on a speculative load

A speculative step can span a whole window of tokens. The worker now tells the batch when a command or stop is waiting so the step ends early, and reads the step's tokens as they are decoded so a streamed reply no longer arrives in bursts. A row that stops itself mid-step ends the step and leaves the batch after it.

* Never treat a checkpoint carrying its own model module as an MLX drafter

mlx-vlm imports a config's model_file when it loads a drafter, so a cached
companion declaring one would run its own code on an Auto load or a memory
estimate without the remote-code approval the target needs.

Save already folds GGUF Auto to the standing preference; hydration wrote it as

* feat(decision): train and predict MLX Clef models on rows with images

A decision row's `images` (PIL images, data URLs, or the bytes / path dicts of an undecoded image column) reach the MLX Clef trainer, and `FastDecisionModel.predict` takes `images` for a Clef. point. Run the pre_patch check in a subprocess so the swapped Llama classes
do not leak into later tests.

Load Whisper in FastModel without auto_model (#13080)

* Load Whisper and other speech seq2seq models in FastModel without auto_model

* Expose AutoModelForSpeechSeq2Seq to the processor selection test harness

* Forward trust_remote_code from the speech seq2seq class probe

Fix TRL PPOTrainer under Unsloth: rollout crash, sampling filters and left padding (#13108)

* Fix TRL PPOTrainer rollouts under Unsloth

PPOTrainer generates through a PolicyAndValueWrapper, which has no
generate() and, before TRL 0.26, no gradient_checkpointing_disable(), so
Unsloth's unwrap_model_for_generation crashed on the first rollout. Also
reset sampling filters the model's generation_config would otherwise
copy over TRL's rollout config (Qwen3 Instruct ships top_p = 0.8), which
biased PPO's KL and importance ratio.

* Free PPO rollout generation logits once scored

* Keep the attention mask in PPO training forwards

Unsloth's training forward drops the attention mask because it assumes
right padding, but TRL's PPO left-pads every query, so policy, reference
and value forwards attended to the pads while rollouts did not. PPO
training now opts those models into keeping the mask.

* Rebind unwrap_model_for_generation in trl.experimental.ppo

TRL >= 0.29 keeps PPOTrainer only under trl.experimental.ppo, which
PatchRL's trl.trainer walk never sees, so PPO there kept TRL's own unwrap
and crashed on PolicyAndValueWrapper.gradient_checkpointing_disable.

* Scope PPO full-distribution sampling to rollout generate calls

Instead of resetting a list of filters on the policy's generation_config
for the whole of train(), PPO rollout generate calls now pass
use_model_defaults=False with a copy of TRL's config, taking only token
ids from the model. Every inherited sampling field is dropped, and the
model's generation_config (and so any checkpoint saved mid-train) is
never modified.

* Shorten PPO patch comments

Fix beam search on the fast decode path (#13053)

num_beams > 1 crashed because Unsloth's decode returns a tuple cache with
no reorder method. Add _reorder_cache, which reorders each attention's
paged K/V buffer in place, since the next decode step reads the buffer and
not the returned tuples.
Fix PPOTrainer with an Unsloth policy: wrapper GC toggles, policy generate, RoPE on value / reward models (#13067)

Let GPTQ checkpoints train and generate with LoRA (#13068)

* Let GPTQ checkpoints train and generate with LoRA

GPTQ linears keep a packed qweight and no dense .weight, so get_peft_model
crashed reading the base dtype, the fused LoRA kernels and the decode fast
path read .weight, and gptqmodel's default Marlin / ExLlama kernels refuse
model.train(). Skip the fused kernels and the decode fast path for packed
bases (PEFT's GPTQ LoRA forward runs instead) and load GPTQ checkpoints with
gptqmodel's auto_trainable backend unless the caller passes a
quantization_config or vLLM loads the weights.

* Pick the trainable GPTQ kernel after FastModel rebuilds the checkpoint config

FastBaseModel.from_pretrained rebuilds kwargs['quantization_config'] from the
checkpoint for pre-quantized models, which replaced the auto_trainable request
and left FastModel on Marlin, failing model.train().
Fix LLaVA image token count when processor_config lacks num_additional_image_tokens (#13091)

Keep paged bitsandbytes optimizer state paged on checkpoint resume (#13092)

* Keep paged bitsandbytes optimizer state paged on checkpoint resume

Optimizer8bit.load_state_dict moves state1/state2 into plain CUDA memory, so a
resumed paged_adamw_* run holds the optimizer state in the CUDA allocator through
the first forward and backward, where a fresh run keeps it in paged memory that
can spill to CPU. Resuming then OOMs on a GPU where the fresh run fit (#2168).
Re-allocate the loaded state through get_state_buffer right after the load.

* Give the CUDA skip an explicit reason

* Stage the resume load on the host and re-page AdEMAMix's doubled state

Load paged optimizer state without moving state1/state2 to CUDA first, so a
state larger than free VRAM still resumes, and copy AdEMAMix's (2, *shape)
state1 into its doubled paged buffer. The test no longer requires unpatched
bitsandbytes to stay broken.

* Re-page loaded state even when it still carries is_paged

torch.save keeps a tensor's Python attributes, so a host copy of paged state
loaded from a checkpoint still has is_paged=True. Skipping on it left that
state as ordinary host memory, which bitsandbytes then prefetches as managed
memory (cudaMemPrefetchAsync invalid argument on a Colab L4). The test now
checks GlobalPageManager membership and device placement instead of the flag.

Turn torch.compile off on GPUs older than Volta (#13085)

* Turn torch.compile off on GPUs older than Volta

Inductor raises GPUTooOldForTriton on compute capability < 7.0, so GRPO,
vision and MoE training died on the first compiled call on GTX 10xx,
P100 and Maxwell cards. Unsloth's own Triton kernels still run there, so
train eagerly: set the compile switches and torch._dynamo.config.disable,
which also covers regions unsloth_zoo wrapped before this module ran.

* Pre-Volta: make the compile disable reach autograd threads; skip vLLM requirement

torch >= 2.12 keeps torch._dynamo.config writes per thread, and this runs
before _gpu_init mirrors config writes, so backward (checkpoint recompute)
on autograd worker threads still compiled and hit GPUTooOldForTriton. Set
the process-wide default too.

FastLanguageModel now drops fast_inference on compute capability < 7 before
demanding vLLM, as FastModel does, instead of asking a Pascal user to
install a vLLM that cannot run there.

* Test the pre-Volta thread visibility without importing unsloth

The subprocess imported unsloth, which needs an accelerator, so the CPU
runners failed it; slice the helper with ast instead, which also keeps
_gpu_init's config mirroring from masking a missing fix.
Keep slow tokenizers transformers cannot convert instead of crashing the load (#13073)

Studio: head a decision score with its most likely level (#13111)

* Studio: head a decision score with its most likely level

The Try a decision dialog named the level nearest the expected score, so a
split answer (83% on 0, 17% on 3, expectation 0.50) was headed with level 1,
which the model gave 0.2%. Use the most likely level, falling back to the
nearest when no probabilities came back.

* test(studio): pin a decision score's top level away from the first level and on ties

The split-score case expected level 0, which an implementation returning the first level whenever probabilities exist also satisfies, and nothing covered a tie. Add a mirrored split that must head with level 3 and a flat distribution that must keep the nearest level. Also shorten the comment in scoreLevels and wrap the reduce the way the formatter does.

Fix returned logit scaling and softcapping when labels are provided (#13069)

With UNSLOTH_RETURN_LOGITS=1 and labels supplied, the shared causal LM forward and the Mistral forward returned the raw LM-head logits while the loss and the unlabeled call used scaled and soft-capped ones. Apply the transforms to the returned logits after the loss on every call.

The cross entropy kernel is still handed the raw logits and its transform arguments, so loss and parameter gradients are bit-identical to before. For models with a scale or soft cap, the returned logits are a tensor downstream of the ones the loss read.

fix(chat): import branch threads parents-before-children on refresh (#13113)

* fix(chat): import branch threads parents-before-children on refresh

A branched thread lost its forks on refresh: an edited user message is written
after its reply, so the reply's createdAt predates its user parent, and
assistant-ui's import() throws on a child that precedes its parent.

descendants.

commits.message:
fix(skills-index): stop shipping skills.sh rows that cannot install

The builder shipped ~1.9k skills.sh rows per run with no resolved_github_id.
Most were rows whose repo 404s or whose fully-read tree has no matching
SKILL.md dir (renamed/removed upstream); every client install of one spent
~40 GitHub calls and failed as stale_index.

- fuzzy match ignores both '-' and '_' (pdb-database slug vs pdb_database dir)
- a single-skill repo (root or generic skills/ SKILL.md) resolves like the client does
- repo 404 or complete tree with no match: the row is dropped, counts logged
- truncated tree: bounded contents/<candidate>/SKILL.md probes, row kept if none hit
- transient errors keep the row unresolved, as before
docs(skills): note inline-shell scoping for nested, external_dirs and unreadable-lock cases

fix(skills): keep inline shell off for nested, cross-profile and unreadable-lock community skills

The inline-shell trust gate matched only the exact install dir from the
active profile's hub lock, and a lock read failure fell through to
expansion. So a nested SKILL.md inside a --force community bundle, the
same skill viewed by another profile through skills.external_dirs, and
any skill under a truncated or wrong-shape lock all ran their !`cmd`
snippets on view. Match descendants of community install dirs, also read
the lock that owns the skills tree the dir lives in, and fail closed when
an existing lock cannot be read.

docs(telemetry): v4 takes additive values in place after its stable release

Owner ruling for gateway_pause_failed: extend package schema v4 in place
(additive only; ingest validates the envelope and every shape already sent
stays valid) instead of bumping to v5. The two sentences that said v4 was
extended only while canary-only now say so.

fix(update): say when the syntax preflight is skipped on a slow object fetch; sort gateway_pause_failed

The timed-out cat-file read is caught in target_syntax_error (the preflight) instead of
read_target_files, so the preflight prints one line saying the post-update check still runs;
publish_recovery_closure keeps suppressing the timeout as before.

fix(update): drop config_unreadable: an unreadable config.yaml also hides consent, so no row is ever sent

The exit is real (RuntimeError from require_readable_config_before_write), but the consent gate
reads the same config.yaml and reads it as collection off: a live run on a scratch install with
an unparseable config.yaml wrote no metrics store at all. A closed value nothing can emit only
widens the contract.

fix(update): pre-apply exits that read exception/subprocess_failed name their reason

hermes.update.run rows with apply_mode=unknown still had three exits with no stop_class on main:

- The startup-syntax preflight (update_cmd_commit.read_target_files) runs `git cat-file --batch`
  under a 120 s limit. On a blobless install (install.sh clones --filter=blob:none) every changed
  blob lazily fetches in its own round trip, so a slow link times out and the uncaught
  TimeoutExpired ended the whole update as `subprocess_failed` after 2+ minutes (31 CLI + 23
  Desktop install-days). An unread batch now counts as unread files, which is the preflight's
  documented contract; the post-move syntax check stays the backstop.
- An unreadable/unparseable config.yaml (require_readable_config_before_write RuntimeError) or an
  invalid configured channel name (ChannelError) while picking the channel read `exception`. They
  now record `config_unreadable` (new) / `channel_unresolved`.
- A failed Windows gateway pause (_abort_on_error / ServicePauseFailed RuntimeError) read
  `exception`; it now records `gateway_pause_failed` (new).

Two closed UPDATE_STOP_CLASSES values, the v4 schema enum and the relay-shared-metrics doc row
change together; every legacy value stays valid.

test(gateway): quote the feishu download test's function-local class annotation

Review finding on #135781: `_FakeAsyncClient.__aenter__(self) -> _FakeAsyncClient` lives in a
class defined inside the test body, so the annotation is evaluated before the name is bound and
the test raises NameError on 3.11-3.13 (cannot access free variable '_FakeAsyncClient'). Same
UP037 strip as the rest of this PR; the module-level scanner skipped function bodies. A scan of
every function-local class for a self-referencing annotation finds only this one.

fix: core modules import again on Python 3.11-3.13 (re-quote eager forward references)

#135348 ran ruff's UP037 autofix with ruff.strict.toml's target-version = "py314". On 3.14
annotations are lazy (PEP 649), so stripping quotes is safe there; on 3.11-3.13 a function or
variable annotation is evaluated when the def or statement runs. Every unquoted annotation that
names the enclosing class (`def clone_for_agent(self) -> ContextEngine`), a class bound later in
the module, or a TYPE_CHECKING-only import now raises NameError on import: 300 modules on main
(gateway.config, run_agent, hermes_state, cron.jobs, the Telegram adapter, ...) fail to import
under 3.11, the update path crashes mid-`hermes update` on any install whose interpreter is
older than 3.14, and the e2e-upgrade suite's retry leg fails with
`NameError: name 'ContextEngine' is not defined`.

- Re-quote exactly the 79 annotations (36 files) that name something unbound when they are
  evaluated (including tui_gateway/server.py's `_TurnScopes`, which only reaches that module's
  globals through register() after import); no other text changes.
- agent/turn_scripted_prelude.py: `Generator[...]` gets its third argument back. d76cce4f116
  applied UP043 (default type args, valid only from 3.13) to a module-level alias, so
  `Generator[Y, S]` raises TypeError on 3.11/3.12 and takes gateway.run, agent.conversation_loop
  and tui_gateway.{server,ws,entry} down with it.
- ruff.strict.toml target-version = "py311", the requires-python floor. With it UP037 leaves
  these quotes alone and only strips the two that are genuinely redundant, which this commit
  strips; any future version-gated fix stays valid on every supported Python.
- tests/ci/test_strict_ruff_target.py pins the target to the requires-python floor (red on main).

test(ci): a hung replayed workflow step fails in 30 s instead of hanging the Windows lane

The Windows-only lane killed tests/ci/test_update_ci_routing.py at the
runner's 300 s cap, mid test_replay_rejects_ineffective_required_step, with
no output. workflow_steps._run used subprocess.run(capture_output=True,
timeout=30). On Windows, run() on timeout kills bash and then calls
communicate() with no timeout. Git's bash.exe launcher spawns usr/bin/bash.exe,
which keeps the inherited pipe open, so that read never ends and the
30 s timeout never surfaced.

Capture to files instead of pipes, so the timeout raises and names the step.
A POSIX probe of the same shape (kill the child while a grandchild holds the
pipe) shows the pipe read still blocked after 10 s; the file-backed run
raises at 2 s. On PR #135560, whose diff touches no CI code.

fix(telemetry): the Windows hand-off's relaunched update child also reads its own claim as failed

On Windows the hand-off names the process it created as the marker's delegate, and
hermes_bootstrap's relaunch (subprocess.call) or the legacy .cmd's cmd.exe makes the updater
its child, so the delegate check now also accepts our parent. The docs sentence moves to the
hermes.update.run outcome row and names the checkout-lock case (another mutator holding it).

fix(telemetry): a Desktop hand-off's update refused by its own claim counts as failed

The hand-off quits the Desktop and launches `hermes update` as the marker's
delegate. When the update lock then refuses that claim (the pre-a28a5d03a9f
whole-second creation-time bug on macOS, still present on installs that cannot
pull the fix through the button), no other updater exists: the Desktop shows
"Hermes couldn't finish updating" and the user retries. The metrics row read
outcome `refused`, which the rollup treats as neither attempt nor failure, so
~320 Desktop update failures a fortnight vanished from the failure rate.

Record that one case (marker names this process as its delegate) as `failed`;
a refusal under another update's claim stays `refused`.

fix(skills): inline shell snippets keep blocking community installs

Review of this PR: the inline_shell_exec downgrade assumed the runtime never
expands !`cmd` in a community hub skill. The runtime gate
(agent.skill_preprocessing._is_community_hub_skill) matches only the hub lock
entry's own directory, so a nested SKILL.md inside a community bundle is listed
as its own skill and expands when skills.inline_shell is on; so does the same
skill seen through another profile's external_dirs, or any read with an
unreadable lock. With the downgrade, such a bundle installed without --force.

inline_shell_exec stays high for community installs. The sudo/bind-all doc
notes and every other rule change are unchanged. Corpus cost: 4 of the 33
skills this PR made installable stay blocked (index 83 -> 71 instead of 68).
chore: map Awshesh12's commit email for the #127414 salvage

fix(skills): decoded archives and curl | sudo bash stay flagged after the doc relaxations

The A/B over the index sample showed two shapes the earlier relaxations let through:
base64 -d into tar (an embedded payload the scanner never sees) and
curl ... | sudo -E bash (base never matched it; sudo_usage in Markdown was the only
finding). Both now fire.

fix(skills): legitimate hub skills no longer trip Skills Guard false positives

A random sample of our own hermes-index blocked ~15% of third-party skills; most
blocks were pattern precision bugs, not threats:

- provider token shapes (AKIA, ghp_, github_pat_, sk-, sk-ant-, glpat-, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY)
  are scoped case-sensitive: the table compiles with IGNORECASE, so `[0-9A-Z]{16}`
  matched the placeholder `AKIAxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx`
- destructive_root_rm exempts the Dockerfile package-cache cleanup
  (/var/lib/apt/lists, /var/cache/{apt,apk,yum,dnf}); traversal out of them, a later
  `/` or `/etc` operand, and `--no-preserve-root /` still fire
- base64_decode_pipe fires when the decoded bytes reach an interpreter at any later
  stage (or inside eval/source), not on `| jq` / `| grep`; plugin_guard's
  is_data_decode step-down is now redundant and is removed (it also stepped down
  `base64 -d x | sh | grep`)
- html_comment_injection needs injection phrasing, not a bare ignore/system/hidden
- setuid_setgid is critical only in executing shapes (set*id( call, cap_set[ug]id,
  chmod u+s / 4755); the bare word is a medium note
- deception_hide's guidance exemption covers diagnosis/diagnostic (diagnos\w*)
- community scans: inline_shell_exec is informational (preprocess_skill_content never
  expands it for a community hub lock entry), and sudo_usage / bind_all_interfaces in
  Markdown docs are notes; scripts keep full severity

SCANNER_VERSION bumps to skills-guard-v9 so cached verdicts rescan.

guards: base64_decode_pipe sees file/openssl decodes and every pipe stage

skills_guard's base64_decode_pipe required the pipe right after the
flag, so `base64 -d payload.b64 | sh`, `base64 --decode < p | bash`,
`base64 -di p | python3` and `openssl base64 -d | sh` produced no
finding. plugin_guard's is_data_decode stepped the finding down to
medium when the FIRST consumer was not an interpreter, so
`base64 -d | gunzip | sh` scored like a data decode into grep.

Widen the pattern to those decode forms (not `||`), and have
is_data_decode read the decode off that same pattern and require every
later pipe stage to be a non-interpreter.

fix(skills-guard): make the AWS key pattern case-sensitive

AWS access key IDs are all-caps by spec, but THREAT_PATTERNS compiles
with re.IGNORECASE, so a case-folded AKIA+16 byte collision inside a
base64-encoded asset fired one unoverridable critical and hard-blocked
the whole plugin install (#132155). Scope the pattern case-sensitive
with an inline (?-i:...) group — same technique as the hardcoded_secret
carve-out (#116221).

fix(skills): curl needs an operand before the pipe-to-interpreter rules

The bare phrase `curl | sh` in documentation prose scored critical, and a
critical on a community source is a dangerous verdict that --force cannot
override, so a skill whose docs name the install method could not be installed
at all. curl with no URL fetches nothing and a real download-and-execute names
its source, so requiring one non-pipe character after the command costs no
coverage. `curl_pipe_python` carried the same optional-operand prefix.

Both scanner versions bump because cached verdicts are keyed on them: without
the bump an already-scanned skill or plugin keeps its dangerous verdict and
stays blocked.

feat(desktop): drop the "This could run on your computer" strip above the composer

The local-setup card appeared above the input after the first finished turn
on any machine whose catalog recommends a local model, and stayed across
relaunches until dismissed. It read as a nag on every new session.

The offer keeps its quiet homes: the "Run locally" row at the top of the
model menu (until setup completes) and the handoff tour's model-pill step.
The card's state machine (armed/shown/dismissed, the message.complete hook,
the menu-open request) existed only for the card, so it goes with it; the
store keeps the eligibility read both remaining surfaces use.

fix(skills): review fixes — raw fetch falls back on DNS block, restore never writes through links or over user files

- _fetch_file_bytes: a DNS-poisoned / NXDOMAIN raw.githubusercontent.com raises
  SSRFConnectionBlocked (a ValueError), which escaped the httpx.HTTPError suppress and
  failed the install before the Contents API fallback. Any transport failure on the raw
  attempt now falls back, and latches raw unusable on the source so a dropping firewall
  costs one 15 s timeout, not one per file.
- ensure_bundled_skill: a leftover dest is refused if any entry in it is a symlink or
  junction (copytree with dirs_exist_ok followed them out of skills/), and only missing
  files are copied (a user-edited file was overwritten). The canonical-path "present"
  check also requires the SKILL.md frontmatter name to match; a dir holding another
  skill's SKILL.md is refused, as on main.
- Docstring: a restore over leftover user files reads as user-modified, so update keeps it.

fix(skills): hub installs download skill files from raw.githubusercontent.com, not one API call per file

`hermes-index rate_limited` (26 events / 9 installs in 14 days): GitHubSource.fetch
paid one Contents API call per file in the skill folder on top of repo + tree,
so an anonymous user (60/h) could never install a skill with ~58+ files and
four average skills drained the hour. Live on origin/main, anonymous:
skills-sh/remotion-dev/skills/remotion-best-practices cost 143 API calls and
failed rate_limited.

A file fetch pinned to the tree's commit sha now reads
raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<sha>/<path> first: the same immutable bytes,
outside the REST limit. A raw miss (private repo, raw outage) falls back to the
Contents API as before. The same install now costs 2 API calls and succeeds
anonymously; anthropics/skills/pdf drops from 16 to 2.

fix(skills): restoring a built-in skill no longer fails on leftovers, and a failed restore is recorded as bundled

Post-fix telemetry still showed `hermes skills install llm-wiki` failing as
failure_class=filesystem_error, source=hub. Two restore paths failed for good:

- A skill dir left behind without its SKILL.md (a manual delete that kept user
  files, or a copy that died partway) made copytree raise EEXIST on every retry.
  The restore now copies around the leftovers (dirs_exist_ok); a dir with no
  SKILL.md is no skill, and user files in it are kept.
- A skill present behind a symlinked category (which the loader follows, so it
  works) was missed by the rglob scan, so the restore ran into the containment
  guard and failed. The canonical SKILL.md now counts as present.

A restore that still fails (read-only dir, a symlinked category with the skill
missing) was recorded as source=hub, because the failed exit returned no bundle
and _record_skill_install fell back to "hub". The bundled branch now marks the
attempt origin=bundled, so every bundled-path outcome, raised or returned,
records source=bundled.

fix(desktop): make mermaid SVG well-formed via the HTML parser, not a void-tag regex The void-tag pass from the previous commit fixes `

Such a label still decodes to a broken image. mermaid.render() returns the HTML serialisation of the diagram, so parse it with the HTML parser it was written for and re-serialise it with XMLSerializer. That fixes the whole class at once. Against mermaid 11.16 in Chromium, across flowchart, class, state, ER, mindmap, block, kanban, sequence, journey, gantt, pie, timeline, gitGraph, quadrant and xychart output, the round-trip yields the same element tree and image size as the regex wherever the regex output is valid XML, and also loads the non-breaking-space cases the regex leaves broken. Drop a label's plain `xmlns` attribute before serialising: the serializer declares the namespace itself, and a spec-conformant one (jsdom) writes both, a duplicate attribute. The tests' fixtures put `
` directly in SVG , which mermaid never emits; replace them with the real 11.16 label shape (XHTML in a ) and assert the label keeps its line break and its non-breaking space. Refs #133089, #134031

fix(tui_gateway): a settled client-gone interrupt beats the wakeup-schedule exemption

An interrupted detached turn sets the client-gone and turn-cancel latches. If
the active /loop or /heartbeat then re-armed the orphan timer after the turn
settled, neither latch ever cleared: no tick could claim the turn and every
reattach was refused with 4009, so the loop never reached its budget and the
session stayed pinned. Collect the settled session as before instead.

Also: TTL eviction checks the cheap clock before the store-reading exemptions,
and the heartbeat branch gets its own reaper tests (active local pins; paused,
cleared or gateway-owned releases).
docs(loops): soften backend-lifetime wording

fix(tui_gateway): keep a detached session alive while it owns an active /loop or /heartbeat

The per-session notification poller is the only driver of a Desktop/TUI
(route-less) /loop or /heartbeat. When the client disconnects, the WS-orphan
reaper collects the idle session ~20s later and the TTL/LRU reapers can
collect it after that; either stops the poller, so the schedule freezes
(status still 'active') until a client reattaches and the overdue tick fires.

Treat an active, non-gateway-routed loop or heartbeat like live delegated
work: the orphan reap re-arms instead of popping the session, and the TTL and
session-cap reapers skip it. Gateway-routed schedules are fired by the
gateway's own scanner and do not pin the session. The exemption is bounded by
the loop's tick budget and ends on stop/pause. Memory-trim quiescence is
unchanged: an idle looping session does not block a trim.

fix(update): a Desktop-only Node dependency failure no longer blocks the TUI and web UI

Every source update installs Node dependencies as one npm ci over ui-tui,
web and, when a built desktop app is present, apps/desktop. Only
apps/desktop brings native addons (node-pty, electron), so a host whose
compiler cannot build them (Ubuntu 20.04's g++ 9 rejects -std=gnu++20)
failed the whole install and lost the TUI and web UI builds as well, with
"a source update could not be finished automatically" on every launch.

When the union fails and the desktop app is part of it, retry once without
apps/desktop: the TUI and web UI build, the desktop build is reported owed
("desktop dependencies failed", the line the hand-off scripts match), and
the update names `hermes uninstall --gui` for hosts that never run the
app. The same hint prints whenever a headless Linux update builds Desktop,
since such a host keeps rebuilding an app nobody launches.

fix(memory): keep a runaway-recall ceiling when prefetch spilling is off

Without the opt-in, external recall is kept whole up to
max(10 x hooks.output_spill.max_chars, 100k chars) and still spills above
that, so one runaway provider can't overflow the context window and wedge
the session. Normal provider-budgeted recall (~16 KB for Honcho) is
unaffected.

hermes gateway restart --all (and status, cron's gateway check, the update

fix(plugins): a linked plugins/<name> slot reads "already installed", not a bad manifest

A memory provider's own installer (mnemosyne-hermes install, its README's

fix(memory): a failed agent-start provider install is not retried by every process start

recover_at_startup tried the configured provider's catalog install once per
PROCESS, so a home whose install fails (PM resolve/clone error, offline) retried

hindsight logged 1048 failures over 204 failing install-days (~5 per day per
install, the retry-loop shape) after it left core.

The left-core migration already had the fix: a failure stamp under

retries. Move that stamp into memory_provider_migration and use it in

fix(mcp): a failed OAuth catalog install from a card or the agent says why, instead of `exception`

The connection-card / manage_connections install of an OAuth catalog entry runs the probe on a
worker thread; `mcp_oauth.start` then rebuilt the worker's error as a bare RuntimeError from its
text, dropping the `failure_class` `_probe_single_server` had tagged. Every pre-authorization
failure (empty or schemeless URL, unreachable host, 404 endpoint, refused client registration)
was recorded as `exception:RuntimeError` -> `exception`.

- run_worker classifies the original exception with probe_failure_class and stores the class on
  the flow; start() re-tags the RuntimeError it raises with it.
- probe_failure_class reads InvalidMcpUrlError (not http(s)://host) as config_invalid.
- _require_rendered_remote tags an unset ${VAR} in url/headers as missing_credentials.
- the "server responded but no token" refusal is auth_required.
- a connect_failed message that does not name the server gets a one-line next step
  ("Could not connect to 'n8n-official' (Not Found). Check its URL ...").

n8n-official is the only catalog entry whose URL is a user-supplied `${VAR}`, so it is the only
one where these user-side errors happen before authorization.

test: keep the two first-run routing invariants

The blank-install pair is the regression contract: --tui reaches the
TUI, --cli still gets the classic guard. The configured-path cases only
restated existing behaviour.

fix(cli): blank-install TUI reaches its own setup screen (#128663)

`cmd_chat` ran the classic first-run guard ("Run setup now? [Y/n]") before
the TUI launched, so `hermes --tui` on an unconfigured install never showed
the Ink "Setup Required" screen. Since 7a06cb50d7 the one-time
shared-metrics offer also runs ahead of the TUI on that path. Both block
the installed-bundle `tui_smoke`, which has failed every termux-deb build
since the keyless-provider removal.

The classic guard now fronts only the classic CLI, and the shared-metrics
offer waits until a provider is configured; it stays undecided, so it is
still asked once on the first configured launch.

fix(release): treat any missing stable baseline as no upgrade arm

A release that skipped bundles never writes the stable baseline pointer,
so its absence is normal at any point, not only before the first bundle
release. Drop the final-tag scan. A 404 on the default pointer now always
plans no upgrade arm. A supplied baseline-manifest that does not exist
still blocks, because that is a bad input.

test(install/macos): poll app quit through the run loop

NSRunningApplication.terminated changes only when the run loop runs.
JXA delay() does not run it, so the check stayed false after the app
quit and the leg failed when the setup app had launched Hermes. Spin
the run loop while waiting. The quit stays the normal one.

fix(pm): use the pinned mirror when the upstream host does not resolve

A macOS release leg could not resolve ffmpeg.martin-riedl.de, and PM
stopped there. A name lookup failure is not a retry case, but the R2
mirror is a different host and the pinned SHA256 still checks the bytes.
Let that failure fall through to the mirror.

fix(release): let the first bundle release pass without an upgrade baseline

No stable release has shipped signed packages yet. Every final tag so far
skipped bundles or predates the claim pipeline. So
releases/stable/release-candidates.json does not exist, and the three
"Pin actual OLD and NEW signed packages" jobs refused with "No published
stable package baseline".

transitions now treats a 404 as a first release only when no final stable
tag records a candidate manifest and no baseline-manifest input was given.
It still validates the receipt, emits empty matrices and baseline=none.
The packaged upgrade arms skip on that output. The gate accepts their skip
only when their own planner succeeded with baseline=none, so a missing
baseline after a real bundle release still blocks.

fix(pm): re-seed the uv cache when an update ships a new lock

uv_cache_dir() wrote a bare ".seeded" marker after the first seed and
never compared against the payload again, so an updated install never
received the new payload's wheels. Enabling a plugin re-resolves without
--offline, so uv fetched the new pins from PyPI instead; for
cryptography 50.0.1 on Windows ARM64, which has no wheel on PyPI, that
is an sdist Rust build.

The marker now records the running uv.lock's digest, so the first call
under a new lock merges the new payload into the existing cache.

fix(pm): finish a partial uv cache seed instead of marking it complete

uv_cache_dir() copies a sealed payload's uv-cache into the machine cache and
writes .seeded only after a clean copy. The retry after a failed or killed
copy skipped every top-level entry that already existed, so the copy that had
created archive-v0/ but not finished it was recorded as complete. uv then
fails on the unfinished bucket, e.g. "The wheel is invalid: Missing
.dist-info directory".

The retry now merges into the existing tree (dirs_exist_ok) and copies each
file that is missing or whose size differs from the payload's, leaving
finished files alone.

fix(local-models): recommend nothing when no model reaches the speed floor

When no resident model cleared 20 tok/s, the resolver still recommended the
fastest one (fastest-resident). A "32 GB" machine without a discrete GPU reads
31.5 GB, where only the 27B fits, at a predicted 13 tok/s, so CPU-only and
integrated-GPU machines were steered to a slow dense model. Those machines now
get no recommendation, and every fitting model stays one click away in Browse.
The no-recommendation copy now says the model must run at full speed, the user
guide states the rule, and the unused fastest-resident tooltip string is gone
from every locale.

fix(local-models): size a Windows integrated GPU from what Windows lets it allocate

With no nvidia-smi answer and no discrete engine device, probe_budget budgeted
all of RAM as unified memory. Windows caps an integrated GPU at its GPU memory
(DXGI dedicated plus shared, Task Manager's figure): an Arc B390 on a 31.5 GB
machine gets 18 GB, yet Local Models showed 31.5 GB and priced the 27B as
fitting. The pool is now capped at that figure, read through DXGI for the
adapter the engine named, else the only non-NVIDIA adapter when a Vulkan or HIP
engine will run the model. The CPU engine keeps the RAM budget, whether the
user chose it or it is the only build for the machine (a Snapdragon). The
engine's own number would overshoot: ggml-vulkan sums every heap of an
integrated GPU, host-visible ones included. The DXGI reader is a cached host
fact in hermes_platform. The cap only lowers the pool; CPU-only machines,
other platforms and a failed DXGI read keep the RAM figure.

fix(desktop): offer local setup only for the recommended model

The composer's "This could run on your computer" card took the recommended
catalog row, else the first row marked `fits`. A row fits when any build runs,
including one spilled to system RAM, so a GTX 1080 with 16 GB of RAM was
offered the 27B, which the resolver never recommends there. The card now names
the recommended model, and a machine without one gets no card.

ci(desktop): re-smoke an already-built package without rebuilding it

The native smoke only ran inside desktop-bundled-release, and it checked out
its test scripts at the same commit as the artifact it fetched. Changing a
test therefore meant a new commit, and a new commit meant a full signed
build (about an hour per platform) just to rerun the smoke.

Add workflow_dispatch: `sha` picks the staged artifact to fetch, and the
scripts come from the ref the dispatch runs on. Release callers are
unchanged.

test(desktop): the MSIX plugin smoke runs with a user's environment, not the CI driver's

The smoke's CLI inherited the driver's HERMES_HOME / HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR /
HERMES_PYTHON, so PM built the plugin's environment on the driver's own
Python under C:\a\_temp\setup-pm and never touched the packaged
interpreter: the bug could not show. Clear HERMES_*/UV_*/PYTHON* and the
driver's tool dirs from PATH in the basic-user batch, and fail if the
install log still names the driver's PM home.

fix(pm): MSIX plugin installs build on a writable copy of the bundled Python (#135236)

Enabling a plugin with Python dependencies, and `hermes pm install`, failed
in the packaged Windows app: uv lock/sync/pip check exit 101 with "Unable to
create process using ...\venv\Scripts\python.exe".

uv queries a venv by running its Scripts\python.exe. That redirector lives
outside the package and CreateProcess's the interpreter named by
pyvenv.cfg `home`. 6a031bf1b3f moved generations onto the packaged
interpreter, so `home` names a file under WindowsApps that a process without
package identity may not start (exit 101 is the redirector's
RC_CREATE_PROCESS). Restore the verified writable copy of the pinned Python
in the user store as the build interpreter for sealed Windows payloads.

venv_command (also from 6a031bf1b3f) stays: Hermes still enters those venvs
on the packaged interpreter, so its own children keep package access to the
bundled git, rg and PM worker.

test(desktop): the Windows MSIX smoke installs a plugin with Python deps as a basic user

The installed-package smoke only chatted, so nothing exercised PM building
a dependency generation inside the package. After the chat it now installs
a local plugin that declares a Python dependency through the package's CLI
execution alias with --enable --yes-deps and requires `plugins list` to show
it enabled.

It runs under a Safer NORMALUSER token at medium integrity: GitHub runners
are administrators, and Administrators can start files in a package
directory without package identity, which a normal user cannot. A probe
that the token is refused the packaged python.exe keeps the check honest.

fix(tests): the test runner kills detached processes a test leaves behind

`_kill_tree` SIGKILLs the per-file pytest process group, which misses any
child that left the group with `start_new_session=True` (an auto-started
`gateway run`, a setsid server). Those are reparented to init and run
forever: one host accumulated 215 orphan gateways (~52 GB RSS, up to 21 h
old), and every `hermes update` listed each as "another Hermes home — left
alone".

After every attempt the runner now SIGKILLs any process whose environment
still points into that attempt's unique temp root (PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT /
TMPDIR, or a HOME / HERMES_HOME a fixture created under it). The root is
unique per attempt, so the match names only that attempt's processes.
Linux-only (/proc); the process-group kill stays the fallback elsewhere.

ci: E2E suites run only on release builds

Pull requests and pushes to main no longer run any E2E suite: ci.yaml's detect gate
forces every e2e* lane off unless the run is a stable-release run (inputs.release) or a
manual dispatch, whatever the diff, the update-path classifier or the run-e2e label
selects. That covers the Python e2e and e2e-upgrade jobs, the Windows E2E and Windows
install + update journey in tests-os, and the Desktop core/update suites.

install-e2e.yml drops its pull_request (path-filtered `pr` route) and 12-hourly
schedule triggers; it runs from the stable-release gate (workflow_call) or by dispatch.
live-providers drops its nightly schedule and keeps the release-tag push + dispatch.

Why: a one-row change to left_core_migration.py held a PR for 40 minutes on the
Windows install + update E2E; the suites cost most of the larger-runner minutes and
the release gate already runs all of them strictly.

Arm the dark fast path only when the previous shot fired at the limit

clearWaitFlags() also runs after bright shots and from preview restore, so it
re-armed the since-last-shot flag even when the scene had just changed. Arm
it only where a wait ends in a capture, and only if that frame reported
FLASH_REQUIRED; any other AE state since then still clears it.

Keep the normal wait for dark shots taken right after a light change

Only take the FLASH_REQUIRED fast path when every repeating frame since the
previous shot reported FLASH_REQUIRED, i.e. the scene stayed at the exposure
limit. If the light changed in between (any CONVERGED/SEARCHING frame, even
while idle between shots), the next dark shot keeps today's wait. On-device,
back-to-back dark shots in a steady scene reported FLASH_REQUIRED on every
frame between shots, so they keep the speed-up.

feat(api,cli): POST /v1/feedback and a kortix feedback CLI command (KRTX-1646) (#9389)

## Review in 60 seconds

- `POST /v1/feedback` — one authenticated route that persists structured
feedback (`source: cli|agent|web`, `kind: bug|idea|friction`, `message`
≤ 4000 chars, up to 8 optional context ids) into a new append-only
`kortix.feedback` table, and returns the stored receipt. Unauthenticated
calls get 401; a per-user token bucket (`KORTIX_FEEDBACK_REQS_PER_MIN`,
default 10/min) returns 429 with `Retry-After` and an audit row.
- `kortix feedback "<message>" [--kind …] [--source …] [--context
<json>] [--json]` — a thin CLI command that files feedback through the
same route. Inside a Kortix session it files `source: agent` and merges
the session and project ids into the context automatically; outside it
files `source: cli`. It prints the stored receipt (or the raw JSON with
`--json`).
- Minimal by construction: one table, one route, one command — plus the
repo gates each change requires (drizzle snapshot + node-pg-migrate
file, audit route label, route manifest + coverage flow, CLI docs row,
MCP CLI-command allowlist decision).

No demo video: code-only change

**Risk:** low — purely additive (one new table, one new route, one new
command). No existing route, default or export changes; rollback is
`DROP TABLE kortix.feedback` plus a revert.

**Verified:** final full `pnpm test` on the committed tree (head
`06bc88570c`, includes dev's apps and notification merges) → exit 0,
attestation written green
(`{"core":"pass","packages":"pass","db-suites":"pass"}`) and committed;
`pnpm test:verify --rev 06bc88570c --branch krtx-1646-feedback` →
`[attest] OK green` (exit 0). Lane evidence below in `## How was this
tested?

Final-cycle re-verification (this session, head `06bc88570c`):
```
$ cd apps/cli && bun test --isolate src/commands/feedback.test.ts
Ran 6 tests across 1 file. [95.00ms]   0 fail · 10 expect() calls
$ cd apps/api && bun test --isolate --env-file=scripts/test.env src/feedback/index.test.ts src/feedback/rate-limit.test.ts
Ran 9 tests across 2 files. [712.00ms]   0 fail · 43 expect() calls
$ bun tests/bin/db-suites.ts feedback store
[db-suites] PASS 4/4 suites, 16 tests, 0 quarantined, 4.2s
$ bun apps/web/scripts/generate-audit-actions-doc.mjs --check   # exit 0
$ cd packages/db && bun scripts/generate.ts probe
No schema changes detected — kortix.ts matches the snapshot. Nothing generated.
```
`.
suna-skills: worktree, testing, learnings, migration, contributing
ponytail: full · review: Lean already. Ship. (net: 0 lines; 0 findings
kept) · markers: 0
Self-review: 23 items found and fixed cumulative — 18 prior, 1 in the
migration-re-date cycle (the migration-order root cause the gate caught;
the guard script now runs clean where it refused before), 3 reviewer
items in this cycle (drizzle snapshot reparent, audit-actions doc count,
biome on the new CLI files) and 1 self-review find (the doc regeneration
moved a content file's git lastModified, so the committed
content-timestamps manifest went stale — regenerated post-commit, fb9's
package-quality caught it, fb10 green).

## Summary

Agents and people had no first-class way to file product feedback: the
ask (reported in #kortix-triage) is a `/feedback` API endpoint plus a
matching Kortix CLI command, so an agent can submit product or CLI
feedback while it works or when it hits an error.

This adds exactly that, in the smallest shape the repo's gates allow:

- **`POST /v1/feedback`** (`apps/api/src/feedback/index.ts`, mounted in
`app.ts`): OpenAPI-typed route behind `supabaseAuth` (browser JWT, PAT
and service-account credentials all resolve an identity). The payload is
`source` (cli|agent|web, default `cli`), `kind` (bug|idea|friction),
`message` (1–4000 chars, trimmed) and an optional bounded `context` map
(≤ 8 keys of ≤ 128 chars → ≤ 256-char values). It persists one row into
the new `kortix.feedback` table (`packages/db/src/schema/kortix.ts`,
migration `20261009194110000_feedback.sql`) and answers `201 {id,
source, kind, created_at}`. The rate limiter
(`middleware/rate-limit.ts`) keys the existing token bucket on the
caller's user id with a client-IP fallback and audits hits through the
shared `createAuditedRateLimitMiddleware`.
- **`kortix feedback`** (`apps/cli/src/commands/feedback.ts`): argv
parse split from the I/O so the parse is unit-tested without a host; the
submit resolves auth through `resolveProjectAuth` (so the injected
sandbox `KORTIX_TOKEN` works without a stored login) and posts to
`/feedback`. Help-table (`command-table.ts`) and docs
(`apps/web/content/docs/cli.mdx`) entries included, and the command is
decided as allowed in the MCP CLI-command decision table
(`apps/api/src/mcp/cli.ts`).

Closes KRTX-1646

## Demo video

No demo video: code-only change

## Type of change

- [x] New feature

## How was this tested?

All numbers below are from this cycle's runs in the worker sandbox
(`/workspace/suna-krtx-1646-fb`, local Supabase up, Docker available —
no skipped-no-db lane).

**Focused tests, before → after the fixes**

```
$ bun tests/bin/db-suites.ts hosts provision            # before: 3+1 pre-existing failures
[db-suites] FAIL apps/api/src/backends/hosts.integration.test.ts: 3 failed
[db-suites] FAIL apps/api/src/backends/provision.integration.test.ts: 1 failed
# after the loopback fix:
[db-suites] PASS apps/api/src/backends/provision.integration.test.ts 5 tests 2.1s
[db-suites] PASS apps/api/src/backends/hosts.integration.test.ts 5 tests 2.9s
[db-suites] PASS 3/3 suites, 13 tests, 0 quarantined, 3.4s

$ cd apps/api && SUPABASE_URL=https://placeholder.supabase.co INTERNAL_KORTIX_ENV=dev \
    KORTIX_BILLING_INTERNAL_ENABLED=true LLM_GATEWAY_ENABLED=true \
    FRONTEND_URL=https://placeholder.kortix.com KORTIX_CONFIG_ARCHIVE_S3_ENDPOINT=https://placeholder.storage.example \
    bun test src/__tests__/unit-routes-manifest.test.ts

$ bun tests/bin/db-suites.ts gateway-keys             # after the de-flake
[db-suites] PASS 1/1 suites, 10 tests, 0 quarantined, 2.4s

$ cd apps/api && pnpm typecheck                        # after the helper-typing fix
# exit 0
```

**Final full `pnpm test` (exit 0, 19m52s) — the green attestation's
lanes**

```
[test] PASS core 1183.0s            (sdk, runner units, route coverage, worktree units)
[test] PASS api-cli-flows 337.2s    (FB-1 feedback flow incl.)
[test] PASS db-suites 293.3s        (275/275 suites, 2295 tests, 1 quarantined)
[test] PASS flow-runner-unit 60.7s
[test] PASS route-coverage 0.4s
[test] PASS worktree-unit 3.7s
[test] PASS sdk 22.5s
[test] PASS package-quality 822.5s  (typecheck + package units; api/cli/web packages)
[attest] wrote tests/attestations/krtx-1646-feedback.json: {"core":"pass","packages":"pass","db-suites":"pass"}

results: 570/570 passed · 0 failed · 0 skipped · 0 todo · 341.1s   (api-cli-flows runner summary, incl. FB-1 PASS)

$ pnpm test:verify --rev ea08b255b7df37dd54151a0e111dd9df617ed4e9 --branch krtx-1646-feedback
[attest] OK green
```

**What this cycle fixed to get there** (each was previously written off
as pre-existing):

1. `tests/spec/routes.generated.json` was committed from a wrong-profile
generation: 764 routes including the 9 self-host `/v1/setup/*` routes
(billing off) instead of the documented cloud profile from the
`dump-routes.ts` header. Regenerated with the documented profile: 755
routes (dev's 754 + the new `POST /v1/feedback`), no setup routes. The 9
setup routes remain in the `externalRoutes` allowlist
(`tests/src/coverage/allowlist.ts`, declared by
`setup-billing-backlog.flow.ts`), so the route-coverage gate stays
green. The prior cycle's claim that the committed manifest was correct
and the runner env was the artifact is corrected: it was inverted.
2. `hosts.integration.test.ts` and `provision.integration.test.ts`
derived their fake-upstream URLs from Bun's `server.url.origin`
(`http://localhost:<port>`), so every in-process fetch depended on the
host resolving `localhost` — unresolvable in this sandbox (no hosts
entry; `getent hosts localhost` empty, `127.0.0.1`/`::1` both fine). The
fakes now bind `hostname: '127.0.0.1'` and hand out explicit loopback
URLs: no name resolution needed, here or anywhere. This was the single
root cause of all 4 "pre-existing" backend failures.
3. `integration-gateway-keys.test.ts` asserted the fire-and-forget
`lastUsedAt` write after one fixed 50 ms sleep; under 6-way db-suite
parallelism the write lands later and the test fails (~1/275 suites,
timing-only). It now polls up to 5 s for the stamp — same assertion, no
fixed-sleep race.

4. dev merged the apps rework (#9463) and the notification fixes (#9464)
mid-cycle. The merge moved the backend suites to
`apps/api/src/apps/kinds/convex/` and rewrote provision/routes tests
around the new model, reintroducing the `localhost` fake-server URLs;
the loopback fix was re-applied at the renamed paths. The routes
manifest was regenerated over the merged table (750 routes: dev's 749 +
`POST /v1/feedback`; the backends routes are gone with the feature) and
the content timestamp manifest over the merged history — both derived
pre-merge are stale by construction.
5. One intermediate run's flows lane failed with ~dozens of 500s (APP-*,
AGP-*, DEL-*): the ke2e runner reuses a healthy local stack without
checking code freshness, so it served the pre-merge API against the
migrated database. Restarting the stack (`pnpm worktree stop`) before
the attested run fixed it; the lane then passed twice in a row (352.1s,
357.5s).
6. The CLI allowlist conflict resolved as dev's list plus `feedback`
(`apps/api/src/mcp/cli.ts`).

**Attestation flow**: the final run executed on the clean committed tree
(fixes and merges committed through `06bc88570c`), then only
`tests/attestations/krtx-1646-feedback.json` was committed — the
attestation hashes exclude `tests/attestations/`, so verify stays fresh
at the pushed head.

## Security & data review

- [x] No secrets, keys, or credentials are committed (verified by secret
scan / review)
- [x] Authorization checks are in place for any new/changed endpoints
(IAM / access control) — the route sits behind `supabaseAuth`; every
anonymous call is rejected with 401 before the handler or the limiter
run.
- [x] User input is validated (e.g. Zod) and output is safe — zod schema
bounds every field (enum vocabulary, message length, context key/value
sizes and count); the receipt returns only the row id, kind, source and
timestamp.
- [x] No sensitive data (tokens, PII, secrets) is written to logs — the
route logs nothing; the rate-limit audit writes the bounded limiter
metadata only.
- [x] No customer names, people's names, emails, or real prod IDs in the
code, commits, this PR text, or the demo video (AGENTS.md → "NEVER write
customer data or PII") — synthetic ids only.
- [x] DB schema / migration changes are reviewed and reversible —
additive `CREATE TABLE` + one index; no `ALTER`/`DROP` of anything
existing; rollback is `DROP TABLE kortix.feedback`.
- [ ] Touches auth / IAM / crypto / billing / migrations → requested the
relevant code owner — the migration uses the standard schema-change
loop; no auth/IAM/crypto/billing surface is touched.

## Rollout / rollback

- Additive migration `20261009194110000_feedback.sql` (fresh table +
index, `lock_timeout`/`statement_timeout` headers per house rules);
`deploy-dev.yml` applies it before the rollout. Rollback: `DROP TABLE
kortix.feedback;` — no data preservation concerns (the table starts
empty).
- No feature flag: the endpoint is inert until a client calls it. The
rate limit defaults to 10/min/user, tunable with
`KORTIX_FEEDBACK_REQS_PER_MIN` without a code change.

## Reviewer checklist

- [x] Change is scoped and understandable
- [x] The demo video shows the change working — `No demo video:
code-only change`; the commands and outputs above are the proof.
- [x] Tests cover the change; current full `pnpm test` is green
(attestation committed, `test:verify` fresh)
- [x] Security & data review above is satisfied

## Prior feedback cycles (condensed)

Thirteen review rounds preceded this body; the per-cycle narratives were
condensed here and corrected where they were wrong:

- Repeated cycles fixed migration re-dating (final
`20261009194110000_feedback.sql`), merge conflicts against a moving
`dev` (main was retired; the PR re-based onto `dev` twice), CLI

Prod: Better Stack pattern `3182bf88…` (issue 2346961) — two stop requests failed fast (333 ms and 617 ms) inside a double-stop race, each with `Sandbox state change in progress (provider status: running)`. - **The fix**: after a failed stop whose status still reads `running`, give the transition a **bounded settle window** — poll the provider status every 2 s for up to 30 s; `stopped`/`removed` resolves the request, a still-`running` sandbox gets one stop retry per poll (a resolved retry also resolves), and an exhausted window keeps today's enriched rethrow (last observed status in the message). The window is injectable (`stopSettleTimeoutMs`, default 30 000) so tests stay instant. The success fast path (first status read says `stopped`/`removed`) is unchanged, and `removed`/`stopped` still short-circuit at every poll. - **Tests**: two new regression tests in `apps/api/src/apps/hosting.test.ts` — conflict-then-settles-stopped (expects event order `stop,status,stop,status`) and conflict-stays-running-then-retry-resolves (`stop,status,stop`) — both watched **failing at the base for the right reason** (13 pass / 2 fail: the base rethrows `Sandbox state change in progress (provider status: running)` instead of settling) and **passing at the head** (15 pass / 0 fail). ## Review in 60 seconds

**Problem.** Review-page change-request file accordions opened with
completely blank bodies — the file list was right, no diff content ever
rendered, nothing errored (`GET …/diff` → 200, `files` full, `patch:
''`).

**Root cause, reproduced end to end (3 stacked defects):**
- The API swallowed the failed `git diff` (`.catch(() =>
({stdout:'',stderr:''}))`): a patch over `runGit`'s 10 MiB `maxBuffer`
shipped as 200 + empty patch + populated `files`
(`apps/api/src/projects/git/merge.ts`).
- The web parser regex never matched git's C-quoted headers (any
non-ASCII path) and cut ` b/`-paths at the first occurrence (old
`splitPatchByFile` in
`apps/web/src/features/review-center/change-files.tsx`).
- Even a correctly-split chunk crashed the renderer: `@pierre/diffs`
throws `TypeError` on quoted headers (error boundary on the live page).

**Fix.**
- API: the failed patch command reports `{stdout:'', truncated:true}`;
`BranchDiffSummary.patch_truncated` and the diff route carry it (files
list kept).
- SDK: `ChangeRequestDiffResponse.patch_truncated?` — optional, so old
clients tolerate the new field and vice versa.
- Web tests: pure-rename chunks read the exact new path from the `rename
to` line — the header heuristic mis-splits when the NEW path itself
contains ` b/` (2 new red-first tests; the rename previously rendered
the missing-chunk notice, never a blank).
- Web: `splitUnifiedPatch` keys chunks the way git writes them (`+++
b/<path>` first — authoritative even for ` b/` paths — then the quoted
header pair, then the raw header split at the last ` b/`) and rewrites
quoted header lines to decoded paths so the renderer parses them;
`change-files.tsx` shows an explicit per-file notice (truncated /
missing chunk) instead of blankness. One new i18n key in all nine
catalogs.

**What this PR does not do:** raise the diff buffer or stream partial
patches — a >10 MB change is now honestly reported instead of silently
blank.

new field and vice versa); the web `splitUnifiedPatch` reads each
chunk's path the way git writes it (`+++ b/<path>` first — authoritative
even for ` b/` paths — then the quoted header pair, then the raw header
split at the *last* ` b/`), rewrites quoted header lines to decoded
paths so the renderer can parse them, and `change-files.tsx` renders an
**explicit per-file notice** when the patch was truncated or a file's
chunk is missing — the accordion never silently stays blank again. One

missing-chunk case reuses the existing "This file has no preview." key.

## Summary

The Supabase performance advisor reports `auth_rls_initplan` on
`public.credit_ledger` (KRTX-1138). The lint is per policy, and the
legacy table carries two bare policies: "Service role manages ledger"

wrap each call in a scalar subquery — `(select auth.role())`, `(select
auth.uid())` — which Postgres plans once per statement (an InitPlan).
`ALTER POLICY` touches only each USING expression, so roles (as found),
commands, permissiveness and the implicit WITH CHECK are preserved.

`public.credit_ledger` is the pre-baseline wallet table (KRTX-1122): the
monorepo baseline (`20260621094136410_baseline.sql`) creates only
`kortix.credit_ledger`, whose policies already carry the wrapped form;
the legacy twin survives on long-lived environments and still receives
rows (~146 in 30 days). The migration is therefore guarded both ways: it
runs only where the table exists, and only where the exact legacy
predicates exist (`qual` matched exactly, both the `auth.*()` and the
search-path-elided printings), so it never rewrites a rule the advisor
did not describe.
