feat(config-releases): config releases run for every project — remove the config_releases flag (#9432)

## Summary

Config releases graduate out of the feature-flag system: every session
of every project runs its base branch's config release. Before this PR,
a project with the `config_releases` flag off (every project but 4 in
prod) read its config from the session's `/workspace` checkout. A skill,
agent or tool merged to the base branch then did not reach a running
session, and the session header showed the older, etag-based state.
#9424 and #9429 removed the last blocker, the 32 MiB repository limit.
This PR removes the flag, following the earlier graduations (#8601
`teams`, #9027 `agent_principal`).

**What changes**

- **API.**
- The `config_releases` registry entry and `config-releases/enabled.ts`
are deleted.
- No route answers `403 feature_disabled` for config releases. The
descriptor route and the archive route serve every project.
- Convergence: the `disabled` and `governance-pushed` outcomes and the
restart-time governance push are gone. Every trigger (resume, restart,
turn end, base move, push) reaches the box.
- Reload: the daemon's `config.release.v1` capability alone picks the
release path. A daemon without it still takes the pre-release path,
including `base_config=1` (the 2026-09-30 learning; its enforcer moved,
see below).
- The turn-start gate, `GET /config` and session-open admission no
longer read the flag.
- A value a project stored for the flag is inert. `PATCH
/v1/projects/:projectId/features {feature:"config_releases",…}` answers
`400 Unknown feature flag 'config_releases'`. Values stay in the
database, so a revert restores every project's choice.
- **API contract:** `config_releases` leaves `FeatureFlagMapSchema`.
- **SDK** (`@kortix/sdk`, non-breaking):
- `config_releases` stays in `FeatureFlagKey` as `@deprecated` and
leaves `FEATURE_FLAG_KEYS` and `KortixProject.experimental`.
  - `useFeatureFlag(id, 'config_releases')` reports `enabled: true`.
  - CHANGELOG entry under Deprecated.
- **Web:**
  - The flag hook map drops the key.
  - The flag's name and description leave all 9 catalogs.
- Fix found while verifying: a page that holds a flag catalog from the
previous API during a deploy rendered a graduated flag's row as the raw
key `settings.featureFlags.flags.config_releases.name`
(`MISSING_MESSAGE` in the log). `localizeFeatureFlag` now falls back to
the English name and description the API sends.
- **Daemon:** comments only. It still reverts to its workspace config on
`403 feature_disabled`, so a rolled-back or older API keeps working
boxes. The built binary is byte-identical to `dev`'s (`sha256
62871459edacd242…`).
- **Docs:**
- `work/runtime.mdx`: "Turning it off" becomes "Try a config change
before it merges". A session created with `base_ref` on a branch runs
that branch's config, verified below.
  - `feature-flags`: Config releases join Graduated flags.
- `work/harnesses.mdx` and the pi starter reference drop the flag
condition.
- `ROLLOUT.md` becomes the operations runbook: status, what to watch
with prod numbers, the fallback chain, and rollback by revert.
- **Flows and spec:**
- The 12 per-flow opt-in steps are gone, and flows that no longer call
the features route drop it from `meta.routes`.
  - CFG-8 now asserts the graduation contract:
    - no `config_releases` key in `experimental`;
    - a project that made no choice gets a release;
    - the old key answers `400` for `false`, `true` and `null`;
    - a stored `false` from before graduation still gets a release;
    - a base commit moves the release.
- **Learnings:** a new entry supersedes
`2026-09-30T171738Z-when-a-mechanism-moves-behind-a-flag…`. That rule
still holds for daemons without `config.release.v1`; its enforcer is now
"reloadSessionConfig on a daemon without config releases".

**Prod impact, measured read-only (2026-10-08)**

| | Projects | Sessions, 14 days | Boxes used, 24 h |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flag on today | 4 (3 active) | 9,230 (67%) | 459 |
| Unset (gets releases with this PR) | 7,633 (702 active) | 4,503 (33%)
| 266 |

- Prod has no project with the flag stored `false`.
- Prod release health with the flag on, 14 days: 62 releases, 60 proven.
27 of 29 failure reports were the 2026-10-02 meta-coordinator incident
(fixed by the `meta` variant). The other 2 were single-session reports,
below the 2-session quarantine threshold.
- Descriptor route, prod logs, 24 h:
- 32,058 requests answered `200`: p50 886 ms, p95 3.3 s, p99 7.5 s, most
of it `git;dur`.
  - 20,910 requests answered `403 feature_disabled` in 27 ms (p50).
- After this PR those `403`s become full requests: about +65% Git
fetches on this route, at a load prod already serves at 61%. Follow-up
below.

## Summary

A failed subagent dispatch left the reader with two dead ends
(KRTX-1746, reported with a screenshot in the [originating Slack
thread](https://kortixworkspace.slack.com/archives/C0BMJKENUPP/p1791298524949969):
`Task failed / Subagent failed (task_id: ses_…): This model does not
support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user
message.`):

1. **The failed thread was unviewable.** `ToolPartRenderer`'s
errored-part branch collapsed every errored tool part into the generic
error card — title "Task", subtitle "failed" — whose trigger has no way
into the child session. The child transcript survived (OpenCode keeps
the failed child; its id rides `state.metadata.sessionId`), but nothing
in the UI could reach it. Now a child-bearing errored `task` dispatch
falls through to its registered renderer: `TaskTool` keeps its row
identity ("Agent · general — Report on the widget"), its "Open full
view" affordance opens the child's transcript, and it draws
`state.error` in the body so the failure reason stays on the row. An
errored `task` with no child id keeps the generic card (nothing to
open), and every non-task tool is untouched.

2. **Recovery re-sent the same prompt.** The `[auto-recovery]` re-prompt
told the model to "re-run it if it did not complete", so after a
mid-task provider death the model re-dispatched the SAME prompt to a NEW
subagent and the failed child's work was lost. `turn-auto-resume.ts` now
scans the last assistant message's tool parts (`interruptedSubagents`):
up to three interrupted `task` dispatches — failed (`status: 'error'`)
or dangling mid-task (`running`/`pending`) — is named in the resume
prompt by its child session id, with the instruction to resume THAT
subagent via the task tool's `task_id` (context intact) instead of
starting a fresh one, plus the child's failure reason when there is one.

Both shapes were verified live against opencode 1.18.23 with a mock
OpenAI-compatible provider before writing any code: a failed task part
ends `status: 'error'` with `state.error = "Subagent failed (task_id:
<childId>): …"` and `state.metadata` retained; a turn cut mid-task
leaves the part `running` with the same metadata. The upstream OpenCode
retry-exhaustion hang found along the way (a child stream that exhausts
its 5 retries never finalizes — the parent turn hangs forever) is a
separate defect and is **not** addressed here.

Concurrency is 8, the same bound as the reclaim; "already gone" counts as done. - It empties each project's session files with the new `sessionAttachmentStore().removeProject` (one list per project, then each session folder). - It deletes each project's repo through `deleteManagedProjectRepo`, which refuses a repo the user connected. ## Summary

Fixes the Supabase performance advisor finding
`multiple_permissive_policies` on `public.user_roles` (Linear
KRTX-1166). Both of the legacy table's permissive policies target
`PUBLIC`, so every non-BYPASSRLS role evaluates two policies per
`SELECT` (the advisor's rule, supabase/splinter 0006, groups permissive
policies by role+action and flags any group larger than one). The
migration scopes each policy to the JWT role its predicate already
requires — the same remediation `20261004173004004` applied to
`public.audit_log`:

- `ALTER POLICY "Service role can manage all roles" ON public.user_roles
TO service_role;`
- `ALTER POLICY "Users can view their own role" ON public.user_roles TO
authenticated;`

Predicates stay byte-identical; access semantics are unchanged. Each
`ALTER` is guarded on the policy's existence: `public.user_roles` is a
pre-baseline legacy table (the managed surface is
`kortix.platform_user_roles`), so the migration is a no-op on every
fresh database and never invents access where the policy shape drifted.

Closes KRTX-1166

gateway: a gateway MAGPIE_ADDR puts on the network asks callers from other machines, a container's host among them, for an enabled gateway key, as sharing does

What changed
- lanGuard: a request whose peer isn't loopback (or that carries a
  forwarding header) is remote. While the gateway is shared, or
  MAGPIE_ADDR names a host other than loopback/localhost (OnNetwork:
  0.0.0.0 in the Docker image, a server's address), a remote request is
  answered only with an enabled gateway key, on every route behind the
  guard; otherwise it is refused (403) as before. Before, a MAGPIE_ADDR on
  the network with sharing off took remote requests with any key.
  A remote request let in with a key is marked as shared-mode ones are,
  so quotas, quota cards, refresh and prices answer it.
  callerGuard follows the same condition. OpenToAnyone is replaced by
  OnNetwork.
- Loopback is unchanged: any key still works on the gateway's own
  machine and inside the container (HEALTHCHECK included).
- CLI keyNote and the console's Connect note no longer describe an open
  gateway; on the network they say other machines need a gateway key
  (`magpie gateway-key add <name>`). The console shows the Gateway keys
  block and network addresses when OnNetwork (gatewayJSON.onNetwork
  replaces open); the "Open to the network" strings are removed.
- Docs: docker.html (en/zh/ja) and remote.html (en/zh/ja) say callers
  outside the container need a gateway key, how to make one, that
  sharing isn't needed for it, and what an upgrade means for agents that
  sent `magpie`; docs/reference.md and providers-accounts.md likewise.
  A MAGPIE_ADDR pinned to one interface's address now asks a key of this

library: skills from GitHub are checked as the skills page opens, and one changed here is marked and asked about before an update replaces it (#1449)

YangZhiqiang98 asked (#1449) that the Library find which skills have
updates and update them. magpie already checked skills from GitHub (a
market install among them) by hand and could update them, but an update
deleted the library's folder, so a skill the user had changed (by hand,
through an agent's link, or in an agent's copy not yet taken in) was lost
without a word, and nothing checked unless the user pressed Check.

- A skill is "changed here" when its library folder no longer hashes to
  what was fetched (Finder's .DS_Store aside), or an agent's copy was
  edited since its mark and not yet taken in (editState, skill_changed.go).
  The view says so (SkillView.edited) and the row shows "Changed here".
- UpdateSkill refuses such a skill with *EditedError unless told to
  replace it. The row's Update asks in the page first (Keep mine / Update;
  Update sends replace). Update N, the group's Update N and the CLI's
  update-all leave it as it is and say so. The CLI takes
  `magpie library skill update <name> --replace-edits`.
- The version an update replaces is moved to the backups when it was

gateway: the loop guard's end-to-end tests bound how soon the loop was cut by what reached the agent, not by how far the fake vendor wrote ahead of a slowed gateway (#1443)

Cause: loopCut failed when the fake vendor had sent more than 2000 lines
by the time it saw its request let go. That count isn't the guard's: the
cut is made in holdWriter.Write, on the write that trips it, and cancels
the vendor's request there. But the vendor's writes succeed as long as the
sockets' and transports' buffers take them, so it runs ahead of a gateway
that reads slowly. Under load (CI macOS -race, a full run at load ~35) it
got ~2,800-3,200 lines ahead of a cut the agent saw at the 259th line.

Fix (test only, the guard was already deterministic): loopingVendor sends
at most 2000 lines of its loop, then holds its stream open until its
request is let go (20s, else it says it wasn't). Being let go therefore
means the guard found the loop within those 2000 lines, however the test
is scheduled. How soon it cut is now checked on what reached the agent:
the loop lines in the stream are at most the guard's window (256) plus one
32K read of the vendor's stream, which the cut's write sends whole.

Run:
- Reproduced by injecting a 300us sleep into holdWriter.Write (not
  committed): the old test failed 140 of 180 subtests (-race -count=5
  -cpu 1,2,4, 16 busy loops beside it), every route and protocol but chat,
  "let go only after 2754..3082 lines", the vendor up to 8322. The agent
  got ~259 loop lines in each.
- The new test with the same sleep and load: -race -count=50 -cpu 1,2,4,
  1800/1800 subtests pass (built-in and plugin, chat/anthropic/responses/
  gemini, and TestLoopEndsTheReplyOnEveryProtocol). At most 470 loop lines
  reached the agent (the bound is 583; 256 + 32768/141 is ~490).
- Without the sleep, under load: -race -count=20 -cpu 1,2,4 of these plus
  TestLoopGuardOff and TestLongReplyThatDoesNotLoopGoesThrough, all pass.
- The test goes red when the guarantee breaks: with cutLoop's h.stop()
  disabled ("the vendor's request was not let go", built-in anthropic,
  responses, gemini; chat is still let go when the failed write ends its
  copy), and with the guard's trips dropped for its first 800 writes ("the
  loop was cut only after 1038 of its lines reached the agent").

provider, docs: a bare model id several providers serve goes by the Providers order, said and tested (MOMO on Discord)

MOMO's {"model":"glm-5.3"} was answered by opencode-go though a6api
serves glm-5.3 too, and they asked for a 409 or for the response to say
which provider was used. The pick was already deterministic, but
Resolve's comment said "exactly one provider" and no doc said what
happens.

Decision: keep serving bare ids, no 409. magpie writes only
provider/model ids into agents' configs (agent/route.go magpieModels),
so a bare id comes from a user's own config, and a 409 would break every
such client the day a second provider adds the model. The rule is now
written down and pinned:
- found groups on (the default): GroupFor takes the bare id to its found
  group auto-<slug>, members in the Providers order, smart routing and
  fail-over to the next provider; a conversation stays with the member
  that answered it while its cache is worth it (affinity).
- found groups off: Resolve takes the first provider in the Providers
  order that exposes it, alone.
- every reply already carries X-Magpie-Provider / X-Magpie-Model
  (member.go), and the usage log has the provider.

row; reference.md, the ways a model is named and the headers;

in the Providers order answers every new conversation, reordering moves
new ones, an answered one stays in the found group, and a 503 from the
first falls over only in the found group. It passes on the old code
too: it pins behaviour that was already there, now documented.

gateway: a resumed reply to a model that takes no prefill is answered after it, not refused (#1447, Edward4226)

OpenCode Go's Claude models (over Anthropic Messages) refuse a
conversation ending with the assistant's message, "This model does not
support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user
message.", and Volcengine's Agent Plan does too, "The last message cannot
be from the assistant for a model that does not support prefill".
magpie took every Anthropic upstream to go on from a prefill, so both a
client's own resume (Codex sends what it has of a cut reply as the last
assistant message) and magpie's own continuation of a cut reply (#853)
ended with that refusal.

The refusal is about the model, so it is remembered for that provider,
model and API in unfit (prefillRefused); the provider's other models,
and every upstream that takes a prefill, are unchanged.

- A Chat or Responses client's conversation ending with the assistant's
  message, which those APIs read as a turn already said, is asked again
  with a user turn after it ("Continue."), the conversation the refusal
  asks for, and so from then on: translated (forwardTranslated, whole
  and streamed) and relayed as is (passthrough, Chat and Responses: the
  Volcengine case).
- An Anthropic client's prefill is its own ask and still gets the
  refusal as the vendor sent it.
- magpie's own continuation is not asked of that model again, and the
  try it refused ends the reply with what cut it, as a reply that can't
  go on did before #853, not with the refusal of an ask the client never
  made. No user-turn continuation there: a re-answer spliced onto the
  part the client has is the garble continuation.go avoids.

The thinking-block refusal in the same report (a signed thinking block
with no text) is a separate fix, in its own commit.

Tests (prefill_test.go), from the report's literal messages: the
issue's Responses repro and a streamed Chat request to an Anthropic
upstream (TestTrailingAssistantToNoPrefillModel, also checks another
model keeps its prefill), Volcengine's refusal relayed on Responses and
Chat (TestTrailingAssistantRelayedToNoPrefillModel), a cut reply
(TestStreamCutOnNoPrefillModel), an Anthropic client's prefill
(TestAnthropicPrefillToNoPrefillModel), userLastBody. With the refusal
unrecognised (the old code's behaviour) the first three fail with the
report's "UP: Upstream request failed: [invalid_request_error] This
model does not support assistant message prefill…" / "…the reply didn't
end with what cut it"; with the remembering removed they fail with
"calls 4 … asked one again" and "calls = 2 … asked to go on again".

server-side auto mode classifier "because your requests go through

- serverReview (automode.go), called from forwardOnce, so passthrough,

  carries delta.safeguard_results to the encoder, which already wrote them.

  gateway, and the setting would hide its eligibility there. Said in

chat or image generators. Refresh removes stale decisions and the editor
receives an explicit empty decision list when none remain.

macOS and Linux/Windows cross-builds, and the Remote magpie browser tests in

test fails on the old code with an empty model list, and the retrieval test

exercise two gateways and simulated upstreams; live vendor accounts were
not used.

relay behind the remote that admits only official clients accepts their

at their own call sites. The two-hop test covers Messages, Responses, Chat

unlisted remote decisions and remove the redundant resolveDecideModel
early return: the explicit model marker and list-only Jev already exclude

Simplify decision classification around the explicit remote list and reuse
model markers while building Available, Catalog and Deciders, avoiding a

path (os.Executable at install). A WebDAV sync carried
C:\Users\...\Downloads\magpie-windows-amd64.exe to a Mac (and a Mac's app
to Windows), and a magpie moved out of Downloads left its old path behind:
the Library page said it couldn't start, and agents were given a program

  program named magpie (magpie, magpie.exe, magpie-<os>-<arch>[.exe]) --
  whose program isn't an existing absolute path here is pointed at this

  bundle Put from another computer is healed before it is written into
  the agents). Every agent writer, project MCP files, the WSL side and
  CheckServers read through load, so all of them get it. A magpie program
  that does exist here (another build) and any server run by another
  program are left as they are.

  with the same library carry the same bundle, so davsync's library hash
  matches and a sync doesn't write one's path over the other's.
- The path given is update.Program (exported cliProgram): the AppImage
  rather than its mount, Homebrew's opt link rather than the Cellar.

  computer runs.

whole call away ("failed to parse function arguments: invalid type:
floating point `2500.0`, expected u64 at line 1 column 77"; `17277.0`,
expected i32), so the turn stopped at its first command. Reported 11 of 11
turns through a sub2api relay in front of grok-4.6 and grok-4.7.

What changed (grok_integral.go):
- grokModel/grokServed: a Grok model is one whose id, as magpie names it
  or as it is sent upstream, has a last `/` segment beginning "grok"
  (relay/grok-4.6, x-ai/grok-4, the plugin's grok-4.7).
- wholeNums: a streaming scanner over the arguments' JSON text. A number
  written with a fraction of zeros and no exponent loses the fraction
  (2500.0 -> 2500, -3.00 -> -3, [1.0,2.0] -> [1,2]). Strings, keys, other
  fractions (2.5, 2.50) and exponents (1.0e3) stay as written. It holds
  only a run of ".0…" until the next byte, so arguments cut into deltas
  anywhere come out the same as whole, and the deltas add up to what the
  done events say.
- Relayed (passthrough): intTidy, beside nsTidy and built like it, on
  Responses (function_call items, argument deltas and done, the completed
  response, a whole reply), Chat (tool_calls deltas and messages) and
  Messages (tool_use input and input_json_delta), streamed or whole. A
  line that carries no call passes as it came. Plugin-served Grok and the
  built-in subscription go through the same passthrough.
- Translated: translate sets Request.Grok; encoder() wraps the client's
  encoder in wholeEncoder (outside usageEncoder) and render() rewrites the
  Result's calls (wholeResult), so every client protocol is covered at
  those two choke points.
- Any other model's reply is relayed byte for byte, as before.
- gateway-routing.md says so, and lists the tests.

Scope, against the reporter's 9fd6855b: that commit rewrote only fields a
tool schema typed "integer" or a fixed list of Codex's (codexInts), only
on Responses, and left deltas as they came, so the deltas disagreed with
the done events, and the list missed Codex's other integers (shell's
timeout_ms, sleep's duration_ms, tool_search's limit, the multi-agent
tools' timeout_ms). Codex's own schemas say "number", and JSON has one number type, so 2500 is the same value as
2500.0 for every client; this drops the zero fraction everywhere in a
Grok model's call arguments instead. Its rollout fixtures are kept
verbatim (testdata/grok_integral_args) and its test helpers adapted.

Tests: TestWholeNumsAnyCut (every split point and byte by byte),
TestGrokCallsGiveCodexIntegers (relayed Responses, streamed with deltas
cut whole, byte by byte and at every '.'/zero, and whole),
TestGrokCallsGiveCodexIntegersTranslated (Chat upstream -> Codex),
TestGrokCallsGiveIntegersOnEveryProtocol (Chat relayed, Messages relayed,
Messages translated from Chat), TestGrokCallsByUpstreamName,
TestGrokPluginCallsGiveCodexIntegers (fake plugin, $FAKE_GROK),
TestOnlyGrokCallsGetIntegers (gpt-5.5 byte for byte on Responses, Chat
and Messages relayed; translated keeps 2500.0), TestGrokModel. Each
recorded case checks that the field Codex's own error names is now an
integer of the Rust type it named, wherever Codex reads the call.
With grokModel forced false, every Grok test fails; with the delta
rewriting turned off (intTidy and wholeEncoder), every streamed case
fails on deltas != done.

neiko on Discord installed a third-party plugin beside a plugin of their
own, added by its folder. Only the third-party one could be seen. Both
plugins' auth hooks name the same provider id. The host's auths() keeps
the last plugin in plugins.json for an id, as OpenCode does, so the
user's own plugin silently lost it:
- its row read "Signs in to nothing magpie can use";
- its provider was gone from the Add sheet;
- keepUnloaded could list the id a second time, from the

plugins stay visible in those cases, because a folder plugin's name is
its path.

- host.js:

    for each id another plugin serves, that plugin's spec (servedBy).

  - Prefer() records a pick and restarts the host.

  - remove, off, options and prefer find a plugin by its exact spec
    before its package name (indexOf), so acting on one plugin never
    reaches another of the same package.

    plugin serves its id now.

library: DeepSeek Harness is given a server's ${NAME} as a !!js expression it reads from its environment (#1435, CnsMaple)

A Library MCP server whose headers or env named a variable as ${NAME}
(#1250) was refused for dsh, because dsh had no reference syntax in
refsOf. dsh does have one: a YAML !!js value is evaluated as the row
activates (dsh 0.2.0-rc.2: cordis-plugin-include's entryListSchema
reads the tag, quoted or not; cordis-plugin-loader's interpolate
evaluates it across the whole config), and dsh-mcp-client's README uses
GITHUB_TOKEN: !!js process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN. A stdio server needs it so:
it inherits dsh's environment without credential-shaped names
(scrubbedParentEnv).

What magpie writes now (refsOf fmtDsh -> refDsh, dshRef):
- a whole ${NAME}: !!js process.env.NAME (bare, as the README has it)
- text mixed with variables: the text as JSON string literals joined
  with (process.env.NAME ?? ""), YAML-quoted. The user's text is only
  ever inside a JSON string literal, so nothing in it runs as code, and
  NAME is the envRef pattern [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. An unset variable
  inside a mixed value is "", not "undefined".
dshUnref reads exactly those forms back as ${NAME}, so an entry magpie
wrote reads as same and a sync changes nothing; any other !!js still
keeps the entry the user's (hasJS), as before.

The reporter asked for the value to be resolved into a literal when the
file is written. This writes a reference instead, keeping #1250's rule
that the token never lands in an agent's file as plain text. dsh
evaluates it from its own environment at load time. Their side note
that a quoted !!js isn't evaluated is not what dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 does: its
own --dump-config prints !!js quoted, and the quoted forms evaluated in
the run below.

Since AgentView.NoEnvRefs comes from refsOf, dsh's chip is no longer
greyed and the GUI notice drops it with no string change.
docs/subsystems/library.md says what dsh gets.

Run:
- real dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 `dsh headless` in a sandbox (HOME and DSH_HOME
  under a scratch dir, never ~/.dsh), on a cordis.patch.yml written by
  magpie's mcpFile: a stdio fixture got T1435_A=<token> (whole) and
  "Bearer <token>" (mixed); an injection string with quotes, backticks,
  ${, backslashes and "'); process.exit(3); ('" arrived verbatim; an
  unset variable in a mixed value gave "pre--post"; a streamable-http
  fixture received Authorization: Bearer <token>, the whole-variable
  header and the literal header. magpie read every entry back as same.
  A whole !!js process.env.UNSET makes dsh leave the server out as an
  invalid config.
- go test -tags nogui ./... (temp HOME, pinned caches): green.
- break by hand: refsOf without fmtDsh, encode writing raw values, and
  decode not unref'ing each make TestEnvRefsDsh fail (decode also
  TestDshImportKeepsJS).
- gofmt -l; go vet ./...; GOOS=linux and GOOS=windows go vet -tags nogui
  ./internal/library; go build for darwin, linux and windows (nogui).

Not run: dsh on Windows (the reporter's system), and a real LLM turn
calling a tool through the server (no dsh account in the sandbox; the
MCP servers had connected before dsh stopped for its missing LLM
credential). No GUI test was run, as no GUI file changed.

usage: Volcengine Ark's Coding Plan and Agent Plan windows, read with the account's access key (#1427, yayoinoyume)

Ark tells a Coding Plan's or Agent Plan's 5-hour, weekly and monthly
windows only to the account's control plane (GetCodingPlanUsage,
GetAFPUsage on open.volcengineapi.com), signed with the account's
AccessKey ID and Secret, never to the plan's inference key. An Ark
provider's editor now takes that access key, and the Usage page shows the
plan's windows as a card.

From yayoinoyume's feat/volcengine-usage, reviewed and reworked:
- Signing is volc-sdk-golang's (base/sign.go GetSignRequest, 06f9ef66):
  signed headers sorted (content-type;host;x-content-sha256;x-date), only
  Action and Version in the query. The branch signed them unsorted and put
  Region in the query. TestVolcSignMatchesSDK pins two signatures the SDK
  made.
- The card is in PlanQuotas beside the Step Plan's (its cache, last
  reading, refresh and `magpie quota wait`), not in the subscription
  cards. One per access key and plan.
- The plan is the endpoint's: /api/coding asks GetCodingPlanUsage,
  /api/plan GetAFPUsage, pay-as-you-go none, in the host's region. The
  branch asked both and showed whichever answered.
- Dropped guessed reply fields; the Coding Plan reply is the one
  pi-ark-usage, dsh-ark-quota and ArkCodingPlanUsage read. AFP buckets are
  read in the forms dsh-ark-quota and arkcli read (Used of Quota or Total,
  or Percent), plus Tier; none was seen from a real account.
- An Ark provider is known by its host, not the preset id, so a copy or a
  custom provider takes the key too.
- The Secret is never sent to the page (accessKey {id, secretSet}); a
  blank Secret keeps it, a save without the ID keeps both, Remove
  (clearAccessKey) drops both, an ID with no Secret is refused.
- The pair goes where keys go: AddCopy, Restore, Mirror, backups and
  davsync carry it only with keys (withoutKeys), and a keyless restore or
  sync keeps this machine's. CLI: access.key, access.secret.
- A changed access key drops the cached cards (ForgetPlanQuotas).
- UI strings in zh, zh-TW, ja and de.

key. A local fake checked the real request PlanQuotas makes against

SDK (Claude Desktop's chats) with 429 "Resource has been exhausted" at
whatever quota is left (#666). The detail text already said it was not a
quota, but when Antigravity was the last one left (a direct model, the
reporter's case) the route still fell through to failureOf: the try was
counted 额度用尽 on the Routing page and in the account's tally, and the

provider: swapping LoginUsage's or Claude /usage's stand-in waits for the readings still running through the old one (data race in CI run 37942751214)

Cause: TestClaudeAccountBackOnceItsWindowRenews (a2c39053) failed the
ubuntu race shard of run 37942751214. Its Cleanup's LoginUsageVia(nil)
wrote the package-level stand-in while a reading Allowances had started
(routing.go:419) was still reading it in loginUsageAt. Allowances reads
in the background on purpose and returns without waiting (only the very
first ask waits, and not for long), so a reading can outlast the caller,
and the test. The window: Allowances deletes c.loading before it tells
the renewed hooks, so the test's next poll can start another reading
just as the rest it waits on is lifted; the test ends with that reading
in flight. In production the stand-in is never set, so there is no
production race; the goroutine outliving its caller is the design (it is
bounded by its 30 s context).

Change: the stand-in is held for reading while it runs, and
LoginUsageVia takes it for writing, so it returns once no reading is
running through the one it replaces and none starts through it after.
That fixes every test that swaps it (gateway claude_renewed and
allowance_stale, provider routing, allowance_renewed,
codex_reset_deadline, window_renewed), not only the one that failed.
UsageClaudeVia's claudeCLIUsage is the same shape (tests swap it, and
Allowances' background reading of a Claude account reaches it through
readClaudeUsage), so it gets the same treatment; claude_usage_test's
restore goes through UsageClaudeVia. ProbeClaudeVia is left: a Claude
account test calls it synchronously, nothing reads it in the background.

Tests: login_usage_via_test.go holds a call through each stand-in and
checks the swap waits for it.

codex: a conversation that searched the web declares cached search to the ChatGPT backend, so its compaction and turns aren't refused "response protection is unavailable" (#1270, #1099)

The ChatGPT backend answers HTTP 200 and only `event: error` "response
protection is unavailable" to any request whose input replays one of its
own web_search_call items while the request doesn't declare the web_search
tool. Probed on a real ChatGPT Pro account (gpt-6.1-sol, 2026-10-09) with
a real searched turn: refused with tools [], with function tools only and
with a compaction_trigger; answered once {"type":"web_search",
"external_web_access":false} is declared. A Responses Lite request refuses
a top-level web_search (400) but takes it in an additional_tools item. So
xjdata's case (Codex compacting a custom provider's conversation itself, a
plain /responses with tools [] that magpie's codexCompact never sees) failed
every time once the session had searched, and congee949's thread
descriptions too.

- provider.DeclareSearch / declareSearch: when the input holds a
  web_search_call and nothing declares search, add cached-only web_search to
  the tools, or for Lite (header, reasoning.context all_turns, or an
  additional_tools item present) to the additional_tools item (prepended
  when there is none). With no tools offered, tool_choice becomes "none" so
  the model can't search; a forced choice is kept. Otherwise the body is
  unchanged (bytes untouched when no web_search_call is in it).
- codexBody (every ChatGPT account route: serveAgent, codexCompact, warmup,
  magpie's codex/* models) calls it; codexUpstreamOn calls it for Codex's

gateway, settings, gui: a reply whose reasoning or text has become a loop of the same few lines is ended with an error the agent can act on, instead of running on to its output limit (#1359, Moody-Sin: WorkBuddy's DeepSeek v4.1 flash at max effort reasoned "Now." "Writing." "Go." "Let me write." "OK." "Producing." … until max tokens, while dsh waited and Pi hung)

holdWriter.Write, which every streamed try goes through (passed through or translated; a key's, a built-in subscription's, or a plugin's fetch, as a moved WorkBuddy's), feeds a loopGuard (loop_guard.go). It reads the reasoning and the text of each protocol's deltas (Anthropic, Chat, Responses, Gemini) and cuts each into units: lines and sentences, compared without case or a closing stop. A list's "1." or a decimal doesn't end a sentence. A unit with no word in it (braces, rules, 0x00, hashes, rows of numbers) isn't counted. When the last 256 counted units of either are among 24 or fewer distinct ones, the try is cut. What came with that write goes out, then the protocol's stream error (Anthropic error event, Chat error chunk, Responses response.failed server_error, Gemini 502 UNAVAILABLE), naming the loop and quoting its units, and the vendor's request is cancelled. The cycle needn't be exact; the reporter's has 9 units in two variants. It falls back to nobody and rests nobody (fail "loop"), and the usage record's err_type is reply_loop. A reply sent whole (no stream, or Gemini without alt=sse) isn't read. Settings › Models › Replies › Stop looping replies (noLoopGuard, on by default) turns it off; new strings in zh, zh-TW, ja and de.

In each case the agent gets the reasoning and then the error, the vendor is let go within 2000 lines, nobody rests, and usage keeps reply_loop.

dsh: Disconnect keeps the model picked in dsh 0.2, which saves it into magpie's agent-default-model entry (#1392)

What dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 changed (read in @deepseek-ai/dsh-settings and
dsh-agent-default-model from npm): ~/.dsh/settings.yaml is gone. On its
first boot dsh renames it to settings.yaml.imported and merges its sections
into the booted profile's patch list (profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml);
nothing reads the .imported file afterwards. A /model pick is no longer
kept in settings.yaml either: agentDefaultModel.saveSelection goes through
ConfigEditor.edit, which replaces the config of the profile's last
agent-default-model entry. That entry is magpie's, so the user's pick sits
under magpie's "# magpie" mark. Profile paths, the home layer, .env and
.credentials.yaml are unchanged.

What broke: Disconnect took that entry for magpie's own, dropped it and put
back what magpie stashed from before it connected, so the model picked in
dsh (or imported from settings.yaml) was lost. Seen with real dsh
0.2.0-rc.2: after the import, Disconnect left `[]` and dsh started on its
shipped deepseek-flash instead of the imported deepseek-v4-flash.

Fix: dshKeepPick, run per profile before Disconnect takes magpie's wiring
out, hands a marked agent-default-model that is off magpie's route back to
the user (mark removed, old stash discarded). An entry on magpie's route,
or one on the pre-0.1.5 wiring, is still magpie's. dshStart still reads a
settings.yaml not yet imported, which dsh will put over the booted profile.

tool), so the Agents page showed nothing about its CLI: no version, no
newest, no update.

xAI's installers (read from https://x.ai/cli/install.ps1 and install.sh):
- install.ps1 copies grok.exe (and agent.exe) into %USERPROFILE%\.grok\bin
  and puts that on the user PATH; no junction, no versioned folder.
  grok update copies the new grok.exe over it (the running one renamed to
  grok.exe.old), so its size and time change.
- install.sh links ~/.grok/bin/grok to ../downloads/grok-<platform>;
  grok update downloads ../downloads/grok-<version>-<platform> and relinks,
  a new real path per version.
- The newest version of a channel is the body of x.ai/cli/<channel>
  (stable, alpha, enterprise; GCS fallback), the channel kept under [cli]
  in ~/.grok/config.toml.

read there instead of PATH for an agent with no Bin) and `latest` (the
newest its own updater installs, for a CLI not on npm). grok's spec: at
.grok/bin/grok(.exe), self = grok update for a real path under
.grok/bin or .grok/downloads, latest = grokLatest (channel pointer, 6h
memo per channel).

gui: a page's own scrollbar is dragged by the mouse (#1213)

Dragging a scrollbar did nothing on any page with content taller than the
window: the thumb would not move, and letting go left it where it started
(emo172, #1089). The wheel worked, so only the drag was broken, and a
scrollbar dragged in a container the app does not listen to scrolled
normally.

"Where the reader is" holds a view still unless the reader asked for the
scroll: the wheel, a touch, the keys, or a drag of the content, each of
which says so through an event. A scrollbar dragged by the mouse has no
such event — Chromium and WebView2 give it no pointermove — so every
scroll it produced was put back as it came, the thumb sliding back under
the pointer. The wheel works because wheel is one of the events.

The press on a scrollbar does reach the view, with the pointer past its
content in the scrollbar's band, and the lift ends the drag. Held from
that press to the lift, the drag's scrolls count as the reader's.

Two more things hold the page still that a wheel already lets go of, and
the drag lets go of the same two:

- what the last click was holding in place, which keeps what was clicked
  on the screen frame by frame for a few seconds after it;
- the reader's window itself, which WebKit needs held open past the lift:
  it sends the drag's last scrolls once the gesture is over, after the
  pointerup, so closing the window on the lift put those back.

A scroll nothing asked for — code setting scrollTop — is still put back:
only the bar's own drag counts as the reader's, not every scroll.

view-scrollbar-drag.test.cjs is new. It drags a page's own scrollbar in
both engines in English and Chinese, straight away and after a click in
the page that holds what was clicked; it checks the page follows the bar
and stays where it was left, that the wheel still scrolls, that a scroll
code set is still put back, and that a scroll arriving after the lift is
still the reader's. It uses the pages' own scrollbar CSS rather than one
of its own: a scrollbar-width set on the view makes Chromium drop every
::-webkit-scrollbar rule (app.css) and draw Windows' classic bar. The
Routing page is dragged at a narrow window, where it has room to scroll:
at a wide one it lays its stage beside the list and has ~35px left, not
enough to tell a drag from a nudge. The scroll arriving after the lift is
checked on the list page only. It was left off Routing while #1249 was
open — WebKit clamped Routing's last stretch there, so a scroll sent
after the lift measured that bug rather than the window held open past
it. #1249 is fixed in main now, so the check could be widened to Routing;
it is not, because that clamp was only ever checked on Windows headless
WebKit here and not on the macOS WKWebView, and widening a check is
beyond what review asked for.

Three of the checks were reworked after they were run four test files at
a time and each was found to pass for the wrong reason, or to race:

- the click in the page lands on a part that leaves the page as it is.
  The Routing page's own header opens the group editor in English,

gateway: a provider that refuses a system message inside messages gets its text on the top-level system, and an empty one left out (#1407, liuyejinghong: Command Code "Invalid input at messages.1.role")

codex: magpie's actor header goes into a [model_providers.magpie.http_headers] table the config already has, instead of failing every model switch (wztlink1013 on Discord)

wztlink1013 (v0.1.1134, Windows, Codex 0.162.0) could not switch Codex's
model on the Agents page: "config.toml: edited TOML is invalid: toml: key
http_headers should be a table, not a value".

Cause: putProvider rewrites [model_providers.magpie] whole with
http_headers = { "x-openai-actor-authorization" = "magpie" }. A config
that holds the headers as their own [model_providers.magpie.http_headers]
table keeps that table (a separate block the rewrite leaves), so the file
defined http_headers twice and writeTOML refused it. Reproduced in a temp
dir with exactly that message, in LF and CRLF files alike, so line
endings are not the cause. With only the subtable and no parent table the
same edit failed as "key http_headers is already defined". Dotted keys
inside the table (http_headers."x-org" = …) did not fail but were
dropped, the user's other headers with them.

the file has: in [name.key] each entry is set with SetTOMLKey's in-place
edit (other headers and comments kept); among dotted keys their lines are
kept as written and each entry set there; otherwise written inline,
byte for byte as before. putProvider passes the header as an Inline.
SetTOMLKey's body moved into setTOMLKeyLines so both share it.

Siblings checked: no other agent writes an inline table with
SetTOMLTable (kimi's providers.magpie and Codex's thread tables are
scalars only); the MCP writer (putCodex) already removes a server's
subtables before writing it. Not changed: a magpie provider spelled by
dotted keys outside its own table ([model_providers] magpie.x = …, or at
the top) still fails as "table magpie already exists"; that is not this
report's shape.

gui: lightweight mode no longer lets go of a main window that is open under another app's, so Command-Tab back to magpie finds it there (#1381, ttmouse)

Cause: lightweight mode (#580) let go of the main window once two of its
30 s looks found it "not shown", and it asked Wails' IsVisible, which on
the Mac is the window's occlusion state. A window the user had
Command-Tabbed away from, covered by the other app's window, counted as
closed: 30-60 s later its webview was dropped and the window closed, and
Command-Tab back to magpie found a blank shell or no window at all. Hidden
with magpie (Command-H) it went the same way, since hiding orders every
window out.

ordered in on any Space, covered or not, minimised, or open as magpie was
hidden (watchHide records those on NSApplicationWillHideNotification).
Only a window magpie closed itself is down. lighten (through lightShown)
and mainShown use it, so the Dock-while-open setting and a restart to
update also keep a covered window as open. Elsewhere windowUp is
IsVisible as before (visible there covers covered and minimised).

willz asked for a cap per window: a friend's account should stop at 50%

What the user sees: the account's pill still sets the cap for all its

redact: a value masked once is masked again wherever a request has it, whatever words are around it

The masking rules find a value by what is around it: DB_PASSWORD= before
a password, a bound an email may not touch (so an email that ends a
sentence isn't one). The vendor writes about a placeholder in words of
its own ("your password is {{SECRET_…}}", "I will write to {{EMAIL_…}}."),
the agent reads the value there (Restore), and on the next turn that text
is in the history, where no rule matches it, so it went out as written.

Now every value a placeholder was made for (redact's in-memory values,
bounded by maxValues, never written anywhere) is also matched as an exact
string in each string Mask and MaskJSON look at, and goes as the same
placeholder it had (same kind, same keyed hash), so history and vendor
caches stay stable:

- only from 8 characters (the assignment rule's minimum): the 3-character
  passwords the user:password@ rule takes, and the user's own words
  (which Options.Words matches everywhere already), are not;
- personal values only while personal masking is on, secrets only while
  secret masking is on;
- not as a piece of a longer value: a phone or card number with a digit
  beside it, an email inside a longer address (a full stop after it may
  end the sentence), a secret with a letter or digit against it;
- where a rule finds the same span, the rule's kind still wins, so
  nothing masked before changes placeholder;
- in what a vendor signed (7137feb4), the values masked elsewhere in the
  request go back as their placeholders as before, and so do known
  secrets, for a turn whose other copies were compacted away; known
  personal values don't, since a number the vendor wrote of its own
  (13800138000) may be one masked in another conversation, and masking
  it would break the signature.

A prefix index and a 4-byte bitset keep the lookup cheap: a ~1 MB body
masked in ~79 ms with 0, 1k or 200k known values alike (rules dominate).
Every route goes through redact.MaskJSON / Mask (chat, Responses,
Anthropic, Gemini, count_tokens, embeddings/rerank, the Codex backend,
image and video prompts), so each gets it; Scrub, the archive's, gets the
known secrets too.

Tests: TestEchoedValueMaskedNextTurn (gateway: two chat turns where the
fake vendor echoes the placeholders in other words; the second request
must not hold the password or the email, and keeps the first turn's
placeholders; then the echoed text alone through /v1/responses,
/v1/messages, count_tokens, Gemini generateContent, embeddings and the
Codex backend) fails on origin/main with the second turn sending
"…password is Mv4kestrelPass28, and I will write to
tomas.ng@quietfield.dev.". TestKnownValueMaskedInOtherWords and
TestKnownInSigned fail there too; TestShortValueNotMaskedEverywhere and

codex: a thread started on a provider config.toml no longer has opens again, through magpie (#1372, obstrux: "ChatGPT 无法加载 config.toml … Model provider `custom` not found")

The Codex app resumes a thread on the provider it was started on, kept in
Codex's state database (app-server thread_processor.rs:
merge_persisted_resume_metadata), whatever config.toml's model_provider is
now, and loads no config for it when config.toml has no table of that id
(core config: "Model provider `{id}` not found"). CC Switch puts every
third-party thread on "custom" and rewrites config.toml whole when it
switches, so a switch to its official provider leaves those threads with no
table, and the app can't open them. magpie never removes [model_providers.custom],
but nothing put it back either.

While magpie is wired into Codex (takeTables: set, Join and Sync), each
provider a thread in state_*.sqlite names that config.toml has none of
(table, inline or dotted) gets a table pointed at magpie's gateway, as
CC Switch's own tables already are. Codex's built-in providers (openai,
ollama, lmstudio, amazon-bedrock[-runtime], ollama-chat) and magpie's own
are left out, and a provider the user has stays as it is. The table stays
when Codex steps off magpie, as magpie's own does, for the threads that
name it. Not wired, nothing is written. sessions.CodexThreadProviders reads
the distinct model_provider of the threads table, read-only.

usage: a Kimi Code membership's k3 is counted at Kimi's API price for kimi-k3, not ≈¥0.000, and kimi-for-coding is unpriced rather than free (#1370, maicent: Kimi Code 的模型计费都是 0)

Why it was 0: magpie already counts a subscription's calls at the API list
price (a Claude or Codex account at its maker's, cf6b82f7). A Kimi Code
provider is looked up in its own models.dev catalog first, and models.dev
lists every model of kimi-code-plan-global / kimi-code-plan-cn at $0 (what
the membership charges per token), so k3, k3-256k, kimi-for-coding and
kimi-for-coding-highspeed were all "priced" at $0. The same $0 catalogs
were also among the maker catalogs, so MakerPrice("k3") was $0 too.

What changed (internal/provider/models.go):
- membershipCatalogs (the two Kimi Code plan catalogs) are never read for a
  price: ListPrice, MakerPrice and PricedName skip them.
- A provider served at a Kimi Code catalog prices its model as the Kimi API
  model it is (kimiCodeAPI), per Kimi Code's docs
  (https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/, read 2026-10-09): k3 and k3-256k are
  K3 -> kimi-k3; kimi-for-coding-highspeed is K2.7 Code HighSpeed ->
  kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed. models.dev's canonical_model_id agrees. The
  prices come from moonshotai's catalog, which matches Kimi's pricing page
  (https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat: kimi-k3 $3 in, $15 out,
  $0.30 cached, $3 cache write; kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed $1.90/$8/$0.38).
- kimi-for-coding is K2.8 Preview, which the Kimi API doesn't sell: it has
  no API price, so it is now unpriced (the "—" / "no known price" the GUI
  already shows) instead of ¥0.000. The user can give it a price with
  `magpie model price kimi-code/kimi-for-coding …` or in Names & levels.
- The alias is scoped to Kimi Code providers: a relay's own "k3" keeps its
  own catalog price; Moonshot pay-as-you-go's kimi-k3, an OpenCode free
  model ($0) and Codex's maker price are unchanged.
- PricedNameFor(provider, model): the Requests list's "API price
  reference" names kimi-k3 for a Kimi Code k3 (internal/gui/usage.go).
Docs: reference.md (What a model costs) and providers-accounts.md.

redact: a tool call's arguments are masked again, whatever their keys are called (7137feb4 let them out)

7137feb4 kept two kinds of strings from the masking rules, and both
reached what the agent itself wrote:

- Any object with a non-empty "signature", "thoughtSignature",
  "thought_signature" or "encrypted_content" counted as sealed by the
  vendor, so its strings went out unmasked but for the placeholders of
  values masked elsewhere. A tool_use input like a mail tool's
  {"signature":"Best, Bob","body":"DB_PASSWORD=… call 13800138000"} sent
  the password and the number in the clear; before 7137feb4 both were
  masked. A text block carrying a "signature" key did the same.
- Every key named id, …_id or …Id was kept, in a tool's arguments too:
  {"user_id":…,"phone_id":"13800138000"} went out as written.

encrypted content, reasoning.* details) or a part with Gemini's thought
signature counts as sealed, and nothing inside a tool_use input or a
functionCall's args does. In those arguments the keys are the tool's, so
no key keeps its value there (an encoded data: value still is); ids
outside them stay as 7137feb4 left them. A signed Gemini functionCall
part still goes back as written. The response side (writer.go) restores
ids again, which changes nothing for a real id and puts back a
placeholder the vendor echoed into a tool's user_id.

redact: what a vendor wrote and checks goes back as it wrote it — signed thinking and tool call ids (Jeremy.Zhou on Discord: OpenCode Zen answered 400 "invalid …" until 脱敏密钥 and 脱敏个人信息 were off)

Masking ran its rules over every string of the request except a fixed list
of keys, including two kinds of text the vendor itself wrote and checks
when it comes back:

- A thinking block (Anthropic's signature; also Gemini's thoughtSignature
  and Responses' encrypted reasoning). The vendor thinks about the
  placeholders it was given, the agent gets the values back (Restore), and
  on the next turn the rules masked that text again. Rules depend on
  what is around a value: "the password is {{SECRET_…}}" came back as
  "the password is hunter2abc1", which no rule matches without its
  DB_PASSWORD=, an email ending a sentence fails the email rule's bound,
  and a number the vendor wrote of its own ("13800138000") turned into a
  {{PHONE_…}}. The text no longer matched its signature, and Anthropic
  answers 400 "messages.1.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking`
  block" — and the value itself went to the vendor in the clear.
  Now an object that carries a non-empty signature, thoughtSignature,
  thought_signature or encrypted_content is masked only by putting back
  the placeholders of the values masked elsewhere in the same request
  (longest first): what the vendor wrote, its own words untouched.
- A chat tool result's tool_call_id. "id", "tool_use_id" and "call_id"
  were kept, "tool_call_id" wasn't. GLM's ids are call_ and 19 digits,
  and ~5% of them pass Luhn as a bank card number, so the tool message's
  id became call_-{{BANK_CARD_…}} while the assistant's tool_calls id
  stayed, and the upstream refused the orphaned tool result ("messages
  with role 'tool' must be a response to a preceeding message with
  'tool_calls'"). Now every key named id, …_id, …Id (and their plurals)
  is left alone.

Account masking (账号打码) is display only and doesn't touch requests.

claude: a client that goes away while the run answers its tool results takes the turn back, not the whole conversation to a new Claude Code (#1365)

What changed: ended() kept a turn's id (turnUUID, backKey) only until the
reply that called a tool. From then on, a client that went away while the
run answered the turn's tool results (a cut connection, or the user
interrupting to send a message queued during the tool call) could not be
rewound: letGo ended the run. The client's next request, its results sent
again or the next turn, logged "tool results no run waiting", and a new
Claude Code was told the whole conversation in one message, with every
image in it, which the model in #1365 took for new. Now the turn's id lasts
across its tool rounds, until a reply ends without calling a tool. letGo
rewinds the run to the turn's user message, its tool rounds with it, and
the run waits at the conversation before the turn. The next request is
resumed there (nextTurn's key is backKey) and told the turn since its user
message. resume logs "a turn taken back goes on in its run" after the
"no run waiting" line. A run started anew for the turn, or one with a call
still in the client's hands, is ended as before. Nothing else sent to
Anthropic changes.

Why: the issue's log showed "no run waiting" four times, then a whole-
conversation replay. On current main a queued message with an image is
sent beside the tool_result (checked with Claude Code 2.1.295 against a
local mock) and match keeps it with the result, so it does not break
matching by itself. The MCP call reaches magpie ~3ms after the tool
reply's message_stop, well inside match's 500ms grace. What drops the run
is a client going away during a tool-result continuation. The exact client
trigger in the report is not confirmed.

provider, gui: a MiniMax Token Plan's video windows say their count, "1 / 5 个视频", as MiniMax's own CLI does (#1366, IamMiao)

the day and 34 / 35 of the week, while magpie showed only a share (used
20%, 3%), and named the windows "Video · 24 hours" in English whatever
the language.

current_weekly_usage_count, the fields mmx-cli 1.0.27 types and shows
(dist/index.d.ts QuotaModelRemain; dist/mmx.mjs). It reads them as the
CLI does: usage_count has held what remains as well as what is used, so
it is taken as whichever the remaining percentage agrees with within a
point, and as no count when neither does or the total is 0 (the general
bucket, which keeps its share alone, as in the CLI). The window carries
the count as Amount of Limit, in "videos" for the video bucket, the way
WorkBuddy's credits are carried, so the Usage page says it before the
share, used or left as the reader picks: "1 / 5 个视频 · 已用 20%" or
"4 / 5 个视频 · 剩余 80%". A used-up window (status 2) counts all of it
used. The video windows aren't routing limits (Aside), so routing is
unchanged. "videos", "Video · 24 hours" and "Video · 7 days" are in zh,
zh-TW, ja and de.

Verified:
- TestReadMiniMaxPlanVideoCounts (new), built from the reporter's
  numbers with mmx-cli's field names: on origin/main's planquota.go it
  fails (video windows have Amount 0, Limit 0, Unit ""); passes now.
  TestReadMiniMaxPlan and the other planquota tests pass.

  counts as above, the general windows share-only, nothing cut, no
  sideways scroll. On origin/main's i18n.js it fails in both engines
  (names untranslated).

  usage-* GUI tests: 165/165 in Chromium and 165/165 in WebKit.
- gofmt -l (nothing), go vet ./internal/provider, GOOS=linux and

read live; which way usage_count runs is taken from mmx-cli's own

gateway: a Codex task sealed by a custom Responses provider still goes back to it after magpie forgets who answered the lead — a day later, after a restart, or after the lead's reply broke off — and the refusal says how to go on (#1367)

Autsunset (#1367): Codex with the lead and its subagents all on
xxxx/gpt-6-astra, a relay of ChatGPT Pro behind new-api. After quota
and overload errors, continuing the task was refused before xxxx was
asked: "This subagent's task was sealed by the ChatGPT backend that
answered its lead ... xxxx/gpt-6-astra is neither."

The cause: who sealed a task (#1109, #1237) was read only from the
affinity stick of the lead's conversation, and that record is lost in
three ways: it is kept 24 hours; a restart reads back only the latest
512 conversations from affinity.json; and a reply that breaks off after
its 200 (response.failed server_is_overloaded) deletes it (unanswered,
#733). Once lost, every later turn carrying a sealed message was
refused before anyone was asked, so nothing could answer the lead
again to remember it: the task stayed stuck.

When the sticks don't make the asked provider a reader, the usage log's
answers to the lead's thread and the request's own conversation in the
last 30 days now count too (loggedAnswers). A refused or failed call,
a title and Codex's own sign-in (Provider "openai" on /backend-api/codex,
still told of as the ChatGPT backend) count for nothing. The sibling
leadFirst, which puts the lead's ChatGPT account first in a group, reads
the lead's key or account from the log the same way. The refusal names
who answered the lead when the log knows, and both messages now say how
to go on: use the lead's model, or have the lead spawn the subagent again.

  400 and pass with the change; the sealed payload reaches xxxx as it
  came.

  an answer older than 30 days stay refused. With the 30-day bound
  removed it fails.

- TestSealedTaskFromChatGPTLeadStillRefused fails if Codex's own
  sign-in is not left out of the log's answerers.
- TestSealedReplyRefusedWhereTheLeadWasNotAnswered now expects the lead

feat(spaces): new shared UI — React web UI in the Mac app and an Electron app (preview) (#4893)

Adds one shared React web UI for Cua Spaces (apps/cua-spaces-web) and two
hosts for it.

- Mac app (SwiftUI): the native UI stays the default. The new UI is an
  opt-in experiment, "New UI (preview)", served in a WKWebView through
  WebUIBridge; live video stays native (VideoToolbox surfaces over the page).
- Electron app (apps/cua-spaces-desktop) for macOS, Windows and Linux: it
  answers the same bridge methods from the same app core (cua-spaces-ffi
  through Node UniFFI bindings, `pnpm native`), decodes video with
  WebCodecs, and on macOS draws the notch with a small Swift helper that
  shares its views with the Mac app (libs/spaces-notch-swift).

Release: the Electron app follows the cua-spaces version and is built and
published only for prerelease versions (X.Y.Z-suffix), as GitHub
prereleases never marked latest, with an opt-in beta-only updater
(electron-updater feed on cua-spaces-latest). Stable releases still ship
only the SwiftUI app. The Sparkle cutover to the Electron app
(make-appcast.sh --electron, the sparkle_electron workflow input, settings
migration, shared bundle id) is in place and off; see
apps/cua-spaces-desktop/docs/sparkle-cutover.md.

Also: parity fixes ported from the SwiftUI app; daemon handoff between the
two apps; Teleport's run listener lowered into the library; Keyvault
refusal messaging for apps not signed by Cua; polkit and Linux packaging
fixes; Windows build, launch-at-login and title bar fixes; sign-in without
a browser; a shared bridge contract checked for both hosts; and
ci-cua-spaces-macos.yml runs on pull requests again, now covering
libs/spaces-notch-swift. New app directories are FSL-1.1-MIT.

Co-authored-by: Francesco Bonacci <f@trycua.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cua-driver): say macOS list_apps omits unknown fields, and test it (#4925)

#4916 stopped sending null optional fields and the always-empty
`windows: []` in macOS list_apps, but the tool description still said
last_used is "otherwise null". The description now says optional fields
are omitted when unknown, the record builder is a function with unit
tests (omission, no `windows`, typed contract round-trip), and the
"Before updating to 0.35" checklist tells raw-JSON callers to treat
bundle_id, launch_path, kind and last_used as optional.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(cua-driver): filter list_windows by app and steer discovery away from host-wide lists (#4916)

In bench run v038 the unfiltered discovery calls were the largest cost an
agent paid for Cua Driver that it does not pay for Codex: list_windows
(~17k characters, every window on the host) and list_apps (~16k, every
installed app) came early in a trial and rode along in the context of
every later turn, about 18% of the tokens of a main-arm trial.

- list_windows takes an `app` filter on macOS, Linux and Windows: a
  case-insensitive substring of the app name, or the exact bundle id on
  macOS. Descriptions say to filter with `app` or `pid`.
- The macOS listing drops the driver's own windows (the cursor overlay).
- The initialize instructions point step 1 at `list_windows({app})` and
  say that unfiltered list_windows/list_apps list the whole host.
- list_apps on macOS points at list_windows({app}) for a pid and window
  id, no longer emits the always-empty `windows` array, and omits null
  optional fields as the contract allows.

The contract input stays the portable subset; `app` is a platform input.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

#4743 made get_window_state lean by default: markdown only, at most 250

perf(cua-driver): cap macOS screenshots at 1366 px by default, desktop captures included (#4917)

Sonnet 5.5 and the other high-resolution Claude models read images up to
2576 px at about w*h/750 tokens each, so the old 1568 px cap still sent
~1.8k tokens for a large window, and get_desktop_state sent the full
1920x1080 display (~2.8k tokens) unless a cap was passed. Screenshots
were about a third of a Cua Driver bench trial's tokens in run v038.

- DriverConfig's default max_image_dimension is 1366, the size Anthropic's
  computer-use guidance names as lower-cost with strong performance.
  Session and per-call overrides, zoom, and `0` for native are unchanged.
- get_desktop_state applies the effective cap (call > session > global)
  when no max_image_dimension is passed; pixels of the capped image already
  map back through its capture_id.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(cua-driver): return quiet actions after 300 ms instead of the full 1 s window watch (#4915)

Every macOS input action polled the window list for the whole 1000 ms
deadline when it opened nothing, the common case. In bench run v038 that
fixed wait was most of the ~1.3 s per press_key/hotkey and ~1.6 s per
AXPress click, and most of the 41 s of tool time per trial (run_actions
averages 25 steps per trial).

The result now waits for a change for at most 300 ms. When nothing has
changed by then it returns, and the rest of the deadline runs on a
detached thread that still holds the focus-steal lease. A window or
activation seen there is reported on the next action's result
("After the previous action returned, it opened new window(s): ...").
The next action and every intentional activation (foreground turns,
activate_pid, focus-without-raise, bring_to_front, launch_app) end the
detached remainder first, so its wildcard lease never reverts an
activation the driver asked for. Poll interval 50 -> 25 ms.

The WebKit text-field focus settle after an AXPress now counts the time
the window watch already spent.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(spacesd-client): assert proxy connection count before run (#4900)

The auto-mode exact CONNECT count is only deterministic when connect()
returns. StartProcess can open another proxied tunnel before hyper-util
returns the probe connection to the pool.

fix(spacesd): ask get_window_state for structured elements in the tool backend (#4908)

cua-driver #4743 made get_window_state return compact Markdown by default.
ToolBackend::a11y_tree still read `structuredContent.elements`, so on
Wayland (Omarchy/Hyprland), macOS and Windows the gRPC accessibility tree
came back with 0 nodes and the doctor's a11y.tree / a11y.act gates failed.
Pass tree_format "elements" explicitly.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci(hyprland-plugin): requalify the plugin for every Hyprland build (#4910)

* ci(hyprland-plugin): requalify the plugin for every Hyprland build

A daily workflow, which can also be dispatched by hand, reads the tracked
packages (hyprland, aquamarine, hyprutils, hyprlang, hyprcursor,
hyprgraphics, glibc, gcc, libgcc, libstdc++, libxkbcommon and wayland) in
Arch and in Omarchy edge, rc and stable. Each build is keyed by package
version and package SHA-256, so a same-version Arch rebuild counts as new.
The workflow also checks the latest Hyprland GitHub release.

For each new build and each plugin source tree (main, the latest Driver tag
and the source Omarchy packages), an Arch container on that channel's
mirrors does the following:

- builds the plugin with the production options against the exact headers;
- runs CTest;
- records the Hyprland binary, header-inventory, compiler and module hashes;
- loads the module into a headless Hyprland on vkms;
- runs a window-targeted background input smoke over cua-input-v3.

The results are merged into compatibility.json and matrix.md, which are
uploaded as an artifact and committed to the hyprland-plugin-compat branch
for Omarchy to read. A failure, or an Omarchy plugin whose exact pins the
channel no longer satisfies, opens or updates one tracking issue.

The workflow publishes no packages, kits or releases and touches no Omarchy
repository.

Refs #4909, #4216.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(hyprland-plugin): fix channel databases, CTest make, and source dedupe in requalification

- Clear the bootstrap's Arch sync databases and force -Syyuu so an older
  channel mirror (rc, stable) is not shadowed by If-Modified-Since.
- Install make for the CMake API probe test's nested configure.
- Identify plugin sources by their build inputs, so docs and the
  requalification tooling under the plugin directory do not split main from
  the release tags.
- Record the focused-holder TARGET as an observation: a headless seat has no
  keyboard or pointer device, so the active window holds no primary focus.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(hyprland-plugin): parse a clean CTest summary; retry failed requalifications

CTest prints "100% tests passed out of 20" without a failed count, which
the summary parser treated as no tests. Only a pass is now final in the
manifest: build-only and fail combinations are retried on later runs, so a
transient mirror error clears and a persistent failure is reported each day.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The executor updated current_step_id and current_step_index only in memory
and wrote them with the next checkpoint, after the step had finished. While a
long step ran, and after a hard crash, state.json still named the previous
step, so `workflow status` and the run payload reported the wrong occurrence.

target) is blocked with a failed result but no binding. The re-entry

fix(comfyui): hand the provider's API key to partner nodes (#21382)

### What this PR does

Before this PR: a ComfyUI workflow that uses a **partner (API) node** —
Flux Pro, GPT Image, Kling, Seedream and the rest of `comfy_api_nodes`
(283 classes on ComfyUI v0.39.2) — failed from the painting page with
`Unauthorized: Please login first to use this node.`, even with a Comfy
API key filled into the provider's API key field. The provider never
read that field (`apiKey` was "accepted for symmetry, never read"), and
the config builder deliberately skipped selecting a key.

After this PR: when a key is set, the transport puts it in the `/prompt`
body as `extra_data.api_key_comfy_org`. ComfyUI hands it to the
workflow's partner nodes, which send it upstream as `X-API-KEY`. Without
a key the request is byte-for-byte what it was.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Partner nodes are part of the workflows ComfyUI ships and that users
build — the shipped templates include them — so "a saved workflow is a
model" should hold for them too. `extra_data.api_key_comfy_org` is the
channel ComfyUI defines for exactly this: `execution.py` feeds it into
the hidden `API_KEY_COMFY_ORG` input,
`comfy_api_nodes/util/_helpers.py:get_auth_header` turns it into
`X-API-KEY`, and the Comfy API v2 spec describes the same `extra_data`
shape as shared by Comfy Cloud and local ComfyUI.

- **Never a header.** The ComfyUI server itself takes no auth, so the
builder still sends `headersWithoutCredentials` and no `Authorization`;
the key only travels in the prompt body, to the server the user
configured.
- **Not retained.** ComfyUI lists `api_key_comfy_org` in
`SENSITIVE_EXTRA_DATA_KEYS` and redacts it from `/history`.
- **Key selection.** The builder moves from `withoutCredential` to
`withSelectedApiKey`, so the key is selected (and rotated, and
attributed in the credential receipt) like any other provider's. With no
key, `resolveApiKey` returns the same `unknown` receipt ComfyUI gets
today. The model listing stays credential-free: listing workflows needs
no key.

The following alternatives were considered: a separate "Comfy API key"
setting (the provider already has an optional key field that did
nothing); sending the key as a header (the server ignores it, and nodes
read it only from `extra_data`).

Links to places where the discussion took place: N/A

### Breaking changes

NONE. Without a key nothing changes; with one, a workflow without
partner nodes ignores it.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- **Live check, ComfyUI v0.39.2+16.** ComfyUI was started with
`--comfy-api-base` pointed at a local logger that records request
headers, then a `OpenAIGPTImage1 → SaveImage` workflow was run twice
through `ComfyuiTransport` (submit + poll). The logged upstream calls to
`/proxy/openai/images/generations`:
  - without a key: `X-API-KEY: null`
  - with a key: `X-API-KEY: <the key>`

  `GET /history` afterwards does not contain the key.
- The existing test `routes ComfyUI without selecting or attributing a
stored key` encoded the old premise ("resolving one would attribute a
key the transport never sends"). The transport now does send it, so the
test is replaced by one asserting the key is selected, reaches
`providerSettings.apiKey`, and never becomes an `Authorization` header.
A transport test covers the body: the key in `extra_data`, no
`extra_data` for an empty or blank key, and the key in no header. Both
new tests fail on the merge base (2 failed / 221 passed).
- `pnpm typecheck:node`, `eslint`, `oxlint --deny-warnings` and `oxfmt
--check` are clean; `config.test.ts` plus the six ComfyUI suites are 223
passed.

of `comfyuiTransport.ts` and merge cleanly in either order.

fix(comfyui): redraw a seed the workflow set to randomize (#21381)

### What this PR does

Before this PR: a ComfyUI workflow whose seed is set to `randomize`
rendered the **same image every run** from the painting page. The
converter skipped each widget's `control_after_generate` mode, so with
no seed typed in, every run submitted the seed the workflow last saved
(and ComfyUI, seeing an identical prompt, may simply return its cached
output).

After this PR: a run redraws every number widget the workflow set to
`randomize`, exactly as the ComfyUI frontend does each time it queues.
`fixed`, `increment` and `decrement` keep the saved value, and a seed
typed into the painting page still wins.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The provider's contract is that the saved workflow decides the settings
and the run supplies the prompt. `randomize` *is* one of the workflow's
settings, and it is the default ComfyUI gives a new sampler — dropping
it turned "generate again" into "show me the same image again".

- **Where the mode is read.** A saved node carries it in two shapes, and
the real templates use both: positionally, after the widget it controls
(`[seed, "randomize", steps, …]`), and in `widgets_values_named` under
the literal key `control_after_generate`. In the named form the
controlled widget is the one the server declares the control on.
- **Promoted seeds.** The Qwen Image 2.1 templates promote the seed to
the subgraph instance, so the interior sampler's `seed` is *linked* and
its value comes from the instance, while the mode stays on the interior
widget the promotion proxies. Redrawing is therefore applied after the
inputs are resolved: any `randomize` widget whose final value is a plain
number is redrawn, and an input fed by another node (`PrimitiveInt`)
follows that node's own control instead.
- **The range** follows the frontend's `valueControl.ts`: the widget's
declared `min`/`max`/`step`, clamped to ±2^50. A legacy `PrimitiveNode`
keeps no range of its own, so only one feeding a seed is redrawn.
- **Only numbers.** On this machine's ComfyUI (v0.39.2+16),
`/object_info` declares `control_after_generate` on exactly three
inputs, all `INT`: `seed` (181 classes), `noise_seed`
(`KSamplerAdvanced`, `SamplerCustom`, `RandomNoise`) and
`PrimitiveInt.value`. A combo set to randomize keeps its saved option.
- Randomness is injected (`convertUiWorkflowToPrompt(…, { random })`),
so the conversion stays deterministic for every existing caller and
test; only the transport passes `Math.random`.

The following alternatives were considered: matching seed names only (it
misses `PrimitiveInt.value`, which the newer templates use); always
randomizing the seed when the user leaves it empty (it would override a
workflow that pins its seed on purpose with `fixed`).

Links to places where the discussion took place: N/A

### Breaking changes

NONE. `convertUiWorkflowToPrompt` takes an optional third argument;
without it the output is unchanged.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- **Live check, ComfyUI v0.39.2+16 on Apple Silicon.** Converting the
two Qwen Image 2.1 templates saved on this machine against the live
`/object_info`: they save their seed as `fixed`, and the conversion
leaves it unchanged; with the mode flipped to `randomize` in memory, two
conversions give two different seeds (before this PR, the saved seed
both times). Then two real runs through `ComfyuiTransport` (submit +
poll, 4 steps) of the randomized `image_qwen_image_2_1_t2i` submitted
different seeds and returned different images.
- New tests: positional and named modes, the declared range and step,
`fixed`/`increment`/`decrement`, a combo, a `PrimitiveNode` feeding a
seed vs. steps, a promoted subgraph seed, and through the transport: two
runs give two seeds, and a typed seed wins. The transport test fails on
the merge base (1 failed / 136 passed).

--check` are clean; the six ComfyUI suites are 139 passed.

<!-- Template from

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Telegram inbound polling could remain pending for grammY's 500-second
request timeout after a suspended network request. The channel was
marked connected before polling startup was confirmed, and a system
resume did not restart the stale poll.

After this PR:

Telegram `getUpdates` requests have a 45-second limit around a 30-second
long poll, without changing the timeout for sends or uploads. The
adapter reports connected only after grammY's `onStart`, and a system
resume coalesces recovery into one stop-and-restart of the existing bot.
Explicit disconnects still prevent polling from restarting.

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)`
format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes #21410

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- The 45-second request limit applies only to `getUpdates`, preserving
grammY's 500-second allowance for message sends and file uploads.
- Resume recovery briefly marks the channel disconnected while replacing
the stale poll, then returns to connected after grammY confirms startup.
- The lifecycle hook has a default no-op so existing channel adapters
require no unrelated changes.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Disabling Electron background throttling does not address a
main-process network request.
- Preventing system sleep would add persistent power usage without
guaranteeing recovery from a suspended request.
- Lowering grammY's global request timeout would also constrain large
file uploads.

Links to places where the discussion took place: #21410

### Breaking changes

None.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- This is a main-process transport fix with no UI changes, so
screenshots are not applicable.
- Focused tests: `pnpm exec vitest run --project main
src/main/ai/channels/adapters/__tests__/TelegramAdapter.test.ts
src/main/ai/channels/__tests__/ChannelManager.test.ts` (`29/29` passed).
- `pnpm check --plan` completed successfully.

files. One unrelated network E2E assertion failed because this machine
resolves `cherry-doctor-test.invalid`; an isolated rerun reproduced that
local DNS behavior. The affected test file is unchanged.
- The original Windows scenario (minimized app resumes receiving after
interacting with the desktop app) was not reproduced with a real
Telegram bot on this Mac. Deterministic transport/lifecycle tests cover
the recovery path; Windows CI remains the platform validation.
