fix(ai-sdk): omit non-msg_ Responses message ids on store:false replay (#20762)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

A Responses-compatible gateway can return a message item whose `id` is a
UUID (no `msg_` prefix). Cherry Studio accepts that response, stores the
id as `providerMetadata.openai.itemId`, and on the next turn
`convertToOpenAIResponsesInput` replays it as assistant input `id` under
`store: false`. Strict providers then reject the request with `Invalid
'id': message id must be a string starting with 'msg_'`, which surfaces
as a failed chat turn / `AI_TypeValidationError`.

After this PR:

Inbound Responses parsing still accepts non-empty UUID-shaped message
ids. On `store: false` replay, only `msg_`-prefixed message ids are
forwarded; other ids are omitted so compatible gateway history no longer
poisons later turns.

Fixes #20237

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Fix at the upstream owner (`@ai-sdk/openai` convert path via the
existing package patch), matching prior Responses compatibility patches
(annotations, assistant status, function_call item id).
- Omit non-`msg_` ids rather than inventing a `msg_<uuid>` rewrite,
because with `store: false` the id is not a server-side reference and
fabricating a prefix could confuse validators that treat it as an
existing item.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Normalize UUID ids to `msg_<uuid>` on receive or send — rejected
because it invents an id the provider never issued.
- Rewrite history downstream in Cherry message persistence — rejected;
the convert path is the owner that emits the invalid request field.
- Always drop assistant message ids when `store: false` — workable, but
unnecessarily changes OpenAI-native `msg_` round-trips that are already
valid.

Links to places where the discussion took place:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/20237

### Breaking changes

None.

- Contract covered by `openaiResponsesMessageIdPrefix.test.ts`: UUID
replay omits `id`; `msg_` replay keeps `id`; inbound UUID message id
still parses.
- Related existing coverage left green: function_call id drop, assistant
status, annotations, reasoning, sampling-params patches.

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

- On Linux with "Use system title bar" off, the main window and
sub-windows are frameless (`frame: false`). React draws its own
min/max/close buttons and drives them over IPC.
- Sub-windows ignore `app.use_system_title_bar`, so they stay frameless
even when it is on. In that case `useHasWindowControls()` returns false,
and the sub-window ends up with **no window controls at all**.
- With the system title bar on, the native bar sits above Cherry's own
44px top bar, giving two stacked bars.

After this PR:

- **Main window (Linux):**
- "Use system title bar" off → `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` plus
`titleBarOverlay` (44px, matching `AppShellTabBar`'s `h-11`). Electron
draws the controls with the system's Freedesktop icon theme (Electron
44, electron/electron#52461).
  - "Use system title bar" on → native frame, unchanged.
- **Sub-windows (Linux):** always use WCO (37px, matching
`TITLE_BAR_HEIGHT_PX`). Pooled standbys are created from static registry
options only, so they cannot read the preference. As a side effect,
sub-windows now always have controls.
- **Theme sync:** overlay `color` / `symbolColor` follow `nativeTheme`
through `setTitleBarOverlay` (new
`src/main/core/window/linuxTitleBarOverlay.ts`). It is only applied to
windows created with an overlay, which avoids the #5571-style error.
- **Renderer:**
- On Linux, `WindowControls` renders a spacer the width of the overlay
instead of buttons. The width comes from `env(titlebar-area-x/width)`
rather than a hardcoded number, and is 0 when the window has no overlay.
  - The sub-window's `--window-controls-width` uses the same expression.
  - `useHasWindowControls()` is now Windows-only.
- **Leading (left-side) controls:** when GNOME's `button-layout` puts
the buttons on the left, the main window reuses the macOS traffic-light
layout: a sidebar spacer plus a tab-strip inset. The sub-window title
bar pads by `env(titlebar-area-x)`. A new
`useLeadingWindowControlsOverlay` hook follows `geometrychange`, so the
layout updates live when the button layout changes.
- **MCP browser window (Linux):** now uses WCO (42px, theme-synced)
instead of drawing its own buttons in `tabbarHtml.ts`. Its tab bar
BrowserView can read `env(titlebar-area-*)` too, so it reserves the
overlay on either side.
- Windows and macOS behavior is unchanged.

Refs #21413 (partial: see reviewer notes for remaining acceptance items)

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- The overlay `color` is fully transparent so Cherry's own top bar shows
through. Its RGB is still chosen to contrast the glyph: Electron's Linux
frame forces `color` opaque and uses it as the inverted glyph color on
hover (Breeze style). A transparent black made hovered glyphs invisible
on the dark hover pill.
- Sub-windows do not read `app.use_system_title_bar`. Before this PR
they did not honor it either. Supporting it would need WindowManager
pool standbys to accept dynamic options, which is an upstream change
left out of scope.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Removing the "Use system title bar" option entirely. It was kept as a
fallback for desktops where WCO is unverified (e.g. KDE, which offers
server-side decorations). Removal touches the preference classification,
migration mappings, settings UI and i18n, so it belongs in a separate PR
once WCO is validated.
- Keeping the React-drawn buttons. That means continuing to maintain
button styling, interaction and maximize-state sync per desktop.

Links to places where the discussion took place: #21413. Approach
mirrors t3code's desktop window (`titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` + transparent
`titleBarOverlay` + `env(titlebar-area-*)` insets).

None. The Linux custom title bar mode changes appearance: native-themed
controls replace the React ones. The preference and its restart-to-apply
flow are unchanged.

### Special notes for your reviewer

Verified on Ubuntu GNOME, native Wayland, 1.333 fractional scale, Breeze
GTK/icon theme, right-side buttons:
- Through CDP, `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` is true for
both window types. The main window overlay is 72×44 on the right.
- The `WindowControls` spacer occupies exactly x=888–960 (the overlay
area), and no title-bar control overlaps it.
- Hovering a control inverts its glyph (Breeze style) in the current
build, confirmed by eye. The earlier `#01000000` overlay color showed no
inversion.
- Left-side buttons (`button-layout 'close,minimize,maximize:icon'`):
- Before the fix: the overlay (x=0–72) covered the sidebar avatar and
the start of the first tab.
- After the fix: the avatar moves below the 44px spacer, and the first
tab starts at x=74. In Settings (no sidebar), the strip pads by 74px.
The sub-window title bar pads by 80px.
  - Switching back restores the original layout live.
- MCP browser on Linux: the tab bar sees the overlay (safe area 1128 of
1200 wide). The tab row pads 80px on the side with the buttons, and the
self-drawn controls are hidden. That the overlay is drawn above the tab
bar BrowserView was confirmed by eye.

Not yet verified / follow-ups:
- X11/XWayland, KDE, and toggling the preference back and forth.
- Blurriness of the native frame when the system title bar is on
(fractional scaling) is a separate issue, not addressed here.

<!-- Template from

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

On macOS, Apple `posix_spawn` rejects otherwise valid pipe descriptors
above 10239 with `EBADF`. A Claude Code Agent session could therefore
fail synchronously while creating its three stdio pipes after Cherry
Studio had accumulated enough open file descriptors. The synchronous
throw also bypassed the existing child-process `error` diagnostics.

After this PR:

`ClaudeCodeProcessManager` retries a synchronous macOS `EBADF` once with
Cherry Studio's unchanged current UID, which selects libuv's fork/exec
path while preserving the existing stdin/stdout/stderr pipe contract. If
either a non-recoverable initial spawn or the fallback still fails, the
existing structured diagnostics record the spawn phase without logging
raw executable paths.

Refs #20407

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The failure is caused by the open libuv/macOS limitation tracked in
[libuv#5204](https://github.com/libuv/libuv/issues/5204), not by an
invalid Cherry descriptor. Keeping stdin piped is also required for the
Claude CLI to observe parent shutdown, while stdout and stderr are part
of the SDK transport and diagnostics contract. Passing the unchanged
current UID is the narrowest available Node/libuv option that selects
fork/exec only after the proven macOS failure.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Normal startup still uses `posix_spawn`; the fallback is limited to a
synchronous `EBADF` on macOS and retries only once.
- The retry uses the current UID, so it does not change the child's
identity or the three-pipe transport contract.
- This PR covers the Claude Code boundary that Cherry owns directly. The
public diagnostic does not identify which registered Agent runtime
failed, so it links to #20407 without changing the issue state.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Removing or redirecting a stdio pipe was rejected because it would
break the Claude SDK transport, diagnostics, or parent-death behavior.
- Forcing every macOS spawn through fork/exec was rejected because the
workaround is only needed after the specific `posix_spawn` failure.
- Patching DSH downstream was not included:
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-sdk-client` currently owns its direct three-pipe spawn
and exposes no spawn injection or spawn-options hook. Upstream master
has the same boundary, so DSH coverage requires an upstream API or a
separately reviewed dependency patch.
- Pi runtime startup is in-process. Its Bash tool has a separate
operation-scoped spawn boundary and is not changed here.

Links to places where the discussion took place: #20407,
https://github.com/libuv/libuv/issues/5204

> ### Branch strategy

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

On Linux desktops that Chromium does not recognise (Hyprland, Sway, i3,
…), `safeStorage` falls back to the `basic_text` backend.
`loadDesktopIdentity()` rejects that backend, so enabling LAN access /
creating a connection code fails with `OS-protected key storage is
unavailable`, and LAN discovery silently becomes `unavailable`. This
happens even when gnome-keyring or KeePassXC is installed, because
Chromium only picks libsecret for GNOME-family desktops.

After this PR:

- `configureChromiumFlags()` appends `--password-store=gnome-libsecret`
on non-KDE Linux sessions unless the user already passed
`--password-store`. An installed Secret Service is now used; when none
is running, Chromium falls back as before. KDE sessions keep Chromium's
own KWallet detection.
- `loadDesktopIdentity()` falls back to storing the identity unencrypted
(mode `0600`, new path key `feature.remote_access.plain_identity_file` →
`remote-identity.key`) when no OS key store is available, instead of
failing.
- An existing identity is never regenerated: a sealed identity whose key
store has disappeared still errors, and a plaintext identity keeps being
used after a key store appears. Replacing the identity would unpair
every device.

Fixes #21365

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- The plaintext fallback weakens protection of the desktop's Ed25519
private key to file permissions only. This was accepted so that remote
access works in every environment; secure storage is still used whenever
it exists.
- The fallback lives in `deviceIdentity.ts` rather than via
`safeStorage.setUsePlainTextEncryption(true)`, because that switch is
global and would change MCP OAuth's deliberate "memory-only when no key
store" behaviour.
- The `password-store` switch is app-wide, so other `safeStorage` /
cookie data on affected desktops will now use libsecret when available.
Existing `v10` (basic_text) data stays decryptable under the libsecret
backend.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Only improving the error message: leaves Hyprland/Sway users without a
working feature.
- Re-implementing Chromium's desktop-environment detection exactly:
fragile; "not KDE → libsecret" is equivalent for recognised GNOME-family
desktops and an improvement for unrecognised ones.
- Auto-migrating a plaintext identity into the key store once one
appears: not needed to fix the issue; left out to keep the change small.

Links to places where the discussion took place: #21365

None.

prompt for unlock on first `safeStorage` use. This matches GNOME-family
desktop behaviour today.

feat(claude-code): identify Cherry Studio in agent CLI User-Agent via CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP (#21411)

## Problem

Cherry Studio's agent mode runs the Claude Agent SDK, whose subprocess
sends API requests with a Claude Code CLI User-Agent:

```
claude-cli/<ver> (external, sdk-ts, agent-sdk/<sdk-ver>)
```

There is no embedder identifier in that string, so from the network side
(gateways, proxies, observability tooling) **agent-mode traffic from
Cherry Studio is indistinguishable from a standalone Claude Code CLI**.
The VS Code extension avoids this by setting its entrypoint
(`claude-vscode` appears in its UA) — Cherry Studio currently has no
equivalent marker.

This matters for anyone routing Cherry Studio through an LLM gateway or
corporate proxy: usage attribution, per-client rate policies and
analytics all collapse agent-mode traffic into the Claude Code bucket.

## Solution

The Agent SDK documents an env var for exactly this (`Options.env` JSDoc
in `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`):

> SDK consumers can identify their app/library to include in the
User-Agent header by setting:
> `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP` - Your app/library identifier (e.g.,
"my-app/1.0.0", "my-library/2.1")

The value is appended to the User-Agent as `client-app/<value>`.

This PR sets it in `buildEnvironment`:

```ts
CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP: `cherry-studio/${app.getVersion()}`,
```

Resulting User-Agent from agent-mode requests:

```
claude-cli/<ver> (external, sdk-ts, agent-sdk/<sdk-ver>, client-app/cherry-studio/1.9.x)
```

Also adds the key to `BLOCKED_ENV_KEYS` so per-agent user `env_vars`
cannot spoof or clear the identifier.

## Notes

- One env var + one blocked-key entry; no behavior change for requests
themselves.
- The chat/completions side is unaffected — it already identifies as
`CherryStudio/<version>` in the User-Agent. With this change both modes
of the app are attributable downstream.
- Verified against the SDK's documented UA construction
(`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT ?? "cli"` + `agent-sdk/<ver>` +
`client-app/<ver>` segments).

## Testing

- New unit test `environment.test.ts` asserts `buildEnvironment` sets
`cherry-studio/<version>` (electron `app.getVersion` mocked).
- Full existing suite for `src/main/ai/runtime/claudeCode/__tests__/`
passes (173 tests).
- `tsc --noEmit` (node project), `oxlint --deny-warnings`, `eslint` all
clean on changed files.

selection, diagnostic and external-open callbacks. The package owns

and host-provided PDF fonts/CMaps. Hosts retain ownership of source byte
buffers; XLSX copies its input before transferring it to a worker. PDF
waits for loading-task destruction before terminating the worker so
pdf.js can release fonts.
- Adds PDF/DOCX/image pinch zoom and spreadsheet tap selection. Zoom
preserves its focal point, slow PDF pinches retain sub-step changes, and
a touch selection is committed once even when the browser dispatches a
following click.
- Handles PPTX XML BOMs on WebKit while retaining tolerant parsing of
optional parts. An empty presentation fails clearly; an individual
slide-render error keeps the remaining presentation readable.
- Makes host callbacks stable internally and sends each terminal failure
once through `onDiagnostic`, followed by `onError` for host state.
Size-limit diagnostics use warning severity; desktop diagnostics
preserve actual `Error` objects for reporting.
- Provides explicit host options for PDF outline overlays, DOCX
fit-width zoom and Symbol/Wingdings normalization, content bottom
insets, and opaque XLSX headers. These are opt-in: desktop layout, zoom
defaults, header appearance and inset placement remain the default. The
host chooses PDF layout from actual available width. Content insets
protect PDF outlines and reserve space below XLSX's fixed footer
controls.

package typechecking and builds, selects preview tests after UI changes,

cancelled results, but cannot interrupt an in-flight desktop IPC read or
synchronous engine parsing.

adapter to renderer internals.
- Changing desktop layout defaults would introduce unrelated visual

feat(knowledge): surface document-processor progress and give the reading status its own label (#21386)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:
- The knowledge data-source status column mixed three unrelated
in-progress labels: **Processing** (a catch-all that also covers the
*longest* phase — the remote document-processor wait of up to 30
minutes), a **reading** status rendered via
`knowledge.rag.file_processing` — the *file-processor config section
title* reused as a live status — and **Embedding**.
- Only the embedding phase ever showed a percentage. During the
document-processor wait the row showed a bare, static "Processing" with
zero feedback, even though the check job already reads the processor
job's progress on every 5s poll round (`reportWaitingProgress`) — it was
simply never surfaced to the renderer.

After this PR:
- The check job mirrors the linked file-processing job's progress into a
new per-item shared-cache key
`knowledge.item.file_processing_progress.<itemId>` — written every poll
round with a 60s TTL (comfortably outlives the 5s cadence, so the value
self-collects if polling ever stops), and deleted when the wait
completes so no stale number lingers through the `processing` →
`reading` flip. The row renders ` NN%` next to the label — exactly the
embedding percentage's established shape. Processors that report no
progress leave the key absent and the bare label shows, unchanged.
- The `reading` status gets its own label key
(`knowledge.data_source.status.reading`, "Reading" / 读取文档中) instead of
borrowing `knowledge.rag.file_processing`, so the column reads as one
pipeline: waiting → processing NN% → reading → embedding NN% → ready.

Fixes #N/A

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:
- **Mirror the child job's progress rather than derive a synthetic
one.** Local PDF OCR reports real per-page percentages and remote
processors report upload/convert milestones; a pollRound-derived
estimate would be fabricated progress. Where a processor reports
nothing, showing nothing is honest — same contract as the embedding
percentage.
- **TTL on every write (60s) instead of no-TTL + linger-TTL like the
embedding key.** The embedding key must survive slow (>60s) batches
mid-run, so it is TTL-free while active. Here the writer re-runs every
5s by construction, so a TTL longer than the poll cadence can never
blank mid-wait, and any abnormal end (app quit, abandoned recovery job,
deleted item) self-collects without extra cleanup paths.
- **One explicit delete site** (wait completed → indexing scheduled).
The other terminal paths flip the item to `failed`, which closes the
renderer's status gate immediately; only the completion path leaves the
row at `processing` until its next poll observes `reading`, which is
exactly where a stale percentage would be visible.

The following alternatives were considered:
- A progress bar / richer per-row phase widget — larger UI surface for
marginal gain over `label NN%`, which the embedding phase already
established as the house pattern.
- Making the 30-minute `FILE_PROCESSING_MAX_WAIT_MS`, poll cadence, or
queue concurrency configurable in the RAG "Advanced settings" — out of
scope here (and counter to keeping the advanced section to
set-and-forget internals); the labels/percentage fix addresses the
observability complaint independently.

None. New cache key is additive; label key swap is renderer-internal
with all 13 locales translated.

- Red-checked: the five new/changed assertions (mirror written, mirror
cleared on completion, reading label key ×2, processing percentage
render) all fail with `AssertionError` on the parent implementation; the
two guard tests (no mirror when processor reports nothing; bare label)
pass on both, as guards should.
- `knowledge.rag.file_processing` keeps its only remaining role: the
file-processor selector's section title in the RAG config panel.

commits.message:
Add opt-in output token replay for OpenAI requests (#52742)

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `output_token_replay` feature to request `output.encrypted_content` from OpenAI providers.
- Preserve encrypted message and tool-call output, message and function-call status, and output-text `annotations` and `logprobs` through history and replay. Update the generated protocol schemas and SDK types.
- Strip output ciphertext from requests to other providers while retaining it in stored history, including after replay is disabled. Remove encrypted content from memory extraction inputs.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for the feature/provider combinations, metadata replay across follow-up requests, and history preservation when resuming with replay disabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: 77729a021b6771933402aebe74ece8eb39c057e2

Allow model catalogs to override incremental tool notices (#52736)

## What changed

Add `model_messages.tools.incremental_tools` overrides for the update hint, tool and namespace removal headers, and namespace instruction update and clearing messages. Missing, null, or over-512-byte values fall back to bundled wording; empty strings omit static text while retaining runtime names and instructions.

Substitute `{name}` in namespace message templates and append runtime instructions verbatim. Wording changes alone do not trigger tool catalog updates.

## Testing

Extend unit tests and MCP request-history snapshots to cover custom wording, empty notices, tool removal and restoration, and namespace instruction changes and clearing without repeating unchanged tools or notices.

GitOrigin-RevId: 22dea0a6fb4cfcd646f5e65346424834c8b7d5a2

Report terminal program status with OSC 7501 (#52725)

## Why

Lifecycle status reporting was limited to direct iTerm2 sessions. OSC 7501 lets other terminals receive Codex's program state.

## What changed

- Emit OSC 7501 with `app=codex` and states `idle`, `working`, or `blocked` whenever stdout is a terminal, including multiplexed sessions. Report `blocked` when user action is required.
- Continue emitting iTerm2's OSC 21337 status and bounded activity details in direct iTerm2 sessions.
- Clear status before handing the terminal to an external program, as well as on suspension and exit, and re-emit the current state after returning.

## Testing

Add coverage for OSC 7501 encoding, combined iTerm2 output, clearing both protocols, and protocol selection across terminal and multiplexer environments. Update lifecycle tests and status snapshots for the new protocol.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6d2a6885687b0e7af825e954fab72db0765c9a07

Add observers for initial exec-server connection attempts (#52724)

## What changed

Expose `Environment::observe_connection_attempts` and `ConnectionAttemptOutcome` to report elapsed time and success, failure, or cancellation for initial connections. Measure from the end of provisioning through client installation, including connection retries.

The first registered observer wins. Past attempts and reconnections are omitted.

## Testing

Extend tests to assert failure followed by success when startup is retried, and a single cancellation notification when an environment is replaced during startup.

GitOrigin-RevId: 88300f38dcf9428b824c5ff36aa1b40d7d466b6f

Add opt-in gRPC over stdio for the code-mode host (#52723)

## What changed

- Add `grpc+stdio://` as a host transport and the disabled-by-default `code_mode_host_grpc` feature flag to select it.
- Share a lazy HTTP/2 channel and host process across code-mode sessions while keeping session state isolated.
- Use HTTP/2 keepalives to detect unresponsive hosts, kill and reap disconnected children, and spawn a fresh host on reconnect. Exit the host when its stdio connection closes.

## Testing

Add coverage for shared-host session isolation, host exit on stdin EOF, and recovery after an unresponsive host is reaped. Exercise nested tool calls with both legacy stdio and gRPC stdio, asserting that the feature flag selects the expected transport.

GitOrigin-RevId: 31389d8540de236b8e0571d3c24e29e117b75c4a

Explain session creation failures during server shutdown (#52721)

## Why

Graceful shutdown rejects new sessions with an invalid-request error. Give clients a structured shutdown reason and show command center users why session creation is paused.

## What changed

- Add `data: {"reason":"serverShuttingDown"}` to app-server shutdown admission errors while retaining JSON-RPC code `-32600`.
- Show a dedicated shutdown message explaining the wait for active turns and automatic reconnection for non-embedded servers. Recognize older servers by their exact draining message only when error data is absent, and preserve retained-worktree cleanup guidance.
- Keep the command center reconnect presentation when a shutdown error covers the initial overview and no conversation is open.

## Testing

Extend admission and WebSocket shutdown assertions, add embedded and daemon shutdown message snapshots, and cover reconnection with a shutdown error over the initial command center.

GitOrigin-RevId: f167144c0ddc77872afdf3daac8bb1c89f3425b4

Migrate the Windows MXC sandbox to split MXC crates (#52707)

## Why

PSEC API symbols can be present on transitional Windows builds where MXC is not enabled. Availability detection needs to verify that a native process security environment can actually be created.

## What changed

- Replace `mxc-sdk` with pinned `appcontainer_common`, `learning_mode_windows`, and `wxc_common` dependencies, and update Cargo and Bazel dependency metadata.
- Use MXC's cached create/close probe for `is_available()` and query native deny-path support through `SecurityEnvironmentApi` before launching requests with denied paths.
- Adapt request construction and the existing policy test to the vector-based environment field, and update the sandbox documentation.

GitOrigin-RevId: e8cc6a35d46884d0a069b747d33e711512ec1596

Retry bootstrap GETs through the system proxy after request failures (#52702)

## Why

Account discovery and cloud configuration GETs can fail after connecting but before receiving response headers. These request failures previously bypassed system proxy fallback.

## What changed

Allow bootstrap GETs to retry through the system proxy on request errors, alongside the existing connection failure and timeout cases, when fallback is enabled.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for connections closed before response headers on `accounts/check` and `config/bundle`, verifying successful proxy retries with the original request headers. Extend coverage to ensure HTTP responses with status `401`, `403`, `407`, `429`, or `503` do not trigger fallback, and network policy denials prevent requests to both the origin and proxy.

GitOrigin-RevId: ac34c3bcfe3bd81c905a7e616d8b821879fbe2c9

Update the exec-server stable compatibility baseline to Codex 0.162.1 (#52700)

Use Codex `0.162.1` instead of `0.156.1` for
`exec-server-stable-release-test`, updating the Bazel release archive version,
checksum, and repository reference.

GitOrigin-RevId: 304108b223da1e5506483f53c476a55a8f31ce71

Fix marketplace path matching for Windows junctions (#52696)

## Why

Equivalent local source paths can fail to match an already-added marketplace, and redirected managed roots can lose their managed classification on Windows.

## What changed

- Compare local marketplace sources after filesystem normalization.
- Reuse the resolved request path when locating an existing local marketplace so retargeting a configured junction does not switch the returned root.
- Accept both the configured managed root and its canonical target on Windows while continuing to reject unowned aliases to that target.

## Testing

Add Windows regression tests for canonical and legacy path spellings, retargeted local-source junctions, and redirected managed roots with unowned aliases.

GitOrigin-RevId: f1ae46e8e7384075ed1baa6b33b2821f795e17f8

Forward per-turn Cyber access programs to Guardian (#52689)

## What changed

Pass the parent turn's `cyber_access_program` to Guardian reviewers and asynchronous classifiers. Use `daybreak_blue` for either Daybreak selection, preserve `standard`, and omit `access_programs` when no program is selected.

Capture the selection with the owning turn so asynchronous observations retain it across later turns. Resolve classifier programs using current authentication and the same provider and API-key feature policy as ordinary model requests.

## Testing

Add regression tests for program changes across reused reviewer sessions with API-key and ChatGPT authentication, snapshot and conversation classifiers at low and high risk, and enabled, disabled, and unsupported-provider API-key policies. Verify parent requests retain their selected program.

GitOrigin-RevId: 447f306df3a6bd6805464b819950690c751b04b4

Add opt-in retention for turn tool outputs (#52686)

## What changed

Add an optional `retain` flag to `TurnToolOutput` for `turn/start`. When set to `true`, pass the output to the core with a retention annotation to request retention in the thread's model history. The flag defaults to `false`, preserving existing behavior.

Update the generated JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python bindings to expose the flag.

## Testing

Add an integration test verifying that a retained tool output reaches the model and preserves client-authored sender metadata in persisted history, including the receiver message ID.

GitOrigin-RevId: 52893a8fcb308f26e77ba8f0bee9990073b26d54

Preserve code mode cancellation during output serialization (#52685)

## Why

Reentering V8 during termination can replace uncatchable cancellation with a catchable JavaScript exception, allowing a script to continue after cancellation.

## What changed

Skip JSON conversion and exception throwing while V8 execution is terminating, preserving cancellation through `image()` getters and JSON fallback.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for cancellation during JSON fallback and reentrant image getters, including prompt termination through the standalone host and continued usability of another session. Extend serialization error tests to cover failing image getters alongside circular JSON.

GitOrigin-RevId: f03dd131a62724106fad96111292ddf5b9dc99f6

Validate Windows sandbox accounts before password repair (#52682)

## Why

A credential mismatch can trigger setup that rotates both sandbox account passwords. Before allowing repair, validate the account that logged on successfully and ensure that neither account has been replaced or has an unowned runtime registration.

## What changed

- Validate runtime records and successful logon tokens, checking account SIDs, rejecting administrators, and requiring enabled `CodexSandboxUsers` membership.
- Before repair, verify recorded account SIDs and reject existing same-family package registrations for unrecorded accounts. Propagate package-query failures while allowing initial migration when no registrations exist.

## Testing

Add tests for malformed records and unrelated logon errors, plus an ignored disposable Windows Sandbox fixture covering successful logons, group membership, SID changes, migration, and unowned registrations.

GitOrigin-RevId: bafedb52cf9bd484250ccac3b163d2041891283f

Reject reserved Serde JSON keys in code mode (#52681)

## Why

JavaScript objects containing Serde's reserved JSON keys can be reinterpreted during deserialization, allowing nested `RawValue` markers to bypass the parser's normal recursion limit.

## What changed

Reject `$serde_json::private::RawValue` and `$serde_json::private::Number` object keys before passing V8's serialized JSON to `serde_json`. Report a `reserved JSON object key` serialization error while continuing to allow marker text in strings and longer keys.

## Testing

Add runtime regression coverage for nested and escaped marker keys, recursion limits, normal JSON conversion, and session recovery without overwriting stored values. Extend the host-backed integration test to verify that stored values remain available across turns after rejection.

GitOrigin-RevId: 27ddce08e1ffe98ec9dffe02473a815ceae2cc89

Add timeout-aware exec-server configuration reads (#52679)

## Why

Remote configuration reads need a bounded wait without disrupting valid in-flight work on connections that cannot reconnect.

## What changed

- Add `read_environment_config_with_timeout` to `ExecServerClient` and `Environment`, bounding RPC sending and receiving after connection establishment. Local reads retain their existing behavior.
- Return a typed `ExecServerError::RpcTimedOut` and classify it as retryable for read-only preparation.
- Share timeout handling with environment-info requests. Close the timed-out transport and request recovery only when a reconnect strategy exists; otherwise, keep the connection open.

## Testing

Add a regression test verifying that a timed-out configuration read preserves an in-flight stdio read and allows subsequent reads on the same connection, including after a late response.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6785d5846f4c3b07a6e7c505e359238609c3a6b6

Refresh persisted capability roots from owner-provided configuration (#52676)

## Why

Resumed threads can retain stale capability root locations when the current environment supplies an explicit owner configuration. Matching roots from that configuration previously could not refresh persisted thread roots.

## What changed

Refresh persisted roots from the current attachment when both the root ID and environment ID match, including roots selected by owner-provided configuration. Preserve persisted locations when no matching root is supplied, and continue using the owner's selected roots rather than the executor's shared roots.

Apply the same merge behavior to capability root inspection and per-step resolution.

## Testing

Extend the remote environment regression test to cover owner-provided configurations with and without refreshed roots, including an executor root location that differs from the owner's selection.

GitOrigin-RevId: ad3a639924b348d6d5337ccc64dc8c08234276e3

Move the exec-server test fixture into shared test support (#52674)

## What changed

Move `ExecServerProcess` into `core_test_support::exec_server` and update the sandbox, plugin, access, and turn-input tests to use it. Preserve the fixture's startup timeout, temporary `CODEX_HOME`, WebSocket URL discovery, and child-process cleanup.

GitOrigin-RevId: 152de3a83f4ad39e2c1223e15438608dba452850

Add retention annotations to submitted tool outputs (#52671)

## What changed

Add `TurnInput::AnnotatedResponseItem` with a caller-supplied `retain` annotation. For function-call outputs, `retain: true` sets `client_authored` history metadata while keeping annotations out of model requests. Accept annotated items through the existing turn submission paths, including continuation.

## Testing

Add an integration test covering retention metadata during turn start, steering, idle submission, and rollout storage. Verify that ordinary outputs remain unmarked and model requests contain neither `retain` nor `client_authored`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7285dde31149b17b0dcf31d4ea1c7cba66d9efe6

Prevent brokered credential aliases from bypassing MITM hooks (#52661)

## Why

A credential bound to a host with MITM hooks could also be used at an alias without hooks, allowing the proxy to inject the real credential without enforcing hook policy.

## What changed

Reject requests to unhooked aliases when their selected brokered credentials are also bound to a hooked host. Check both HTTP forwarding and MITM requests before replacing dummy credentials, returning `403` with `blocked-by-mitm-hook` for denied requests.

Use the same destination and credential-selection rules for alias checks and injection, including configured URL prefixes, safe paths, equivalent credentials, merged Basic authentication fields, and environment scope.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for built-in and configured provider aliases, IPv6 destinations, credential selection, and unrelated credentials. Add an agent-started proxy test that verifies credential masking and alias denial.

GitOrigin-RevId: 12be41654761cedcf87b170f7661d6566f7a864e

Handle completion events in either order in shell snapshot tests (#52660)

## Why

A tool can return before its background watcher emits `ExecCommandEnd`. Waiting for that event first can discard an earlier `TurnComplete`, causing the shell snapshot test helper to time out.

## What changed

Update `run_tool_turn_on_harness` to track both the matching `ExecCommandEnd` and `TurnComplete` in a single event loop, returning only after both have arrived regardless of order.

GitOrigin-RevId: c9b749a46eda1244aa3e80fd88b663d110d67d1b

Add an opt-in feature for subagent model context defaults (#52659)

## What changed

Add the disabled-by-default `subagent_default_context_limits` feature and expose it in the configuration schema. When enabled, shared configuration for spawning and resuming subagents clears inherited `model_context_window` and `model_auto_compact_token_limit` overrides so subagents use their model's default context window and auto-compaction threshold.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5168ae2b4fbe72c533d8c6152922a8bceb2c5cbd

Bound local exec-server output draining after process exit (#52652)

## Why

A local command can exit while a descendant keeps its inherited output pipes open, delaying `exec_command` completion and turn completion.

## What changed

Start the bounded output drain when a local exec-server process exits, whether exit is reported by an event or recovered through `process/read`. Remote execution continues waiting for output closure so buffered or delayed output is retained.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for local shell snapshot execution completing before a descendant releases stdout, preserving the foreground output and exit code. Add remote event-stream cases that retain output arriving after both reported and recovered process exit.

GitOrigin-RevId: d38bcd394be42cf48d2af02733e883b02d1dd62f

Limit daemon feature compatibility checks to explicit CLI overrides (#52648)

## Why

A running shared background server owns its feature settings until it restarts. Differences from a client's configuration files or defaults should not trigger a compatibility warning or a restart request.

## What changed

- Check shared-service features only when explicitly overridden on the command line.
- Exclude overrides superseded by active legacy managed configuration or feature requirements, while supporting older servers without `configRequirements/read`.
- Pass only the remaining explicit feature overrides to a requested daemon restart.

## Testing

Update compatibility tests for stale daemon overrides, explicit enable/disable requests, managed configuration, and older servers. Extend CLI startup tests to verify the feature overrides persisted after a restart.

GitOrigin-RevId: ac92c9c02cd70fa233203ebef1182fd119325dd1

Count interrupted goal continuations toward the no-activity limit (#52640)

## Why

Interrupted automatic goal continuations reset the empty-response counter, allowing repeated interruptions without activity to keep a goal running indefinitely.

## What changed

Count interrupted automatic continuations without activity toward the existing three-turn limit that marks a goal as `blocked`. Defer evaluation until the thread is idle and serialize it with turn-start accounting. Activity and user turns still reset the counter.

## Testing

Extend accounting tests to cover interrupted and mixed empty continuations, including resets after tool activity or user turns. Add an app-server regression case where a `PreCompact` hook repeatedly interrupts automatic continuations and verify the `thread/goal/updated` notification reports `blocked`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4c34e3ed1ae612e97cf067c2aa76836b10c50ef5

Add experimental thread item lookup by ID (#52637)

## What changed

Add `thread/items/read` to retrieve persisted items by `threadId`, `turnId`, and 1–100 `itemIds`. Return matching items in canonical stored order, omitting missing IDs and items outside the requested turn.

Add item ID filtering to the thread store while preserving inherited history and fork cutoffs. Require the experimental API capability for the new endpoint.

## Testing

Add coverage for stored ordering, turn scoping, missing IDs, request size limits, experimental capability gating, and inherited items across fork cutoffs.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9b243dd87577bd4fe36900c388a386b2e26ff2e0

Skip background workspace routing reads without ChatGPT auth (#52635)

## Why

Background workspace routing reads reload configuration even when signed out or using an API key, although routing requires ChatGPT authentication.

## What changed

Check cached authentication before reading accounts for workspace routing at app-server startup and connection initialization. Skip these background reads without ChatGPT authentication, while preserving configuration reloads for explicit `account/read` requests.

## Testing

Add regression tests covering signed-out and API-key startup and connection initialization, explicit `account/read` configuration reloads, and routing after ChatGPT sign-in, including propagation of configuration errors.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8b90ee609ed24f8618cd21f160eb7001703b8bd1

Consolidate local message board storage helpers (#52629)

## What changed

- Move the SQLite schema, database filename, and shared pool registry into `local/pool.rs`.
- Share channel insertion between runtime writes and template setup, using typed board IDs and channel descriptions.

GitOrigin-RevId: c57a79c49fe9003b3c73f38010ce9293275a714c

Add template setup for local agent message boards (#52621)

## What changed

Expose `LocalBoardSetup` and `configure_local_board` to load initial channels and optional descriptions before agents start. Add a `configure_board` example and setup documentation.

Save version 1 templates and channels atomically in SQLite. Identical templates are safe to retry; conflicting templates, previously used boards without a pinned template, and deleted boards are rejected. Setup accepts an optional creation timestamp and leaves agent access unchanged. Remove the pinned template when deleting a board.

## Testing

Add an integration test covering channel metadata after reopen, identical retries, conflicting template rejection, retries after adding a channel, and rejection after board deletion.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0b5c5439ab127fb5c275f024962a373a56635ad0

Align Linux sandbox names and docs with bubblewrap and seccomp (#52610)

## Why

The Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and seccomp for syscall filtering, but its command type, syscall-filter module, and integration test suite still used Landlock names.

## What changed

- Rename `LandlockCommand` to `LinuxSandboxCommand`, `src/landlock.rs` to `src/seccomp.rs`, and `tests/suite/landlock.rs` to `tests/suite/sandbox.rs`, updating imports and existing tests.
- Clarify the retained legacy Landlock implementation and its filesystem-policy limitations.
- Update the README to describe existing network filtering, `AF_VSOCK` and `io_uring` restrictions, and managed-proxy Unix socket behavior, including allowed Unix socket pairs.

Sandbox enforcement behavior is unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: be4769d5a10b90605990eb58451e83fdf1c31222

Upgrade `hyper` to 1.11.1 and test connection closure (#52608)

## Why

Requests with `Connection: close` must not reuse the connection even when the server responds with `Connection: keep-alive`.

## What changed

Update `hyper` from 1.8.1 to 1.11.1 in `codex-rs/Cargo.lock` and add the corresponding Bazel lockfile metadata.

## Testing

Add a regression test that sends two requests with `Connection: close` to a server that ignores the header and verifies that the second request uses a new connection.

GitOrigin-RevId: 72b464c8ea3d9a1ad5d9e62f7896ea9a4f15a93c

Fix races in remote environment and session replacement tests (#52591)

## Why

The remote environment test can steer before the wait tool call is recorded, discarding the call. The session replacement test can close the client while agents overview RPCs are still pending, leaving the proxy writing to a closed socket.

## What changed

- Wait for the `wait-for-active-environment` function call event before steering the active turn.
- Wait for `AgentsOverviewThreadsLoaded` before shutting down session replacement test cases that open the agents overview.

GitOrigin-RevId: 886112a56ff6e1016efe30dbbd0256807bc1cc85

Expose message board permissions and structured denials (#52568)

## Why

Remote boards can allow replies while denying new threads. Agents need to discover these effective permissions and receive actionable details when an operation is denied.

## What changed

- Expose optional `board_permissions` and per-channel `permissions` in `get_channels`, preserving the legacy response shape when permission metadata is absent.
- Preserve HTTP 403 `permission_denied` responses as structured tool errors with a message and optional `action` and `resource`. Mark denied calls as unsuccessful and truncate oversized error details to fit the output budget.
- Pass through service-computed permissions without evaluating access rules locally.

## Testing

Add remote-board scenarios for direct tools and code mode covering legacy responses, reply-only permissions, a denied post, and a successful reply, plus a snapshot of the direct tool exchange.

GitOrigin-RevId: 76594bbc0a1283ff3c3c8682bd7615baa5ade428

Forward clipboard copies to the terminal in Herdr sessions (#52557)

## Why

Herdr sessions can gain attached clients after Codex starts. Successful native clipboard copying should still forward the text to the attached terminal, even without inherited SSH variables.

## What changed

Detect Herdr sessions with `HERDR_ENV=1` and enable terminal forwarding for `/copy` and `Ctrl+O` even when native copying succeeds. Use OSC 52 directly when outside tmux, while preserving the native copy result.

## Testing

Add a routing test verifying that a Herdr session copies natively before sending OSC 52 and retains the successful native clipboard lease.

GitOrigin-RevId: c43c08ca037ff51e902267dc8636889493f5c30c

Add opt-in history prefix preservation for full agent forks (#52535)

## What changed

Add `preserve_fork_prefix` to the multi-agent v2 configuration, defaulting to `false`. When enabled, full forks retain the parent's model-visible history, including commentary and tool records, and append the child's instructions. Legacy compaction without a reusable context baseline still rebuilds the child context.

Mark copied history as inherited, complete unfinished tool calls in the fork snapshot, and exclude inherited manual approvals from authorization review while retaining them in model context.

## Testing

Add coverage for preserved request prefixes, child instructions, legacy and paginated histories, Code Mode, missing inherited tool outputs, compaction fallback, and approval isolation across checkpoint replay. Update the noisy helper failure test to read its response before starting cleanup.

GitOrigin-RevId: ce9235dfa111c88d6ce66cb93d564fb63b326489

Avoid an extra blank quote line when pasting text with a trailing newline (#52418)

## Why

Pasting text ending in a newline into a composer line beginning with `> ` adds an unnecessary empty quoted line before the next Markdown block.

## What changed

Remove one trailing newline from nonempty blockquote paste content before adding quote prefixes. Preserve interior blank lines and the two unquoted newlines that move the cursor to the next block.

## Testing

Add a trailing-newline regression case, update the CRLF/CR expectations, and exercise trailing-newline input in the existing rendering snapshot test.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2367efa8253dd0512de8ba6333b39eba6381fba8

Add experimental app-server thread read-state updates (#52395)

## Why

Clients need to mark threads read or unread without overwriting unseen results or another window's explicit mark.

## What changed

Add `thread/readState/update` for eligible durable local threads, gated by `initialize.capabilities.experimentalApi`. Requests include `threadId`, `expectedRevision`, and an operation of `{type:"read"}` or `{type:"unread"}`.

Marking read clears `firstUnread`; marking unread sets it to `threadStart`. Successful updates return the read state and notify subscribers through `thread/readState/changed`. Both operations require an exact revision match. Stale requests return `-32600` with `readStateConflict` and the current read state, requiring a fresh user action rather than a blind retry. Updates do not change thread recency.

## Testing

Add app-server coverage for experimental capability gating, explicit unread marks and notifications, conflicts for both stale operations, and marking read with a fresh revision.

GitOrigin-RevId: 775f6e9584dc91bd3c2ee9a309144b5baf0edffa

Notify subscribers when thread read state changes (#52384)

## What changed

Add the experimental `thread/readState/changed` notification with `threadId` and the committed `readState` receipt. Send it to existing thread subscribers when terminal activity updates read state or a revert clears a removed unread position. Emit terminal read-state updates before `turn/completed` so completion remains the last notification for that result.

Expose the notification in generated JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python SDK models. Document experimental capability gating, subscription lifetime, notification opt-out, and refreshing receipts when concurrent responses disagree.

## Testing

Extend the read-state integration test to assert that the notification receipt matches the receipt returned by `thread/read` after terminal activity.

GitOrigin-RevId: 28935352a881b7a5e2e7f629173c3b2061bd7941

Preserve per-session routing for gRPC code mode (#52381)

## Why

Sessions sharing a transport can be admitted to different hosts. Each session needs its own routing token so subsequent RPCs reach the host holding its state.

## What changed

- Capture the optional `x-code-mode-route` metadata from successful `OpenSession` responses and attach it to subsequent session RPCs. Reject tokens longer than 256 bytes and keep new admission attempts free of existing session routes.
- Invalidate a routed session when an `Unavailable` response explicitly sets `x-code-mode-route-lost: true`, allowing a later operation to reopen it without replaying the failed execution. Ordinary `Unavailable` responses preserve the session.
- Allow up to five admission attempts for `Unavailable` and `ResourceExhausted`, with an immediate first retry followed by jittered exponential backoff.
- Order session failure with shutdown so late callback errors cannot cancel an in-flight `CloseSession` RPC.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for independent routing on a shared provider, route-loss recovery without execution replay, preservation of unaffected session state, and callback failures racing shutdown. Extend admission tests to verify the five-attempt limit and recovery tests to distinguish explicit route loss from ordinary unavailability.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5d60ef1afa56beb8c70ba7ab27865128225b0d3d

repos.description: Happy is the open-source desktop app for Claude Code, Codex, and Grok, with an iOS and Android app to control your coding agents from anywhere.

commits.message: app: wait 2 seconds before showing Sending… on an idle send

app: give every assistant text message its own always-present copy button

The copy button was attached only to the final text message of an agent
turn, so it jumped between rows and mounted/unmounted while the agent
ran, shifting layout. Each non-thinking agent-text row now always renders
a copy button for its own text. Removes the per-turn agentTurnCopy logic.

app: keep user message rows a fixed height across send states

The status line under a user message mounted only while Sending…/Sends
after this turn or a send failure was showing, so the row grew and shrank
and the chat jumped. Always render one single-line status Text with a
fixed 14pt height and switch only its text and colour. Also add 6pt of
top padding above user messages.

feat(server): let a machine socket subscribe to session updates

Adds session-subscribe / session-unsubscribe on machine-scoped sockets so a
daemon can receive updates for all its sessions over one connection instead
of one session-scoped socket per session. Subscribing joins the same room a
session-scoped socket joins at connect, so routing and skip-sender are
unchanged. Rooms vanish on disconnect; clients resubscribe after reconnect
and detect old servers by ack timeout.

fix(codex): align default model and minimum version (#1885)

Co-authored-by: Jody <jody@Jodys-MacBook-Air-2.local>

feat(app): rebuild phone Welcome and Link Your Computer on one template

Both first-run screens now come from OnboardingScreen: header with the gear,
one centred block of content, primary and secondary action, and Get help in
the bottom right. The content slot and the secondary action each hold the
visible layer over invisible, accessibility-hidden copies of both screens'
content, so the top of the content, the primary button and the secondary
action sit at the same place on both screens at any width and text size,
with no measured or hard-coded positions. Very large text scrolls instead.

Welcome: stacked Happy Engineering wordmark (react-native-svg), "Claude,
Codex, Grok / in your pocket", one value prop per line, full-width Create
account, Restore existing account under it, Get help.

Link Your Computer: title in the welcome headline style, the two-step
checklist, a reserved error line, Scan QR code enabled only while both boxes
are ticked, "Can't scan QR code? Paste link instead". Linking shows a
spinner with "Linking…" until the session list replaces the screen; a
failure shows "Couldn't link. Scan the code again." inline instead of an
alert. No swipe back on home, and Android's back button is held while the
link screen is focused.

chore(cli): require Agent SDK 0.3.295 so Sonnet and Haiku 5.5 get 1M context

The Claude Code bundled with Agent SDK 0.3.283 (2.1.283) predates Sonnet 5.5
and Haiku 5.5. It still runs them, but treats an unknown model as 200K, so
app sessions on either compacted at a fifth of the model's window and
misreported its cost. Sonnet 5.5 is in Claude Code's model table from
2.1.287 and Haiku 5.5 from 2.1.293; 0.3.295 bundles 2.1.295, which knows
both as 1M-native. Run through query() on 0.3.295, claude-sonnet-5-5 and
claude-haiku-5-5 each report a 1,000,000-token context window.

2.1.295 also stops a `[1m]` model failing every request on a gateway,
Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry that refuses the context-1m beta.

One behaviour change rides along from 0.3.286: an omitted permissionMode is
now left to Claude Code instead of being sent as `default`. Happy omits it
only when nothing was picked, which runClaude already documents as "apply
Claude's own settings"; that is now what happens, including a settings
defaultMode and Claude Code's own auto default on third-party providers or
with telemetry off.

The lockfile change is the SDK and its platform packages only.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Happy <yesreply@happy.engineering>

feat(app): one row per Claude model, add Haiku 5.5, drop Sonnet 5

The Claude picker listed Opus 5.5, Opus 5 and Sonnet 5.5 twice, once plain
and once with `[1m]`. Each is 1M-native in Claude Code's model table, so the
plain ID already gets the 1M window (Opus on the SDK-bundled 2.1.283; Sonnet
5.5 from 2.1.287), and the suffix only adds the context-1m beta header, which
gateways, Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry can refuse. The rows are now Fable 5.1,
Fable 5, Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, one each.

Haiku 5.5 is `claude-haiku-5-5`, as listed on Anthropic's models overview
and in Claude Code's own model table from 2.1.293. It was run through the
Agent SDK 0.3.283 query() path happy-cli uses and answered; that older
bundle treats it as an unknown model and so caps it at 200K.

Saved picks keep working. A `[1m]` key in agent defaults or a new-session
draft maps onto the row that runs the same model, and an existing session
keeps sending the key it was started with while its chip shows that row.
Sonnet 5 still runs, so a saved Sonnet 5 is kept as its own "saved model"
row rather than swapped for a different model; before this, any Claude key
missing from the list sent the new-session picker to the head of the list.

fix(app): remember the harness picked in the new-session composer (#1884)

Since f0fc3bb1 a harness tapped in the composer lasted one session: the
pick lived in memory and was cleared after every start, so the next
composer, and every app restart, went back to Happy.

The pick is now its own persisted draft field, pickedAgentType, kept
until the person picks another harness. It is separate from agentType,
which the composer moves to whatever the selected computer can run. A
computer without the picked harness falls back (to Happy when it has
Happy Agent) without overwriting the pick, and the pick comes back on a
computer that has it.

f0fc3bb1's reason still holds: a draft saved before picks were
remembered loads with no pick, so its implicit Claude Code still starts
Happy on a computer with Happy Agent. A new chat like an existing one
keeps that chat's harness for that start only, and bots are unchanged.
Choosing a Happy Agent project, which only Happy can open, now picks
Happy. Otherwise a remembered pick would take the harness back.

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)
via [Happy](https://happy.engineering)

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Happy <yesreply@happy.engineering>

fix(cli): re-attach session handlers registered while offline after reconnecting (#1858)

Backends register their user-message and RPC handlers once, on the offline
stub when the server is unreachable at startup. The real session that replaces
it never got them, so app messages, abort and kill were ignored.

feat(app): default Claude to Opus 5.5 on happy-cli 1.2.6-beta.0 and newer (#1883)

App-started sessions run the Claude Code bundled with the CLI's Agent SDK,
and copies older than 2.1.280 get a 400 for Opus 5.5. 1.2.6-beta.0 is the
first happy-cli to require SDK ^0.3.283, so the Claude code default is
claude-opus-5-5 from that version on and claude-opus-5 below it.

Unlike the auto gate, a missing or malformed version keeps the old model:
guessing wrong would leave a session whose every turn fails. A saved
default still wins everywhere, and running sessions keep the model pinned
at spawn. Settings describes the defaults for the first machine it lists,
which every other caller already does for the selected machine.

fix(ble): re-request history once a foreign transfer that deferred us ends

A claim that stood down for another client's transfer (refresh pre-check,
last look before the request, withheld queued request, INIT) now arms one
link-scoped timer that re-requests once that transfer's window closes, or
shortly after its COMPLETE. While the window is live it re-checks every
quiet period, so it never spins. Before this, a late START answering our
own aborted request during the retry's pre-request waits deferred the
retry and nothing re-armed it until the 15-min periodic backfill.

Such a START inside a claim's pre-request waits also keeps our own-task
tail, so re-offered ENDs of that straggler cannot keep reopening the
window. Transfers this app did not request are still never answered.

throws.

Cursor writes were swallowed by catchError, so a session whose bookmark never

Localize Coach API format picker and document Responses sampling omission

The new API dropdown label and helper text were hardcoded English on an
otherwise localized setup screen; add coachApiFormatLabel/coachApiFormatHelp
