app shell: keep each tab once in Back history

Switching back and forth between two tabs added one Back press per
switch, so leaving the app took as many presses as tab changes. Keep
each tab at most once, most recent last, with Home kept as the way
back into the app.

events: a re-sent gen5 frame repairs its undecoded band_events row

Rows written before the band profile reached insertEvent sit as bare
EVENT_<id> with an empty payload, and the (device_id, hex) conflict
ignored the corrected decode when the band re-sent the frame. On a gen5
link, rewrite name and payload of such an undecoded row only; a decoded
row is never touched. INSERT OR IGNORE + UPDATE, no UPSERT (SQLite 3.18
floor).

docs: drop stale replay-ledger claim on Sample, reflow split comments

models.dart still said raw hex is kept as the replay ledger; raw_records
was dropped at v19 and only undecodable records reach raw_archive. Also
rejoin five comment lines the previous commit left broken mid-sentence.

docs(archive): drop the 'everything else imported' claim from two doc comments

The skipped-archive count can sit next to an import that landed nothing,
so the field docs on AppState and ImportOutcome no longer say the rest of
the backup imported (the user-facing string was already fixed).

two-device golden: strain's provenance label for the personal quiet level

The golden's day has no quiet-level history, so strain abstains, as it
did before. Only the absent metric's inputs_used changes, from the lump
form's (trimp, wake_minutes, quiet_waking_hrr) to the series form's
(hr_1hz, profile, quiet_waking_hrr_history). No number moves. Rides the
kAlgoVersion bump this change already requires.

strain: hash the newest quiet level once a later day sits on it

The rescan signature left the newest quiet_hrr entry out on the
assumption that only unfinalized days come after it. A day too short to
write its own level (under 360 wake minutes) can follow it and be
finalized, priced on that newest level; moving the level then never
re-priced it. The newest entry is now left out only while no baseline
series has a later day, which keeps today's rewrites from triggering a
rescan.

Also restores the missing space in `_rhr28 = await`.

docs(hrv): keep LocalRepository's doc on the class; reflow rmssdHistory doc

rmssdFromSessionEstimator was inserted between LocalRepository's doc
comment and the class, so the class doc attached to the function.

copy(hrv): describe the nightly RMSSD as the mean of 5-min sleep windows

The Health catalogue blurb (all locales) and the HRV method text still
described the old headline (cleanest / longest artefact-free window,
Lipponen-Tarvainen corrected). The headline is now the sleep-session
mean of qualifying 5-minute windows, filtered per window, and absent
when none qualifies or the beat stream is over-counted.
copy(hrv): write 20% without a space, matching the rest of the method sheets

test(workout): expect the host platform's strength activity type in the export test

The health exporter maps 'strength' to TRADITIONAL_STRENGTH_TRAINING on
Apple hosts (iOS and macOS) and STRENGTH_TRAINING elsewhere. The test
hard-coded the Health Connect name, so it failed when run on a macOS
host. Derive the expectation from healthActivityForType and
HealthExporter.isApple instead.

backup: show folder name, report kept grant, release unsaved picks

- Report a backup in a chosen folder as '<folder>/<file>' instead of
  its content:// document URI.
- Treat prefs.clear() returning false as a failure; when a folder grant
  is still saved, report reset backup cleanup as incomplete.
- Save a picked folder even if the screen closed, and release the new
  grant when saving it fails so no unreferenced grant is left.

Keep home widget durations in its fixed English format; count weekdays like the medication executor

The native widget is not localized yet and can be pushed from a background
isolate that never binds the app's language override, so the shared, now
locale-aware hm() mixed localized durations into otherwise English widget
labels. Use a local fixed-format formatter there.

The Russian medication confirmation now treats numeric weekdays the way
CoachActions.addMedication does (round any num, dedupe, 1-7) before
deciding the schedule is every day.

alarm: schedule the tick timer outside build

Move the timer into initState/didUpdateWidget so a Home rebuild on new
data no longer cancels and re-creates it; the callback reschedules for
the next boundary itself. build is now a pure read of the clock.

coach: validate full IPv4 literal; keep 'stays on your machine' note to private hosts

_ipv4LeadingOctets now uses Uri.parseIPv4Address, so a host like
100.64.0.999 or 192.168.1.999 (a registered name to Uri, not an
address) no longer counts as local and skips the API key.

The setup screen's data note claimed questions 'stay on your own
machine' for every local host, including 100.64.0.0/10, which may be
carrier-grade NAT. Gate that note on isPrivateCoachHost, matching the
ECG consent gate.

strain: the quiet-level seed picks measured days first and moves the rescan gate

The seed read only the newest window of result rows and dropped imports,
skipped and partial rows afterwards, so a long import newer than the
measured days filled the window, nothing was seeded, and the seed was
marked done. It now selects measured days first (payload-free), applies
the window to those, and reads each bundle on its own.

A seed that wrote levels left the rolling artifact's signature as it
was, so on a pass with nothing to derive rescanRecent saw no change and
never re-scored the days the new levels price. The artifact is now
refreshed after any nonzero seed, ahead of every early return, under its
own guard.

copy: the rough-night note names the resting-heart-rate signal, not an illness watch

The note shown when the overnight resting-heart-rate verdict also
flagged a rough night credited an "illness watch" in every language. The
detector reports an accumulated rise in one signal and names no cause,
so the note now names that signal (en, de, es, fr, hi, zh, the English
fallback and the gallery fixture). The copy test now also bans each
locale's illness-detector phrasing across the illness card strings.

fix(ble): never answer history transfers this app did not request

A band's notifications on a shared link reach every client that enabled
them, so when another app on the same phone runs a history transfer edge
sees its START/data/END/COMPLETE frame for frame. Edge had no notion of
"a transfer I asked for": it adopted the other client's transfer and
wrote into it — a success result trimming the band to that client's
marker even when that client had counted the burst short, failure
results that forced re-offers of bursts it had accepted, an abort after
fifteen of them, an idle-watchdog abort plus its own retry request after
60 s of silence, and the post-offload policy (stuck-strap SET_CLOCK,
auto-continue request) on its COMPLETE. Two clients answering one
transfer is the trim-cursor race the in-process _bandOwners guard was
written for; that guard only covers engines inside edge's own process.

Ownership is now explicit. Both claim sites (INIT and refresh, which
auto-continue also goes through) run one synchronous _claimHistoryTask
helper that records the generation this link requested. One classifier
decides, at ARRIVAL and for every ingest path (the serialized queue and
history reassembled on cmd_from/events), whether a frame is ours: a task
of ours is open, its SEND_HISTORICAL_DATA is going out, and its
HISTORY_COMPLETE has not arrived yet. Nothing that arrives during a
claim's range/clock waits can be the band answering a request it has not
been sent, and anything arriving after our COMPLETE, even while its tail
is still being banked, belongs to someone else. All of that state lives
on the session, so a reconnect starts with none of it.

Traffic we do not own is observed only: markers are never answered and
never arm a watchdog, raise the offload claim, touch the HPS terminal or
run the post-offload policy. Its records go through the same single
ingest path into a separate drain controller, built before notifications
are enabled so a transfer already running at connect is covered, and are
banked with a null trim token: strap_trim never moves for them and no
result is ever written after them, so edge keeps the data without being
able to trim anything on the other client's behalf. A record that
arrived while no task of ours was open is banked even if a claim bumps
the generation before the drainer reaches it. When the link goes away,
ingress freezes first, then every such row — buffered, queued or in the
drainer's hand — is snapshotted and banked by a job detached from the
teardown (the other client's ACK, not ours, trims them from the band):
it waits for banks in flight, and if the final bank fails the rows are
logged and counted, never carried to another link or past a reset. The
teardown itself releases all engine state before its first await, so a
reconnect is never clobbered by it. The headless and Shortcut runs, whose
process may be suspended the moment they return, wait (bounded at 12 s,
or the Shortcut's own deadline) for that final bank before they finish —
including when the connect itself fails after setup has already taken in
such rows. Every bank is stamped with the
family of the band that sent the rows, captured when the link's buffer
is built, and counts exactly the rows it stored.

Adopting incidentally kept edge from starting a competing transfer; keep
that explicitly. Another client's activity — its markers and its records,
since joining mid-burst shows data first — is recorded on arrival, ahead
of our own ended-task latch: while it was seen within the last 10 s
(closed early by its COMPLETE, and by 60 s without a START or record so
an abandoned transfer's re-offered END cannot hold it open) a refresh or
auto-continue is deferred, a refresh or INIT re-checks inside its queued
write, immediately before the request's bytes go out (and withholds it),
and maintenance writes pause. Nothing that arrives before our request can arm our idle
watchdog, and a claim that stands down cancels it. So our own re-offered markers and last
in-flight records never defer us: after our task ends (abort or COMPLETE),
and until our next request goes out or another client's START shows a new
transfer, only a START opens that window. Under Stuck nothing is
recorded. A frame of a revision this build cannot read is archived into
the same tokenless buffer while such a transfer is live.

The engine's monotonic stopwatch now comes from package:clock so these
windows are testable under fakeAsync; production behaviour is unchanged.
Commit-before-ACK for our own tasks is unchanged; the existing history
tests now claim a task explicitly instead of relying on adoption.

fix(ble): a request whose write failed is answered by nothing

The opcode-22 gate marks the request as gone out right before the
transport write. When that write then failed, the refresh and INIT
rollbacks left the mark set, so a straggler frame from before still
counted as this task's answer: a leftover HISTORY_COMPLETE was handled as
the task's own completion instead of being ignored. Both rollbacks now
clear the mark.

l10n: translate the nightly RMSSD labels in Investigate

investigateRmssdNightly and investigateRmssdStored existed only in
English, so Investigate showed them untranslated in de, es, fr, hi and
zh. A test checks every shipped language has its own text for both.

strain: seed quiet levels on the live derive's ceiling

The one-time quiet_hrr seed priced each stored day on that bundle's
max_hr_used, while the live derive prices it on estimatedMaxHr at the
current profile age. After a birthday or a profile edit the two are on
different scales, and the trailing median mixes them. The seed now uses
the same ceiling as the live derive; without an age it seeds nothing and
stays armed, as the live derive also abstains.

The live gauge's quiet-level fill gets its own guard, so a failure there
cannot skip the resting-HR refresh. The strain rescale's comment now
states why one current level prices every rescaled day.

fix(db): clearing an orphan readiness pin never deletes a newer one

frozenHeadline() read the pin, found its day gone, then deleted the
cursor by name. A derive that pinned a new headline in between lost it,
and the ring, chart and push lost their pinned readiness. The clear is
now compare-and-delete: only the value that was read as the orphan is
removed.

One readiness number for the pinned day, gone when the day is deleted

The push and the ring read the frozen morning headline. The recovery
chart, and the Observations log built from it, read `metric_series`,
which drops null rows entirely. A partial derive can pin the headline
without writing the day's readiness, or a later derive can write it as
null. Then a pin of 22 buzzed "Low readiness" and filled the ring, with
no chart point and no log entry to back it. The chart now gives the
pinned day its point when its series row is missing or null.

That made the pin the only record of the day's readiness, and the pin is
a cursor, not a day row, so `deleteDays` never touched it. A deleted
pinned day came back on the chart, in the log and in a push: data the
user asked to destroy. `deleteDays` now clears a matching pin inside its
transaction. As defence in depth, `frozenHeadline()` removes a pin whose
day has no day_result, however the orphan arose (an older build's delete,
say), so it cannot come back as the pin once that day is derived again.
The ring, chart, log and push all read the pin through it, and one
parser reads the cursor for both.

Tests drive the ring (getToday), the push planner, the chart and the
Health loader's log for a pinned day with no stored or a null stored
value, and check all four agree. They delete the pinned day, reopen the
database and check there is no cursor, chart point, log entry or push.
They also cover an orphan made some other way.

Low readiness on the ring's band, once the night is settled

"Low readiness today" fired when readiness fell below 34. The ring, the
widget and the briefing band the readiness composite at its own
quantiles (26 / 37 / 61), so 34 is not a cut-off the ring has. It sits
inside "Take it easy": the phone buzzed under a ring reading
"30 · Take it easy". The push also judged today's composite while the
night was still draining, the reason the morning headline is frozen at
all.

One rule for every surface:
- The band cut-offs move from the widget into findings.dart, and
  `kLowReadiness` is the ring's lowest band, "Rest today" (about one
  morning in twenty by construction).
- `servedReadiness` is the number the ring and the recovery chart show:
  the frozen morning headline when it is pinned to the day, else the
  stored composite. `lowReadinessFinding` decides "low" for the push and
  the log alike, and the finding carries the ring's own score.
- The push considers low readiness only on a settled anchor row, the
  same rule the log uses. An absent composite is "not scored": no
  finding, and never a fallback to the glass-box.

The whole push decision moves into the pure `planExceptionNotices`, so
the production rule is tested rather than the helpers beside it.
`_runNotifications` only reads its three inputs and emits the result.
The finding titles no longer say "today", because the log renders the
same Finding under past dates.

Wording, threshold and source only; no derived value changes.

Honest illness copy: no HRV, no "illness", no streak

The illness finding read "Possible illness onset: Elevated resting HR +
suppressed HRV over recent nights." Its detector is a CUSUM on nightly
resting heart rate ONLY. The detector's own contract (illness_cusum.dart
in analytics) says it reports a state, not a diagnosis, and that the
word "illness" needs corroboration from a second signal.

A red state is also accumulated evidence, not a run of high nights. The
accumulator clears only after two normal nights, so one very high night
followed by an ordinary one is red on the ordinary night. The in-app
illness cards still claimed a streak in every locale: "Several nights in
a row are away from your normal", and bodies saying the rate "has been
running above" baseline.

Say what the state means, the same way on every surface: recent nights
add up to a rise above your own baseline, from one very high night or a
few slightly raised ones. The push and the Observations log use the
finding title "Resting heart rate has been raised". The weekly lookback
reads "resting heart rate raised ×N". The red card title, the five
card bodies and the rough-night note that names the same verdict ("a
sustained rise") are reworded in all six locales, and the English
fallbacks match. The "watches one signal only, a pattern not a cause" sentences
stay.

Tests: the finding copy claims no signal the detector does not read. A
regression runs the real detector on a spike-then-normal sequence and
checks the copy claims no streak. Every locale's illness-card strings
are scanned for that locale's streak phrasing, and the widget tests
check the rendered cards.

test: the exception-notice pass and its seed share one clock

The test took today/yesterday from the real clock when the file loaded,
while the notification pass read the clock again when it ran. A run that
crossed local midnight seeded a night that was two days old by then and
missed the expected push. The pass now takes an optional `today` (test
entry only; production still reads the clock), and the test pins one
fixed day for both the seed and the pass.

fix(archive): a failed unarchived delete no longer ends the prune pass

Past the hold, a bucket whose archive keeps failing is deleted
unarchived. That delete ran unguarded inside the catch, so one failure
(e.g. a concurrent writer holding the lock) threw out of the pass: the
remaining buckets were skipped, every failure count made this pass was
lost, and the rest of the prune (cursor raise, samples/events deletes)
never ran. The delete is now guarded: the bucket stays live and keeps its
count for the next pass, and the counts are saved in a finally.

The skipped-archive import line no longer claims "Everything else
imported normally" — false when nothing else landed or another read
failed. The new action and archive strings are translated into de, es,
fr, hi and zh.

fix(ble): a re-wait on a running task keeps waiting; an ended task's 0x16 is withheld

_runSyncBurst stopped on a report with zero batches. Reports now carry
only progress not reported yet, so a wait that gave up (timeout or no
progress) while the history task was still running could hand back zero
batches and end the burst mid-drain. While the task is still running and
not complete, the burst now waits on it again; the stop rules only judge
a task that has ended.

The opcode-22 beforeTransport gate marked the request sent only for the
current task but still let the write through when the task had ended
while the request sat queued, so the band was asked to drain for a task
nothing would ACK. The gate now withholds it. The refresh path already
treats that as a stale claim; the INIT path no longer rolls back state
its terminal (or a replacement task) now owns.

coach: keep the ECG consent prompt for 100.64.0.0/10 hosts

100.64.0.0/10 is RFC 6598 carrier-grade NAT space before it is
Tailscale's, so an address in it doesn't show the coach is the user's
own machine. Classifying it as local is fine for dropping the API key
requirement and applying the local timeout, but isLocalEndpoint also
gated the ECG "send this reading to your model?" confirmation, so a
non-Tailscale host in that range would have received the full waveform
without asking.

Split the predicate: isPrivateCoachHost (loopback, .local, RFC 1918)
now gates consent via CoachConfig.isPrivateEndpoint; isLocalCoachHost
is that plus the shared space and still drives the key/timeout logic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
refactor(workout): share _newLiveSession and _resetWorkoutStepState between start and resume

coach: treat Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10) hosts as local endpoints

isLocalCoachHost only recognised loopback, .local and the RFC 1918
ranges, so an Ollama reached over Tailscale (100.x) was classified as a
cloud provider. With no API key that left `configured` false: Save
stored the settings, popped the screen, and the caller saw the coach as
still unconfigured and backed out too. It also pinned the request
timeout to the fixed cloud value.

Accept the RFC 6598 shared address space, which is where Tailscale
assigns node addresses. Fixes #564.
Fix remaining localization review findings
Address localization review findings

backup: allow choosing a folder on Android

Signed-off-by: Matteo Fari <matteofari06@gmail.com>
Cover Russian localization and presentation compatibility
Localize Flutter presentation and accommodate Russian text
Add Russian translations and missing presentation messages

Review fix: report observed host commit failures as storageFailed

BandHost now emits 'host_commit_failed' when _commit(all: true) fails,
and OuraLink maps it to OuraSyncCategory.storageFailed; the adapter's
later generic 'oura_batch_unconfirmed' keeps that specific cause
instead of overwriting it with checkpointUnconfirmed. The adapter
comment no longer overclaims the persistence outcome. Fixes a missing
closing paren in the packed-frame adapter test; adds regression tests
for the priority (note-handler seam), the FAULT-E follow-up sync, and
the BandHost checkpoint contract (fault + control case).

Co-authored-by: BucciMobile <BucciMobile@users.noreply.github.com>

test: two AppState test descriptions say what they pin

The dispose test accepts a breathing recompute that lands after dispose (and
pins that it does not notify); its name said the result was dropped. The export
test header now states the actual guard: a session is not exported when its
stored end is not after its start at one-second resolution.

refactor(state): SyncController owns the band session and sync loop

Session and sync orchestration moves out of AppState into
lib/state/sync_controller.dart: openSession and the foreground lease and
intent, the reconnect loop and its supervisor, the backfill timer, the sync
burst, pauseForBackground and iOS recovery, syncNow, forceResync,
foregroundCatchUp, syncForShortcut, endSession and the link side of unpair,
the background cold-start connect, and status, lastDataAt, lastRecordAt and
the sync activity window.

No behaviour change. The moved bodies match the previous AppState token for
token apart from comments and callback substitutions: every busy, intent,
lease and recovery exit keeps its order, the foreground flip still precedes
the busy early return, reconnect generations, burst totals and the Shortcut
completion after dispose are unchanged, and the quiet timer is still
cancelled first on dispose. The commit callback that gates the band ACK, the
engine callbacks, alarm handling and the static iOS hooks stay in AppState,
which keeps every public member with the same signature (busy stays
writable).

sync_controller_test drives the controller with a recorded trace; the AppState
sync and Shortcut tests pass unchanged except one source assertion that now
looks for the recovery re-arm in sync_controller.dart.

refactor(state): WorkoutController owns live workouts

The live-workout lifecycle moves out of AppState into
lib/state/workout_controller.dart, together with LiveWorkoutState (re-exported
from app_state.dart): start, stop and its failed-stop retry, delete (torn down
before the row goes, notifying in finally), the 1 Hz tick and pause clock,
tally persistence and restore, orphan reconcile with its last-tally end bounds,
route tracking, zone alerts, Live Activity updates, workout step state and
Health export.

No behaviour change. The moved code matches the previous AppState token for
token apart from comments and callback substitutions, including every
DateTime.now() read and await point. The connection-level pedometer stays in
AppState and feeds the workout through three calls placed exactly where it
used to mutate the workout's step state (a gait sample with its ingest time, a
completed minute's steps, and a rebase before the counter resets). Dispose
still only cancels the tick timer. AppState keeps every public member with the
same signature, including the writable fields tests assign.

workout_controller_test drives the controller with a recorded trace of stop,
delete, tally, step-coverage and orphan-bound behaviour; the AppState workout
tests pass unchanged.

refactor(state): BreathingController owns breathing sessions and windows

Breathing sessions, quiet measurement windows, the periodic coherence
recompute, the banked history and the breathing haptic cues move out of
AppState into lib/state/breathing_controller.dart.

No behaviour change. The moved bodies keep their statements, await points,
notification and Live Activity calls, the three clock reads (breathingNow) and
the timer creation and cancellation points; the frame router hands over the
same RR-bearing frames at the same point; a recompute that finishes after
dispose is still accepted. AppState keeps every public member with the same
signature, including the writable fields tests assign.

breathing_controller_test pins the 60 s banking boundary, the cue ids, the
order of clock reads, notifications and stream nudges, and the late result
after dispose; the AppState breathing tests pass unchanged (one now freezes
its clock).

refactor(state): GestureController owns the double-tap dispatcher

The GestureDispatcher AppState built in both constructors now lives in
lib/state/gesture_controller.dart, built at the same points with the same
settings, log and in-app action callbacks. AppState still persists the band
event, gates on a data reset and handles the alarm before handing the event to
the controller, synchronously, at the same place. gestureSettings, the three
in-app actions and the water-write latch stay in AppState.

No behaviour change; the AppState gesture tests pass unchanged and
gesture_controller_test drives the controller directly.

refactor(state): LiveStreamController owns live HR and IMU stream ownership

Who wants the live streams moves out of AppState into
lib/state/live_stream_controller.dart: the live-HR viewer count, the
movement-sampling window, the passive strap-step owner, the owner set the
engine reads, and the nudge that asks the engine to reconcile.

No behaviour change. Every nudge stays where it was relative to awaits,
notifications and state changes; the owner set is computed the same way; the
engine is still reached lazily and fire-and-forget. AppState keeps
retainLiveHrView, releaseLiveHrView, setMovementSamplingWindow and
debugLiveOwners, and both engine registrations still read its owner tear-off.
Frame routing, the pedometer and the live-HR trace stay in AppState.

live_stream_controller_test pins the owner set per transition, viewer
counting, movement-window idempotence and that each nudge already sees the
ownership it announces; the AppState live tests pass unchanged.

refactor(state): DeriveCoordinator owns derive orchestration

AppState's derive scheduling moves into lib/state/derive_coordinator.dart:
the DeriveScheduler and its run callback, the post-drain pass (_afterDrain,
including the awaited heavy rescan and the recovery-ready, phone-step,
health-export and disk-reclaim steps it triggers), the insights revision
notifier, and the activity-review rollup with its retry backoff.

No behaviour change. The moved bodies keep their statements, await points,
notification order, logs and timers; the coordinator and the derivation
engine stay lazily built; AppState keeps forwarding members with the same
signatures (insightsRevision is still one ValueNotifier for the app's
lifetime) and disposes everything in the same order. The coordinator takes
callbacks and getters, never AppState itself.

derive_coordinator_test drives the coordinator directly; the existing AppState
derive tests pass unchanged, with one strengthened to pin that a resume which
finds busy held does not reset the activity-review budget.

test: pin AppState's derive, live-stream, gesture, workout, breathing and sync behaviour

Characterization tests for the parts of AppState that are about to move into
their own controllers, written against the current implementation so the move
can be shown to change nothing:

- derive: light/heavy passes, the awaited heavy rescan holding the scheduler
  job, revision identity and notification cadence, activity-review retries
  (backoff, ten-attempt cap, background suppression, budget reset on resume),
  recovery-ready after light and heavy passes;
- live streams: owner set and engine reconciliation, HR viewers, movement
  window, RAM-only frame routing;
- gestures: double-tap mapping, recency window, debounce, reset gating, the
  water and mark-moment actions, the workout toggle;
- workout and breathing: tick and pause clock, tally persistence and restore,
  orphan reconcile bounds, teardown-before-delete, step coverage gap rules,
  route and export, dispose, breathing windows and banked minimum;
- sync: openSession foreground/background transitions, reconnect generations,
  link drop during setup, burst aggregation, syncNow / forceResync /
  foregroundCatchUp, Shortcut sync phases and post-dispose completion, the
  commit callback reporting only after a durable commit.

Test-only hooks, each defaulting to the existing call at the same place:
debugDeriveRun / debugRescanRecent / debugRefreshActivityReviews /
debugAfterDrain / debugDeriveScheduler, debugOnLiveFrame, breathingNow, and
GestureDispatcher.now.

repos.description: AI that sees your screen, listens to your conversations and tells you what to do

commits.message: feat(backend): observe owner identity retry funnel (#21095) Observe owner identity candidate attempts on first finalization and late pusher repair with `omi_owner_identity_retry_total{pass,stage,reason}`. Existing `unverified_inventory` refusals now have a closed primary diagnostic reason, without changing the refusal, transcript, speaker labels, embedding cache, or read/model budgets. This makes invisible inventory/read and placement failures distinguishable from insufficient speech and admission/CAS denial. - Add the 28 funnel pairs plus 30 resolver-exit pairs, with `pass=first|late`. Children are lazy, collector registration is reload-safe, and labels contain no account/conversation/segment/speaker IDs, scope, exception or content. - Count late candidate entry, slot/scan/pass-cap skips, eligibility and existing early exits. Count CAS outcomes only after the outer transaction returns, including no-op commits; transaction callback retries emit no additional terminal count. - Tag first-finalization calls using the existing `already_observed` determination. An already-observed reprocess emits no first funnel. No extra transcript/profile/storage reads, retries, embedding calls, placement/proof work or writes. - Keep `omi_owner_identity_repair_total` and `omi_owner_recognition_conversations_total` unchanged. Zero-duration acceptance, partial inventory/selected-window reading, floors, manual/channel authority and old-cache policy are unchanged. ### How to read it ```promql sum by (pass, reason) (increase(omi_owner_identity_retry_total{stage="resolver_exit"}[1h])) sum by (stage, reason) (increase(omi_owner_identity_retry_total{pass="late",stage!="resolver_exit"}[1h])) ``` These count attempts, not unique conversations, owner candidates, or owner additions. Late entry is deduplicated per scheduled batch, including candidates refused by capacity. Eligibility follows the snapshot checks. `slot_limit`, `scan_limit` and `pass_limit` are unscanned capacity, not acoustic evidence. Late terminals are `skipped + cas_refused + cas_committed`; entry minus those terminals is unfinished work across the interval boundary. `eligible` and `resolver_exit` are intermediate; an unavailable/no-op resolver may still commit. Compare `owner_added` from the existing repair counter to `cas_committed` to see the actual identity-change yield. First entry means a first-finalization attempt reached the shared resolver, not every finalization request. First eligibility means a nonempty conversation model; channel/private-cloud/audio policy is observed at its existing resolver gate. First resolver exit ends its acoustic attempt, not later summary/persistence. Earlier processing admission returns are outside this counter. Neither pass backfills or identifies David's historical 41 rows; the metric attributes future population attempts without account labels. Primary precedence preserves executed gates: placement deadline before later proof; at the global veto, manifest ambiguity → zero/other invalid text → uncovered window with a validated index → unvalidated manifest → capture coverage hole. Then actual inventory proof retains read/listing, object metadata, manifest inventory, count/pair equality, fetch/decode, decoded duration/overlap/coverage order. `read_budget` includes the existing count/bytes/deadline/transient-listing refusal. `no_proven_window` covers missing origin/provider position, explicit unplaced alignment and legacy clock refusal. Usable partial resolution emits `partial` even if later embedding capacity was exhausted; failure/budget is primary when no resolution was produced. Full closed pair table and semantics are in `backend/docs/listen_pusher_pipeline.mdx`. ### Deployment, cost and residuals Deploy pusher for late and pusher-hosted first passes; deploy backend/listen and Cloud Run backend, backend-sync and backend-sync-backfill for their first-pass coverage. No new flags or prod env changes, schema/index/wire changes, app release, or backfill. Mixed images are safe: old images emit no new samples. Existing recognition flags retain their values. Added service reads/model calls/storage operations/writes: **0 per session-hour**. Existing late ceilings remain two concurrent batches per process, 128 scanned candidates and eight eligible passes per batch, five seconds and 24 model attempts per eligible pass. At most 58 closed pairs per pass / 116 counter children per process, lazy rather than idle zeros. Only local scalar diagnostics and counter increments are added. Missing audio, global inventory vetoes, zero-duration poisoning and whole-inventory download caps remain deliberate residuals for separately authorized behavior work. ### Validation All four full backend CI shards passed (`--all --shard 4/K`, K=1..4): 425 + 425 + 425 + 424 = 1,699 selected files. Each runner returned exit 0. Focused regression suite: 75 passed. Literal origin/main implementation versus instrumented resolver: byte-identical conversation JSON and encoded cache bytes; inventory-proof refusals have identical I/O calls. Real first-finalization lifecycle verifies first emission and suppression on subsequent reprocess. CAS refusal reasons, callback replay, no-op commit, encrypted/compressed manual authority and metric-failure isolation are covered; existing identity/finalization counters remain unchanged on no-op commits. Red proof using the literal main resolver at the finalization boundary: `1 failed, 74 passed, 14 warnings in 13.78s`; the first-funnel delta was `{}` instead of entry/eligible/no_audio. feat(speakers): shadow provider-aware conversation grouping (#21064)

Conversation-wide acoustic grouping can merge the owner with another
voice even when the stored provider partition kept them separate. This
adds three cached-evidence alternatives beside the incumbent and a
config-only authority switch. `owner_link` is shadow-only and rejected
by authoritative configuration with shadow on or off. Only `incumbent`,
`provider_strict`, and `provider_cannot_link` are allowed authoritative
modes. Shadow output never changes transcript attribution, summaries,
memories, or prompts; `SPEAKER_GROUPING_MODE=incumbent` remains the
default everywhere.

Design:
- G1 pools original `(provider, scope, id)` partitions, then constrained
average-linkage across scopes at 0.70. G2 starts with segment units and
uses same-scope cannot-links plus cross-scope 0.60 (configurable).
Constraints also apply to absorption and automatic identity merges.
- G4 uses G1 plus cross-scope pooling only between independently
accepted owner groups (5 s / 0.50 / 0.10). Non-owner identity linking is
absent on the free path. All variants share the incumbent's admitted
prints: free owner recognition, paid automatic person naming. Manual
receipts remain authoritative.
- Persist minimal original provider partition ID/epoch scope/provider
before rewriting public IDs, in bounded independently encrypted sidecars
within the existing transcript write; excluded from JSON/OpenAPI and all
app/developer webhooks. Stored IDs are conversation-local
partition-preserving renumberings, not raw provider integers.
Reprocessing uses that provenance, never inferred `conversation:{id}`
IDs. Missing/historical/ambiguous provenance skips. Frozen per-segment
predictions use the same always-encrypted sidecar for later committed
positive-correction agreement; winning negative receipts are excluded
from exact agreement and counted as `correction_negative_skipped`; no
extra storage calls, audio, or vectors.

Cost/cohort/observability:
- Zero extra embedding/model/profile/audio/network calls. Heap-based
constrained AHC, maximum 256 input segments, shared cooperative 300 ms
budget for all variants; errors/budget/limits fail open to incumbent.
Projection/NumPy/logging can slightly overrun a deadline check. No new
finalization worker or wait.
- Code defaults shadow off. Prod declarations enable `cohort` at a
stable EXP-004 salted UID slice of 10%, plus David's configured
allowlist, on pusher, backend-listen, backend, backend-sync,
backend-sync-backfill, backend-integration. Allowlisted accounts
additionally log segment IDs and owner/person/unknown only. This is
source configuration, not a deployment claim.
- `omi_speaker_grouping_shadow_total{variant,outcome}` has bounded
vocabularies only: owner changes, mixed-proxy, fragmentation, group
delta buckets, skipped/error outcomes, committed correction agreement.
One content-free summary per resolution/variant includes gained/lost
counts, group counts, incumbent proxies, provider/source/surface. No
transcript text or UID metric labels.

Ship criteria: David gates any authoritative config change. Zero newly
introduced false-owner segments against independently reviewed owner
labels; population owner_gained substantially above owner_lost;
mixed-proxy and fragmentation no worse; improved correction agreement;
consistent Soniox/Deepgram/Parakeet and source/surface evidence, with
paid/free and skip denominators. Rollback all six hosts to shadow off /
mode incumbent.

fix(memories): bounded large-account list reads — truncated prefix on scan-budget exhaustion, no false-empty on canonical failure (#21092)

## What

`GET /v3/memories` on the largest canonical account returned HTTP 200
with an **empty** array after ~24s (plus intermittent 30s edge 504s) —
rendering "No Memories Yet" for an account with 3,400+ visible memories.
Root cause chain: first-page keyset scan trips its 6s sub-budget → route
fell back to the offset reader → `read_canonical_memories` →
`fetch_authoritative_product_memory_items` **streamed the entire
`memory_items` collection** (Pydantic-validating every doc) → request
budget died → empty/truncated-200. The same path also emitted two
warning lines per expired short-term item per read (>1000/day in prod)
because the keyset reader invokes the visibility filter with singleton
lists.

## Changes

**Backend**
- `read_page` sub-budget exhaustion now returns the keyset prefix
already walked as a truncated page (`X-Omi-List-Truncated: true`, no
cursor) instead of raising into the offset-read fallback. Other
`MemoryBackingStoreUnavailable` causes (cursor secret, historical index
building) keep the offset fallback.
- `CanonicalMemoryBackend.read` (all offset list reads) walks the same
indexed keyset in bounded chunks (`_read_keyset_window`) with a raw-row
cap — it no longer streams the whole collection. `MemoryService.read`
callers that need the full authoritative collection (released product
search) use the new explicit `read_authoritative` seam, which keeps the
previous full fetch. Chat/MCP retrieval untouched.
- Expiry observations batch through a ContextVar: one warning per
request instead of one per expired row. **Visibility is unchanged** —
§1.3 holds (processed active short-term past TTL stays visible pending
disposition).

**Flutter**
- A truncated page with zero rows is now a load failure: the provider
sets the existing error flags (memories page shows its retry state) and
preserves any already-loaded list instead of overwriting with empty.
Truncated-with-rows stays a partial success.

## Tests

- Backend: 9 touched suites green when run in separation/standard orders
(217 tests), incl. new contract tests: scan-budget exhaustion must not
start the offset reader (`service.read.assert_not_called`), offset reads
must not full-fetch (`read_canonical_memories` patched to explode),
pagination clamp + parity goldens.
- Flutter: provider load-failure + progressive-load + temporal-view
suites green (59 tests) incl. the new truncated-empty test.
- Known pre-existing base-side issue (NOT from this branch): running
`test_list_read_budget_contract.py` immediately before
`test_memories_archive_and_read_contracts.py` in one pytest process
fails 2 ledger-history tests via module-state pollution — reproduced on
pure `origin/main` (a92ebcf29e). Tracked separately; does not block.

## Product invariants affected

INV-MEM-3 (memory-canonical-fail-closed): this PR enforces it — a
canonical read failure with no usable content now re-raises (503)
instead of presenting an empty success; the historical fallback path
marks the response truncated rather than complete.
INV-MEM-4 (memory-promotion-authority): unchanged visibility semantics —
expired active Short-term items remain visible pending canonical
disposition (§1.3); no TTL-only hiding, no new promotion route, only
observation-logging is batched.
INV-MEM-1: list reads keep the universal authority ordering (canonical
authoritative, historical compatibility merge); the bounded keyset
window reads through MemoryService only, no direct legacy reader.

## Failure-Class

Failure-Class: none

UI-Evidence: none -- no new UI surface; the provider change reuses the
existing memories load-error/retry state (couldNotLoadMemories /
tryAgain) with changed trigger conditions only (truncated zero-row page
now sets the same flags)

fix(backend): fail open Redis cache writes on connection errors (#21066)

## Summary

- Best-effort Redis cache writes (`_cache_set_fail_open`) now skip
connection-class faults as well as maxmemory. `AuthenticationError`,
`TimeoutError`, and `ConnectionError` log `redis cache write skipped
reason=<auth_error|connection_error|timeout|capacity_full>
prefix=<prefix>` and call `record_fallback(component='other',
from_mode='cache_write', to_mode='skip', ...)`. `TypeError` and
`KeyError` still raise. The Oct 8 dev credential drift raised
`AuthenticationError` from this helper and 500'd every listen accept for
about two days.
- `auth_error` and `connection_error` are allowed fallback reasons (they
would otherwise bucket to `other`). `timeout` and `capacity_full` were
already allowed. Listen and pusher initialize the four zero series so
`increase()` can see the first sample.
- Grafana alerts `omi-redis-cache-conn-warn` (any of those reasons over
10m, for 10m) and `omi-redis-cache-conn-page` (fail-open count / listen
accepts > 0.5 with at least 50 accepts in 5m, for 5m) cover
`job=~backend-listen-metrics|pusher-metrics`. `capacity_full` is
excluded so a maxmemory event does not page this pair.

## Alert signal

Sibling rules in `backend/charts/monitoring/alerts/` are Grafana
unified-alerting JSON, not PrometheusRule CRDs. The `omi_fallback_total`
rules in `alerts/resilience.json` query that counter directly. This PR
follows that path: no new recording rule, and no kube-prometheus values
change, because those files are not how these alerts are registered.
`alert-rules.json` is updated so the split and combined exports stay
equal. The 2026-10-08 incident predates these reason labels, so the
thresholds are structural (healthy ratio 0, every-accept failure about
1.0) rather than a Prometheus replay.

## Sibling cache helpers in `backend/database/redis_db.py`

- `_cache_set_fail_open` — changed. This was the only helper that
fail-opened solely on `OutOfMemoryError` and re-raised everything else.
Callers on the listen path: `set_in_progress_conversation_id`,
`set_conversation_meeting_id`. Also `cache_user_name` and
`cache_user_geolocation`.
- `_fail_open_raw_text` — unchanged. Deserialize fallback for legacy
cache values, not a cache write.
- `try_catch_decorator` (`set_generic_cache`, speech-profile and share
helpers, credits signal) — unchanged. Already swallows every exception,
including programming errors.
- `add_filter_category_item` — unchanged. Already fail-opens on
`redis.exceptions.RedisError`.
- `cache_signed_url` — unchanged. Direct `SET`, not a fail-open wrapper.
- `check_tts_rate_limit` — unchanged. Already returns a fail-open status
on any exception.
- `try_acquire_client_device_write_lock`,
`try_acquire_user_platform_write_lock` — unchanged. Already fail-open.
- `release_daily_summary_lock`, `release_notifications_job_run_lock`,
`release_conversation_goal_lock` — unchanged. Best-effort deletes, not
request-path cache sets.

`ConnectionError` subclasses other than `AuthenticationError`
(`BusyLoadingError`, `AuthorizationError`, `MaxConnectionsError` in
redis-py 5.0.8) map to `connection_error` because they are
connection-class faults. `AuthenticationError` is matched first so it
stays `auth_error`. `TimeoutError` is not a `ConnectionError` subclass
in this redis-py and keeps its own reason. The class-name fallback runs
only when redis-py does not expose that class, so a same-named exception
from another module, including the builtin `TimeoutError`, still raises.

tapping Start Speaking, DeviceGuidedVoiceIO.stop() ran while start() was
still awaiting the recorder's own start-up. stop() unconditionally called

landed during the race, instead of leaving it abandoned.

fix(listen): refill speaker embedding budget and skip unavailable pooled PCM (#21047) Follow-up to #20964 (merged a02bee4794; deployed to production listen 2026-10-08 21:08Z). Long-lived pendant sockets exhaust the lifetime embedding caps, and one unavailable pooled PCM interval aborts otherwise usable speech. Before measurements supplied with the incident (not independently queried): - `embedding_budget`: 106k exits in 11.9h (8.9k/h), over twice all live decisions (~47k). - 2026-10-09 06:00–08:00Z: 130 of 1,004 live sessions hit the budget; budget exits were 25% of all speaker-ID log lines. - `no_pcm`: 1.4/h → 1,280/h. - Live owner pending decisions: 1,018/h → 1,199/h. Replace lifetime socket exhaustion with a monotonic-wall-time token bucket: initial/capacity 16, refill 240/3600 attempts per second (one per 15 seconds). Attempts over t socket-hours are bounded by floor(16 + 240*t): ≤256 in the first hour and ≤240/hour asymptotically, at ≤10s query PCM per attempt (≤2,560s first-hour and ≤2,400s/hour steady-state query audio). An arbitrary one-hour window can use up to 256 including saved burst credit. Idle credit caps at 16; failures spend tokens; reservation precedes awaits. Conversation/profile churn and client audio timestamps cannot mint tokens. Reconnection still creates a new socket budget, as before; this is not an account-wide cap. Keep 12 attempts per voice per conversation. Reset uncarried IDs on rollover; carried manual mappings and validated automatic owner carry retain their attempts. Profile refresh within the same conversation preserves attempts. Accepted voices stop spending. All rejected voices, including far/noisy rejections, retain fresh-audio recovery opportunities within the 12-attempt allowance and socket bucket. Later clean clips can evict noisy evidence and re-arbitrate owner claims, withdrawing a competing automatic owner mapping. Failed one-second reconnect evidence is also allowed to accumulate normal full-length owner evidence. Retained evidence can still be re-arbitrated or rechecked against a recovered owner without more model calls. Skip unavailable PCM intervals; emit `no_pcm` only for an entirely unusable pool and recheck actual remaining PCM duration. Metric names, labels and exit reasons stay unchanged; the proposed `decided_voice` reason and early stop were removed after the independent review. Acceptance thresholds, margins, carry eligibility and paid non-owner naming/free owner recognition are unchanged. fix: stop reporting destructive-operation fences as backend-sync crashes (#20912)

## What changed and why

backend-sync reported a live destructive-operation fence as a crash at
`legal_holds.py:396`. The fence is correct: a running gate must refuse
provider writes. Callers emitted that exception as a traceback instead
of treating it as an expected refusal.

Error group (verbatim):

{"source": "gcp", "service": "backend-sync", "group":
"legal_holds.py:396 |
database.legal_holds.DestructiveOperationInProgress: external data write
blocked by destructive operation", "count": 12, "id":
"gcp:backend-sync-legal-holds-py-396-database-legal-holds-destructiveoperationinprogress-external-data-write-blocke"}

## Root cause

`external_write_fence` raises `DestructiveOperationInProgress`
("external data write blocked by destructive operation") when a
non-obsolete gate is still running. Cloud Error Reporting groups that
frame only when a traceback is logged.

1. Audio-merge artifact upload (`upload_playback_artifact` /
`upload_conversation_playback_artifact`) sat outside the handler's build
try/except. An unhandled fence became a Starlette 500 traceback. On the
final attempt the handler then called `mark_playback_unavailable` /
`mark_conversation_playback_unavailable`, which are the same fenced GCS
write (`owner_storage_write_gate` → `external_write_fence`). That second
fence escaped the upload `except` and reproduced the crash, so the
marker was never written while the gate was up.
2. Fire-and-forget postprocess writes (`save_structured_vector`,
transcript chunk vectors, non-reprocess action-item vectors) go through
`submit_with_context`. `_log_background_failure` logged them with
`exc_info`, which is this error group. The write is still dropped;
retrying the stale in-memory payload after the gate clears could
resurrect provider copies the deletion just purged.

Sync jobs, the conversation finalizer, precache, and the atom keyword
index already catch this fence without a traceback.

## Fix

- Audio-merge v1 and v2 uploads use the existing build contract: retry
with HTTP 500, and on the final attempt log without a traceback and
return 200 `failed_final`.
- The final-attempt playback-unavailable marker write has its own guard.
If that write raises `DestructiveOperationInProgress`, the handler logs
an info line and still returns `failed_final` instead of a Starlette
500.
- Background tasks that fail with `DestructiveOperationInProgress` log
an info line and do not attach a traceback. Other background failures
still log with `exc_info`.

## Product invariants affected

none

## How it was verified

From `backend/` with Python 3.11:

```
python -m py_compile routers/sync.py tests/unit/test_sync_audio_merge_job_tombstone_guard.py
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_sync_audio_merge_job_tombstone_guard.py tests/unit/test_executors.py::test_submit_with_context_defers_destructive_operation_fence_without_traceback tests/unit/test_executors.py::test_submit_with_context_still_logs_unexpected_background_failures -q --tb=short
```

Result: `22 passed` (exit 0). py_compile succeeded.

## Tests

-
`test_submit_with_context_defers_destructive_operation_fence_without_traceback`
— fence is info-only, no ERROR and no traceback.
- `test_submit_with_context_still_logs_unexpected_background_failures` —
other background errors still log.
- `test_v2_upload_fence_retries_instead_of_escaping` — v2 upload fence
returns 500 `retry` and does not stamp or mark unavailable.
- `test_v1_upload_fence_retries_instead_of_escaping` — v1 upload fence
returns 500 `retry` and does not write the marker.
- `test_v1_upload_fence_marker_fence_returns_failed_final` and
`test_v2_upload_fence_marker_fence_returns_failed_final` — the real
marker write hits `external_write_fence` on the final attempt; the
handler logs info and returns 200 `failed_final` with no traceback.

## UI evidence

UI-Evidence: none -- backend-sync fence handling only

Line-Count-Exception: backend/routers/sync.py | 2501 -> 2592 |
Final-attempt playback marker fence stays in the audio-merge handler.

feat(cli): omi app, a local test harness for Omi app webhooks (#20970)

* feat(cli): omi app, a local test harness for Omi app webhooks

Testing an app's webhook meant the phone app plus a publicly reachable URL:
trigger a memory from Developer Tools, speak for the real-time transcript, or
wait for the day summary cron tick, with webhook.site standing in for a
receiver. omi app replays the same deliveries locally and receives them
locally:

  omi app events                  what an app can receive
  omi app payload <event>         the sample body
  omi app send <event> --to URL   post it the way the backend posts it
  omi app verify --to URL         report whether a URL works in production
  omi app serve                   receive deliveries and print them

send mirrors the real request: the query parameters the backend appends, the
content type per event, the Idempotency-Key header, and the event id as that
key for button events. It exits non-zero unless the receiver answers 2xx and
reports what Omi would do next: whether the delivery would be retried or
dropped, and whether a realtime_transcript reply was long enough to reach the
user as a notification.

blocked new recovery admissions. Read-only production verification on
October 9 found all 100 pending jobs completed while all 100
conversations remained processing; examples had been completed since
September 28–29. The completed-job/noncompleted-conversation branch
waited forever. Queued, leased and BYOK-blocked entries had the same
unbounded-slot risk.

Bound pending waits to one hour using an immutable admission timestamp,
migrate legacy entries from job creation time, and reclaim expired
leases and BYOK-blocked slots before same-tick admissions. Preserve live
leases, existing job ownership, the ten-admission cap, and critical
content/binding/shrinkage refusals. Completed-job timeouts page only
after a successful cursor CAS as an aggregate; expiry never asserts
successful verification. The existing durable reconciler owns replay of
the original job; this change does not create second recovery
generations.

fix: add currency, letterlike, minus to latin-ext (#3801)

## Summary

* **What is the goal of this PR?** Give `latin-ext` fonts the Euro sign.
The preset stopped at General Punctuation (U+2000–U+206F), so every SD
font built with it lacked `€` and the other currency symbols, `™`, `№`,
and the minus sign `−`, even though the built-in fonts carry currency
and minus. The reader has no fallback font for SD fonts, so those
characters fall back to U+FFFD, and a font without U+FFFD does not draw
them at all (`EpdFont::getGlyph` returns null and `renderCharImpl` skips
it).
* **What changes are included?** `latin-ext` also covers Currency
Symbols (U+20A0–U+20CF), Letterlike Symbols (U+2100–U+214F) and U+2212.
`docs/sd-card-fonts.md` describes the new coverage, and its custom-range
example uses Arrows instead, since Letterlike Symbols is now in the
preset.

Every family in `sd-fonts.yaml` that uses `latin-ext` has `€` in its
regular source. The 23 built without `reading` dropped it (and `−`,
where the font has one), and all 31, `reading` included, dropped `™`,
which no preset covers today.

## Verification

`python3 fontconvert_sdcard.py --list-presets` shows the larger
`latin-ext` count. Converting Literata Regular at 18 pt with
`latin-ext,greek,cyrillic,ipa-chars` goes from 1,056 to 1,083 glyphs and
from 250,247 to 256,103 bytes (+2.3%); the converter already drops
codepoints a font lacks, so fonts pay only for glyphs they have.

## Scope Check

- [x] I have read SCOPE.md and ROADMAP.md.
- [x] This PR is **not** a new built-in theme (themes are temporarily
closed pending the move to SD-loaded themes).
- [x] This PR is **not** a new external network connector (sync engine,
cloud storage, remote file access, etc.).
- [x] This PR is **not** an interactive app, writing tool,
RSS/news/browser, media playback, or PDF feature.
- [x] The stock firmware does not already handle this well, **and** no
other popular CrossPoint fork already does (or, if one does, I explain
why CrossPoint still needs it below).
- [x] If this PR touches `freeink-sdk/`, `lib/hal/`, the bootloader,
OTA, or recovery code, I have coordinated with the relevant maintainer.

## Additional Context

* Host-side only; no firmware, RAM, or flash change, and the `.cpfont`
format is unchanged. SD font files grow by roughly 2% per style.
* The published catalog changes only when `release-fonts.yml` is next
dispatched.

---

### AI Usage

Did you use AI tools to help write this code? _**YES**_ — Claude found
the gap, wrote the change, and measured catalog coverage and size.

fix(KOSync): resolve upload XPaths for text outside

/

  • (#3923) ## Summary * **What is the goal of this PR?** Push an exact reading position to KOSync for EPUBs whose body text is not inside `

    `/`

  • `. Fixes #3665. Some Kindle/MOBI-derived EPUBs (Calibre output from a MOBI authored with div paragraphs) put every paragraph in `
    ` and leave a single empty `

    ` at the top of each chapter. For those books the upload resolver found no text at the page's visible offset, and every fallback (paragraph index, intra-chapter progress, byte percentage) resolved to that empty `

    `. The pushed progress was `/body/DocFragment[N]/body/p[1]`, so KOReader opened the chapter's first page instead of the page being read. A chapter with no `

    ` at all degrades one step further to the bare `/body/DocFragment[N]/body` (the second report in #3665); both come from the same filter and both are covered here. Confirmed on the wire against both the reference kosync server and crosspoint-sync with CrossPoint 1.6.5. * **What changes are included?** * `ChapterXPathResolver`: the visible-offset and progress resolvers now count every visible body codepoint, the same rule `ChapterHtmlSlimParser` uses to record page offsets, so the path can land in any element. * Whitespace-only runs are never used as anchors; a target that falls in one is carried forward to the next text run. The progress resolver measures up to the last non-whitespace codepoint so 100% still resolves inside real text. * `text()[N]` numbering is unchanged from 1.6.5: every non-empty run counts. crengine additionally drops a whitespace-only first child of a block element, but decides "block" and "pre" from the computed CSS (`display`, `white-space`), which this resolver does not see, so that rule is deliberately not mirrored. * Header docs updated; three new host tests, one obsolete assertion removed. ## Scope Check CrossPoint is intentionally narrow. See [SCOPE.md](../blob/master/SCOPE.md) and [ROADMAP.md](../blob/master/ROADMAP.md). Please confirm: - [x] I have read SCOPE.md and ROADMAP.md. - [x] This PR is **not** a new built-in theme (themes are temporarily closed pending the move to SD-loaded themes). - [x] This PR is **not** a new external network connector (sync engine, cloud storage, remote file access, etc.). - [x] This PR is **not** an interactive app, writing tool, RSS/news/browser, media playback, or PDF feature. - [x] The stock firmware does not already handle this well, **and** no other popular CrossPoint fork already does (or, if one does, I explain why CrossPoint still needs it below). - [x] If this PR touches `freeink-sdk/`, `lib/hal/`, the bootloader, OTA, or recovery code, I have coordinated with the relevant maintainer. (Not applicable: `lib/KOReaderSync` and its host test only.) ## Additional Context * Follow-up to #3174, which made the visible-text offset authoritative for uploads but kept the resolver's `

    `/`

  • ` filter from #1686. The layout parser never had that filter, so the two passes counted different characters whenever text lived elsewhere (divs, headings, blockquotes, table cells). * Verified against a real KOReader anchor for the same book: KOReader reported `/body/DocFragment[16]/body/div[45]/span/text().94`; the patched resolver, given the layout offset of that spot, emits `div[45]/span[1]/text()[1].94`. crengine's `createXPointerV2` treats an explicit `[1]` like the bare name, so both forms name the same node and character. * Host tests: `koreader_xpath_resolver` (20 tests) and the full suite pass. * Memory / flash: no new heap allocation patterns and no new tables; the per-element state is unchanged apart from counting text in every element. The resolver runs only at sync or bookmark time and streams the chapter once, as before. * Verified on an Xteink X3: the patched build pushes `/body/DocFragment[14]/body/div[201]/span[1]/text()[1].1051` for the same spot that 1.6.5 reported as `/body/DocFragment[14]/body/p[1]`, and a KOReader 2026.07 pull lands on that page. --- ### AI Usage Did you use AI tools to help write this code? _**YES**_ (analysis, implementation and tests drafted with Claude Code, reviewed and verified by me).
