feat(buzz-db): run push enqueue and channel TTL refresh in app code (#8135)

## Summary

Moves the producer side of the two event follow-up triggers into
application code. The triggers stay in place, so both producers run
until a later change drops the triggers after this ships to every pod.

Builds on #8130 (`AdmittedTx`). Refs BUZZ-176.

### Push match enqueue

New `store::event_follow_up::enqueue_push_match` replaces the
`events_enqueue_push_match` trigger
(`schema/functions/enqueue_push_match_job.sql`, migration 0023) and
matches it exactly:

- Same kind allowlist (9, 40002, 45001, 45003), now `PUSH_MATCH_KINDS`.
- Takes the same SHARED `buzz_push_gate:<community>` advisory lock as
its own statement, so under READ COMMITTED the lease check gets a
snapshot taken after the lock is granted. Lease activations still take
it EXCLUSIVE in `push.rs`.
- Same lease predicate (`active AND endpoint_enabled AND expires_at >
now`), then `INSERT push_match_queue ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
- Fails closed: any error rejects the event, as the trigger did.

It runs right after the INSERT, only when the insert affected a row. The
consumer side (claims, `lease_until`, attempts, reaper) is already
app-owned and is unchanged.

### Channel TTL refresh

`AdmittedTx` now records every channel that received an event (except
kind 9007 and channel-less events). `AdmittedTx::commit()` refreshes
their `ttl_deadline` as the last statement before COMMIT, which keeps
the commit-time behavior of the deferred `events_refresh_channel_ttl`
trigger (migration 0024):

- One savepoint per channel, in sorted order, under the same SHARED
`buzz_channel_ttl:<community>:<channel>` lock.
- Runs the same `UPDATE` with the same `archived_at`/`deleted_at`
filters as its own statement after the lock, so its snapshot follows the
lock grant. Its `ttl_seconds IS NOT NULL` qual filters a permanent
channel before any tuple lock, so a permanent channel's row is never
locked. An ephemeral channel's row lock is held through the remaining
refreshes and the COMMIT round trip (the trigger held it only inside
COMMIT).
- Lock keys come from one builder per protocol
(`channel::channel_ttl_lock_key`, `push::push_gate_lock_key`), shared by
the SHARED and EXCLUSIVE sides. The shared push-gate wait is observed
through `observe_advisory_lock(LockType::PushGate, …)`.
- On failure it rolls back the savepoint, logs a warning, and increments
`buzz_db_channel_ttl_refresh_failures_total{reason}`, where `reason` is
`lock_timeout` or `error`. The event still commits, matching the
trigger's `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS`. A cancelled statement (`57014`) still
rejects the transaction, because plpgsql never caught that either.
- While both producers run, an app refresh that hits `lock_timeout` is
counted, and then the trigger retries it inside COMMIT and may succeed.
So during the dual window the failure counter can over-report and the
worst-case wait doubles. Both go away when the retirement PR drops the
triggers, after which the counter is exact.

### Call sites

Every production `INSERT INTO events` calls
`event_follow_up::after_admitted_insert`:

- `insert_event_on`
- `insert_event_with_thread_metadata_tx`
- `LockedMemberSnapshot::replace_member_event`
- `replace_addressable_event`
- `publish_nip43_membership_locked`
- `accept_lease_event` (kind 30350, a no-op today, kept so the policy
has no exceptions)

`replace_parameterized_event_in_transaction_impl` inserts inside the
`parameterized_replace` savepoint. It enqueues the push job inside the
savepoint, so a rollback to that savepoint also drops the job, and
records the TTL channel only after the savepoint is released.

The two rolled-back verification probes (`verify_floor_guard_behavior`,
`verify_channel_roster_fence_behavior`) are named exceptions, because
they never commit.

### Source policy

`tests/observability_source.rs` adds
`every_production_event_insert_runs_the_follow_up_hook`. It scans every
`crates/*/src` and fails on any function that inserts into `events`
without the hook. Matching is normalized (letter case, whitespace, `\`
continuations, `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes, optional `public.`). The file is
masked once first: comments (`//`, nested `/* */`) and string,
raw-string (including `br"`/`cr"`), and char literals become spaces.
`#[cfg(test)]` markers, `fn` signatures and the hook are all found in
that masked view, so a marker in a comment (even a multiline block
comment) strips nothing, an `fn` line inside a multiline string doesn't
split a function, and a commented-out or quoted hook doesn't count. SQL
is still matched in the original text. A table test pins the masker's
output for each literal form. A fixture test pins what the scan rejects
(no hook, push without TTL, a hook in a line comment, block comment, or
string, lowercase or line-broken or escaped SQL, writers after test-only
items or under comment mentions) and what it ignores (writers in
`#[cfg(test)] mod`). A floor of seven hooked writers catches a scan that
silently stops seeing writers.

### Tests

`src/store/event_follow_up_postgres_tests.rs` is the contract suite from
the BUZZ-176 discovery work, ported to the `AdmittedTx` API. It is a
crate-internal `#[cfg(test)]` module because it runs `SET LOCAL`
timeouts and in-transaction reads through the crate-private
`AdmittedTx::conn()`. It runs on both the desired and migration schemas,
in two arms:

- **dual**: production during the migration window, with the triggers
and the app code both running.
- **app-only**: drops both triggers in the disposable database (and
asserts no partition clones remain), the way the retirement migration
will.

The trigger-only baseline is the base branch, where the same suite
passed before this change. The suite also pins the two branches that
differ from "swallow everything": a `lock_timeout` failure increments
`buzz_db_channel_ttl_refresh_failures_total{reason="lock_timeout"}`
exactly once, and a statement cancel (`57014`) during the refresh
rejects the event with no row, job, or deadline change.

## What got simpler

Nothing yet. This adds a parallel producer during the migration window.
It is what lets the follow-up PR delete two plpgsql functions, two
triggers, and the "keep in sync with migrations/00xx" duplication
between `schema/functions/` and `push.rs`.

commits.message:
(1/3) Harden hull() against degenerate input (#2100)

* Skip entities that lie inside or on a circle

_pt_arc takes sqrt(l**2 - r**2), which has no real value when the point is
inside the circle and degenerates to the point itself when it is on it: a
line end inside a circle, or a circle inside a bigger one, raised
ValueError; a line end on the circle produced an empty segment. Such an
entity cannot touch the hull beyond the circle, so it is not a candidate -
report it the way get_angle already reports an entity against itself.

Partially addresses #1190 and #1224.

* Return the start circle when nothing else can be reached

A circle with every other entity inside it is its own hull, but the march
raised "Hull could not be closed". The lone-circle shortcut was one instance
of this and is folded in.

* Treat edges of one circle as one entity

Two arcs on the same circle became two entities: arc_arc divided by the
distance between their centres, and since the march closes on identity it
could come back to the other one and fail to close. The merged bounds only
steer select_lowest_arc; every tangent takes the full circle.

Fixes #1888. Partially addresses #943 and #1224.

docs(sessions): correct the rationale for InMemorySessionService event deduplication

The deduplication guard in `InMemorySessionService.append_event` was documented as protecting against an orchestrator broadcasting the same `Event` to several concurrent `Session` references (#5723). ADK has no such broadcast: within one invocation all parallel branches share a single `InvocationContext.session` and serialize their appends, every produced event carries a fresh id, and persistent backends reject stale snapshots with `StaleSessionError` and enforce unique `event.id` keys.

The guard is still worth keeping for a different reason: it makes `append_event` idempotent for an equal re-delivery of an event, which callers that retry the call (e.g. a write buffer behind an RPC) rely on to avoid double-applying state or inflating their buffer. fix(python): preserve Decimal precision in table updates (#4431)

Python `Decimal` values and Arrow decimal scalars raise
`NotImplementedError` in `table.update(values=...)`. Register a Decimal
converter that emits quoted fixed-point text so the native cast to the
target column preserves every digit, including decimal128 and decimal256
values. Non-finite Decimal values raise `ValueError` with a static
message.

Closes #4360.

Validation with the native extension built from the current source at
7f593359, on macOS arm64 and Python 3.12.14:

- All 33 new regression cases failed before the fix and passed
afterward. They cover Python and Arrow scalar updates, signs, zero,
exponents, full 38/76-digit precision, and a Decimal context precision
of 6.
- 16 existing converter, update, and Decimal expression tests passed.
- Repository Ruff formatting and lint passed; formatting left all 156
files unchanged.
- A native round-trip check confirmed that an unquoted SQL number rounds
a high-precision value while the quoted Decimal update preserves it
exactly.

The full suite, other Python versions, and remote API were not
exercised.

AI assistance: Codex helped implement and validate the Decimal
conversion and its regression tests.

fix: preserve adaptive IVF probe defaults (#4168)

Keep IVF probe fields unset by default so Lance supplies adaptive
behavior. Preserve `nprobes`, `minimum_nprobes`, and `maximum_nprobes`
independently through Rust, Python, namespace, and remote request
construction, with compatibility fields serialized only when explicitly
configured.

The final Rust namespace and LSM propagation update depends on the Lance
release containing lance-format/lance#9184.

fix!: centralize entity name validation for remote APIs (#4490)

Centralize the entity name validation for tables, views, functions,
namespaces, secrets, and databases. This helps in several ways. One is
that percent-encoding is no longer needed in most cases (the exception
is database names, which can contain slashes). Another good thing is
that LLMs looking at this repository can now understand what the naming
rules are, since they will be the same here as on the server side.
Finally, this will help with the upcoming authZ code, since it also
needs to serialize these names, and needs to know that they don't
contain (among other things) colons.

feat!: carry a FunctionVersion's creation time as epoch millis (#4482)

Moves Function timestamps on the wire from RFC 3339 strings to epoch
milliseconds.

## What

- `FunctionVersion.created_at` (an RFC 3339 string) becomes
`created_at_millis` (milliseconds since the epoch, as an integer).
That's the shape Secrets, jobs and `FunctionErrorRecord` already use.
- Rust: `FunctionVersion::created_at() -> &str` becomes
`created_at_millis() -> i64`.
- Python: `FunctionVersion.created_at: str` becomes `created_at_millis:
int`.
- Fixtures and the mock server now send `1787270400000`, the old
`2026-08-21T00:00:00Z`.

Node.js doesn't expose `FunctionVersion`, so it doesn't change.

## Compatibility

Breaking, and it must ship together with the matching server change: a
server that still sends `created_at` fails to deserialize on this
client. Functions aren't deployed yet, so nothing is migrated.

## Tests

- `cargo test --features remote --test first_class_function_slice1`: 10
passed
- `cargo test --features remote --lib function`: 51 passed
- `pytest python/tests/test_first_class_function*.py`: 100 passed
- clippy, `cargo fmt --check`, ruff check and ruff format are clean

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011gDgA5ivgURRmvyyW92ubB

weekly-external: close a flake issue when it passes, and keep the checkpoint cache alive (#1151)

weekly-external.yml carried one permanently open `weekly-flake` issue, #1046,
since 2026-09-14, and re-downloaded 1.3 GB of model checkpoints every Monday to
produce the failure it reported. Three defects behind that.

THE LIFECYCLE NEVER CLOSED ANYTHING. Both jobs only opened issues and commented
on them, so a flake that got fixed left a standing open issue with no way back.
Each job now classifies its whole JUnit report and acts on the passes as well as
the failures: a notebook that passes gets a comment and
state_reason: completed, a notebook that fails afterwards reopens the same
thread instead of starting a new one, and a skipped notebook closes nothing,
because closing on a skip retires a failure nobody fixed. An open weekly-flake
issue now means a standing failure, and #1046 is retired by the first run after
this merges, by the job itself.

The parse moved out of the workflow into .github/scripts/weekly_issues.py,
which uses an XML parser and has tests. #1146 fixed the attribute regex in place
in both jobs; one tested parser replaces the pair, and it is what can report
`passed` at all. The issue listing also replaces the issue search, whose index
lags by up to a minute, so an issue a job had just created could come back
absent and be created twice. Duplicate suppression reads the most recent
comments rather than the oldest hundred.
tests/test_weekly_junit_attribute.py is deleted: it asserted the workflow's
literal regex text and then re-implemented the pattern in Python, checking

documented 10 GB limit.

THE SAVE NEVER RAN ON A RED WEEK. actions/cache@v4 declares post-if: success()
in its own action.yml, so its save step runs only when the job succeeded - and
this job fails on exactly the notebook whose download the cache exists to
remove. A cold run populated the cache in the prefetch step and then discarded
it. Split into actions/cache/restore before the prefetch and actions/cache/save
immediately after it, which is before pytest runs at all; the only condition on
the save is the cache miss.

THE ENTRY EXPIRED BETWEEN RUNS. GitHub removes entries not accessed in over 7
days, and this workflow ran only on Monday: 168 hours plus the scheduler's
queueing delay, so one missed week guaranteed the loss. A stable key is not
retention. Wednesday and Friday crons now route to a restore-only
hf-cache-touch job that runs no notebooks, downloads nothing and saves nothing.
Dropping any one scheduled run still leaves a five-day maximum gap, which the
test computes from the crons rather than asserting.

AND THE TOUCH JOB COULD NOT HAVE RESTORED MONDAY'S ENTRY AT ALL, found by the
pre-push review. actions/cache hashes the `path` input into a cache version, and
an entry is addressed by key AND version, so ${{ github.workspace }}/.hf-cache
keyed the save on /__w/<repo>/<repo>/.hf-cache inside the container and the
touch job's restore on /home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>/.hf-cache on the host.
Same key, different entry, every week, reported as a plausible miss. The
compression method is hashed in as well. Both halves are settled by
construction: all three cache steps take the relative literal `.hf-cache`, and
the touch job runs in ml4t/ml4t:latest, the image that saves the entry. The test
I had written compared the two `path` inputs as YAML text and they were equal,
which is why it passed; it now asserts the path carries no `${{` expression and

That a restore counts as an access has evidence from this repository rather than
from the documentation alone. The six hf-ch* entries test.yml maintains were
each created on one day and last accessed days later with their byte sizes
unchanged - hf-ch11-12-2026W40 created 2026-09-28T13:45:53Z, last accessed
2026-10-05T14:08:27Z, 814,967,808 bytes - and a restore is the only thing that

creation date and last-accessed date into the step summary after the restore, so
the claim the job rests on is measured on the runner instead of assumed. It
exits 0 on an absent entry, an unreadable API or a missing token, and was
exercised against the live API on all three paths. A touch miss is a warning,
not a failure: that is the normal state after a pin moves. Nothing here protects

Publish a contribution policy and report incoming pull requests against it (#1149)

Fourteen agent-written pull requests arrived across these repositories on
2026-10-07, one of them here (#1146). The code was not the problem; the review
cost was. The library ones bundled four to nine unrelated fixes apiece with no
issue behind them, and verifying the smallest properly took a full build and
about eighteen minutes of compute. This repository had nothing to point at: no
CONTRIBUTING.md, no pull request template, no issue templates.

CONTRIBUTING.md asks for one defect per pull request, an issue with a minimal
reproduction that the pull request closes, and a test that fails on main and
passes with the change. Each one moves the cost of checking a generated patch
from the maintainer to the contributor, which is the only thing that scales. A
verified defect gets fixed whatever it moves, and the policy says so; what a
report has to state is the compatibility impact, since a correction can change
a committed notebook output and the artifacts fitted under it. Changing a
convention - an annualization factor, a sign convention, a default, a label
definition - is a different request, because code elsewhere already depends on
the current one, so it starts with an issue about what the quantity should be.
The scope is fixed: no new chapter, notebook, model or dataset. AI use is
disclosed and the contributor answers for every line in review.

The notebook instruction is measured rather than assumed. Plain `jupytext
--sync` survives editing words inside an existing markdown cell and fails the
provenance gate when a markdown cell is inserted, so the policy asks for
`notebook_provenance.py sync-prose` for any text change and says which case
each command covers.

.github/workflows/pr-triage.yml reads a pull request's metadata and diff and
writes a report into the run summary. Every finding is decidable without
judgement: more than one chapter or case study touched, no closing keyword, an
.ipynb changed without its .py, no test beside a code change, nothing said
about AI tools. It posts nothing. The job's only grant is
`permissions: contents: read`, so no token in the run can comment, review,
label or close, and no second workflow republishes the findings; below the
report it renders the contributor-facing text as a reply for a maintainer to
edit and send, or to ignore. An earlier revision of this branch had a
workflow_run job that created and updated that comment itself, which is the
wrong authority for a mechanical check to hold over someone's work, so the
publication path is deleted rather than disabled. The job never gates a merge,
never closes anything and never fails, and it skips pull requests from
write-access authors, whose work is tracked elsewhere.

.github/workflows/claude.yml responds to @claude from a maintainer, which the
action already restricts to write access. Running a model over every incoming
fork pull request would put untrusted diff text in front of it with a key in
scope, and would pay per run for the cases that should be closed with a pointer
to the policy. It needs an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret, which is not set, so the
workflow is inert until it is.

The parsing lives in a tested script rather than inside the workflow because
the last piece of YAML-embedded parsing here read `classname=` as the test name
and filed three weeks of weekly failures under one wrong title (#1046).

Verified: tests/test_pr_triage.py 13 passed. Eight cases pin both directions of
each finding - the split request fires on a two-chapter diff and stays silent
when the second path is tests/ or utils/; the notebook check fires on an
unpaired .ipynb and stays silent on a pair; "See #1145" counts as no closing
keyword while Closes, fixed and a full issue URL all count. Five pin the
authority rather than the wording: the workflow grant is read-only and no job
overrides it, nothing in the repository triggers off this workflow's name and
could republish the findings, the triage script names none of the publishing
APIs, the author_association gate is parsed and evaluated, and every finding
survives into the draft reply. Five negative controls run, each failing the
suite: restoring the publisher workflow, a workflow-level write grant, a
job-level write grant, a gate that also skips CONTRIBUTOR, and dropping the
draft reply. Dry run against #1146's real files and body asks for the missing
issue and notes the missing AI disclosure, and does not ask to split a pull
request that should not be split. ruff check and format clean, every YAML file
parses.

ch08: the vol-scaled momentum formula now matches the annualized denominator the cell uses (#1150)

The cell divides a 21-day return by rolling_std(21) * sqrt(252), while the markdown
three lines above printed r_21d / sigma_21d, so the displayed vol_scaled_mom column
did not equal the formula the reader had just been given. Reported by an outside
contributor on #1146, who asked whether the annualized denominator was intentional
rather than guessing.

The formula is the thing that was wrong, and the feature pipeline says so.
case_studies/us_equities_panel/03_financial_features.py builds vol_{h}d as
rolling_std(returns, h) * sqrt(252) and then sharpe_{h}d as ret_{h}d / vol_{vol_h}d -
the same construction as this cell, under a section comment that calls them
"Sharpe-like return/vol ratios". A vol_<h>d column means an annualized rate estimated
on an h-day window everywhere in this repository, so the cell computes the quantity
the codebase intends. The two readings of vol_scaled_mom differ by a factor of
1/sqrt(252) = 0.062994, which is why the formula had to be corrected rather than
waved at.

The markdown now states that sigma_21d is annualized, writes the sqrt(252) into the
expression so it matches the column, names the pipeline that shares the convention,
and says what the ratio is not: the numerator is a 21-day cumulative return and the
denominator an annual rate, so it is not a standardized return and does not compare
across horizons. The rank invariance is stated as what it is, a property of the
percentile rank the feature is immediately turned into, not a reason for the choice.

Verified: with the annualizing constant and without it, vol_scaled_rank is identical
across 12 synthetic series over 300 days; markdown-only, so
notebook_provenance.py sync-prose kept the outputs and the execution stamp (0 stale,
0 outputs-changed). The notebook carries a pre-existing library-drift advisory that
this edit neither causes nor clears.

zephyr-cp: don't claim PWM drivers reject unproducible periods

`pwm_nrfx` skips the period check at 0 % and 100 % duty and never checks
the minimum COUNTERTOP, so out-of-range frequencies can be accepted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

zephyr-cp: allocate PWM only by channel

Remove the public whole-instance `iobroker_pwm_allocate()`. A PWM
allocation is always a channel, identified by its device and channel
number, like the GPIO, ADC and DAC allocations. A caller that needs a
group to itself asks for an exclusive channel: pwmio for a variable
frequency, and neopixel_write, which programs a whole nRF instance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

zephyr-cp: compute the PWM period in pwmio, not iobroker

iobroker now uses the requested frequency only to decide which channels
share a group, and returns just the device and channel. common-hal/pwmio
turns the frequency into a period from `pwm_get_cycles_per_sec()`
(truncating, as before) and passes it to `pwm_set_cycles()`.
`iobroker_pwm_period_cycles()` and the `period_cycles_out` parameter
are gone.

feat(durable): read returns images, optional Photon image processor

read returns an image file as one image block (programs get an ImageContent) plus an info diagnostic,
instead of an unsupported_image error. Limits are the conversation model's inputLimits.images.resize,
by default 2000x2000 pixels and 4.5 MB of base64.

- Without a processor: PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP within the limits pass through undecoded; the byte limit
  is checked before reading the file, dimensions from the header. Larger images and BMP are error results.
- With createCodingTools({ images }): the processor orients by EXIF, converts BMP to PNG, and shrinks to
  fit. ImageProcessor.prepare is async.
- @earendil-works/pi-durable/images: createPhotonImages(wasm) on @silvia-odwyer/photon 0.3.3 (web build);
  /images/node and /images/cloudflare load the wasm. The root and ./tools entries never reach it (enforced
  in check-entry-graphs).
- An image must be read whole: one that changes while read is read again, unlike a growing text file.
- A model without image input gets a diagnostic that it sees a placeholder.

feat(durable): nested tool calls, structured output, callers; storage errors end the Session

Nested tool calls: ToolExecutionApi.executeTool() runs another tool as its own pi.tool task owned by the caller,
keyed for replay-safe reattachment. Results for programs live in the caller's NestedResultDoc until it settles;
pi.live.nestedTools shows each call with the arguments it runs with and a summary. TaskOptions.abandonOnRestart
aborts work its creator awaited only in memory before it runs again after a restart.

Structured output: structuredOutputSchema and structuredOutput, validated; a tool without a schema gives programs its
bounded output (one text as a string, one image as itself, else the list). ToolExecutionResult.content is now output.
callers and modelTools decide who may call a tool.

Storage errors: any error a Storage method throws fails the Session, which closes itself; later calls and waits reject
with SessionFailed, watches end with session_failed, and Session.closed settles. Nothing retries in the Harness.
StorageRejected is removed; StorageRequestError marks invalid reads that fail only their call. Listener and onReport
errors are contained and reported.

Also updates scripts/issues/triage.ts and the vacation experiment for the content -> output rename.

feat: add local issue triage tool in scripts/issues

Syncs issues with gh, triages new ones with a pi-durable agent (category, duplicates, summary, p0/p1/none suggestion), and serves a web UI for decisions.

The nested worktree dedup compared the context file's realpath with the
main repo's file, so a worktree AGENTS.md symlinked to the main repo's

commits.message:
src/extra.i: fix segfault when a get_cdrawings() callback raises.

jm_append_merge() reports a failed callback with messagef() before calling
PyErr_Clear(), so messagev() runs with the callback's exception still set.
Its function-local statics were initialised on the first call with
PyImport_ImportModule("pymupdf"), which returns NULL while an exception is
set, and the NULL was then passed to PyObject_GetAttrString(), so the first
exception raised by a callback in a process killed the interpreter with
SIGSEGV instead of being reported. Once the statics were set, later calls
still called pymupdf.message() with the exception set, which prints only
part of the message.

messagev() now puts any pending exception aside with PyErr_Fetch() before
its static variables are initialised, and restores it with PyErr_Restore()
after the message is output, discarding any error from the output itself in
that case; with no exception pending, an error from the output is left set
as before. The behaviour for a failing callback is otherwise unchanged: the
failure is reported and the exception is cleared.

tests/test_drawings.py:test_cdrawings_callback_exception() runs the case in
a child process, because the crash only shows when there has been no
earlier messagef() call in the process, and checks the message is output
whole.

commits.message:
Fix StopWatch controls and circular icon layout (#163)

* Fix StopWatch controls and circular icon layout

* Turn off StopWatch green LED on battery power

Turn off the Watcher's LCD rail and amp at rest; keep its battery run in flash (#60)

* Turn off the Watcher's LCD rail and amp at rest; keep its battery run in flash

While the screen is off, the SenseCAP Watcher now powers down its LCD and
touch rail (EXP_PWR_LCD) as well as sleeping the panel. The QSPI lines go to
GPIOs held low first, so the idle bus doesn't feed the unpowered panel. On
wake the rail comes back, the panel is reset and set up again, and LVGL
redraws the whole screen.

The speaker amp's enable (EXP_PWR_CODEC_PA) now follows the codecs: off once
muse_audio closes them to rest, on 20 ms before they open. The amp runs from
the battery, so left enabled it idled all night. The codecs have their own
always-on supply and keep their setup. This goes through a new muse_board_t
hook, audio_power; other boards leave it NULL.

The battery meter also saves its run to NVS at the periodic saves and when
USB comes back (not at the start), so a run survives a battery that runs flat
and takes the RTC memory with it. battery_boots counts boots on battery since
USB power was last seen, and tools/muse/power.py reports it when above one.
The battery test harness gains a file-backed NVS fake to test both.

* Address review: touch lines low with the LCD rail, amp after the codecs, battery_boots fixes

- Hold the touch bus (TP_SDA/TP_SCL) low while the LCD rail is off, as init()
  does, and hand it back to the I2C peripheral on resume.
- muse_audio: the amp goes on once the codecs are open and set, and off before
  they close. A failed open leaves neither codec open and the amp off.
- battery_boots: counted once per boot that began on battery, so power.reset
  no longer counts; cleared in flash as soon as USB power is seen.

* Watcher: give the panel 200 ms after the LCD rail, and clear it before it's on

On hardware, waking with only 50 ms between the rail and the panel's setup
sometimes left garbage on screen: the SPD2010 runs its own firmware, which
takes a while to start, and at boot ~150 ms pass there. Wait 200 ms, and clear
the panel's memory to black before turning it on, so nothing random shows
before LVGL's redraw lands.

[Core] Report provisioning errors on an existing cluster instead of asserting INIT (#11002)

The retry loop assumed every error raised for an UP or STOPPED cluster
carried no_failover, and asserted INIT otherwise. Invalid credentials or
config, an unsupported feature, or a cloud identity error do not, so the
user saw 'AssertionError: ClusterStatus.UP' instead of the error. Raise
the last error with no_failover for such a cluster; an INIT cluster still
fails over.

docs(tts): document Kokoro English dictionary versus BART comparison (#1006)

### Why is this change needed?

Kokoro callers need to understand why English pronunciation uses
dictionary lookup before BART fallback, and why a nonempty fallback
result is not evidence of a correct pronunciation. Add a bounded 40-word
comparison with all outputs, CMU reference alternatives, source/model
hashes and explicit limits on interpretation.

The note distinguishes the older dictionary-only probe from current
main, whose initialism rules already protect uppercase API/CPU/GPU. It
reports coverage and raw agreement rather than an unsupported accuracy
rate, and does not attribute observed errors to conversion or to BART
architectures generally. Link it from the documentation index and Kokoro
guide; include the CMUdict attribution/license alongside the reference
excerpts.

Validation: checked all 40 records, summary counts, source hashes and
relative links; the analysis harness passed three tests for reference
variants, missing entries and inference-failure accounting; `git diff
--check` passed. Documentation and recorded data only; no new model runs
or runtime changes in this PR.

fix(asr): take seam-token timing from the window that heard it mid-window (#975)

### Why is this change needed?

Word timings around chunk seams in long-form batch TDT are
systematically early, by enough to open gaps that are not in the audio.
The reported case (#971): `actually` 27.20–27.44 followed by `go?` at
28.16, a 0.72 s "gap" where the speech is continuous. Anything that
consumes word timings — subtitle cues, clip export, silence removal — is
affected.

#### Cause

Emission timestamps are reliable across the 15 s window except at its
edges. Decoding the same audio at many window positions and comparing
each word against the decodes that heard it mid-window:

| Position in window | Start bias | End bias | Words off by > 160 ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 s – 13 s | within ±20 ms | within ±20 ms | 0–2 % |
| 13 s – 14 s | ≈ −50 ms | ≈ −100 ms | 5–7 % |
| final ≈ 0.9 s | ≈ −190 ms | ≈ −300 ms | ≈ 55 % |

Same curve on English read speech, an English conference talk and a
German interview.

The overlap decodes every seam token twice, once in each position, but
`mergeUsingMatches` kept the **left** window's copy of each matched
token, timing included:

```swift
result.append(left[leftIndex])
```

So the tail timings went into the transcript and the good ones were
discarded. Roughly one word in ten of any recording longer than a window
sits in the affected zone.

#### Change

For a matched token, `timestamp` and `duration` now come from the right
window's copy once that copy is at least `seamTimingHeadGuardFrames` (6
frames, 480 ms) past the right window's start. The token's identity —
piece, casing, confidence — still comes from the left window, which had
real left context. Nothing is re-decoded.

- `ChunkProcessor` records each chunk's start frame and passes it to
`mergeChunks`. Without one the merge is unchanged, which is what the
dual-decode arbitration path and existing callers get.
- `ASRConfig.seamTimingRealignment` (default `true`) and CLI
`--no-seam-timing-realignment` reproduce the previous output exactly,
for A/B measurement. The flag is carried through the two config rebuilds
in `AsrManager`.
- A "Seam Timing" section in `Documentation/ASR/LongTranscription.md`.
- `SeamTimingRealignmentTests` (7 tests); the existing chunking and seam
suites pass unchanged (315 tests).

#### Measurements

Seam-tail words, end timing off by more than 160 ms against the
mid-window reference, on this branch (`main` + this change):

| Recording | Before | After | Interior words, for comparison |
|---|---|---|---|
| English read speech, 108 s | 40 % | 0 % | 6 % |
| English conference talk, 400 s | 37 % | 7 % | 3 % |
| German interview, 400 s | 27 % | 8 % | 6 % |

Applied to v0.15.6 (fixed-stride, mel-context path) the figures are 62 →
4 %, 36 → 7 %, 23 → 6 %. The reported phrase becomes `audio[26.72-27.44]
actually[27.44-28.08] go?[28.08-28.72]`, with no gap.

#### What it does not do

- Text can still change at a seam, because later passes read the
timestamps. On the three recordings above it removed one spurious repeat
at a seam (`actually go? they go?` → `actually go?`) and changed nothing
else; on v0.15.6 it removed a duplicated word (`came from from?`) and
changed one mumbled aside.
- Unmatched tokens between two matches and the `mergeByMidpoint`
fallback keep their existing behaviour.
- Gaps that open inside a window are a different failure and are not
addressed.
- The `swift format lint` error on `AsrManager.swift:250` (`decoder_`)
is pre-existing on `main`.

Closes #971 for the seam class; the ~0.5 s word-end truncation reported
there is this mechanism.

Avoid unnecessary CTC vocabulary inference (#993)

### Why is this change needed?

Vocabulary rescoring currently computes CTC evidence even when no
transcript
word is eligible for correction. This adds `hasCTCRescoringCandidates`
to the
rescorer and prepared session so callers can skip that work. It uses the
existing
matching rules, including aliases, compounds, multiword terms and
thresholds.

Empty vocabulary or timings return false. Acoustic rescue conservatively
returns
true for nonempty inputs. Callers that need standalone keyword
detections must
still run rescoring. Term forms are also prepared once, and transcript
words are
normalized once per request.

Initial measurements on one Apple Silicon Mac reduced unnecessary
separate CTC
work from about 140–153 ms to 0.3 ms, and shared-head work from about 12
ms to
0.3 ms. These are component timings, not whole-dictation speedups.

### Validation

- 144 selected checks pass, including parity against real CTC evidence
across
12 candidate cases, threshold handling, empty inputs and acoustic
rescue.
- Contribution lint, strict lint for changed Swift files and formatting
checks
  pass.
- The default Intel build passes, as does Intel Release compilation for
macOS 14
  with the optional text-processing trait disabled.

The streaming vocabulary test class is excluded: its first-word
replacement
failure also reproduces on unchanged main. The full suite and hosted CI
have not
been verified green.

fix(wordspotting): zero CTC keyword-spotter audio padding (#1003)

### Why is this change needed?

prepareAudioArray now builds the window through makePaddedAudioArray.
That helper still allocates a rank-1 [maxSamples] or rank-2 [1,
maxSamples] array in the mel input's float32 or float16 type, calls
reset(to: 0) on the buffer, then writes the clamped leading samples. New
tests check short clips, an empty clip, a clip that fills the window, a
clip longer than the window, both dtypes, and both ranks, and require
the copied prefix to match and every padding index to be finite and
zero.

CTC keyword spotting on short clips often returns log-probs that ignore
the audio. Different sentences can greedy-decode to the same empty
string and share one identical matrix, and the same clip can succeed or
fail from run to run. prepareAudioArray allocates a fixed-length
MLMultiArray for the mel window and copies only the clip into the front.
The removed comment treated the tail as zero because
MLMultiArray(shape:dataType:) was assumed to zero-fill; that initializer
leaves storage uninitialized, and the mel model reads the whole window,
so a non-zero or non-finite tail drives the log-probs.

Fixes #991

Co-authored-by: Matt Van Horn <455140+mvanhorn@users.noreply.github.com>

[rollout, vllm, trainer] fix: restore default vLLM compile caching (#8167)

### What does this PR do?

Resolve the TODO in `verl/trainer/constants_ppo.py` that disables vLLM's
compile cache due to vllm-project/vllm#31199. That concurrent
cache-write bug was fixed by vllm-project/vllm#35420, first included in
vLLM 0.17.0; Torch 2.10+ also contains the native atomic-write fix from
pytorch/pytorch#162432. verl now requires vLLM >=0.18.0, so remove the
obsolete workaround and restore upstream defaults.

Explicit `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE` values are still forwarded to Ray
workers for troubleshooting. The checkpoint server-adapter test also
uses upstream defaults. On recent Torch versions, removing this override
also restores vLLM's default AOT selection.

No open PR addressing this change was found in the duplicate checks
below. This PR does not claim to resolve the separate LoRA issue #3149.
AI assistance was used to research and implement this change.

[data] fix: correct enable_thinking_default YAML value and loss mask mismatch (#8086)

### What does this PR do?

Two bugs in `MultiTurnSFTDataset` cause a mismatch between tokenization
and loss masking when the chat template produces different token counts
for thinking ON vs OFF.

1. **Wrong YAML type**: `enable_thinking_default: none` in
`sft_trainer_engine.yaml` is the string `"none"`, not Python `None`.
`bool("none")` evaluates to `True`, so `_process_single_message`
silently enables thinking mode.
2. **Loss mask ignores thinking mode**:
`extract_system_prompt_and_generation` (which measures the generation
prompt length for loss masking) receives `apply_chat_template_kwargs`
but never `enable_thinking_default`. It always measures with the
template's built-in default, regardless of what
`_process_single_message` uses.

Bug 1 triggers bug 2: `_process_single_message` renders with thinking
ON, while `extract_system_prompt_and_generation` measures with the
template default. When the two modes produce different prefix lengths,
template tokens get non-zero loss and are trained on as content.

This PR fixes both:
1. **YAML default**: `none` → `null`, so the value becomes Python `None`
and both methods skip passing `enable_thinking`, letting the template's
built-in default apply consistently.
2. **Loss mask**: `extract_system_prompt_and_generation` now receives
`enable_thinking_default` via `apply_chat_template_kwargs`, matching
`_process_single_message`. This prevents the mismatch from reoccurring
if a user explicitly sets `enable_thinking_default` to `true` or
`false`.

[rollout, vllm] feat: add request hooks to vLLMHttpServer.generate (#8082)

### What does this PR do?

Adds two request hooks to `vLLMHttpServer.generate()`, so a server
subclass can change a request's sampling parameters and its output
without overriding `generate()`. Admission, pause/resume, and
weight-sync coordination stay in `generate()`.

This implements the hook option discussed in #7735 ([maintainer
comment](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/7735#issuecomment-5884513068)).
The motivating user is
[verl-project/verl-genrank#4](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-genrank/pull/4),
which needs per-request `logprob_token_ids` and the selected-token rows
in the output. Today `generate()` keeps only the sampled token's log
probability, so verl-genrank overrides the whole method and copies its
admission bookkeeping (`_submission_paused`, `_resume_event`,
`_admitting`). That copy is already behind main: since `e42d6af6`, the
commit verl-genrank pins, `generate()` moved admission into
`_park_until_admitted()` and started rejecting late arrivals.

verl-omni also overrides `generate()`. Its pinned verl (`fefb080`)
predates the admission gate, so these hooks may help it keep upstream
admission when it updates.

-
https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+logprob_token_ids
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Environment: `uv sync --frozen --all-packages --extra vllm` (vllm
0.29.0, torch 2.13.0), on a machine without a GPU.

- `pytest
tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_submitter_gate_on_cpu.py`: **16
passed** (12 existing, 4 new).
- With the source change reverted, the three hook tests fail and the
default-behavior test passes.
- The full "Run vllm CPU unit tests" list from `vllm.yml`: 97 passed, 5
failed. The 5 failures are all in `TestCliArgsVllmParserRoundTrip`
("Failed to infer device type") and fail the same way on unmodified
main, because this machine has no GPU; the CI runner has one.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: passed.
- GPU tests were not run. The change calls an empty hook before
`SamplingParams` is built and passes both return values through a hook
that returns them unchanged.

### API and Usage Example

```python
class SelectedTokenServer(vLLMHttpServer):
    def _preprocess_sampling_params(self, sampling_params):
        sampling_params["logprob_token_ids"] = sampling_params.pop("selected_token_ids")

    def _postprocess_output(self, output, final_res, sampling_params):
        rows = final_res.outputs[0].logprobs if final_res.outputs else []
        ids = sampling_params.logprob_token_ids
        output.extra_fields["selected_logprobs"] = [[row[t].logprob for t in ids] for row in rows]
        return output
```

The subclass is selected through `vLLMReplica.server_class`, as today.

### Design & Code Changes

Both hooks sit in the existing "Hook methods for subclass overrides"
section; their defaults keep the current behavior.

- `_preprocess_sampling_params(sampling_params: dict) -> None`
- Input: the request's sampling-parameter dict after upstream fills its
defaults (`max_tokens` already removed, `logprobs` set to 0 or `None`,
`detokenize` defaulted).
- Order: before `SamplingParams` is built and before
`_park_until_admitted()`.
- Errors: an exception fails the request; it is never admitted, so the
admission counter is untouched.
- `_postprocess_output(output, final_res, sampling_params) ->
TokenOutput`
- Input: the `TokenOutput` built by upstream, the engine's
`RequestOutput`, and the built `SamplingParams`.
- Order: after the engine stream ends and the admission counter is
released; runs for normal outputs and for requests aborted with empty
outputs. Requests rejected at the admission gate return before it.
  - Errors: an exception fails only this request.
- Hooks should add to `extra_fields` rather than replace it: the PD
prefill leg reads `kv_transfer_params` from there.
- With PD disaggregation, each leg calls `generate()` with its own copy
of the sampling parameters, so the hooks run once on the prefill server
(whose output is discarded) and once on the decode server.
- CI: `test_submitter_gate_on_cpu.py` imports vllm, which the `cpu`
extra does not install, so `cpu_unit_tests` skips it and it was not in
the vllm workflow's CPU list. This PR adds it to the "Run vllm CPU unit
tests" step, which also starts running its 12 existing gate tests.

[hardware, profile] fix: improve existing pytorch profiling to support other pytorch supported device (#8151)

### What does this PR do?

`get_torch_profiler` knew exactly one device activity,
`ProfilerActivity.CUDA`, and
`TorchProfilerToolConfig` accepted exactly one device keyword, `"cuda"`.
On an accelerator that is
not CUDA there was then no way to record device kernels: the default
`contents=[]` asks for CUDA,
torch logs `CUDA is not available, disabling CUDA profiling` and the
trace holds CPU ops only, while
naming the real device in `contents` fails config validation.

torch exposes one `ProfilerActivity` member per backend it can profile,
named after the device type
it profiles, and a single profiler session records exactly one of them.
So the active platform's
`device_name` is both the activity to collect and the `contents` keyword
that requests it. This PR
resolves it that way instead of hardcoding CUDA, and takes the accepted
device keywords from
`torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity` rather than from a verl-maintained
list.

**No new `PlatformBase` API** — `device_name` is already an abstract
property.

### No change for existing platforms

`PlatformCUDA.device_name` is `"cuda"`, and `PlatformROCm`,
`PlatformMetaX` and `PlatformIluvatar`
inherit it (torch exposes HIP as `torch.cuda`), so all four build
exactly the same `activities` list
as before. Platforms with no matching member (`npu`, `mlu`, `musa`,
`gcu`, `tpu`, `supa`) still get a
CPU-only trace, exactly as they do today when torch disables the
unavailable CUDA activity — the
warning explaining it is now verl's, and it names the device.

`xpu`, `hpu` and `mtia` start working with no further verl change and no
plugin code.

### Out-of-tree backends whose activity is not named after the device
type

`DEVICE_ACTIVITIES` is a module-level `device type -> ProfilerActivity`
map, so a backend that needs
a different pairing can add one entry from its plugin:

```python
from verl.utils.profiler.config import DEVICE_ACTIVITIES
DEVICE_ACTIVITIES["mlu"] = torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.PrivateUse1
```

This is deliberately data rather than API: it keeps the mapping out of
`PlatformBase` while leaving
privateuse1-based backends a one-line override. In practice those
backends all select a vendor
profiler through `global_profiler.tool` instead, which this PR does not
touch.

`CPU` and `PrivateUse1` are excluded from the map and `"privateuse1"` is
not an accepted `contents`
keyword: CPU activity is collected in every trace regardless of
`contents`, and `PrivateUse1` is
torch's slot for an out-of-tree backend rather than a device type any
platform reports as its
`device_name`, so accepting it would validate a value that is then
silently never recorded.
`"cpu"` remains accepted.

### Why this is not a duplicate

- #7988 proposed the same fix through two optional `PlatformBase` hooks,
`torch_profiler_activity()` and `torch_profiler_content_name()`. This PR
drops both: `device_name`
already carries the information, which removes the paired-hook invariant
between them, removes the
requirement for every plugin to implement them, and leaves
`platform_base.py` untouched.
- `gh pr list --repo verl-project/verl --state open --search "profiler
activity"` — nothing else open
  in this area.

### Test

```bash
pytest tests/utils/test_torch_profile.py
# 50 passed, 18 subtests passed

VERL_PLATFORM=intel     pytest tests/utils/test_torch_profile.py   # 50 passed, 18 subtests
VERL_PLATFORM=cambricon pytest tests/utils/test_torch_profile.py   # 50 passed, 18 subtests

ruff check verl/utils/profiler/config.py verl/utils/profiler/torch_profile.py \
           tests/utils/test_torch_profile.py                        # clean
ruff format --check <same three files>                              # clean
```

New tests:

- `TestDeviceActivityFromPlatform` — a non-CUDA device is recorded and
CUDA is *not* added alongside
it (torch checks CUDA before every other device, so leaving it in would
disable device profiling
altogether); CUDA platforms are unchanged; every entry in
`DEVICE_ACTIVITIES` resolves to its own
activity, so the lookup holds for whatever members a given torch build
exposes; a device with no
member warns; a CUDA-written `contents` run on another accelerator warns
and records no device
activity; `contents` naming only profiler options warns nothing; a CPU
platform does not add CPU
  twice.

The non-CUDA cases take their device from whatever
`torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity` the running
build exposes rather than hardcoding one accelerator, and skip if a
build offers none.
- `TestDeviceContentsConfigValidation` — every keyword in
`DEVICE_CONTENTS` validates, profiler
options still validate, an unknown keyword and `"privateuse1"` are both
rejected.

Two pre-existing tests (`test_get_torch_profiler`,
`test_cpu_activity_added_for_device_only_contents`)
assert the CUDA activity, which until now was hardcoded and so held on
any machine. They now patch in
a CUDA platform, stating the assumption they always had — without it
they fail when the suite runs on
non-CUDA hardware.

No new e2e CI test: CI has no non-CUDA device. Manually verified end to
end on Intel Arc Pro B60
(device kernels present in the chrome trace, which was not the case
before this change).

### API and Usage Example

No API change. On a non-CUDA accelerator, the default config now records
device kernels:

```yaml
global_profiler:
  tool: torch
  global_tool_config:
    torch:
      contents: []          # records the active platform's device activity, e.g. xpu
      # contents: [xpu]     # equivalent, explicit
      # contents: [stack]   # CPU-only, as requested, no warning
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/profiler/config.py` — `DEVICE_ACTIVITIES` map built from
`torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.__members__` (keyed by lowercased
device type, so the lookup does
not depend on how torch capitalizes a member); `DEVICE_CONTENTS` derived
from it for config
validation, replacing the hardcoded `["cuda", "cpu", "memory", "shapes",
"stack"]`.
- `verl/utils/profiler/torch_profile.py` — `get_torch_profiler` resolves
the active platform's
`device_name` through that map; warns when the platform has no activity,
and when `contents` names
  a device activity belonging to a different backend.
- `docs/perf/torch_profiling.md` — documents the device keyword per
accelerator.
- `tests/utils/test_torch_profile.py` — as above.

[hardware, recipe] feat: DeepSeek-V4-Flash GRPO on ROCm (MI355X) with QAT, FP8 or BF16 training (#8146)

### What does this PR do?

Makes DeepSeek-V4-Flash GRPO run end to end on AMD MI355X with an FP8
rollout, and gives it one recipe with three training modes. Follow-up to
#7050 (ROCm enablement) and #7455 / #7470 (Megatron-Bridge path). Two
commits:

1. **`[docker]` image.** `docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4`
builds the versions the runs were validated with: Transformer Engine
2.18 (ROCm build: Triton grouped GEMM path that avoids a bf16
grouped-GEMM backward hang on gfx950, float-scale blockwise FP8 GEMM), a
libhsa-runtime that returns memory under `expandable_segments` on ROCm
7.2.x, Megatron-LM `fd1121b8f` plus the `deepseek-v4-rocm-support`
commits (config-driven FP8 fake quantization, FP8-training alignment
options, and the `index_select` gather of the unfused CSA sparse
attention that upstream introduced with the reworked SBHD path in
NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#6400, which this older base predates),
Megatron-Bridge 0.5.0 plus a fix that keeps the FP8 weight export on the
checkpoint's power-of-two scale grid, and four vLLM 0.26.0 patches
applied at build time (NaN guard on the FP8 indexer logits; CuMem wake
cache release, vllm#49857; indexer K-cache block-flat layout on
gfx950/gfx942, vllm#50455; SwiGLU clamp on the FP8 Triton fused MoE
path).
2. **`[recipe]` one script, three modes.**
`examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh`,
`TRAIN_MODE=qat|fp8|bf16`. `qat` is BF16 training with Megatron's FP8
fake quantization (weights on 128x128 power-of-two scales, inputs on
1x128 float scales, straight-through estimator) and an FP8 W8A8 vLLM
rollout; `fp8` is Transformer Engine blockwise FP8 training with float
activation scales; `bf16` is BF16 training with a BF16 rollout. All
modes round the KV latent and the indexer q/k the way the rollout's FP8
KV cache and FP8 indexer do. Everything is a transformer-config
override; the only environment variables are the two Transformer Engine
kernel selectors.

Why the alignment matters: on ROCm, vLLM quantizes FP8 activations with
float scales (amax / 448) while Transformer Engine's blockwise recipe
uses powers of two, so the same training code that aligns on NVIDIA
(DeepGEMM) does not align here. With the rollout's rounding reproduced
in training, `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean` at step 1 drops to the
BF16-forward level and the train/rollout KL stays flat over 300 steps.

The Megatron-LM and Megatron-Bridge changes live in the author's forks
while they are proposed upstream; the Transformer Engine wheel and the
libhsa-runtime are published as release assets because no official ROCm
package carries those fixes yet.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs.
https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+deepseek-v4+rocm
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (FP8 checkpoint), 4 nodes x 8 MI355X, ROCm 7.2.3,
GRPO/GSPO on DAPO-Math, validated on AIME-2024 every 10 steps:

| Mode | step-1 `rollout_probs_diff_mean` | step-1 `rollout_corr/kl` |
300 steps | AIME-2024 acc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| qat | 0.0096 | 0.0021 | KL 0.0022 -> 0.0029, no NaN/hang | 0.60 ->
0.76 |
| fp8 | 0.0097 | 0.0021 | KL 0.0022 -> 0.0039 | 0.60 -> 0.76 |
| bf16 | 0.0060 | 0.0008 | KL 0.0008 -> 0.0011 | 0.59 -> 0.79 peak |

On the image built from this branch, a 7-layer cut of the model (single
node) gives diff / KL of 0.0129 / 0.0068 in `qat` and 0.0130 / 0.0069 in
`fp8` over 3 steps, matching the earlier runs. Per step on 32 GPUs: ~490
s (`qat`), ~420 s (`fp8`), ~330 s (`bf16`), of which ~85 s is the weight
sync.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -f docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4 -t rocm-verl-dsv4 .
# Ray on every node (commands in the script header), then on the head node:
WK=<wandb key> TRAIN_MODE=qat bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh
TRAIN_MODE=fp8 TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=5 bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh trainer.val_before_train=False
```

`fp8=e4m3 fp8_recipe=blockwise fp8_blockwise_act_pow2_scale=False`),
applied to both the actor and the reference policy.

stm32/eth: refill only RX slots without buffers

The Xarxa pool migration assumed that consuming an RX descriptor always
takes the buffer out of the slot. But some slots (invalid frames and timestamp
context descriptors) can keep their buffers when skipped by
`pop_current()`.
Naive refilling would therefore overwrite an occupied slot and decrement
the empty-slot count without actually filling any empty slot. When the count
reached zero, RX stalled.

This skips slots that still have buffers when refilling the RX ring.

Fixes: b74e7284ea44

stm32/usb: support double-buffered bulk endpoints on USB v1

Implement `alloc_endpoint_bulk_{in,out}_double_buffered()` for the USB
v1 peripheral (STM32F1, F3 and L1), tested on an STM32F103.

A double-buffered endpoint uses both packet buffers of its hardware
endpoint, so the endpoint number can't be used in the other direction.
Only one buffer is handed to the hardware at a time and the interrupt
handler releases the other one, so every transfer completion is seen.
SW_BUF and STAT are written separately when releasing a buffer, as
toggling STAT in the same write would undo the hardware's own NAK to
VALID transition.

Merge pull request #7216 from ArthurHeymans/usb-double-buffer

embassy-usb: allow double-buffered bulk endpoints

Merge pull request #7215 from ArthurHeymans/stm32-usb-pma-copy

stm32/usb: faster copy of USB packet memory

embassy-usb: add double-buffered bulk endpoint allocation

Some USB controllers can double-buffer bulk endpoints, so the hardware
can transfer the next packet while software handles the previous one.

Add `Driver::alloc_endpoint_bulk_{in,out}_double_buffered()` as provided
methods that allocate an ordinary bulk endpoint by default. Drivers that
support double buffering override them and return their regular endpoint
type, so classes don't need to change. Expose them through
`InterfaceAltBuilder::endpoint_bulk_{in,out}_double_buffered()` and add
`CdcAcmClass::new_double_buffered()`.

stm32/usb: copy packet memory without per-word memcpy

Copying each packet-memory word through a slice with a runtime length
made the compiler emit a memcpy call per word, which dominated the
per-packet CPU time. Convert whole words with fixed-size arrays and only
handle the tail separately.

stm32/low-power: reject unimplemented families, implement G4 Stop

Enabling `low-power` on a family with no `enter_stop` branch used to compile a `sleep()` that set SLEEPDEEP and entered whatever PWR defaulted to, without clearing wake-up flags or restoring the clock on exit; it is now a `compile_error!`, and STM32G4 is implemented and removed from the list. G4 enters its low-power-regulator stop (`LPMS = 0b001`), clears `WUF1..5`/`SBF` via `PWR_SCR` and re-inits the clock on exit because it has no `STOPWUCK`, and was validated with CI's feature sets and `-Dwarnings` across all 11 implemented families plus 7 rejected ones, with `cargo fmt --check` clean.

Prevent reentrant AbstractCodeWriter state failures (#3314)

Section interceptors can push and pop temporary writer states while popState() visits parent states. Growing the live ArrayDeque invalidates its iterator and can throw ConcurrentModificationException.

Snapshot the parent states before invoking interceptors. This preserves the existing order and stack behavior while allowing scoped context and nested section interception. Add regression tests and a changelog entry.

jsonText(_:) and jsonObject(_:) rendered the key bare, so jsonText("0") read
array index 0 instead of the key "0", and jsonText("a.b") was a PGRST100.
A String is now always a quoted key, with \ and " escaped the way PostgREST
reads them, and a new Int overload renders a bare array index.

test(postgrest): lock the unrepresentable-query property (#1497)

* test(postgrest): lock the unrepresentable-query property

A parent filter cannot be ORed with an embedded one: PostgREST sends them
as separate query parameters and always ANDs them. The typed API keeps
that query unwritable because _PostgrestFilter<R> only joins filters of
the same relation. Add a fixture that tries it, and a script that
requires it to fail to compile with the expected diagnostic. Run the
script in the CI spm job.

feat(postgrest): add @Aggregate for aggregates in @SelectionOf (#1495)

* docs(postgrest): select aggregates through @SelectionOf via Columns extensions

Declaring an aggregate on the relation's Columns lets a @SelectionOf
property select it under its own alias, so two sum()s no longer collide
on the response key. Document the pattern on the aggregate and
@SelectionOf docs, replace the string-select workaround in the sum()
note, and lock the select string and decoding in with a test.

Follows the SDK-1810 discussion.

* feat(postgrest): add @Aggregate for aggregates in @SelectionOf

A selection property can now declare an aggregate of one of the
relation's stored columns:

    @Aggregate(.sum, of: \Order.amount) var total: Double?
    @Aggregate(.count) var rows: Int

The entry is aliased with the property name, so two aggregates of the
same function no longer collide on the response key. The key path names
the stored property because an attribute argument is type-checked
before @Table expands, so Order.columns.amount does not resolve there.
The expansion coerces the aggregate to
any PostgrestColumnExpression<Relation, Property>, which rejects both a
key path rooted on another relation and a property typed other than
the aggregate's result.

PostgrestAggregateFunction becomes public as the attribute's argument
type. @Table rejects @Aggregate, and @SelectionOf diagnoses unreadable
arguments and @Aggregate combined with @Relationship. A Columns member
stays the documented escape hatch for casts, JSON paths, aggregates
through an embed, and sums decoded as Int or Decimal.

SwiftSyntaxBuilder and printed with swift-format under a built-in
configuration, so the output is the same on every machine.

* fix(postgrest): escape quotes and backslashes in names the macros splice

@Table, @Column and @SelectionOf read their string arguments with
representedLiteralValue, which undoes the author's escapes, then spliced
the value between quotes in the expansion. A relation or column name
holding " or \ produced an expansion that did not parse. The name is now

* refactor(typegen): move supabase-typegen into its own package under tools/

SwiftPM fetches the dependencies of every product a package vends, so

separate package, and the root manifests are back to their previous
dependencies.

The generator's CamelToSnake.swift is a symlink to the @Table macro's
source, replacing the copy, so @Column is decided by the macro's own

* fix(typegen): rename relations that would shadow types @Table's expansion uses

A relation named draft, columns or coding_keys became a struct whose
name matched a type @Table nests inside it, so PostgrestColumn<Draft, …>
inside the nested Columns resolved to Draft.Draft and the file did not
compile, with exit 0 and no note. Those names, and the Postgrest* types
the expansion spells unqualified, now get the Table suffix and a note.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(typegen): emit readOnly and the @PrimaryKey, @Generated and @Default markers

* feat(typegen): generate Postgres enums as RawRepresentable structs

Each enum in a selected schema, and any other enum a generated column
uses, becomes a RawRepresentable struct conforming to
PostgrestFilterValue; enum columns and arrays of enums use it. Labels
go through the identifier and collision rules, with rawValue, init and

from the Swift enums postgrest-typegen emitted.

* feat(typegen): generate Postgres enums as Swift enums

Generated code is regenerated by its user, so a label added to a
Postgres enum is not a breaking change for it; the SDK's Enum-like
Values rule covers the SDK's own types. Each enum is now a String enum
conforming to Codable, Hashable, Sendable and PostgrestFilterValue,
matching postgrest-typegen's Swift output, with an explicit raw value
only where the case name differs from the label. The V3 migration note
is dropped: the old generator already emitted Swift enums.

* style(typegen): fit the enum test fixture in 100 columns and reword a comment for cspell

* test(typegen): compile the golden output in root test targets (SDK-1588)

The integration, postgrest-typegen and hostile goldens, generated with
--access-control public, are now the Generated.swift sources of three root
test targets built with -enable-library-evolution. A macro or PostgREST
change that breaks generated code fails swift test at the root; EmitterTests
in tools/supabase-typegen compares the generator's output with those files
and rewrites them under SUPABASE_TYPEGEN_RECORD=1, so they cannot drift.

SupabaseTypegenOutputTests runs queries through the generated types:
relationName, a snake_case column, a Draft without an ALWAYS identity column,

relationships in a hand-written @SelectionOf. The postgrest-typegen target

IntegrationTests compiles the integration-schema golden through a symlink

Columns extensions in Tests/IntegrationTests/Postgrest are gone; the
@SelectionOf types now point at the generated relations.

A temporal_values table (timestamptz, timestamp, date) backs a live
round-trip test. Both timestamps round-trip. A date column encodes, but
the shared decoder rejects PostgREST's date-only value, recorded as a
known issue.

* fix(postgrest): decode Postgres date values without a time

PostgREST sends a `date` column as `YYYY-MM-DD`. The shared decoder
accepted only full timestamps, so every model with a `date` column (any
supabase-typegen output with one) failed to decode. String.date now
falls back to a date-only ISO 8601 value, read as midnight UTC, and
requires it to be the whole string.

The integration date round-trip now asserts the decode for real.

* fix(build): pass -enable-library-evolution to the typegen output targets on Apple platforms only

commits.message:
trivial: Use USB IF instead of BT SIG namespace (#3505)

Device Information Service 1.1 says that the vendor ID can be either
come from the Bluetooth SIG or USB IF namespace. Zephyr by default uses
1=BTSIG instead of 2=USBIF.

The default VID/PID come from the common-use OpenMoko USB vendor ID.
Also most commercial entities probably have a USB VID but maybe not a
Bluetooth VID.

Logitech devices advertise with this setting set to 2.

Signed-off-by: Daniel Schaefer <dhs@frame.work>
feat(boards): Add ZMK variant for upstream rp2040 board (#3175)

fix(behaviors): declare all behavior config structs as `static const` (#3515)

Lower-memory devices (such as the STM32F04 used on the Ferris) tend to
struggle with bigger keymaps, in part due to the fact that behaviors
have a (sometimes) non-negligeable memory impact.

The worst offender being macros, who’s list of bindings often hold long
a decent amount of pretty heavy data structures, all on the RAM.

Declaring all of the behavior config structs as `static const` allows
the compiler to move them from RAM (which can be pretty limited) to the
progmem (which is *very* abundant for the needs of the firmware, even on
the Ferris).

On the Aekeynox community-keymap (of which I am a core maintainer), this
saves about 1400B, which is about 8.5% of the total RAM of the Ferris,
with no noticable difference at runtime.

commits.message:
chore(release): prepare v2.2.32 documentation and version

Summarize the latest security improvements, safer imports, proxy handling, cache fixes, and text rendering improvements.

Add a standalone v2.2.32 Recent Updates section, synchronize usage and development documentation, and bump the package version to 2.2.32.

fix(import): show and confirm new shell commands

List new Custom Command shell commands in full before applying an import.
Require confirmation for Replace All and Merge, with Cancel selected by
default. Imports that add no new commands continue to apply immediately.

Escape control characters in preview values, paths, and commands so imported
text cannot hide commands or manipulate the terminal.

fix: bound how long a stalled proxy or jj call can hold up the status line

The usage and status-page requests set `timeout`, which only covers an
idle socket. Behind HTTPS_PROXY the request has no socket until the proxy
answers CONNECT, so a proxy that accepts the connection and never answers
held the render forever. Destroying the request wouldn't end it either:
the proxy agent opens its own connection and keeps it until the proxy
answers, and that connection kept the process alive after printing.

- Both requests now have an overall deadline (the same 5 seconds). At the
  deadline the request is destroyed and the agent's connection to the
  proxy is closed through an AbortSignal (`createProxyAgent`).
- jj calls get git's 5 second timeout; they had none.

fix(git): parse .git files and remote URLs in linear time

Both parsers backtracked quadratically on input a repository controls:

- A `.git` file is read in every folder above the session's directory.
  `gitdir:\s*(.+)$` could split a run of whitespace between `\s*` and the
  path at every position, rescanning the line each time: a 100 KB file
  took about 5 seconds per render. The path now has to start at a
  non-space.
- A remote URL's path had its slashes trimmed with `/^\/+|\/+$/g`, which
  rescans a run of slashes from every position in it. The path is now
  split on `/` and its empty segments dropped, with the same result.

fix: connect directly to hosts NO_PROXY excludes

The usage and Claude Status requests used HTTPS_PROXY whatever NO_PROXY
said. The usage request carries the account's OAuth token, and a user who
keeps api.anthropic.com off a proxy (for example a TLS-inspecting
corporate one) had it sent through that proxy anyway.

Both requests now connect directly when NO_PROXY (or no_proxy) lists the
host or a domain it's in: `*`, `anthropic.com`, `.anthropic.com` or
`*.anthropic.com`, optionally with `:443`. HTTPS_PROXY itself is still
read in uppercase only, as documented.

fix: keep private settings files private when saving and backing up

- Saving ccstatusline's settings writes a temp file and renames it over
  settings.json, so the file took the temp file's default permissions:
  one the user had made 0600 came back 0644. The temp file is now created
  with the permissions of the file it replaces.
- The .bak and .orig backups of Claude Code's settings.json were created
  0644 whatever settings.json's permissions were, and that file can hold
  secrets (env, apiKeyHelper). Backups now get settings.json's
  permissions. An existing backup is removed first, since overwriting a
  file keeps its old permissions.

fix(skills): keep the skills log inside its folder for any session id

The skills hook and the status line build the log path from the payload's
session_id. An id containing `/` or `..` named a file outside
~/.cache/ccstatusline/skills: the hook appended to it and the Skills widget
read it. Session ids are UUIDs, so only letters, digits, `-` and `_` get a
log now; any other id writes nothing and shows no skills.

fix(git-review): pass branch and host names after -- to gh, glab and ssh

The Git PR widget passes the current branch to `gh pr view` and `glab mr view`,
and the origin's SSH host to `ssh -G`, as plain arguments. A branch or host
named like an option (a planted .git/HEAD can say `ref: refs/heads/--web`, an
scp-style remote can name its host `-oProxyCommand=...`) would be read as one.
They now follow `--`, which ends option parsing in all three.

fix(powerline): download fonts into a private temp folder

The font installer cloned into os.tmpdir()/ccstatusline-powerline-fonts-
<timestamp> and then ran install.sh from it. On Linux /tmp is shared, so
another account could create that folder, world-writable, between the
installer's existence check and the clone. The clone then succeeds into
a folder that account owns, and it can replace install.sh before it runs.
The folder now comes from mkdtemp: a random name, created 0700 for this
account.

git and install.sh also run without a shell now, so the temp path is
never parsed as shell syntax.

fix(update-checker): accept only release versions from the npm registry

The registry's `version` went unchecked into the install commands the TUI
shows, and into the update it runs. For npm on Windows that runs npm.cmd
through cmd.exe, so a version such as `2.3.0 & calc` would have run a
second command. checkForUpdates now treats anything but a plain semver
version as a registry failure, and runGlobalPackageInstall refuses one.

fix(git): stop respawning git outside repos and across session cwds (#631)

Two cases defeat the persistent git cache and make every render spawn git
again, forever:

- Outside any repository, getGitRepoMetadata finds no git dir, so the
  persistent cache is never read or written and `rev-parse
  --is-inside-work-tree` (plus the remote lookups of the origin/upstream
  widgets) run on every render. runGitArgs now returns null without
  spawning when git is certain to fail: no GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/
  GIT_COMMON_DIR in the environment and no `.git` entry or `HEAD` on the
  physical path from cwd up to the root. Every command runGit issues needs
  a repository, so the result is the same null git's exit 128 gave.
- The cache file was keyed by git dir but stored a single file-level cwd,
  so two sessions in one repo at different cwds (root vs a subdirectory)
  discarded each other's entries on every render. The file is now keyed by
  (git dir, cwd). Some outputs are cwd-scoped (`ls-files --unmerged`), so
  sharing entries across cwds would not be correct either. Existing
  per-repo cache files are simply no longer read.

Measured (git spawns per render, heavy config, ttl 0): non-repo cwd 4 -> 0;
root/subdir sessions alternating 14 -> 0 once warm. bench2, 20 interleaved
passes, load 42-53 on 6 cores, CPU median (user+sys incl. children):
git17 root 1642 -> 1422 ms (-13%), git17 subdir 1711 -> 1389 ms (-19%),
heavy root 2102 -> 1837 ms (-13%). stdout is byte-identical.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(ansi): fast-path ASCII and memoise cluster widths (#633)

getVisibleWidth() is called on every widget, separator and line during a
render, and each call walked the text cluster by cluster: a code-point copy
to strip escapes, then for every cluster an Array.from plus several
\p{...} regex tests and two string-width calls. On a heavy powerline
config that was ~12% of render CPU.

- getTextDisplayWidth: a printable ASCII character followed by a code
  unit below U+0300 (the first \p{Mark}; ZWJ, variation selectors, the
  keycap and emoji modifiers are all higher) is a one-column cluster on
  its own, so count it without building the cluster.
- getClusterWidth: memoise cluster -> width in a bounded per-process Map
  (cleared at 4096 entries), and call string-width once per cluster
  instead of twice.
- getVisibleText: copy each run between escape introducers with one
  slice instead of one code point at a time.

Results are unchanged: a differential test of old vs new
getVisibleWidth, getVisibleText, truncateStyledText (widths 0-7, with and
without ellipsis) and applyLineGradientSegment over every string of up
to 4 tokens from a 24-token alphabet (ASCII, controls, CJK, text and
emoji pictographs, VS16, combining marks, keycap, ZWJ, regional
indicators, skin-tone modifier, lone surrogate, PUA powerline glyph,
SGR, OSC 8 BEL/ST, C1 CSI/OSC, lone ESC) - 346,200 strings, 6.6M
comparisons - plus 20,000 random strings with random code points from
all planes, found 0 mismatches. Rendered stdout is byte-identical on the
heavy, default, livelike, block and git17 configs.

Measured (node, fork/exec, interleaved, 45 passes, load ~59 on 6 cores):
heavy config CPU median 2007 -> 1849 ms (-7.9%), p90 2257 -> 2062 ms,
new faster in 38/45 paired passes, RSS 128 -> 106 MB. Default config
unchanged (paired ratio 0.998). In-process getVisibleWidth: 243-char
ASCII line ~190x faster, heavy rendered lines ~20-30x, CJK/emoji ~8-12x.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ansi): never truncate to a line wider than maxWidth (#625)

truncateStyledText measured each run of text between escape sequences
separately, while getVisibleWidth measures the escape-stripped text. A
grapheme cluster split by an escape (U+2764, SGR, U+FE0F) therefore
counted as 1 + 0 columns instead of 2, the loop never overshot, and the
function returned the original, over-wide text.

Cluster the escape-stripped text, as getVisibleWidth does, and copy
escapes that fall inside a cluster. This also drops the rescan of the
rest of the visible run for every cluster.

fix(cache-timer): stop reporting HOT after interrupts and local commands (#628)

scanTailForState treated any trailing main-chain user row as an in-flight
request. Claude Code also writes user-role rows that never reach the API:
the "[Request interrupted by user]" marker left by Esc, and the
bookkeeping rows of local slash commands such as /cost or /model
(<local-command-caveat>, <command-name>, <local-command-stdout>). A
session ending on one of those showed HOT indefinitely, even after the
prompt cache had gone cold, which is the state the widget exists to warn
about.

Treat those rows like an assistant row that refreshed nothing: they end
the turn, and the countdown keeps anchoring on the newest assistant row
with cache activity. Rows with any other content (including isMeta
prompt-command expansions and hook context, which are sent to the model)
still count as in flight.

fix(install): keep unreadable Claude settings instead of overwriting them (#627)

installStatusLine caught any error from loadClaudeSettings (a JSON parse
failure such as a trailing comma, EACCES/EBUSY, or a read racing Claude
Code's own write), printed a warning, fell back to {} and then saved a
settings.json containing only statusLine. Permissions, hooks, env, model
and every other key were lost: the .bak written by saveClaudeSettings is
immediately overwritten by the widget-hook sync, and the .orig backup is
overwritten by the next install.

loadClaudeSettings already returns {} when the file does not exist, so
any error it throws means the file exists but cannot be read or parsed.
In that case install now aborts with an error naming the file and the
reason, leaving it (and any previous .orig) untouched; the .orig backup
is taken only after a successful read. This matches uninstallStatusLine,
which already refuses to modify unreadable settings. The TUI shows the
error text in an "Install Failed" notice instead of a 2-second flash.

feat: add a Session Cost Rate widget (#671)

* feat: add a Session Cost Rate widget

Session Cost shows what a session has cost so far, but not how fast it's
spending. Session Cost Rate divides the session cost by time, the
agent's hourly rate: `Rate: $5.00/hr`.

By default it divides by the time Claude spent working (the API
duration Claude Code reports), which reads as the rate for the hours it
actually worked. A `t` keybind switches to clock time, the whole session
including time spent waiting for the user, which reads as the burn rate.
It shows nothing until a full minute of the chosen time has passed,
since a rate over the first seconds swings wildly.

* fix: enable session cost rate label editing
