feat: add an Extra Usage Daily Budget widget (#672)

* feat: add an Extra Usage Daily Budget widget

With a monthly extra usage limit, the useful number during a day is how
much can still be spent per day without running out before the limit
resets. Extra Usage Daily Budget shows what's left of the monthly limit
divided by the days left in the month, today included, so it rises on
light days and falls on heavy ones.

Monthly limits reset at 00:00 UTC on the 1st, so days are UTC days.
A `w` keybind switches to counting weekdays only (Saturday and Sunday
in UTC); today always counts, even a weekend day, so the budget never
divides by zero. Once the limit is used up it shows $0.00; without a
monthly limit it shows nothing, like Extra Usage Remaining.

fix(tui): hold install and update screens until their action finishes (#676)

* fix(tui): hold install and update screens until their action finishes

Confirming an install, uninstall or global update started its async action
and left the Yes/No dialog live. A second Enter started the same action
again, so `npm install -g` ran twice at once and both runs went on to write
Claude's settings.json. ESC returned to the previous menu while the action
kept running, and when it finished it jumped the TUI to the main menu (or the
Install Complete notice) from wherever the user had gone. The pinned version
mismatch screen's "Update npm global install" item had the same problem.

App now runs these actions one at a time. While one runs, the confirm
dialog and the mismatch screen show a working line in place of their options
and ignore ESC; a ref blocks a second start even before that screen
re-renders. When the action settles, its own navigation takes over as
before, including the failure paths.

* test(tui): share the whole-App render harness

Move the scratch config, probe stubs and Ink rendering used by the App
tests into helpers/render-app.ts, next to wait-for-ink.ts, so other tests
that drive the whole TUI can use the same setup.

* test(tui): put chalk's color level back after a whole-App test

The App sets chalk's global color level from the settings it loads, and
the whole-App test helper didn't restore it. Test files that run later in
the same process then rendered at that level instead of their own: a
No Color check could see 256-color codes. The sandbox now restores the
level along with the mocks and the config path.

fix(jsonl): stop the reverse reader looping on a chunk's leading newline (#675)

* fix(jsonl): stop the reverse reader looping on a chunk's leading newline

iterateJsonlLinesReverseSync walks each chunk backwards with
chunk.lastIndexOf(0x0a, end - 1). When the newline it just consumed sat
at index 0, end became 0 and the next search ran with an offset of -1,
which Buffer.lastIndexOf counts from the end of the buffer. The reader
jumped back to the chunk's last newline and yielded the same lines
again, forever.

That happens whenever a transcript starts with an empty line, or when
the byte at size - k * 1 MiB is a newline. Thinking Effort falls back to
this reader when the payload's effort.level is present but not a level
it accepts (for example ""), so a matching transcript kept the status
line spinning at full CPU and never printing.

Stop searching once end reaches the start of the chunk.

* refactor(jsonl): route both reverse newline searches through one helper

The reverse reader searched for the previous newline in two places, and
only the one inside the loop needed the guard against an offset of -1.
lastNewlineBefore() holds the guard and the reason for it, so both
searches behave the same and the loop body stays as simple as it was
before the fix.

fix(hooks): only point widget hooks at ccstatusline's own command (#674)

Saving settings with a hook-enabled widget (Skills) syncs Claude Code
hooks that run `<statusLine.command> --hook`. That happened whatever the
status line command was. With ccstatusline configured but another tool
installed as the status line (for example `bash ~/.claude/statusline.sh`),
every ctrl+s or Save & Exit added PreToolUse(Skill) and UserPromptSubmit
hooks running that script with `--hook`. The script then ran on every
prompt and Skill call, and Claude Code adds UserPromptSubmit output to
the conversation, so whatever it printed reached the model.

Hooks are now added only when the status line command contains
`ccstatusline`, the same test the legacy-hook cleanup already uses to
recognize ccstatusline hook commands. npx/bunx with any version, a global
or absolute-path binary, a local ccstatusline.ts checkout and
shell-wrapped commands keep their hooks. For any other command the sync
only removes ccstatusline-managed entries, which also cleans up hooks an
earlier save pointed at another tool's script.

fix(tui): ignore letter shortcuts when ctrl or alt is held (#669)

* fix(tui): ignore letter shortcuts when ctrl or alt is held

Letter shortcuts compared the typed character without checking
modifiers, so ctrl+letter and alt+letter ran the plain-letter action:
ctrl+r toggled raw value, ctrl+d deleted a widget, and on macOS alt+arrow
(sent as ESC + letter) fired whatever letter followed. A few handlers
patched ctrl+s one key at a time with `&& !key.ctrl`; widget keybinds
checked ctrl but not alt.

Shortcuts now compare against getPlainInput(), which is empty while ctrl
or alt/option is held, across the line editor, widget keybinds, Edit
Colors, Global Overrides, Powerline setup/themes/separators, the line
selector and the hide-state checklist. Arrows, Enter, ESC, shift and text
entry are unchanged, and modifier combos are free for bindings of their
own.

* test(tui): wait for each shortcut's effect instead of a fixed delay

The shortcut tests sent keys and checked the result after a fixed 25 ms. On a
busy machine Ink can take longer, so the bare-key cases could fail even though
the shortcut works. They now wait until the shortcut's effect shows (up to
3 s), and a follow-up key waits for the previous key's redraw. Checks that a
modified key does nothing give it 150 ms to act.

After each wait the test also gives React two setImmediate turns: React draws
a frame, then attaches the new input listener in a scheduled effect, so a key
sent the moment the frame shows could reach no listener.

* feat(tui): edit a widget's label with e

The label editor opened with b (la(b)el…). Custom Text, Custom Command,

fix(powerline): keep separator inversion list dense when editing (#673)

The separator editor wrote `separatorInvertBackground[i]` straight into a
copy of the saved list. That list is often shorter than the separators: its
schema default is `[false]`, and hand-edited or imported configs commonly
add separators without extending it. Toggling (t) or cycling (left/right) a
separator past the end of the list left holes in the array, which JSON saves
as `null`. With three separators and the default list, selecting the third
and pressing `t` saved `[false, null, true]`; the next load failed
validation, so both the TUI and the status line fell back to defaults with
the invalid-config warning.

Pad the list to one entry per separator, defaulting to false, before any
edit. Missing entries already rendered as not inverted, so nothing changes
visually; add, insert and delete now also work on aligned entries.

fix: show Extra Usage Utilization before the month's first charge (#668)

Until the first extra-usage charge of the month, the usage API reports
`utilization: null` alongside the monthly limit and the amount spent
($0). The widget treated the missing utilization as no data and
rendered nothing, so it looked broken on every account with extra
usage enabled until the first charge.

When the API reports no utilization, work it out from the amount spent
and the monthly limit. An API-reported value still wins, and accounts
without a monthly limit render nothing, as before.

fix(widgets): describe the Extra Usage widgets for Enterprise accounts too (#670)

* feat: label Extra Usage as spend on accounts without plan limits

On usage-based plans (Claude Enterprise) the usage API reports every
rate-limit window as null and no limits[] entries: there's no plan limit
to go over, and extra usage is the account's whole spend. The Extra
Usage widgets still called it overage ("Overage Used: $123.45"), and
their picker descriptions only mentioned pay-as-you-go overage, so
Enterprise users had no reason to think these widgets were theirs.
Searching the picker for "enterprise" or "spend" didn't find them.

The parser now flags a response that explicitly reports no plan limits
(`noPlanLimits`). The flag is kept in the usage cache and through the
merge with statusline rate_limits, and the three widgets label their
value "Spend Used", "Spend Left" and "Spend" when it's set. Only an
explicit null counts and any limits[] entry counts as a limit, so every
uncertain case keeps the "Overage" label. A cache written before this
change keeps the old label until its next refresh.

The widget descriptions now mention both Pro/Max overage and Enterprise
spend, which also makes the picker's search find them.

* test: cover the Spend label with an edited label

Upstream's label editor (#601) gives each widget one default label,
while Extra Usage Used, Remaining and Utilization pick "Overage" or
"Spend" by account. The editor offers the Overage label, since it has
no usage data, and an edited label replaces whichever one the account
would show.

* refactor: keep the Enterprise wording, drop the Spend label detection

With the label editor (#601) in main, anyone on a usage-based Enterprise
plan can relabel the Extra Usage widgets' "Overage" to "Spend" in a few
keys, so detecting those accounts from the usage API's response shape
isn't worth its cache field and heuristics.

What stays is the wording: the three widgets' descriptions say they
cover Pro/Max overage and Enterprise spend, the docs say the same and
point at the label editor, and picker searches for "enterprise" or
"spend" list the three widgets first, which a new test checks.

* test: check the picker lists the Extra Usage widgets first, however many there are

* test: look for the Extra Usage widgets among the widgets that mention the word

* refactor(widgets): share Extra Usage Used and Remaining's code

The two widgets were the same class apart from how the amount is worked
out, and their label, name, description and preview sample. They now
extend ExtraUsageAmountWidget, the way the Tokens widgets share
TokenCountWidget. Rendering is unchanged.

fix(powerline): customize a theme with the colors it showed (#677)

Customizing a Powerline theme (c in the theme list) copied the theme's
colors onto the widgets by counting every widget in a line, restarting at
the first color on each line. The renderer counts differently: a widget
merged into the next one shares that group's color, and with Continue Theme
on, each line picks up where the previous one stopped. So the copy could
differ from what the theme had just shown. With Model merged into Context
Length, the pair shared one background under the theme, but the copy gave
Context Length the next color and shifted every widget after it; with
Continue Theme on, every line after the first restarted at the first color.

Number the widgets with the same slot rule the renderer uses to carry the
theme across lines, now shared from powerline-theme-index, and continue the
numbering across lines when Continue Theme is on. Lines without merges and
with Continue Theme off get the same colors as before.

fix(renderer): truncate at zero width, keep FLEX text, no custom colors at No Color (#678)

* fix(renderer): keep truncating when the reserved width leaves no columns

Full minus 40, and Full until compact past its threshold, subtract 40
columns from the terminal width; Full subtracts 6. On a narrow terminal
that went to 0 or below, and every width check treated a non-positive
width as "no width detected": the line printed at full length and
wrapped, while 41 columns still truncated to a single ".". The TUI
preview cut the line at the terminal edge instead, so it no longer
matched what Claude Code received.

Clamp the effective width at 0 and treat any detected width, 0
included, as known, in both the plain and Powerline renderers. When the
reserve takes the whole terminal the line now truncates to nothing, the
continuation of what 41-43 columns already show. An undetected width
(null, or 0 from the caller) keeps the fallback behavior.

* fix(renderer): stop reading widget text FLEX as a flex separator

The plain renderer stood each flex separator in the assembled line as
the string 'FLEX' and later split the line on that string. A widget
whose rendered text was exactly FLEX with no color codes around it (No
Color mode, or a color name the palette doesn't have) matched too: its
text vanished and the line got a second flex gap.

Push null for a flex separator instead, which no widget output can
equal. Powerline mode already uses its own marker and is unchanged.

* fix(colors): emit no 256-color or truecolor escapes at Basic and No Color

getColorAnsiCode returned raw 256-color and truecolor escapes for hex:
and ansi256: colors at every color level. With No Color selected, which
the TUI describes as disabling all color output, a widget colored
hex:FF0000 on hex:0000FF still printed \x1b[48;2;0;0;255m\x1b[38;2;255;0;0m;
Basic did the same.

Return no code for these formats at the ansi16 level (Basic and No
Color), as the function already does for gradient specs. This matches
the TUI, which only offers these formats at 256 Color and Truecolor and
clears them from widgets when switching to Basic or No Color, so they
only reach these modes through a hand-edited config. Named colors are
unchanged.

* refactor(renderer): flatten the no-width flex fallback branch

The else branch re-checked terminalWidth === null, which the preceding
condition (a flex separator and a known width) already implies when a
flex separator is present. Chain it as else-if on hasFlexSeparator
instead of nesting an if/else inside the else.

* test(custom-command): start each runtime once before its capture tests

On a fresh CI machine the first start of a runtime can take seconds while
its binary is read from a cold disk. The capture tests start Node for the
first time in their opening case, so that case once ran past its 5s limit
(5018 ms) while the same case one test later took 146 ms and the rest about
60 ms. Each runtime now starts once in a setup hook with its own timeout,
before the timed tests.

fix(git): detached HEAD, tag-shadowed branches, submodule worktrees and wide PR titles (#679)

* fix(git-branch): show detached HEADs and branches shadowed by a tag

On a detached HEAD (a tag checkout, a rebase in progress, a bisect),
`git symbolic-ref` fails, so Git Branch showed "no git" (or hid itself
with hide-no-git) inside a perfectly good work tree. It now shows the
short commit in parentheses, as git prompts do, e.g. "⎇ (0449a12)", and
the repo link points at that commit.

When a tag has the same name as the current branch, `symbolic-ref
--short` disambiguates the name to "heads/<branch>", so the widget
showed "⎇ heads/release" and linked to .../tree/heads/release. It now
reads the full ref and strips "refs/heads/", which is always the plain
branch name.

* fix(git-worktree): recognize the main worktree in submodules and separate git dirs

Git Worktree decided "main worktree" by the git dir's path: ".git" at
the end, else a ".../worktrees/<name>" pattern. A submodule's git dir is
.git/modules/<name> and a --separate-git-dir repo's is wherever it was
put (e.g. /x/repo.git), so both showed "no git". The path pattern could
also misread a repo kept under a directory named "worktrees".

It now asks git for both the git dir and the common dir in one call. A
linked worktree's git dir is always <common dir>/worktrees/<name>; any
other git dir belongs to the main worktree.

* fix(git-pr): truncate titles by display width and whole characters

PR titles were cut with title.slice(0, 29), counting UTF-16 code units.
An emoji at the cut lost its second half and showed as U+FFFD ("�"), and
a CJK title passed the 30-unit limit while taking 59 columns, since each
character is two columns wide.

Truncation now goes through the same display-cluster and width logic
the renderer uses for max widths, keeping the 30-column limit and the
single "…" ellipsis.

* refactor(git-worktree): swap path separators with replaceAll

A plain replaceAll says what the line does without a global regex.

* fix(git): preserve Node.js 14 worktree path normalization

fix(config): don't migrate a settings.json with a non-numeric version as v1 (#680)

loadSettings treats a file as v1 only when it has no `version` key, but
needsMigration/detectVersion treat any `version` that isn't a number as
v1. A current config with `"version": "4"` or `"version": null` (after a
hand edit, for example) therefore skipped v1 validation and then ran the
v1->v2 migration anyway. That migration rebuilds the config from `lines`
and the v1 fields only, so the result validated and was written back
over the file: Powerline, defaultPaddingSide, minimalistMode, separators
and every other v2+ setting were dropped, widget ids were regenerated,
and the status line announced "ccstatusline updated to v2.0.2".

needsMigration now reports no migration for a version that is present
but not a number. The config then reaches schema validation, which
rejects it, so it takes the existing invalid-file path: defaults in
memory, the load error recorded for the warning badge and TUI banner,
and the file left untouched. Import validation shares needsMigration, so
an import file with a non-numeric version is now rejected instead of
being reduced to its v1 fields.

fix(tui): keep the TUI usable after updating the pinned install from it (#681)

* fix(tui): keep the TUI usable after updating the pinned install from it

Running a global update from Check for Updates records the new version as
the pinned install. On the next render the TUI, still the older version,
saw a pinned install newer than itself and replaced everything with the
"Pinned Install Version Mismatch" screen, whose only option is Exit. Ctrl+S
is a no-op on that screen, so any edits made before the update were lost.

That screen exists so a TUI doesn't write settings for a pinned runtime of
a different version. Here, though, the settings being edited were loaded
before the update, so saving them afterwards is the same as saving a moment
earlier. The TUI now remembers the version its own update installed and
doesn't treat that version as a mismatch for the rest of the session, so
the menus and both save paths stay available. A fresh launch of the older
TUI still gets the mismatch screen.

* test(tui): put chalk's color level back after a whole-App test

The App sets chalk's global color level from the settings it loads, and
the whole-App test helper didn't restore it. Test files that run later in
the same process then rendered at that level instead of their own: a
No Color check could see 256-color codes. The sandbox now restores the
level along with the mocks and the config path.

---------

Co-authored-by: Matthew Breedlove <sirmalloc@gmail.com>

fix(colors): keep the number format when resetting colors (#682)

Edit Colors' (r)eset and (c)lear all removed each widget's numberFormat
along with its colors, bold and dim. Precision used to be cycled from Edit
Colors, but it moved to Edit Lines (the `.` key), and the reset paths kept
clearing it. So resetting a widget's colors silently undid its number
style: a Context Length set to whole numbers went from `Ctx: 19k` back to
`Ctx: 18.6k`, though neither the key help nor the clear-all confirmation
mentions anything but colors.

Reset and clear all now remove only color, background, bold and dim.

fix: time out keychain reads, drop tput's made-up width, expire future-dated usage cache (#683)

* fix(usage): time out keychain reads and back off when no login is found

On macOS the usage credentials come from `security find-generic-password`
and, for the default profile on a miss, `security dump-keychain`. Neither
call had a timeout, so a `security` that blocks (for example on a keychain
unlock prompt) held the whole status line until someone answered it. With
a fake `security` that sleeps 12s, every render took 24s.

Both calls now time out after 5s, like the git and usage API calls.

A lookup that finds no OAuth login was also repeated on every render: an
API-key user with a usage widget has nothing to cache, so each render ran
both `security` calls, the full keychain dump included. The miss is now
remembered for 30s across renders (as it already was within one process),
in ~/.cache/ccstatusline/usage-credentials.lock. The record names the
credential stores it covers (the keychain service and config directory),
so one profile's miss never suppresses another profile's lookup. As with
the usage lock, a deadline further ahead than the backoff itself is
ignored, so a clock set back cannot stretch it.

With the same fake `security`, the first render now takes 10s and the
next ones inside the backoff about 0.2s.

* fix(usage): stop counting a usage cache dated in the future as fresh

The file cache is fresh while `now - mtime` is under 180s. For a file
modified in the future that age is negative, so it always passed. After
one render under a clock running ahead (since corrected, e.g. by NTP or a
VM resume), the cached usage stayed on screen with no refetch until real
time passed that mtime plus three minutes: a clock a day fast froze the
usage widgets for a day.

A file dated ahead of now now counts as fresh only within one cache
lifetime. That still covers a concurrent render writing the file just
after this one read the clock; anything further ahead cannot be right and
is refetched. The usage lock already ignores deadlines too far ahead for
the same reason.

* fix(terminal): report no width instead of tput's default of 80

When the ancestor walk finds no terminal, the probe fell back to
`tput cols`. That runs with piped stdio, so tput cannot see a terminal
either: it prints $COLUMNS if exported, otherwise the terminfo default for
$TERM, which is 80. So with no terminal found and TERM set, the status
line was truncated at 74 columns in full-width mode (40 in full-minus-40)
however wide the real terminal was, and flex separators padded to that
made-up width.

It also meant the probe never returned null in that case, so the
per-session "no TTY" cache was never written and the whole `ps` ancestor
walk re-ran on every render.

The fallback is gone. With no terminal found the probe returns null, which
the renderer already handles: no truncation, and flex separators render as
plain separators. That result is now cached per session as intended.
CCSTATUSLINE_WIDTH still overrides detection for anyone who wants a fixed
width.

fix(input): accept null version, cost, workspace and output_style (#684)

The status payload schema accepted null for context_window, effort, vim,
worktree and rate_limits, but not for version, cost, workspace or
output_style. A payload with any of those four set to null failed
validation as a whole: the CLI printed "Invalid status JSON format" and
exited 1, so no status line rendered, even when no widget on the line
reads that field.

Mark the four fields nullable like the others. Every reader already
goes through optional chaining or a truthiness check (Version, Session
Cost, Session Clock, Output Style, and the git and Claude settings
lookups that fall back from workspace to cwd), so a null field renders
the same as a missing one. Wrong types are still rejected.

fix(current-working-dir): don't count ~ as a segment, and preview every segment count (#685)

With abbreviate-home on, the leading "~" counted as one of the kept
segments. ~/a/b with segments=2 had three parts, so it rendered
"~/.../a/b" though nothing was left out; /a/b with segments=2 renders
"/a/b". The "~" is always kept in front, so it no longer counts.

The preview was a set of fixed strings for one or two segments, so
segments=3 or 4 still previewed two (".../example/project"), and those
strings didn't come from the sample path itself. The preview now runs
the same segment logic over the sample path that a real path goes
through, so it shows what the setting produces.

fix(colors): number keys and hidden separators in Edit Colors (#686)

* fix(colors): stop number keys from leaving Edit Colors

ink-select-input selects the item at a digit key's position, the same as
Enter on it. Edit Colors ignored digits in its own key handler, but its
list still passed them to onSelect, and choosing the Back entry there
called onBack. So on a line with two colorable widgets, pressing 3 left
the screen; with eight, 9 did.

Edit Colors now handles Enter on Back itself and gives the list no
onSelect, so digits do nothing, as the handler already intended. Enter on
a widget still does nothing, and Enter on Back and ESC still go back.

* fix(colors): keep a live highlight when hiding separators

With separators shown in Edit Colors, highlighting one and pressing s
again hid it but left the highlight pointing at it. The list redrew with
the marker on the first item, but every key that acts on the highlighted
item looked up the hidden separator and found nothing: b, d, r and
left/right did nothing, a color entered after a, h or g was dropped, and
the "Current foreground" line went blank.

When hiding separators takes away the highlighted one, the highlight now
moves to the first widget, where the list already draws the marker.
Showing separators, or hiding them while a widget is highlighted, keeps
the highlight where it was.

fix(renderer): keep a preserve-colors widget's Powerline background after its resets (#687)

* fix(renderer): keep a preserve-colors widget's Powerline background after its resets

In Powerline mode a widget that preserves its own colors (a Custom
Command with preserve colors on) gets its segment background once,
before its text. Command output usually ends with \x1b[0m, and Custom
Command appends one after cutting colored output to its max width; that
reset cleared the background too, so the trailing padding, and any text
after a reset mid-output, showed the terminal's background before the
separator arrow:

  \x1b[48;5;26m \x1b[31mhello\x1b[0m \x1b[0m<arrow>

Re-apply the segment background after each SGR sequence in the
preserved text that clears it: a full reset (0 or an empty parameter,
alone or combined like 0;32) or 49. The arguments of extended colors
(38/48/58;5;n and ;2;r;g;b) are skipped, so a 0 or 49 among them isn't
read as a reset. The command's own colors, including its own
backgrounds, are kept, and the full reset after the widget is
unchanged. Widgets without a background, and plain mode (which colors
the padding separately), are untouched.

* fix(renderer): honor backgrounds set after resets in combined SGR codes

Powerline widgets with preserveColors enabled restored the segment
background whenever an SGR sequence contained a reset. For output such as
ESC[0;41m, that restoration overwrote the explicit red background set
later in the same sequence. Indexed and truecolor backgrounds were also
affected.

Process all SGR parameters in order and track the final background
operation. Restore the segment background only when the sequence leaves
it cleared; preserve standard, bright, indexed, and truecolor backgrounds
set after a reset. Continue skipping extended color arguments so channel
values such as 0 and 49 are not interpreted as background operations.

Add parameterized helper and Powerline renderer regression coverage for
reset-before-color and color-before-reset ordering, empty reset parameters,
extended color arguments, and restoration after a subsequent reset.
Confirmed 16 new cases fail before the fix.

Validation:
- bun test: 2811 passed, 0 failed
- Targeted ANSI and Powerline tests: 63 passed, 0 failed
- bun run lint: TypeScript and ESLint passed
- git diff --check passed

---------

Co-authored-by: Matthew Breedlove <sirmalloc@gmail.com>

fix: JJ Bookmarks on merges, speed k-boundary, and time cursor on timers (#688)

* fix(jj-bookmarks): keep bookmarks on different heads apart

JJ Bookmarks lists the bookmarks of heads(::@ & bookmarks()) with the
template "bookmarks". jj log --no-graph prints each commit's template
output back to back with nothing in between, so when @ sits on a merge
of two bookmarked heads the names ran together: "feature-afeature-b".
The template now ends each head's output with a newline, which the
whitespace split already handles; bookmarks on one commit were always
space-separated and still are.

* fix(speed): switch to "k" at the rounding boundary

formatSpeed switched to "k" at exactly 1000 t/s, but values just below
round up when shown: 999.96 t/s rendered as "1000.0 t/s" instead of
"1.0k t/s" (and 999.6 as "1000 t/s" with whole numbers). It now
switches once the value would round to 1000 at the shown precision,
1000 - 0.5 / 10^decimals, the same boundary formatTokens uses for "M".

* fix(usage): show "time cursor" only on widgets that draw one

The time cursor is a usage bar setting (cursor metadata), and the
widget picker keeps metadata when it changes a widget's type. After
changing a usage bar with the cursor on to Block Timer, Block Reset
Timer or Extra Usage Utilization, the editor row said "time cursor",
though those widgets never draw one and have no key to turn it off.

The modifier text now lists the cursor only for widgets that ask for
it, as it already does for compact and date: the usage percent widgets,
which draw it. The metadata itself is left alone, so changing back to a
usage bar keeps the setting.

* refactor(jj-bookmarks): write the template as a raw string

String.raw shows the template exactly as jj reads it, "\n" included,
instead of a doubled backslash.

* test(usage): check only that a carried-over cursor isn't shown

The three time-cursor tests compared the whole modifier text, so they'd
also break on any change to how the bar mode itself is described. They
now check the part they're about: the bar mode still shows, and the
time cursor doesn't.

fix(tui): line editor edge cases (merge on the last widget, move wrap, save guard return) (#689)

* fix(tui): let m clear a merge left on the last widget

The merge toggle was guarded to widgets with another widget after them,
because the last one has nothing to merge into. But a widget can become
last with its merge still set: merge Git Branch into the widget after it,
then delete that widget. Git Branch still shows "(merged→)", m does
nothing, and "(m)erge" is gone from the help line, so the flag can't be
cleared. The next widget added after it then merges into it silently
(`⎇ mainModel: Claude` in the preview).

On the last widget, m now clears a merge that is set, and the help line
offers it there. It still can't set a merge on the last widget, and the
merged, merged-without-padding and off cycle is unchanged elsewhere.

* fix(tui): keep the other items in order when a move wraps

Move mode wraps past either end of the list, but it did so by swapping the
moved item with the one at the other end. Moving Model up from the top of
Model, Context Length, Git Branch, Git Changes gave Git Changes, Context
Length, Git Branch, Model: Model reached the bottom, but Git Changes jumped
from the bottom to the top. The line selector's move mode did the same
with whole lines.

Both move modes now take the item out and put it back in at the target, so
wrapping past either end moves only that item and the rest keep their
order. A move to a neighbour is still a swap.

* fix(tui): return to the current screen from the invalid-settings save guard

When settings.json is invalid, Ctrl+S first asks before overwriting it. The
question can come up on any screen, but both answers went to the main menu:
with Edit Line 1 open, Ctrl+S then ESC (or Yes) left the line editor, and
you had to navigate back in to carry on.

The guard now returns to the screen Ctrl+S was pressed on, for both
answers. Save & Exit, the other route into the guard, starts from the main
menu and still returns there. The screen comes back as it does when you
navigate to it: a sub-editor that was open on it, such as the label editor,
and its unsaved text aren't restored.

* test(tui): put chalk's color level back after a whole-App test

The App sets chalk's global color level from the settings it loads, and
the whole-App test helper didn't restore it. Test files that run later in
the same process then rendered at that level instead of their own: a
No Color check could see 256-color codes. The sandbox now restores the
level along with the mocks and the config path.

Nothing reads them: verify_build only runs codesign on the .app inside
Products/Applications. They came along with the xcarchives in #12394
and are 2.4 MB of Mach-O that OpenSSF Scorecard flags as binary
artifacts.

* [fastlane_core] spec fixtures: build the verify_build apps at spec time instead of committing them

The three .app fixtures lose their Mach-O executable and the
_CodeSignature it sealed. verify_build_spec copies the bundles to a
scratch directory, compiles a one-line main into each and ad-hoc
signs it before running codesign on them. A named identity would
keep the Authority expectation, but codesign only finds one through
a keychain in the user's search list, which the parallel workers
share. The Authority and provisioning type parsing moves to a spec
with stubbed codesign output, which also covers the iPhone
Distribution and Apple Development cases the fixtures never did.

Removes 3 of the 8 binaries OpenSSF Scorecard flags in the repo.

commits.message:
appender: document that the rolling appender constructors panic (#3632)

## Motivation

`RollingFileAppender::new` and the `minutely`, `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly` and `never` helpers panic when the appender can't be initialized, for example when the log directory or file can't be created. Their docs didn't say so. Only the docs for `RollingFileAppender::builder` mention it.

## Solution

This adds a `# Panics` section to each of the six, pointing to `RollingFileAppender::builder` and `Builder::build` for callers who need to handle the error.

No behaviour change. Making these constructors return a `Result` would be a breaking change, which #1138 proposes.

Refs #3631

tracing: simplify check for interest before creating events/spans/logging/etc in macros (#3626)

This just slightly simplifies some macro-generated code.

## Motivation

This macro-generated code was just a teensie bit unnecessarily complex. So I've simplified it here (mainly with the intention of helping compile times on `tracing`-dependent crates)

## Solution

As far as I can tell, this change doesn't alter semantics in any way. I'm guessing that this code was originally written in this somewhat-complex way to avoid registering interest (which is what happens when `__CALLSITE.interest()` is called), but this PR's code also avoids registering interest in the same way, so I'm not quite certain why the code looked that way before this PR.
chore: bump tracing-attributes to syn 3.0 (#3594)

attributes: fix duplicate check for `parent` and `follows_from` (#3630)

## Motivation

In `tracing-attributes/src/attr.rs`, the `parent` and `follows_from` branches of the `#[instrument]` argument parser look for a duplicate argument by checking `args.target`, not their own field (#3621). This has two effects:

- A repeated `parent` or `follows_from` is accepted, and the last value wins.
- `target` followed by `parent` or `follows_from` is rejected. `#[instrument(target = "my_target", parent = None)]` fails with ``expected only a single `parent` argument``.

The second effect is not in the issue. I found it while writing the tests.

## Solution

Check `args.parent` and `args.follows_from` in their own branches.

Tests:

- `tests/ui/fail/duplicate_args.rs` checks that a repeated `parent` and a repeated `follows_from` are rejected.
- `tests/ui/pass/target_with_parent.rs` checks that `target` followed by `parent` or `follows_from` compiles.

Both fail without the change.

Fixes: #3621

Fix/dsi dma2d psram buffers (#24949)

* Fix silently-dropped LVGL flush chunks on ESP32-P4 DSI panels

esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap()'s DMA2D path takes an internal draw
semaphore with a 0 timeout and returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE (without
drawing anything) if the previous async transfer hasn't completed yet.
DSIPanel::pushColors() ignored that return value, and lv_flush_callback()
always calls lv_disp_flush_ready() regardless, so LVGL believed the
flush succeeded even when the chunk was silently dropped - leaving
stale framebuffer content on screen for that region.

Retry instead of dropping the chunk. The transfer typically completes
in well under 1ms, so poll in short bursts rather than 1ms FreeRTOS
ticks; a bounded retry count still catches a genuinely stuck transfer
and logs it instead of looping forever.

* Allow LVGL DSI draw buffers to use PSRAM on ESP32-P4

lv_pixel_buf/lv_pixel_buf2 previously preferred MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL,
costing ~120KB of scarce internal SRAM on boards where PSRAM is
otherwise nearly idle (e.g. a 1024x600 DSI panel at 60 flushlines).
Prefer MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM instead, falling back to internal RAM if
PSRAM is unavailable - safe now that the previous commit fixes the
DMA2D transfer race that PSRAM's slower read speed was exposing.

Also switch the flush-timing debug log from millis() to micros() and
drop its DMA-path exclusion: at a ~60KB/transfer chunk size the whole
operation completes in a few hundred microseconds, so millisecond
resolution just read back 0 or 1 and the DMA path - the one we
actually needed data from - was never logged at all.

* Remove defaulting to PSRAM for now

commits.message:
Validate large blob parameters before mutating write state (#797)

In LargeBlobState::process_command, an offset == 0 write mutated
self.expected_length before checking max_large_blob_array_size() and
TRUNCATED_HASH_LEN, and updated self.expected_next_offset = 0 before
verifying pin_uv_auth_param and checking that the chunk fits within
expected_length.

If an offset == 0 request failed validation or authentication while a
multi-fragment write was in progress, self.expected_length and/or
self.expected_next_offset were overwritten while self.buffer retained
the previous write's bytes. In particular, an offset == 0 request with
length > max_large_blob_array_size() after an initial valid chunk left
self.expected_length set to the oversized length and allowed subsequent
chunks at offset > 0 to bypass max_large_blob_array_size().

Validate length, authentication, and chunk bounds before mutating
LargeBlobState on offset == 0, and clear the state when the final chunk
is processed regardless of whether the hash check succeeds.

Reject minimum PIN lengths that no PIN could satisfy (#793)

* Reject minimum PIN lengths that no PIN could satisfy

A PIN is at most 63 bytes long, since it is padded with at least one
zero byte to 64 bytes. Accepting a larger minimum PIN length would make
it impossible to ever set or change the PIN again, permanently locking
out PIN-based user verification (in particular after a forced PIN
change). Reject such values with CTAP2_ERR_PIN_POLICY_VIOLATION.

* Reuse PIN_PADDED_LENGTH instead of a hardcoded PIN length limit

Follow-up to review feedback: derive MAX_PIN_LENGTH from
PIN_PADDED_LENGTH in client_pin.rs, and use the constant in the test
so that it does not fail if the value were to change.

---------

Co-authored-by: 17krishna8 <17krishna8@users.noreply.github.com>

Reject user handles that are empty or longer than 64 bytes (#791)

* Reject user handles that are empty or longer than 64 bytes

WebAuthn requires the user handle to be between 1 and 64 bytes, and
rejects anything else before the request reaches the authenticator.
Nothing enforces that limit for software that talks CTAP directly over
USB HID, so a MakeCredential request could ask us to store a discoverable
credential with a much larger user handle, which then fails at storage
time with a confusing KEY_STORE_FULL error, or wastes store space first.

Check the length when parsing the parameters, so the request is rejected
with CTAP1_ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER before anything is allocated.

* Move MAX_USER_HANDLE_LENGTH below the imports

Follow-up to review feedback.

---------

Co-authored-by: 17krishna8 <17krishna8@users.noreply.github.com>

Propagate USB read errors during user presence checks (#796)

UserPresence::wait_with_timeout unwrapped the result of
wasefire::usb::ctap::read(), panicking the applet if the USB read
failed, whereas HidConnection::recv maps the error to a CTAP status code
with convert_error.

Propagate the error with map_err(convert_error) so a USB failure returns
a CTAP status code instead of panicking.

Remove enrolled fingerprints before clearing persistent storage on reset (#794)

In CtapState::process_reset, reset(env) was called before iterating
over env.persist().template_infos() to remove enrolled templates from
the fingerprint sensor. Because reset(env) invokes env.persist().reset(),
which deletes all non-persistent keys including FRIENDLY_NAMES where
template_infos are stored, template_infos() was always empty and
env.fingerprint().remove_enrollment() was never called during a CTAP
reset.

Move the fingerprint template removal loop into reset(env) before
env.persist().reset(), and clear fingerprint_enrollment_status in
CtapState::process_reset.

Use constant-time comparison for Hmac256 verification (#795)

WasefireEnv's Hmac256::verify and Hmac256::verify_truncated_left
compared MACs with standard slice/array equality (==), which is not
constant-time and violates the Hmac256 trait contract for verifying
PIN/UV authentication tokens and credential IDs.

Provide default implementations for verify and verify_truncated_left on
the Hmac256 trait using subtle::ConstantTimeEq, and use them in
WasefireEnv.

Go codegen for ClickHouse, DuckDB, Spanner and SQL Server under database/sql (#4621)

* plugin: carry the analysis core's type expression on Column

The core analyzer types every column and parameter as an expression: a
name, whether a value may be null, and nested arguments, so
decimal(10, 2), array(array(integer)) and struct(x: integer) survive
intact. The plugin request flattened that to a single type name plus
not_null, is_array, array_dims, length and unsigned, which is not enough
for a type mapper to tell nvarchar(max) from nvarchar(50) or to see the
element of an array or the fields of a struct.

Add a recursive TypeExpr message to the plugin proto and a type_expr
field on Column, populated from the core's tree in the shim. It is only
set when the analysis core typed the column; the legacy path leaves it
unset and the flat fields stay as they were, so existing plugins keep
working. When a database analyzer overrides a column's flat type in
combineAnalysis, the tree no longer describes the column and is dropped.

A DuckDB codegen_json case pins the shape with decimal arguments, nested
arrays, a labeled struct, a map and a sized array. The existing JSON
request goldens gain the new field, unset, on every column.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015rfiHyC4iRLyRWc3UmYEtT

* codegen/golang: map ClickHouse, DuckDB, Spanner and SQL Server types

The Go generator ran for the four engines the analysis core handles but
knew none of their types, so every field came out as any. Add a mapper
per engine that reads the column's type expression rather than the flat
name, which is what lets it see the element of an array, the key and
value of a map, the fields of a struct, and the type LowCardinality or
SimpleAggregateFunction wraps. Each maps to the Go types the engine's
database/sql driver hands back: shopspring decimals, orb geometries and
pointer-typed nullable elements for clickhouse-go; duckdb.Composite,
duckdb.Decimal, duckdb.Interval and duckdb.Map for duckdb-go, with a
list parameter typed as the slice itself since a Composite is not
accepted as an argument; the spanner package's Null types for
go-sql-spanner, whose arrays decode into them; and
mssql.UniqueIdentifier for go-mssqldb.

The tree-reading mappers render the whole type, arrays included, so
goType leaves the dimensions to them. Model columns come from the
catalog, which the core path flattened, so catalog.Column now carries the
expression too and the shim forwards it. The queries for these engines
pass slices straight to the driver, so pq.Array wrapping is limited to
PostgreSQL under database/sql, where lib/pq needs it. Import detection
follows a package qualifier into map keys and values and through any
number of slice and pointer prefixes.

A core_types case per engine generates the analyze_types schema and
queries with database/sql and pins the output; the end-to-end module
gains the drivers so the generated code compiles.

- docs: say which of the new engines' types still come out as any, and
  how DuckDB's JSON columns are read.

* duckdb: make JSON a type of its own

DuckDB's catalog lists JSON as a spelling of VARCHAR, so the seed made it
an alias and a JSON column came out as string. But DuckDB keeps JSON
apart: typeof() reports it as JSON, and duckdb-go decodes a JSON value

commits.message:
Stamp the requested client on legacy translation requests

Summary:
A legacy (`--api ax`) read now carries `AccessibilityRequestOptions.clientType` on every translator request it makes, from resolving the element (a frontmost resolution or a point hit-test) through serializing it. A read that names no client resolves to `noClient`, which is what every request already carried, so default reads are unchanged.

- `AXTranslationRequest` holds the resolved client, and a retried request keeps it.
- The dispatcher's bridge callback stamps it on each request before forwarding it to the simulator.
- `resolveElement(for:clientType:)` takes the client explicitly, because a point read's hit-test happens before any options reach serialization.
- `describe` and `hitTest` pass `options.resolvedClientType`. Actions, frames and waits take no request options, so they use the client a default read resolves to.

The dispatcher now always stamps the client rather than forwarding the translator's own value. A translator stamps a non-zero value only while its process is servicing an incoming macOS accessibility request, which an idb process never does. The pinned expectation from the previous commit changes from `[0, 5]` to `[0, 0]` accordingly.

Differential Revision: D124356756

fbshipit-source-id: a72f04c0dc2fd717c786ee36ab9f43b1aa99af9b

Pin the requests AXTranslationDispatcher forwards

Summary:
No behaviour change. Covers the legacy accessibility backend's bridge callback, which until now no test reached: the translator double sends no requests through the dispatcher.

The translator double can now send real `AXPTranslatorRequest`s through its bridge-token delegate during a frontmost resolution, as the macOS translator does when it reads an application's attributes. A new test pins that the dispatcher forwards each one to the simulator with the `clientType` the translator stamped, here 0 and 5.

The test bundle can't link against the private framework's classes. So the requests are built, sent through the callback, and read back through the Objective-C runtime.

Differential Revision: D124356170

fbshipit-source-id: 8bc00175da7e644422d6da6bd33fa08f1bbf194d

Build the guest bridge, ReplHost and the Repl shim for iOS 17.0 too

Summary:
The open-source build of the guest bridge failed once its protocol module moved to the iOS 17.0 floor:

```
error: compiling for iOS 15.0, but module 'FBSimulatorBridgeProtocol' has a minimum deployment target of iOS 17.0
import FBSimulatorBridgeProtocol
       ^ (in target 'SimulatorFrameworkBridge-iOS' from project 'SimulatorFrameworkBridge')
```

Raising the floor set each simulator target's `deploymentTarget`, but the iOS and tvOS bridge targets, ReplHost and the iOS Repl shim also set `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` or `TVOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` to 15.0 explicitly, which overrides it. Those settings now say 17.0, as does the iOS Shimulator xcconfig, whose value the target's own setting already overrode. The macOS targets keep their deployment targets.

Differential Revision: D124361358

fbshipit-source-id: cd4e796f4da18fb5d2ec65758cf5492f34772259

Add a requesting client to AccessibilityRequestOptions

Summary:
`AccessibilityRequestOptions` gains `clientType: AXClientType?`, the assistive client a read's translator requests should claim to come from, and `resolvedClientType`, the one place a nil client resolves.

Nil resolves to `noClient`, which is what every translator path sends today. No backend reads the option yet, so behaviour is unchanged. `AXClientType` is the bridge protocol's `BridgeAXClientType`, re-exported the same way as `AXTraversal`.

The options' description names the client only when one is set, so default logs are unchanged too.

Differential Revision: D124355829

fbshipit-source-id: 1c567eda317c35e456ada7f568967a8f8cbca6eb

Add accessibility client types

Summary:
Adds `BridgeAXClientType` and `BridgeAXRequestingClient` to the protocol shared by the host and the in-simulator bridge. Nothing reads them yet, so behaviour is unchanged.

- `BridgeAXClientType` is the value of `-[AXPTranslatorRequest clientType]`: which assistive client a translator request says it comes from. Its raw values are the integers the translator carries (0 `noClient` to 11 `accessibilityInspector`). Each case names the macOS client that produces it.
- `BridgeAXRequestingClient` is the iOS-side value an application's accessibility runtime answers for. Its raw values are the runtime's integers.
- `requestingClient` records how the simulator's translator maps one onto the other.
- `deservesAutomation` records which clients an application answers with its automation tree, rather than the flattened tree VoiceOver reads.

The mapping is the same on every iOS runtime from 26.4 to 27.0.

Differential Revision: D124355882

fbshipit-source-id: 65bd896d147d8deaaa24a8c7075cf60985dfb553

Raise the iOS deployment floor to 17.0

Summary:
The open-source build of `libShimulator-iOS.dylib` failed to link, which failed the companion build and every test job that builds the simulator shims:

```
Undefined symbols for architecture arm64:
  "__swift_FORCE_LOAD_$_swiftCompatibility56", referenced from:
      __swift_FORCE_LOAD_$_swiftCompatibility56_$_ShimulatorAudioInjectionBootstrap in libShimulatorAudioInjectionBootstrap.a[2](AudioInjectionBootstrap.o)
      ...
ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture arm64
```

The shim is Objective-C but links Swift archives, and Swift built for anything older than iOS 15.4 references a back-deployment library that Xcode only links into targets with Swift sources of their own. Rather than name that library, and the next one, in the shim's linker flags, idb's simulator binaries now build for iOS and tvOS 17.0. Their Swift then references no back-deployment library at all, the 5.6 compatibility library included, and neither does anything that needs the Swift 5.9 runtime.

That covers the shims, the guest bridge, ReplHost and the iOS test fixture, in both the Xcode projects and the Buck build. Simulator runtimes older than iOS 17 can no longer load them. The host binaries keep their macOS 15.0 floor.

Reviewed By: bryanyantx

Differential Revision: D124342745

fbshipit-source-id: 526daaaedef3a3b7d2d7220bd25c4bb2fae22eb5

Pass HID event logging to Simulator

Summary:
No behavioral change. A `Simulator` now carries its HID event logging level, set when it is constructed, instead of `SimulatorHID` reading it back through `simulator.set?.configuration`. Simulators vended by a `SimulatorSet` take the set configuration's level as before; a `Simulator` built without a set defaults to `.redacted`, which is what the old `nil`-set fallback produced.

This removes one of the two places a `Simulator` depends on the set it came from.

Differential Revision: D124341216

fbshipit-source-id: d04fcfa29d99d3b43d840f3801b4d1a39b7a267a

Pin SimulatorSet identity

Summary:
No behavioral change. Covers how `SimulatorSet` hands out `Simulator` instances:

- Repeated `simulator(withUDID:)` lookups return the same instance, and it is the same instance `allSimulators` returns.
- Unavailable devices are not found by lookup or enumeration.
- A device removed from the underlying device set is no longer found.
- A `Simulator` the caller drops is kept alive by the set.
- Looking up a single UDID constructs a wrapper for every device in the set.

The CoreSimulator doubles gain a full device list with `devicesByUDID`, per-device availability, and a count of `deviceType` reads. Inferring a `Simulator`'s configuration reads `deviceType` exactly once, so the count is the number of wrappers built around a device.

The set's state-change path to its `delegate` is not covered: it only accepts notifications whose `device` is a real `SimDevice`, which a double cannot be.

Differential Revision: D124341214

fbshipit-source-id: 6274f73a43b13158f040af2d8ca097f3004de62c

Split XCTestReporter into a Swift protocol and a narrow Objective-C sink

Summary:
No behavioural change. `XCTestReporter` was an `objc` protocol refining `NSObjectProtocol`, with three `optional` members. Every reporter therefore had to subclass `NSObject`, and callers either probed with `responds(to:)` or used optional chaining. The only Objective-C caller, `FBTestReporterAdapter`, uses nine of its members.

- `XCTestReporter` is now a Swift protocol, `AnyObject`. The three formerly optional members have empty default implementations, which is what an absent optional amounted to.
- `TestManagerReportSink` is a new `objc` protocol with just the nine members the Objective-C DTX layer calls, keeping their selectors. `FBTestReporterAdapter` and `FBTestManagerAPIMediatorIDEInterface` take it. `TestManagerAPIMediator` wraps its reporter in an internal `XCTestReporterSink` forwarder.
- `FBTestReporterAdapter`'s `respondsToSelector:` checks, `LogicReporterAdapter`'s `responds(to:)` check on a required member, and the `testPlanDidFail?` optional chaining are gone.
- `IDBXCTestReporter` and the test reporters no longer subclass `NSObject`.

Differential Revision: D124306253

fbshipit-source-id: ce5b2983768d2f3f405d5a572aaff32a5cf80a61

Give the Objective-C DTX layer its own one-method log sink

Summary: No behavioural change. `FBTestBundleDTXConnection` and `FBTestManagerAPIMediatorIDEInterface` took an `id<ControlCoreLogger>` but only ever call `log:` on it, and they were the only reason `ControlCoreLogger` had to be `objc`. They now take an `id<TestManagerLogSink>`, an `objc` protocol with just `log(_:)`. The Swift side wraps its `ControlCoreLogger` in an internal `ControlCoreLoggerSink` at the two construction sites. This prepares for making `ControlCoreLogger` a plain Swift protocol in the next diff.

Differential Revision: D124302534

fbshipit-source-id: 7215b6b79e8ac0e8824e1e7a3dac856ba0ec1114

Build command objects with initializers instead of commands(with:) factories

Summary:
No behavioural change. Every simulator and device command type exposed a `public static func commands(with:)`, a port of Objective-C's `+commandsWithTarget:`. Most of them only forwarded to an internal initializer. The factories are removed and callers use initializers:

- A factory that only forwarded leaves its initializer public. Structs that relied on the implicit memberwise initializer get an explicit public one.
- A factory that computed dependencies becomes a public initializer that does the same and delegates. That covers the debugserver path, the shared crash-log notifier and store, the device crash store, and the delta-update directory.
- Factories that passed a fixed default, the device's AFC calls and `xcodebuild` working directory, become default arguments.
- `SimulatorHIDCommands` gets a public `init(simulator:)` that delegates to its internal initializer, which takes an internal transport type.

The `Simulator` and `Device` command properties, and the extension modules', construct the same objects as before.

Differential Revision: D124301898

fbshipit-source-id: 2924dd25818c702403665dcb03f28562c78cd339

Find the Swift back-deployment libraries in the default toolchain when linking libShimulator

Summary:
`libShimulator-iOS` has no Swift sources of its own but links the Swift audio-injection archives, so `Shims/Shimulator/project.yml` adds the toolchain's Swift library directory to its search path for the back-deployment libraries those archives auto-link (`swiftCompatibility56`, `swiftCompatibilityPacks`).

It spelled that directory `$(TOOLCHAIN_DIR)`, which is not always the default toolchain: when another toolchain component is installed, as the Metal toolchain is on GitHub's macOS 26 runners, `TOOLCHAIN_DIR` resolves to it. The link then cannot find `libswiftCompatibility56.a` and fails with an undefined `__swift_FORCE_LOAD_$_swiftCompatibility56`, which breaks every CI job that builds the shims.

Name `XcodeDefault.xctoolchain` under `$(DEVELOPER_DIR)` instead. Xcode refuses `DT_TOOLCHAIN_DIR` in `LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS`, so it cannot be used here.

fbshipit-source-id: 8379e7921303d264e7b83936074da8c67d773a54

Remove the unused frame pusher factory

Summary: No behavioural change. Removes `SimulatorVideoStream.framePusherFactory`, a test seam for refusing frame pushers that nothing uses. A stream still makes every frame pusher through `newFramePusher(consumer:)`.

Differential Revision: D124337601

fbshipit-source-id: b860d50b3c985e83ad31384553b1416c3e49bc8c

Build the frameworks in Release

Summary:
`build.sh build frameworks`, which CI's frameworks job runs, now builds `FBControlCore`, `FBXCTestCore`, `FBSimulatorControl` and `FBDeviceControl` in Release rather than Debug.

The test schemes already build every framework in Debug, so the frameworks job compiled nothing they did not. In Release it builds what ships instead, and the job's size report shows Release sizes rather than Debug ones, which are unoptimised and overstate how big a framework is. `build_target` still defaults to Debug for anything else that calls it.

Differential Revision: D124332407

fbshipit-source-id: ddbe313bf63d80f6c0d43980d03bd329f5490659

Say which build configuration every binary size comes from

Summary:
The size report now names the configuration each binary was built in, so a Debug size is never read as the size of what ships.

Each row gains a Build column, taken from the Xcode products directory the binary sits in (`Debug`, `Release`, or either with an SDK appended), or from `--configuration` when its path names none, as an assembled distribution's does not; without either it reads `unknown`. Each per-module table names it too. A report with any Debug binary opens with a warning that Debug builds are unoptimised and keep code a Release build strips, so their sizes overstate the shipped size. CI's distribution report passes `--configuration Release`, which is what `build.sh build all` builds.

Differential Revision: D124332406

fbshipit-source-id: 7619caadec2183537b8ca5fd02b6616e937a6e6c

Report the frameworks job's binaries, whatever configuration it builds

Summary:
The frameworks job's size report found nothing:

```
## Binary sizes: Frameworks

No binaries found.
```

It searched `Build/Products/Release`, but `build.sh build frameworks` builds the Debug configuration, so the job's products are in `Build/Products/Debug`; only the companion's Release build fills `Build/Products/Release`. The report now searches all of `Build/Products`, and each row's path names the configuration it came from.

Differential Revision: D124332405

fbshipit-source-id: 2e75627d07b166bf25c58a67ec5a72b22f9bfd1b

Add the microphone-injection shim

Summary:
Link microphone injection into `libShimulator-iOS.dylib` through seven CoreAudio HAL interposes, so an unmodified simulator app can capture an injected WAV through its normal recording API. The Swift HAL implementation supplies input buffers and synthetic input-device properties; C provides the private declarations, interpose records and load-time flag read.

The shim caches `IDB_AUDIO_INJECTION` at load. Unless it is `1`, replacements forward the original arguments and result without starting injection work or changing the host microphone. App arming and the client command are supplied by the other audio-stack layers.

Reviewed By: lawrencelomax

Differential Revision: D119702585

fbshipit-source-id: 6d7e27d5274f28743f9761d86d7e92b87ef2b407

Make a stream's frame pushers through one method

Summary: No behavioural change. A video stream makes every frame pusher, for a mount or a spare, through one method, and tests can stand in a factory there to refuse or replace pushers. This lets a test drive a mount that fails because its pusher cannot be made, as when the encoder for a new size is refused.

Differential Revision: D124328076

fbshipit-source-id: 2406c175eecde3a7b215dbac396f6defd6ab5521

Remove the TargetCommand protocol

Summary:
No behavioural change. `TargetCommand`, a port of the Objective-C `FBiOSTargetCommand`, required a `static func commands(with: any Target) -> Self`. Nothing used it generically, yet `Target` inherited it, so every target type had to implement a factory returning itself:

- `Simulator`'s and `Device`'s trapped if handed another kind of target.
- `MacDevice`'s asserted and returned `NSNull` bit-cast to itself.

The protocol and those three factories are deleted, along with the one in a test double. The two command classes that adopted it directly, `TargetXCTraceRecordCommands` and `DeviceDiagnosticInformationCommands`, are built with their initializers instead.

Differential Revision: D124301161

fbshipit-source-id: 36fc7e9dd2738dc89b4eeb91d1b7975b2c0b5577

Declare type members of final classes and enums static

Summary: No behavioural change. 82 type methods and properties across 44 files were declared `class func`/`class var`, as their Objective-C ancestors were, on `final` classes and enums where nothing can override them. They are now `static`. Calls are written the same way. Members that override a superclass's class method are left as they are, and the Objective-C-visible ones keep `objc` and remain class methods to Objective-C.

Differential Revision: D124300604

fbshipit-source-id: 499ab79d243212462cc5f1f5f2a256ac8d297884

Expose to Objective-C only what the test-manager layer uses

Summary:
No behavioural change. The `FBXCTestCore` types the Objective-C test-manager layer works with exposed every member to it, although that layer uses only a few. It builds summaries with `fromTestSuite:…`, reads statuses with `statusForStatusString:`, builds exceptions with `initWithMessage:file:line:`, reads a context's session identifier and test configuration, and builds errors through `XCTestBootstrapErrors`. Those keep `objc`. The rest drop it:

- `TestManagerResultSummary`'s properties, initializer and `statusString(for:)`.
- `TestExceptionInfo`'s properties and `init(message:)`.
- `TestManagerContext`'s timeout and environment.
- `XCTestBootstrapErrorCode`.

`TestManagerContext` also stops conforming to `NSCopying`: nothing copies it, and its `copy(with:)` returned itself.

Differential Revision: D124300131

fbshipit-source-id: ab5676e5aa19798a506078f7ebe2b05de974762f

Load additional libraries alongside the REPL shim

Summary:
Every way of starting a REPL host on a Simulator now takes `additionalLibraries`: dylibs loaded into the host alongside the `libRepl` shim, before any code is injected, so injected code resolves their symbols at load. An app gets them after the shim in `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, a logic test in its injected libraries, and the guest bridge loads them globally after the shim.

The guest bridge's `repl start <socket> <libRepl>` accepts further library paths and loads each with `RTLD_GLOBAL` before serving, failing the start if one cannot load. It previously ignored arguments past the shim's path.

This is what lets the idb command API become a library of its own that only `idb-repl` injects, rather than being linked into the shim. Callers that pass no additional libraries are unaffected.

Differential Revision: D124310769

fbshipit-source-id: 6f037929c1c26b1ce64ce5a4d01d62681ea5db9c

Move the REPL control-socket client into FBSimulatorCodeInjection

Summary:
The client for the socket the injected REPL shim serves -- reading its greeting, having it `dlopen` a compiled dylib and call its entry point, and answering the host commands the injected code sends back -- is now public in `FBSimulatorCodeInjection` as `ReplControlClient`, beside the code that launches the host. Together they are the whole of injecting code into a Simulator process, with no gRPC: a tool can launch a host with `simulator.repl`, connect to the `LaunchedRepl`'s socket and execute dylibs it compiled itself.

The companion's `repl` method is now an adapter over it: it streams the driver's dylibs to `ReplControlClient` and its results back, and maps the client's `ReplControlError` to the same gRPC status codes and messages as before. No behavior changes.

Differential Revision: D124293141

fbshipit-source-id: 9f0d01685ccad88cbf96d74ac53b1684e6775323

Report the size of every binary CI builds

Summary:
The frameworks and distribution jobs in CI now write a size report to their log and to the run's summary, so a size change shows up on the commit that made it rather than being found later by comparing releases.

The report is a Markdown table of every Mach-O product under the built directory: its file size, and its code and data, which leaves out the debug information a static library carries. Each linked image (an executable, dylib or bundle) also gets a table of the bytes attributed to each Swift module, from the module its symbols' mangled names start with. That is how a library linked statically into a tool is measured: FBSimulatorControl has no file of its own in the distribution, but its share of `idb_companion` is listed by name. Every module this project owns is always listed; anything else below 1% of the image is folded into one row.

`CI/binary_sizes.py` is stdlib-only, so it runs on the runner's own `python3`. It reads the arm64 slice of a universal binary, and skips `.dSYM`, `.xctest` and `.swiftmodule` directories and symlinks, so a framework's binary is counted once.

Differential Revision: D124319637

fbshipit-source-id: cc2873eac8cce8d4912eba2d6ae4b1278e703f98

Pin frames and recorder screenshots keeping the panel's orientation

Summary: No behavioural change. Covers a stream whose mounted display reports a rotated interface: its frames and its stdin screenshots keep the panel's own orientation, so a landscape interface is recorded and screenshotted sideways. The assertions are marked as pinning that behaviour, which the following commit changes; an upright interface is covered beside it and does not change.

Differential Revision: D124321795

fbshipit-source-id: cd4592c8a5090ed3848df4bb5ee98dbd15ba881c

Set frame pushers up from a description of their source

Summary: No behavioural change. A frame pusher is set up from a `VideoFrameSource`, the width, height and pixel format of the frames it will be given, rather than from a pixel buffer, which was only ever read for those three. `VideoFrameSource` is the key spare pushers are kept under, so a pusher can be set up for frames that no buffer holds yet, such as a source rotated before it is composited.

Differential Revision: D124321794

fbshipit-source-id: 79b10943f30a8e8cd3593173af2114e526e92c43

Descend axbridge hit-tests to the element at the point

Summary:
An axbridge `hittest` now answers with the element a tree read shows under the point. Before, it returned whatever Apple's accessibility hit-test returned, which is the element VoiceOver would focus. That can be a container that is a single accessibility element over its own controls: a post header that is one element over its Follow and options buttons answered as the header at every point inside it, while a tree read of the same screen listed the buttons as its children.

The guest now descends from the element the hit-test returns, through the last-drawn child whose frame contains the point, until it reaches a control or an element with no child under the point. A hit on a button names the button rather than the text inside it, and cells are still entered so a control inside a cell is found. The hit-test has already answered by the time the descent runs, so a read that fails or raises never costs it that answer: a child that cannot be read is skipped, as a tree read drops it, and an element whose own read fails ends the descent there.

Controls are typed the way XCUITest types an iOS element. XCUITest's `+[XCElementSnapshot elementTypeForAccessibilityElement:usingAXAttributes_iOS:useLegacyElementType:]` converts the element's automation type (`XC_kAXXCAttributeAutomationType`) with `XCTElementTypeFromAXAutomationType`, an exported function in XCTAutomationSupport, and the guest now calls the same function. The conversion matters because the two numberings differ. In the Xcode 27.1 simulator's copy, the function is a bounds check and a lookup in an 89-entry table: automation types 0-8 are reordered (Other, Application, Window, Sheet, Drawer, Group, Alert, Dialog, then 83), 9-82 are unchanged, 83 is Other, and 84-88 are all Button. The element types the descent stops at are named in `FBXCUIElementType`, whose values are copied from `XCUIAutomation.framework/Headers/XCUIElementTypes.h`, where every case is explicit. A runtime without the conversion answers `Any`, so the descent simply never stops early.

Only the `hittest` verb descends. Center-point frontmost resolution only needs the owning process, which every descendant shares, and point writes and the reachability explanation keep their current behaviour.

Differential Revision: D124314351

fbshipit-source-id: 6593ad543ef7962464266725b07fedd5e36186cb

Pin hit-tests answering with a control's container

Summary:
No behavioural change. Covers what an axbridge `hittest` answers when Apple's accessibility hit-test returns a container that is a single accessibility element over its own controls, such as a post header over its Follow button.

The tests pin the current answer: a point on the button returns the container, including when another child of the container raises when read. The assertions that pin this are marked as a bug and are flipped by the change that descends to the control under the point. A point under no child returning the container, and a container that cannot be read failing the request, are pinned as correct behaviour.

`FBXCUIElementType` is declared here, restating the cases of XCTest's public `XCUIElementType` that the bridge names, so the tests can mark an element as a button. Nothing reads it yet.

Differential Revision: D124319563

fbshipit-source-id: 58101541e9be1fd38029fa136da1100144169205

Give activity records Swift-shaped properties and make attachments a struct

Summary:
No behavioural change. Changes:

- `FBActivityRecord` stays an `objc` class, because `FBTestReporterAdapter.m` builds one with `from(_:)` and hands it to reporters. Objective-C never reads its properties, so they drop `objc`.
- `subactivities` becomes `[FBActivityRecord]` instead of an `NSMutableArray` that the companion's reporter cast back with `compactMap`.
- `FBAttachment` is never seen by Objective-C, so it becomes a plain struct.
- Both still read XCTest's private records through KVC, since those headers cannot be imported from Swift.

Differential Revision: D124299188

fbshipit-source-id: 0c76ee0f6867c7e58ffe017072ee2f40bcda0916

Stop subclassing NSObject where the protocol only needs a class

Summary: No behavioural change. `MacDevice`, `TargetStateChangeNotifier`, `IDBLogger`'s log operation, `DeviceEraseStrategy`'s operation and `DeviceManager` subclassed `NSObject` as their Objective-C ancestors did. The protocols they conform to (`Target`, `TargetSetDelegate`, `LogOperation`, `TargetSet`) only require a class, and nothing reaches these types through the Objective-C runtime. `MacDevice` talks to testmanagerd over XPC as a client and is never the exported object. They become plain Swift classes. `DeviceManager` keeps its `description` through `CustomStringConvertible`.

Differential Revision: D124298136

fbshipit-source-id: e44af1c0f62aa8a448763f4a96e49dfed9b7b857

Keep the testmanagerd lookup's last error as an Error

Summary: No behavioural change. Waiting for the simulator's testmanagerd socket path stored each failed lookup's error as an `NSError`, only to hand it to `SimulatorXCTestError.environmentVariableUnavailable`, which already takes an `Error?`. It now keeps the `Error`.

Differential Revision: D124297500

fbshipit-source-id: c6f92f59bcda8a503d6950fd8fade77cd9eb4e6d

Make XcodeConfiguration a Swift enum

Differential Revision: D124146340

fbshipit-source-id: 08355a0da110d6a5a1e563db2c13c24686b6a77d

Play injected audio into CoreAudio IO procs

Summary:
`ShimulatorAudioInjectionHAL` is the engine behind the controller. It wraps a process's CoreAudio IO procs and copies injected samples into their input buffers, resampled to the device's rate. It is written against an injectable `AudioHAL`, so it is tested on the Mac against a fake HAL, and nothing links it into a binary yet.

- **Realtime-safe.** The audio thread only try-locks around the sample copy, and skips the fill rather than wait. Allocation, HAL property reads and freeing finished audio happen on the client thread.
- **Registrations are keyed on the `ioProcID` the HAL returned**, not the client data (`NULL` is legal) or the device (two recorders can share one). A destroy waits for a callback already in flight, and the context is never freed: a callback that has been handed it but not yet counted itself in finds it retired, not freed memory, and returns without reaching the app.
- **Playback position belongs to the IO proc**, so two recorders each hear the whole file. An injection is finished when nothing is still playing it and something played it to the end.
- **Claim only what was played:** the controller reports `accepted` only once the audio thread has taken samples.

`include/IDBAudioInjectionPrivate.h` declares the HAL types and symbols the iOS SDK uses but does not export, and the audio thread's lock-free counters. The Shimulator shim targets exclude `AudioInjection/` from their header glob, so their builds are unchanged.

fbshipit-source-id: 47a57b92feb03d5404f3caca0dd8eb9a085a01f7

Keep a warm encoder for each display a stream can switch to

Summary:
No behavioural change to what a stream produces. A stream on a simulator whose integrated displays have more than one surface size, such as an iPhone Duo, no longer starts an encoder when it switches display:
- When a configuration names those displays, the stream sets up an encoder for each surface size it is not showing and warms it with one throwaway frame whose output is discarded.
- A switch takes the encoder prepared for the new surface. Spares are keyed by the surface's size and pixel format, which is all an encoder's setup reads from its source; the configuration and edge insets are fixed for the stream's life, so a spare is set up exactly as the switch would set one up. A surface whose format does not match sets up an encoder of its own.

- Spare encoders are torn down when the stream stops.

A simulator with one integrated display, or displays of one size, prepares nothing and replaces its encoder on a surface change as before.

On an iPhone Duo the first frame after a switch now arrives 9–38 ms after it is submitted, against 52–110 ms for a new encoder. Preparing takes one encode per size, right after the stream starts, after its first frame.

ci: make the AI first review precise and stop review loops (#4730)

An audit of 53 AI reviews on 31 PRs found about 15% wrong findings, two
false blocker or major verdicts from guessed dependency APIs, review loops
of up to 6 rounds on small points, and findings that ignored the replies
of the PR author.

- Give the model the PR discussion (inline threads with replies, reviews,
  PR comments) instead of only the earlier AI comments.
- Use the severity terms of the review skill: blocker, question,
  suggestion. Only an open blocker sets ai:review-changes, so a round with
  small points cannot flip the label.
- Limit automatic reviews to two per PR. /ai review still runs more.
- Ask for a quote of the code line, move the finding to that line, and drop
  a finding whose quote is not in the file.
- Install the base branch dependencies (without torch and CUDA) so that the
  model reads their source.
- Keep HTML and mentions in code spans and suggestion blocks, and keep code
  spans in titles and summaries.
- Do not skip the review for a duplicate that is closed or from the same
  author.
- Rewrite the prompt: at most 5 findings, look for regressions outside the
  PR example first, no test or style nits, no recap of the PR description.

Signed-off-by: Michele Dolfi <dol@zurich.ibm.com>
