fix(ocr): read PP-OCRv6 languages through rapidocr's list_supported_langs

rapidocr 3.10.0 removed the PP_OCRV6_LANGS constant from
rapidocr.utils.model_resolver. docling allows rapidocr>=3.9.1,<4.0.0, so a
fresh install now gets 3.10.0 and every RapidOCR language resolution raises
ImportError.

Read the vocabulary through list_supported_langs(TaskType.REC,
OCRVersion.PPOCRV6) instead. It exists in 3.9.1, 3.9.2 and 3.10.0 and returns
the same 52 codes.

Signed-off-by: Yihang Chen <yhc0720@berkeley.edu>

fix(ocr): do not OCR programmatic text because a vector shape crosses it (#4209)

* fix(ocr): do not OCR programmatic text because a vector shape crosses it

The PDF-aware OCR region selector asked backends that implement
has_content_in() whether any shape or bitmap intersects a layout cluster
and sent every hit to OCR. Rules, underlines and table borders cross
clusters of perfectly good programmatic text on most documents, so on the
threaded docling-parse and pypdfium2 backends (the only ones that answer
that query) large parts of text-native pages were rasterised and OCR'd.
The classic docling-parse backend has no shape query and fell back to a
bitmap-only index, which is why the default flip to the threaded backend
in 2.123.0 (#3764) surfaced this as a CPU regression (#4174) and as worse
text in regions that already had a text layer (#4139).

Only bitmaps can now override programmatic text. Clusters with no
visible programmatic text are still OCR'd, so vector-outlined text keeps
working, and the spatial-index path no longer indexes connected shapes so
that every backend applies the same rule.

Resolves #4174

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017KuQqvDhDkiW6n1YjhChn3
Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(ocr): cover the spatial-index path without the removed classic backend

DoclingParseDocumentBackend is now a deprecated wrapper around the threaded
backend (#4244) and no longer supports load_page(). Drop that case and
exercise the spatial-index fallback by disabling has_content_in on the
threaded page backend instead, which still exposes connected shapes.

Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ocr): keep OCR-ing shapes the text layer cannot account for

Gating OCR on the mere presence of programmatic text in a cluster dropped
clusters whose text layer only covers part of them, so glyphs drawn as
filled vector paths beside real text were never recognised (reported on
#4209 with a mixed native/vector reproduction).

Shapes still do not force OCR on their own -- that is the #4174 / #4139
fix this preserves -- but a cluster is now only cleared when every shape in
it is accounted for: either a stroked segment (a rule, an underline, a
table border, as reported by get_shape_lines) or a shape with programmatic
text inside it (a highlight, a filled table cell). Stroked-vs-filled is a
structural property of the content stream rather than a heuristic, and it
separates the two cases exactly. Where a backend cannot report stroked
segments (pypdfium2 returns None), the shape's extent decides instead: a
0.8pt rule measures 145:1 long-to-thick, the stems of a 24pt vector "HI"
measure 6:1 and 1.3:1.

The shape geometry is read at most once per page and only when a cluster
carries both text and shapes, so the text-only fast path is unchanged.

Tests cover the five cases across the threaded, pypdfium2 and
spatial-index selection paths: a rule crossing text and a highlight behind
text must not OCR; vector glyphs beside native text, vector glyphs alone
and an empty region must.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ocr): require a shape's extent to agree before it counts as a rule

Building fixtures for the two edges the previous commit documented showed both
of them losing content on the default backend, and the crude extent test getting
both right where the stroked-segment report did not:

- Letterforms drawn as stroked axis-aligned segments are reported by
  get_shape_lines() exactly as a rule is, so a cluster of them was cleared.
- A rule crossing a filled glyph merges with it into one connected shape, which
  then overlaps a reported segment, so that cluster was cleared too.

Both constructions carry text the text layer does not have, so both need OCR.
The extent is now the necessary condition and the backend's report only confirms
it, which fixes both edges on docling-parse while leaving the five existing cases
unchanged: a 0.8pt rule measures 145:1 long-to-thick, vector letterforms measure
1.3:1 to 6:1 whether filled or stroked, and a rule fused with the glyph it
crosses measures 2.6:1.

This also makes the two backends agree. pypdfium2 does not implement
get_shape_lines(), and it was already deciding on extent alone -- which is why it
was the one getting these two cases right.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ocr): decide what a rule is from its extent, not a stroke report

A rule drawn as a filled rectangle -- `re f` rather than `m l S`, which plenty of
producers emit -- is never mentioned by get_shape_lines(), so requiring that
report to agree sent exactly the #4174 case back to OCR on the docling-parse
backend. pypdfium2 got it right only because it has no such report and was
already deciding on extent alone.

The stroked-segment report turns out to be wrong in both directions: it misses
filled rules, and it reports letterforms drawn as stroked segments exactly as it
reports a rule. The shape's extent alone separates every case in the fixtures, so
the report is no longer consulted and the plumbing for it is gone.

Adds the filled-rectangle rule as a third region of the edge-case fixture, since
it is the commonest of these constructions and the one whose regression would be
least visible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ocr): judge text behind a shape only inside the cluster

A connected shape can reach far beyond the cluster it touches: an
outlined glyph fused with a page-wide fill, say. Probing the whole
shape for text then finds native text under the fill elsewhere on the
page, counts the glyph as accounted for, and the cluster is never
OCR'd. Clip the probe to the cluster first, and dismiss a sliver of a
neighbouring fill that merely crosses the cluster edge the way a rule
is dismissed.

New fixture tests/data/pdf/vector_glyphs_merged_fill.pdf pins both
constructions on the threaded, pypdfium2 and spatial-index paths.

Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ocr): require text to cover a thick shape before it counts as accounted for

On a DocLayNet page an aeronautical chart drawn entirely as paths, one
connected shape, carried a single native caption in its corner. Judged
on text presence alone the chart was cleared and its vector-drawn
labels never reached OCR. Text now accounts for a shape in two ways: a
band no thicker than two text lines (a highlight, a table stripe, a
filled cell) is explained by any text on it, while a thicker shape
needs text over at least a tenth of its clipped area. Across 1,956
shape/cluster pairs in a 227-page corpus this moves 24 clusters back
to OCR, all vector figures or sparse shaded tables, and changes no
band, highlight or cell fill.

Both paths now decide from the page's text cell geometry, read lazily
on the native-query path, so the two backends agree by construction.

New fixture tests/data/pdf/vector_glyphs_in_figure.pdf pins the
figure, the band and the sidebar on all three selection paths.

Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(latex): resolve \input and \includegraphics for str sources (#4697)

A str source is read into a stream before it reaches the LaTeX backend,
and the handlers resolved \input, \include, \includegraphics and the

silently dropped every included file and figure image.

ci: do not report an unreadable reference file as added (#4690)

* ci: do not report an unreadable reference file as added

The AI triage classified a changed groundtruth file only by the blobs it
could read. read_blob returns None for any git failure, so a modified
file whose base blob could not be read was reported as "added", the kind
that gets the least review. The fetch uses --filter=blob:none, so a blob
read can fail without any attacker.

summarize_file now takes the file status that GitHub reports. A file is
added or removed only when GitHub says so. A missing blob for any other
status is reported as unparsable.

ci: render AI triage model text as literal Markdown (#4691)

The model answer of the AI triage can be steered by text in the pull
request, and the bot signs the comment that shows it. sanitize_text
escaped only <, > and |, and defanged mentions. A summary or a reason
could still add a link, an image, a heading, or a code fence that hides
the CI-safety verdict below it.

Escaping happened at parse time, and publish parses the stored result
again. So the second pass escaped the escapes: "a | b" became "a \\| b",
which turns the pipe back on in a table cell.

Split the work. clean_text reduces the text to one printable line and
gives the same result when it runs twice. At render time, markdown_text
escapes every ASCII punctuation character, which CommonMark renders as
the character itself, and breaks bare URLs and mentions with a zero-width
space. markdown_code puts a path in a code span that the path cannot
close.

The review summary goes through the same path. A finding body keeps its
Markdown, so that it can quote code in a fenced block.

Signed-off-by: Michele Dolfi <dol@zurich.ibm.com>

Needle 3 MLX forward pass (#149)

* feat(model): MLX port of the Needle 3 forward, with a parity test against JAX

needle/model/architecture_mlx.py runs SimpleAttentionNetwork.__call__ on
MLX: conv-tap GQA attention with separate qk/v head dims, sliding window
and global layers, the Hadamard MLP, the engram lookup, the four-lane

and any mask. Config, geometry and the Hadamard permutations are
imported from architecture.py rather than copied.

* feat(model): QAT numerics for the MLX forward

needle/model/quantize_mlx.py mirrors quantize.py for what the training
loss uses: CQ weight quantisation with its straight-through estimator

fix(platform): keep the old file when a download is cut short (#160)

Platform._fetch_to opened its destination for writing before the first
byte arrived and copied the response into it. When the connection dropped
partway, http.client's read(n) returned what had arrived without raising
(only a bare read() raises IncompleteRead), so the call returned normally:
a model re-downloaded over a working one was replaced by its first few
bytes with no error at all, and `needle platform jobs <id> --out DIR`
reported the truncated weights as downloaded. A signed link that had
expired, or any other failure there, escaped as a raw urllib exception
rather than the PlatformError every other Platform call raises, so the
CLI printed a traceback.

The download now goes to `<dest>.part`, is checked against the length
the server announced, and replaces `dest` only once complete; the partial
file is removed on any failure. HTTP and network failures become
PlatformError (`http_<status>` or `network_error`).

Signed-off-by: kevin9327 <5299031+kevin9327@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: read and write tool and training files as UTF-8 on every platform (#159)

The tools JSON and the training JSONL are UTF-8, but every open() that
reads or writes them passed no encoding, so Python used the locale's. On
Windows that is the ANSI code page: "set the café lights to 22°C" in a
training file came back as "cafÃ©" and "22Â°C" (cp1252) or "caf챕" and
"22째C" (cp949) with no error, and a line holding an emoji stopped
`needle finetune` with UnicodeDecodeError. The same happened to the files
read by `needle generate-data` (--tools and --augment), `needle platform
generate`, and `needle run --tools`.

The reads in read_examples, augment_jsonl, generate_main, run.main, and the
platform's generate command now pass encoding="utf-8", and so do the writes
of generated data, so a file needle writes is read back the same anywhere.

Signed-off-by: kevin9327 <5299031+kevin9327@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(tools): keep a docstring argument's wrapped lines in its description (#158)

A Google-style argument description that wraps continues on lines indented
under the argument. _parse_doc matched each line on its own and dropped the
ones without a "name:" prefix, so only the first line reached the schema:

    time: The alarm time in 24-hour HH:MM form, for example 07:30
        or 18:45. Never a relative time like "in ten minutes".

gave the model "The alarm time in 24-hour HH:MM form, for example 07:30",
and the constraint on the second line never reached constrained decoding.

A line indented deeper than the argument it follows is now the rest of that
argument's description. The argument list also ends at the next section
header ("Returns:", "Raises:"), so a Returns entry that shares a
parameter's name no longer overwrites that parameter's description.

Signed-off-by: kevin9327 <5299031+kevin9327@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(tools): keep an Optional argument optional when it is Annotated (#171)

`_is_optional` looks for a Union with None at the top of the
annotation, so `units: Annotated[Optional[str], Field(description=...)]`
is not recognised and lands in `required`, while the same argument
written as `Optional[str]` does not.  Adding a description or a
constraint the way the docs show therefore turns an optional argument
into a required one, and the engine fills it: with the published 3.0.1
engine, "What's the weather in Paris?" returns `units: "imperial"` for
the Annotated form and no `units` for the plain one.

Look through `Annotated` before checking for Optional.

Signed-off-by: breken-ai <312387581+breken-ai@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: breken-ai <312387581+breken-ai@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(fetch): refuse a machine no engine is built for instead of handing it x86_64 (#161)

_platform_tag() mapped every machine other than arm64 to the x86_64 engine,
so a 32-bit ARM, riscv64 or i686 Linux box, or a 32-bit Python on Windows,
downloaded and cached a library it could not load ("wrong ELF class",
"not a valid Win32 application"), and on Linux downloaded the other libc's
x86_64 build as well before failing. The two published architectures are
now recognised by name and anything else raises a RuntimeError that names
the machine and points at NEEDLE3_LIB_PATH / NEEDLE2_LIB_PATH.

Signed-off-by: kevin9327 <5299031+kevin9327@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

cancel_download() dropped the task from _active_tasks while _reap_payload was still aborting xet, so a delete right after a cancel removed the tree before the writer stopped. The task now stays there until _run_download finishes.

Drop the ._____temp sweep, which hub 1.x does not use (it is ModelScope's temp folder name), and point test_cancel_download at hub's real staging layout so it no longer waits out the blocked worker's 5s timeout. Trim the long docstrings and fold the duplicate cleanup tests.

fix(downloads): keep aborting xet until a cancelled download's writer stops (#4373)

* fix(downloads): clean hub's real partial files and cancel a download before deleting its model

Cancel removed nothing from disk and deleting a model left its download
running.

`_cleanup_partial()` swept `<target>/._____temp`, the staging directory
huggingface_hub 0.x used. The pinned hub (>=1.19.0) stages an unfinished file
as `<target>/.cache/huggingface/download/<name>.<hash>.<etag>.incomplete` and
renames it into place on completion, so cancel left the partial behind -- a
real download shows exactly that path. The `.metadata` files next to it stay:
they are what lets the next attempt skip files it has already verified.

`DELETE /api/hf/models/{model_name}` removed the tree without consulting the
downloader, and `remove_task()` refuses a DOWNLOADING task, so no path from
that route ever cancelled the transfer. The route now cancels the task that
writes into the directory it is about to remove.

What still does not stop is the transfer itself: `snapshot_download` runs in a
detached `asyncio.to_thread` worker, and `abort_xet_session()` only reaches the
groups already in flight while the hub builds a fresh session for the next
file. Fixing that means running the download in the existing child-process
worker, which this change deliberately leaves alone.

Fixes #4347

* fix(downloads): keep aborting xet until a cancelled download's writer stops

Cancelling a download left the transfer running: `abort_xet_session()` only
cancels the downloads already in flight, and the hub builds a fresh session
for the next file it starts (`get_xet_session()` recreates the session the
abort dropped), so the cancelled task returned -- row "cancelled", partial
files swept -- while its worker thread kept pulling bytes into the same tree.
Measured on a real xet repo, cancel just after the payload starts left
279.6 / 11.4 / 279.6 MB written after the cancel, and one run transferred for
the whole 2 min 14 s window the reporter saw.

The payload call is now held as a future and awaited under `asyncio.shield`,
so a cancel leaves it where it can be watched instead of detaching it, and
`_reap_payload()` aborts the session again every 0.5 s until that call
returns. Its return is the only proof the writer stopped; the download
semaphore is still held meanwhile, so the abort cannot land on a queued task.

Same repo, same cancel point: 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0 MB written after the cancel, the
worker back 1.1-1.5 s later after 3-4 aborts, no executor thread left.
`cancel_download_for_dir()` now also waits for that return, so the delete
route removes the tree only after its writer stopped.

IoT Hub: filter the catalogue by the creator's verification status (#16165)

* feat: filter the IoT Hub catalogue by the creator's verification status

Adds a "Verified creators only" control to every IoT Hub filter panel the
platform renders: the catalogue page, the embedded browse a dialog opens, and
the widget picker in the dashboard editor. It applies through the new
creatorVerified parameter on /api/versions/published, so the result count and
the page count reflect it rather than only the rows on screen, and it joins the
rest of the panel's state - chips, the count on the filter button, "Clear all",
and the reset that happens when the mode changes.

The control is a single checkbox above the facets rather than a section of its
own: one boolean has no list to collapse, and a one-option accordion reads as a
heading whose section never grows. The catalogue's sidebar had no name for its
panel at all, which left that checkbox sitting under nothing, so the sidebar now
carries the same "Filter" title the drawer has, with the same rule under it.

The parameter is matched, not switched, the shape peOnly/ceOnly already have:
creatorVerified=false means "only *un*verified". An unchecked control therefore
omits it entirely and never sends false - MpItemVersionQuery.toQuery() writes
the parameter only when the option is true, and both panels pass undefined
rather than false.

Two surfaces need the facet applied by hand. "Installed from IoT Hub" filters a
cached list in the browser instead of asking the server, so it gets the same
predicate locally; without it the panel would offer the control and the list
would not move. And the widget picker's category landing passes the parameter
to /api/item-listing/widgetCategories, so it stops offering a category whose
only widgets the grid then hides - which is also why the filter button is now
shown on the landing while the flag is set, the one place the panel is
otherwise hidden and the filter would have been unclearable.

The creator page and the search page run the same reads through a component
with no filter panel, so the parameter never reaches them.

Copy names what it filters - the creator's verification status - and claims no
quality tier.

test: openraft: use TypeConfigExt for time and runtime calls

# Summary

Tests get the current time, sleeps, and oneshot channels from the type
config's runtime instead of naming `TokioInstant`, `TokioRuntime`, or
`std::time::Instant` directly.

# Details

Naming the Tokio types ties a test to Tokio. For example, comparing
`TokioInstant::now()` with `vote_last_modified()`, which returns
`InstantOf<C>`, compiles only while the type config's runtime is Tokio.

`t11_client_reads` also stops using `std::time::Instant`. The
linearizer wait timeout it measures fires on the runtime clock, and a
virtual-clock runtime would make the two clocks differ.

add() uploads batches from a thread pool, get_nodes() scrolls from a
producer thread, and ingests run concurrently. Interleaved writes leave
the collection's arrays with different lengths, which fails later inside
Qdrant, e.g. "IndexError: index 1699 is out of bounds for axis 0 with
size 1699" when uploading a file.

When the builder creates a local-path client, make every public
QdrantLocal method hold one shared re-entrant lock. Remote clients are
unchanged.

Fixes #2392

Signed-off-by: onevcat <onevcat@gmail.com>

fix: close the resize-session guard gaps found in review

Round-1 review of #150 found four gaps in the resizable app session
stop-gap; all are closed here.

- `paste --via-menu` is a long-press plus edit-menu taps, so it is a
  touch path: refuse it before the pasteboard is written and again after
  `--target-id` resolution. Cmd+V paste stays ungated. Messages and docs
  now say "Cmd+V paste" and name `--via-menu` as refused.
- `batch` checks every touch step after parsing and before dispatch, not
  only before the loop: a selector step's tree fetch can turn a cached
  "no session" into an active one, and a long batch outlives the cache
  TTL. The session error propagates unchanged so the hint survives.
- The cache bypass takes scene evidence (the AX root size) instead of a
  flag and re-probes only when that evidence differs from the cached
  probe's; `resizedSceneEvidence` also treats a uniform panel downscale
  (iPhone mini 375x812 over 360x780) as a device size. A downscaled
  display no longer spawns devicectl on every fetch.
- The bundled skill's compatibility floor moves to 0.15.0 and
  PreflightScriptTests cover both sides of it: the Resize Mode recipe
  relies on detection a 0.14.0 CLI does not have.

Unit coverage: evidence semantics, downscaled sizes, per-step kind
classifier, floor cases. E2E: paste --via-menu refused for coordinate
and id targets with Cmd+V still accepted, and a batch started inside the
stale cache window refused at its first touch step with nothing landing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Signed-off-by: onevcat <onevcat@gmail.com>

fix: detect Xcode 27 resizable app sessions and refuse undeliverable touch input

Xcode 27 Resize Mode moves the frontmost app onto a virtual "Resizable"
display while the main display keeps SpringBoard. Every simulator
primitive sim-use drives is bound to the main display: HID touch
(digitizer target 0, main-screen normalisation), the framebuffer
(displayClass 0) and the accessibility point hit-test. During a session
taps reported success and delivered nothing, screenshots captured the
wallpaper, hit-test recovery spliced SpringBoard nodes into the app tree
and the orientation probe read a resized scene as rotated (issue #143).

Detect the session through `devicectl device info appResize` (document
classified, not exit status) behind a per-UDID 5 s TTL cache that lives
in the daemon, skipped on Xcode < 27 and under
SIM_USE_RESIZE_SESSION_CHECK=0. An AX root that is neither the device's
portrait size nor its landscape swap bypasses a cached "no session", so a
session that just started is noticed by the first `ui` or selector tap.

- tap, long-press, swipe, touch, gesture, multi-touch and a batch with a
  touch step fail with an explanation and a hint instead of a false
  success. Keyboard verbs are untouched: keyboard HID reaches the
  resized app (verified live).
- screenshot captures the Resizable display through
  `simctl io … screenshot --display=<uuid>` and says so in a
  resizable_app_session advisory.
- ui returns the app's own tree in identity calibration with the same
  advisory, skipping calibration probes, collapsed-children recovery and
  the remote-content retry; ui --point carries the advisory because its
  answer describes SpringBoard.

Unit coverage pins the captured devicectl documents, the cache rules and
the messages; ResizeModeTests drives a real session end to end and skips
itself where devicectl cannot host one. docs/ai/xxxx-resizable-app-session
records the reproduction, the touchscreen(0x104) digitizer finding, the
spike that did not land a tap, upstream idb's Duo display plumbing and
the follow-up tiers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Signed-off-by: onevcat <onevcat@gmail.com>

FindNanopb: handle NANOPB_OPTIONS given as a list

NANOPB_OPTIONS is turned into a list as soon as find_package()
COMPONENTS are appended to it, and it is natural to write it as
set(NANOPB_OPTIONS --source-extension=.cpp --header-extension=.hpp)
as well. In that case two things went wrong:

- the extension regexes stop only at a space, so the match for
  --source-extension swallowed the following list items and e.g.
  "--header-extension=.hpp" ended up as an entry in PROTO_SRCS.
- the semicolons were passed through into --nanopb_opt, so CMake split

that sets list-form options together with a component.
